jobs.title: Translator & Interpreter (Re-advertisement - for internal and external candidates), Grade 17
jobs.company: UN Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East
jobs.description:
## Org. Setting and Reporting

UNRWA is a United Nations agency established by the General Assembly in 1949 and is mandated to provide assistance and protection to a population of some 5.8 million registered Palestine refugees. Its mission is to help Palestine refugees in Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, West Bank and the Gaza Strip to achieve their full potential in human development, pending a just solution to their plight. UNRWA's services encompass education, health care, relief and social services, camp infrastructure and improvement, microfinance, and emergency assistance. UNRWA is the largest UN operation in the Middle East with more than 30,000 staff. UNRWA is funded almost entirely by voluntary contributions.

If you are looking for a rewarding opportunity to make a tangible difference for one of the most vulnerable communities in the world, UNRWA would like to hear from you.

- Supervisor: The incumbent reports to the Director of Communications.

## Responsibilities

- Translates documents, reports, and website content from English into Arabic and vice versa for internal or external use, ensuring accuracy and precision.

- Acts as interpreter at internal and external meetings, press briefings and other official occasions as required.

- Assists the Head of Creative Digital Multimedia Communications with editing of UNRWA's official Arab language materials; collaborates with the Communications Division's Arabic desk in these tasks.

- Edits and proofreads agency-wide documents, as required, including sensitive documents, pertaining to the work of the Executive Office and from other departments such as the Department of Legal Affairs, Department of Human Resources, Ethics Office, Office of the Ombudsman, Protection and Neutrality unit; and assists such departments in overseeing the final production of their key

documents, bulletins and other issuances.

- Performs other duties as may be assigned by the Director of Communications, including, where required, in support of other offices or departments in the Agency.

## Competencies

UN Core Values of Integrity, Professionalism and Respect for Diversity, and Core Competencies of Communication, Working with People and Drive for Results apply by default.

- Applying Technical Expertise
- Analyzing
- Planning and Organizing
- Delivering Results
- Demonstrating Self-Awareness
- Ability to work independently or in a team.
- Tactful and well-developed political awareness.
- Knowledge and experience of using computer with proficiency in word processing in English and Arabic.

## Education

- Advanced university degree (Master's or equivalent) from an accredited educational institution in English, translation and interpretation or a related field.

## Job Specific Qualifications

**Work Experience**

Indicate your current involvement in any outside activities, as it is required. Including but not limited to employment, independent contractor/freelance consultant, board member (corporate, academic, etc), expert group, lobby, public speaking/writing (article, book, blog, social media etc), teaching, conferences, training, press statement, voluntary work, political activity, fundraising/donation for non-UNRWA entity, running for public office, role in political party or orgs, owning business, work for gov./NGO/private company/charity, UNRWA partner/vendor, full/part-time, paid or not. A "yes" answer doesn't necessarily lead to exclusion from future work at UNRWA, yet misrepresentation in providing accurate/complete info can lead to disqualification/termination of appointment, if hired.

- You are required to have at least seven years of experience in translation and interpretation work from Arabic into English and vice-versa, of which three years were in an international organization.

- Excellent command of written and spoken English and Arabic is required.

- You are required to have an advanced university degree (Master's or equivalent) from an accredited educational institution in English, translation and interpretation or a related field.

- Are you currently residing in Duty Station. It is required that you specify your current location.

- Do you currently hold a contract of 1 year or more with UNRWA? If yes, please confirm whether you have completed your mandatory probation period is required.

- Have you previously been a recipient under the EVR (Early Voluntary Retirement) or EVS (Early Voluntary Separation) Schemes? You are required to answer.

## Languages

English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, English **and** Arabic are required. The table below shows the minimum required level for each skill in these languages, according to the UN Language Framework (please consult [https://languages.un.org](https://languages.un.org/) for details).

## Required Languages

**Language**

**Reading**

**Writing**

**Listening**

**Speaking**

**English**

UN Level III

UN Level III

UN Level III

UN Level III

**Arabic**

UN Level III

UN Level III

UN Level III

UN Level III

### Assessment

During the assessment, the applications will be given preference based on the following desirable qualifications:

- Previous experience at a UN agency or international non-governmental organization;
- Knowledge of contemporary Middle East political and cultural affairs.
- Provided very good understanding of the context of Palestine refugees and UNRWA operations.

The shortlisted candidates will be afterward evaluated based on:

- Technical Test
- Competency-based Interview

Candidates who meet the post requirements and the required language level will be considered for the ongoing competitive process.

To ensure alignment with the UN language levels, please refer to the guidance below: Level I: Basic knowledge of English.

Level II: Good to very good command of English. Level III: Excellent English language skills.

Level IV: Expert level or native proficiency.

### Special Notice

Providing incorrect, incomplete or misleading information on an application form will result in the immediate disqualification of the candidate.

Contract Type:

Fixed Term Appointment for 1 year; 1 year probation period, with the possibility of further extension, subject to the availability of funds, satisfactory performance, and continuing need.

Grade and Salary:

Grade 17 Monthly basic salary JD 1156.600 fils. Special Occupational Allowance (SoA) 69.9% of basic salary. The salary may be subject to a reduced work schedule.

Other benefits: Other benefits include monthly Provident Fund contribution (15.4% of basic salary paid by the Agency), compulsory medical insurance, 30 days of annual leave, and dependency allowance (if applicable).

Additional benefits:

-2 days of sick leave for each completed month of service.

-14 weeks of Maternity Leave.

-2 weeks paternity leave.

Department/Office: UNRWA - External Relations and Communications Duty Station: Headquarters Amman

Other Information:

- The incumbent may be required to travel in the Agency's areas of operations within the Middle East, including on short notice.
- The incumbent may be expected to work beyond regular working hours.

Equivalency:

Equivalency may apply for this post.

- Candidates with a combination of additional relevant academic qualifications and/or additional years of progressive work experience may also be considered on equivalency.

NB: Work experience alone or formal qualifications with no relevant work experience are not considered an acceptable combination.

General Information:

- This vacancy notice is open to internal and external candidates. Only candidates residing in Jordan, and within commuting distance of the duty station with authorization to work in the duty station at the time of application are eligible to apply.

- The Agency will not assume responsibility or accountability to support or facilitate the issuance of work permit in Jordan, and without a valid work permit, the appointment may be rescinded.

- Since the Vacancy is an Area Staff post, the Agency will not provide coverage for relocation costs.

- Preference will be given to registered Palestine refugees and candidates assisting the Agency to meet its commitment to gender parity. UNRWA welcomes applications from qualified candidates with disabilities.

- To ensure efficiency and timeliness of the recruitment process, if a large number of applicants pass the test, the Agency may decide to invite to the interview only the candidates with the top scores to ensure a manageable number of candidates to proceed to the personal interview stage.

- UNRWA is committed to achieving gender balance in its workforce. Qualified and experienced female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply.

- A roster may be created from the selection exercise, and successful candidates may become eligible for appointment to the same post or a similar post. In the case of multiple or recurring posts, that a roster will be created from which the candidates will be selected for appointment;

- Only applications that have been fully completed in UNRWA's online e-recruitment system inspira will be considered and no late applications will be accepted. The PHP should be completed with full relevant work experience under the experience tabs as per the requirements in the Job Opening. All acquired university degrees must also be stated, if applicable. Please make sure that your application is filled in properly, correctly, and completely; any missing or incomplete information may lead to the rejection of the application by the system. Applicants applying to positions for Grades 12 to 20 or LDC Bands E to H must submit a cover letter/motivational statement in order to be considered.

Additionally, providing incorrect or misleading information on an application will result in the immediate disqualification of a candidate.

- Applicants will be disqualified when it becomes apparent that he or she provided incorrect, incomplete or misleading information on his or her personal history profile or during the recruitment process. If the applicant is also a staff member, the provision of incorrect, incomplete or misleading information in the personal history profile may also amount to misconduct. The Agency may indefinitely refuse to accept applications from an applicant who has previously provided incorrect, incomplete or misleading information on his or her personal history profile or during a recruitment process or committed plagiarism.

- For UNRWA internal staff, they are required to specify and include their current UNRWA grade level. To do so applicants should select under "Category" RLG, scroll down to see all categories, then select their local grade.

- Please find below the link to a video that guides applicants on how to apply to Job Openings: https:

//drive.google.com/file/d/1MH-IYA6Y8kxA1fgao5qyTV8VwNajgx4u/view?usp=sharing

- Advertisements published only in English will only accept applications in English, and Arabic submissions will not be considered.

- UNRWA has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNRWA, including sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA), sexual harassment, racism/racial discrimination and other forms of conduct, including but not limited to discrimination, abuse of authority and harassment. To uphold these standards, background checks are conducted for

all recommended candidates and those placed on a roster to help ensure that individuals with a history of such conduct are not hired. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles. Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s), employment history, ClearCheck and INTERPOL, as well as certification of non-conviction, where available. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check. By applying for a position with UNRWA, candidates acknowledge and consent to these verification processes.

- The Agency may disqualify applicants whose name appears on the UN Sanctions List or a UN database of staff separated for reason of misconduct or of staff who separated whilst misconduct processes were pending.

- UNRWA shares investigation and misconduct information with other UN Agencies, and past and prospective employers about staff members who have been separated for misconduct, or who have separated while an investigation and/or disciplinary process for misconduct was underway; and those individuals may be prohibited from employment with the United Nations.

- The Agency will immediately disqualify applicants who are ineligible for any reason in accordance with the Agency regulatory framework.

- UNRWA is funded almost entirely by voluntary contributions from UN member states, regional

bodies, business foundations and individual contributions. The mission of UNRWA is to help Palestine

refugees achieve their full potential in human development under the difficult circumstances in which they live.

For more details on UNRWA, please visit: [https://www.unrwa.org](https://www.unrwa.org/)

- Applications from UNRWA staff member who had been demoted with deferred eligibility for promotion will not be considered.

- Applications from Staff members who were recipients under the Early Voluntary Retirement or Exceptional Voluntary Separation Schemes will not be considered.

- Applications from Internal candidates serving for less than one year in their current post will not be considered.

- The Agency reserves the right not to make an appointment, to make an appointment at a lower grade, or to make an appointment with a modified job description or to change the contract Modality.

- A candidate is not eligible for consideration if he or she was short-listed and found not suitable for the same post within the previous 12 months unless the post description has since been altered by 30% or more, as determined by ODCS.

- UNRWA reserves the right to proceed only with internal candidates or proceed with the candidates of an under-represented gender for any vacancy announcement when it determines that the short-list for a single post at any grade level is excessively long.

### United Nations Considerations

Staff members are subject to the authority of the Commissioner-General of UNRWA and to assignment by him or her.

UNRWA is committed to achieving gender parity at all levels of staffing under the current UN-wide gender agenda and strongly encourages applications from qualified applicants from under-represented groups.

At UNRWA, the paramount consideration in the recruitment and employment of staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence and integrity, with due regard to geographic diversity. All employment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications and organizational needs. UNRWA is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment of mutual respect. Reasonable accommodation for applicants with disabilities may be provided to support participation in the recruitment process when requested and indicated in the application.

UNRWA Considerations

UNRWA staff are expected to uphold the highest standards of efficiency, competence, neutrality,

impartiality and integrity. This includes respect for and commitment to human rights, diversity and non-violent means of dealing with all kinds of conflict. Only persons who fully and unconditionally commit to these values should consider applying for UNRWA jobs. Candidates will not be considered for employment with UNRWA if they have committed violations of international human rights law, violations of international humanitarian law, sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, or sexual harassment, or if there are reasonable grounds to believe that they have been involved in the commission of any of these acts. Candidates who have committed crimes other than minor traffic offences may not be considered for employment. The Agency may disqualify applicants who have separated for reason of misconduct, who left a UN Agency while misconduct processes were pending, or who appear on the UN Sanctions List.

UNRWA is a non-smoking work environment.

jobs.title: Deputy Program Manager - Cell 4
jobs.description:
**Join MSF OCG as a Deputy Program Manager - Cell 4!**

**We are looking for passionate candidates ready to contribute to our humanitarian mission.**

**Below, you will find the job details and the qualifications we are looking for.**

## Inclusivity and Diversity at MSF

Do your qualifications and experience not exactly match all requirements of the job?

At MSF OCG, we are committed to an inclusive culture that supports and amplifies the diverse voices of our staff members. We strive to create workplaces where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together to advance MSF's social mission and create better outcomes for our patients and the communities we work with.

We understand that some people may hesitate to apply for employment if they don't meet all listed job requirements. Research shows that this is especially true for women. If you believe your profile is a good match for this position, we invite you to apply even if you don’t fulfil every listed qualification.

We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment. All selected candidates will undergo reference checks.

## Context & mission

Médecins Sans Frontières is an independent, international medical and humanitarian organization that provides care to people in need, people affected by natural or man-made disasters, and victims of armed conflict, without discrimination and without regard to race, religion, creed or political affiliation (MSF Charter).

We are looking for an experienced **Deputy Program Manager (ARP)** to join **Cell 4**.

Reporting to the Program Manager, the Deputy Program Manager plays a key role in steering MSF’s operations within Cell 4, contributing to operational decision-making and ensuring the relevance, timeliness and quality of MSF’s assistance. The role supports operational planning, resource mobilisation, programme monitoring, security and advocacy, while supervising and supporting Heads of Mission. As a central operational role within MSF, the Deputy Program Manager acts as a key interface between missions and headquarters, ensuring effective information flow, coherent HQ support and a shared understanding of operational priorities across OCG. The role also contributes to the internal visibility of programmes and to critical reflection on operational challenges and MSF’s social mission.

## Tasks & Responsibilities

By delegation of responsibilities and tasks from the Program Manager:

- In accordance with the Charter, the Chantilly / La Mancha agreements and OCG operational policy, the Deputy Program Manager ensures the overall relevance, timeliness and quality of MSF’s assistance to populations in danger within a selected group of countries.
- Is responsible for steering the operations planning cycle, ensuring that transversal internal processes are respected, that MSF policies are translated into action unless otherwise justified, and that resources are adequately mobilized to support operational objectives and the chosen intervention strategies.
- Ensures that key medical and/or humanitarian stakes are identified within each mission and project, prioritizes them, and carries them internally and externally through bilateral meetings, documentation, témoignage and communication; determines how MSF will address the issues at stake and defines its public position.
- Creates and maintains a network of relevant political, humanitarian, medical and academic contacts to ensure the best possible knowledge of the environment for teams working in the field, especially in tense contexts.
- Monitors the level of exposure to risk affecting teams in the field and validates the security framework proposed by the Heads of Mission for each project.
- Supervises, advises, supports and evaluates the Heads of Mission in the fulfilment of their overall responsibilities and duties; in this perspective, provides them with all relevant information and visits missions at key moments (exploratory missions, programme definition phases and/or reorientations due to evolving needs, context or policy).
- Organizes the best possible level of headquarters support to field operations by optimizing the input, expertise and control functions of professionals from different departments, each representing a technical field necessary for the effective running of projects in the field.
- Monitors programme implementation and the effective running of missions by analysing situation and programme reports submitted by the coordination and providing feedback; is accountable for timely reporting on operations, including institutional donors supporting MSF’s action in the field.
- Aims to continuously improve MSF’s medical assistance by evaluating results achieved, leading thematic working groups on intervention strategies, initiating critical reviews as needed, supporting operational research projects, and contributing to the design and delivery of training modules for coordinators.

## Your profile

*Education*

- University-level degree in international relations, social sciences, medicine, public health, a paramedical field, or equivalent professional experience.

*Experience*

- Experience in humanitarian aid, ideally as an MSF Head of Mission or Emergency Coordinator. Previous experience as a Medical Coordinator is an asset.
- Expertise in analysing and managing unstable contexts and crisis situations.
- Experience in, and interest in, the medical, social, economic and political dimensions of countries affected by humanitarian crises, whether acute or protracted, or undergoing development, is an asset.

*Languages*

- Fluency in English and French is mandatory.
- Knowledge of a third language is an asset.

*Skills/ professional competencies*

- Strong representation and diplomatic skills, with proven negotiation abilities.
- Strong strategic planning and orientation skills.
- Ability to analyse humanitarian contexts, with a sound understanding of medical issues and MSF intervention strategies.
- Ability to design and plan medical programmes, build and maintain networks, motivate and lead teams, organise responsibilities and delegate tasks effectively.
- Excellent writing skills.

*Personal Abilities/Qualities*

- Dynamic and flexible, with strong initiative and decision-making skills.
- Strong analytical and synthesis skills, with a clear sense of priorities.
- Highly developed stress-management skills.
- Strong communication and public-speaking skills.
- Participative management style.

## Terms of employment

- Full-time position 100% (40h/week)
- 3 years contract, renewable once.
- Working place: Based in Geneva, with very frequent international travel.
- Ideal start date: 1st of December 2026
- Gross annual salary (for 100%): from CHF 110’652.- to CHF 129’348.- (salary commensurate with equivalent experience and internal salary grid)
- Paid vacation: 25 days per year, prorate temporis, plus any Swiss public holidays falling within the contract period.
- Pension plan: pension contribution covered 3/4 by MSF, 1/4 by staff member.
- Relocation support available for eligible candidates.

jobs.title: Market Systems Technical Coordinator
jobs.description:
**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Market Systems Technical Coordinator contributes, under the leadership of the FES lead, to the design of Oxfam's market systems and enterprise portfolio in Syria, across humanitarian, recovery and development programming. Key responsibilities cover market analysis and programme design, enterprise development and financial inclusion, support to producer organisations, engagement with private and public market actors, partner and team capacity, and integration with WASH, protection, gender and MEAL. The role pays particular attention to the participation and role of women, vulnerable groups and other excluded actors within the market system. The role contributes market evidence to funding proposals and to Oxfam's policy and advocacy work.

In the first 12 months, the post holder is expected to: (1) lead on a value chain selection exercise and deliver two value chain or market studies with intervention designs; (2) map priority producer organisations, market actors and open working relationships with chambers, agro-processors and financial institutions; and (3) supply market evidence and results frameworks to at least two funding proposals and/or learning papers.

**Market analysis and programme design**

- Lead the selection of value chains, using economic, environmental, employment and gender criteria, starting from a shortlist of two to three sectors agreed with the FES Lead for year one, drawn from the priority sectors in the FES strategy, including but not limited to: livestock and fodder, fruit and olive, vegetables, dairy, fisheries, textiles, handicraft and heritage, and construction and mechanics.
- Design and manage market assessments, value chain studies, feasibility studies and market actor mapping; commission and quality-assure consultancies where needed.
- Apply market analysis to humanitarian as well as recovery design, including EMMA and market monitoring for cash programming, so that emergency response supports rather than displaces local markets.
- Translate analysis into intervention logic: identify where the constraints (input supply, finance, storage, transport, standards, regulation, information) and support or lead the design of interventions against it.
- Contribute market evidence and results frameworks to concept notes, proposals and donor reports, working with the funding team.

**Enterprise development and financial inclusion**

- Design and quality-assure business development services, delivered through hub teams and partners, including advisory support, business planning, market information, incubation and links to buyers.
- Develop financial inclusion pathways for small producers and enterprises: savings groups, cooperative finance, and engagement with microfinance and other financial actors as liquidity allows.
- Ensure enterprise support reaches women and young people on terms that do not push them into unprotected informal work, and design against that risk explicitly.

**Producer organisations and collective action**

- Design Oxfam's approach to producer collective action (aggregation, quality improvement, direct market linkage and internal governance, with representation of women and young members) and support hub teams and partners to deliver it, so that producers strengthen their bargaining position with traders and middlemen.

**Market actor and private sector engagement**

- Build working relationships with the chambers of commerce, agriculture and industry, agro-processors, input suppliers, traders, transporters and financial institutions.
- Identify where private actors will co-invest, and develop arrangements, for agreement by the FES Lead and project budget holders, designed to hold after the project ends.
- Engage public institutions on market regulation, standards and licensing at governorate and local level, in coordination with the policy and advocacy function.
- Represent Oxfam in technical working groups, coordination forums and consortia on livelihoods, markets and early recovery, as relevant.

**Partner and team capacity**

- Assess partner capacity in market programming and provide structured accompaniment as needed.
- Build market systems literacy across the Food and Economic Security Oxfam teams, so that market thinking is applied across all interventions.

**Integration, learning and influencing**

- Work with the WASH, protection, advocacy, and MEAL functions so that market interventions address water-linked enterprise and shared infrastructure, decent work and exploitation risks, and documented learning shared between hubs.
- Collaborate with gender justice teams on addressing challenges at the intersection of women’s economic participation and unpaid care work.
- Supply evidence to Oxfam's advocacy on market regulation, fair competition, protection of small producers and social protection for informal workers.

Other duties may be reasonably required in supporting the delivery of team objectives and outcomes.

**EXPERIENCE, KNOWLEDGE & COMPETENCIES**

**Essential**

**Core competencies:**

- Agility, complexity and ambiguity
- Relationship building
- Systems thinking
- Decisiveness
- Enabling

**In addition:**

- Bachelor's degree in agricultural economics, economics, business administration, development studies or a related field, with at least seven years of progressively responsible experience in livelihoods, value chain development, agribusiness, financial inclusion, enterprise or SME support, or private sector development.
- Good understanding of rural economies, agricultural livelihoods, producer organisations, and MSMEs.
- A technical diploma in a related field with at least seven years of the same experience may be accepted in place of a bachelor's degree.
- Experience coordinating technical work across teams, field locations or partner organisations without direct line management.
- Demonstrated experience of at least 5 years analysing and developing agricultural, rural or other relevant value chains, including identifying market opportunities.
- Experience conducting or commissioning market assessments, value chain studies or feasibility studies, and using the findings to change a programme design.
- Familiarity with market-based programming and market assessment approaches (for example EMMA or comparable tools).
- Experience working with producers, cooperatives, associations, small enterprises or private sector actors (including financial institutions), with credibility among business people as well as communities.
- Understanding of gender dynamics in Syrian markets and labour, and commitment to designing so that women and young people gain rather than absorb risk.
- Fluency in Arabic; working proficiency in English, sufficient to write reports, assessments and proposal inputs.
- Numerical analysis skills: able to build and interrogate a simple cost structure, margin calculation or business plan.
- Strong facilitation and negotiation skills, including with government bodies, chambers and traders.
- Willingness and ability to travel regularly to hubs across Syria, up to 40 per cent of time.
- Understanding of security protocols and access constraints in conflict-affected areas.
- Commitment to Oxfam's mission, feminist principles, safeguarding policies and code of conduct.

**Desirable**

- Master's degree in a relevant field.
- Familiarity with market systems development (M4P/MSD) approaches through formal training or project experience.
- Experience with cash and voucher assistance in a market analysis role.
- Experience with cooperative or solidarity economy models, savings groups or microfinance.
- Prior INGO or donor-funded project experience, including institutional donor compliance.
- Experience linking programme evidence to advocacy or policy dialogue.

jobs.title: SIEGE – Chargé support financements institutionnels H/F
jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION DE L’ASSOCIATION**

La Chaîne de l’Espoir est une ONG internationale fondée en 1994. Elle a pour vocation de renforcer les systèmes de santé pour donner à chacun et en particulier aux enfants les mêmes chances de survie et de développement. Nous intervenons dans 25 pays par une approche globale, centrée sur l’enfant mais également sur les mères et les communautés défavorisées :

- Prévention et dépistage dès le plus jeune âge, notamment dans le cadre de programmes de santé à l’école.
- Soin et chirurgie, afin de répondre aux besoins les plus urgents des enfants et de leurs mères.
- Formation et transferts de compétences aux équipes locales grâce à notre réseau international d’experts dans tous les domaines de la chirurgie.
- Construction et équipement de structures hospitalières adaptées aux besoins locaux.

**CONTEXTE**

La CDE est partenaire de la DG ECHO depuis la signature de la CCP 2014-2020. La CDE a renouvelé son partenariat avec la DG ECHO et s’est vu attribué un certificat de partenariat standard humanitaire de l’UE en 2021. Parmi les actions humanitaires de la CDE, la DG ECHO a contribué de 2018 à 2023 au financement de son intervention en Jordanie. La DG ECHO contribue aux financements des interventions de la CDE au Liban depuis 2024, avec un contrat de partenariat en cours, et la CDE est également sous-partenaire d’une subvention de la DG ECHO en Syrie depuis mai 2026.

Le prochain certificat de partenariat humanitaire de l’UE doit entrer en vigueur pour la période 2028-2034, et, pour le signer, les organisations candidates doivent présenter à la DG ECHO les résultats d’une évaluation ex-ante effectuée par un auditeur externe accrédités, d’ici le 31 mars 2027, afin de garantir la réception de la certification au 1er janvier 2028.

**POSTE ET MISSION**

Dans le cadre de l’application pour la certification de partenariat humanitaire de la DG ECHO pour 2028-2034, la Chaîne de l’Espoir recrute un chargé support aux financements institutionnels, afin de d’assister à la préparation, à l’organisation et au suivi de l’audit Ex-Ante de l’organisation.

Cette mission vise à soutenir la responsable financements institutionnels chargée de l’organisation de cet audit, d’abord dans la collecte de justificatifs et le nettoyage des archives, puis dans la préparation des équipes, l’accueil des auditeurs, l’organisation des entretiens et le suivi des demandes complémentaires.

La mission de support se déroulera en partie à Paris, au sein de la Direction des Opérations, sous la supervision de la Responsable des financements institutionnels et en collaboration avec le responsable de l’audit et du contrôle interne et les équipes différentes équipes sièges.

**ACTIVITÉS PRINCIPALES**

**Récolte et organisation pièces justificatives pré-audit**

- En collaboration avec la Responsable Financements Institutionnels, analyse le questionnaire d’audit et établi la liste et la sélections des pièces justificatives en amont de l’audit
- Collecte, organisation et revue des pièces justificatives en lien avec les responsables des équipes au siège et sur le terrain (direction programme, direction administrative et financière, direction ressources humaines, direction communication et développement, direction de l’expertise technique, etc.)
- Contrôle la conformité des pièces justificatives avec les conventions de financement, les procédures internes de l’association, les exigences fiscale et sociales applicables et les règles bailleurs
- Collecte l’ensemble des pièces justificatives des procédures sélectionnées des pièces comptables (bon commande, factures, contrats, preuves de paiements), des dossiers logistiques (dossiers d’achats et de mise en concurrence), des dossiers RH, des documents supports « programmes » rattachés au contrat.
- Organisation et revue des dispositifs d’archivages, tableaux de suivi et de partage de documents en liens avec l’audit.

**PRÉPARATION DE L’AUDIT**

- Assiste la Responsable Financements Institutionnels dans l’organisation de l’audit, notamment les jours de missions des auditeurs aux bureaux de la Chaîne de l’Espoir
- Organisation de l’emploi du temps pour les différents entretiens, envoi des invitations, réservation des salles de réunion, suivi des invitations
- Participe aux réunions de préparation pré-audit avec les équipes du cabinet et le siège de la Chaîne de l’Espoir
- Participe aux réunions de préparation pré-entretien avec les différents services et salariés de la Chaîne de l’Espoir qui participeront à l’audit

**Participation à L’AUDIT**

- Participe à l’accueil et au suivi de l’emploi du temps des auditeurs externes lors du déroulement de l’audit
- Assiste la Responsable Financements Institutionnels à constituer et organiser les dossiers d’audit.
- Assiste la Responsable Financements Institutionnels à assurer le suivi de la collecte des documents manquants auprès des équipes siège et terrain.
- Participe à la relecture du rapport final de l’audit externe.

## Profil recherché

**FORMATION ET EXPÉRIENCE PROFESSIONNELLE**

- Formation Master en Relations Internationales Humanitaire, Développement et Coopération, Sciences Politiques et Instituts d’études politiques
- Une première expérience ou une connaissance est souhaitée en gestion de projet, au siège ou sur le terrain
- Une première expérience en audits et/ou suivi des obligations des bailleurs institutionnels fortement appréciée (AFD, ECHO, Union Européenne, etc.)

**COMPÉTENCES ET QUALITÉS REQUISES**

- Très bon relationnel, savoir travailler en équipe et avec de multiples interlocuteurs
- Sens de l’organisation et capacité à analyser un volume important de documents
- Adaptabilité, polyvalence et autonomie
- Rigueur documentaire et sens du contrôle et du détail
- Dynamisme, réactivité, résistance au stress, capacité à travailler sur plusieurs dossiers de manière concomitante
- Anglais et Français courant.
- Maîtrise des outils informatiques (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, Sharepoint)
- Capacité à évoluer au sein d’un environnement multiculturel
- Adhésion aux principes humanitaires et au code d’éthique de La Chaîne de l’Espoir

**CONDITIONS**

- Statut employé – CDD de 3 mois
- Date de démarrage souhaitée : décembre 2026
- Mutuelle prise en charge à 80%
- Remboursement abonnement transport à hauteur de 50 % ou indemnité mobilité durable (vélo) de 45 euros/mois
- Tickets Repas d’une valeur de 12,10 euros pris en charge à 60%
- Charte de télétravail : occasionnel
- 23 jours de RTT annuel
- Fourchette salariale : entre 31 200 et 36 000 euros brut annuel selon profil et expérience
- CE: chèques cadeaux

jobs.title: Head of Mission - Iran
jobs.description:
INTERSOS is an independent humanitarian organization that assists the victims of natural disasters, armed conflicts and exclusion. Its activities are based on the principles of solidarity, justice, human dignity, equality of rights and opportunities, respect for diversity and coexistence, paying special attention to the most vulnerable people.

**Terms of reference**

**Job Title:** Head of Mission

**Code:** SR-58-10281

**Duty station:** Tehran with field missions in projects' locations

**Starting date:** 01/01/2027

**Contract duration:** 5 months (Extendable)

**Reporting to:** Regional Director

**Functional Supervisor:**

**Supervision of:** SMT

**Type of Duty Station:** Non-family duty station

**General context of the project**

Iran hosts the largest refugee population in the region, the vast majority from Afghanistan, amidst a fragile landscape worsened by sanctions and record inflation. The context is currently defined by a dramatic regional escalation placing Iran at the center of a volatile geopolitical crisis. The number of internally displaced people is anticipated to rise further as hostilities, infrastructure damage, and insecurity continue. INTERSOS provides life-saving assistance through Integrated Health & Protection programs, focusing on inclusive access to national health system for Afghan refugees and vulnerable host community. Navigating shrinking humanitarian space and increased scrutiny, the Head of Mission must exercise sophisticated humanitarian diplomacy with national authorities and donors. The mission's priority remains maintaining operational access and high-quality programming despite regional instability and severe economic strain.

**General purpose of the position**

The Head of Mission represents INTERSOS in the country and acts on behalf of the Director General, leading the organization’s response. This includes strategic design and resource mobilization in a volatile regional context, ensuring the mission is equipped for both long-term refugee programs and acute emergency interventions. The HoM is responsible for identifying new funding opportunities, planning resources, and overseeing the management and implementation of programs while navigating complex humanitarian diplomacy and regional conflict dynamics.

**Main responsibilities and tasks:**

- **Strategy and vision**Lead the continuous monitoring and analysis of the political and humanitarian situation in Iran and neighboring countries. Translate regional conflict dynamics into actionable contingency plans and identify immediate entry points for emergency interventions.
- Design, propose, and evolve the country strategy in alignment with INTERSOS values, ensuring the mission can pivot between long-term refugee support and acute conflict response.
- Explore and secure new funding opportunities; lead fundraising activities with institutional and private donors to expand the mission’s portfolio and leverage impact for affected communities.
- Monitor shifting donor priorities and regional intervention strategies. Guarantee strict adherence to INTERSOS and donor procedures, ensuring the mission remains a top-tier, low-risk partner in a highly scrutinized environment.
- Oversee the development and implementation of programs through periodic field visits (security permitting).
- Evaluate project evolution against international standards to ensure technical excellence and ethical integrity.
- Greenlight and fast-track project proposals and emergency responses. Evaluate and lead the development of additional, rapid-response programming based on real-time assessments of the regional crisis.
- Lead the comprehensive country strategy planning process, prioritizing actions and resources to achieve high-impact objectives in a resource-constrained and volatile landscape.

**Representation and advocacy**

- Represent the organisation and manage relations with the authorities ensuring smooth and timely implementation of planned interventions and safeguarding impartiality and independence.
- Follow up, guarantee and monitor government recognition procedures for the organisation in compliance with the host country formalities.
- Maintain a productive communication with donors and ensure that the assessed needs are communicated to impact on donors’ priorities.
- Represent INTERSOS in relevant fora
- **People management**Ensure that the senior management team is effective, mutually supporting and sufficiently involved in key decision-making processes.
- In coordination with the HR Coordinator, guide and supervise the staff performance process for international and national staff.
- Ensure the respect organisational values, Code of Ethics, Organization Management and Control Model, and INTERSOS procedures.
- Maintain high ethical standards and promote teamwork and ensure a productive working environment.
- Empower staff to meet organizational goals and work as a highly functioning and cooperative team.
- **Finance, logistics and supply**Together with the Finance Coordinator, define and oversee the overall financial management of the mission, striving towards financial sustainability and assume responsibility for the mission funds management (NGO budget).
- Ensure that allocated resources are managed effectively and transparently.
- Together with the Logistics and Supply Coordinator, ensure that required and efficient supply services and processes are in place.
- **Safety and security**
Hold final accountability for security, including development and validation of country security plan and ensuring adherence to procedures, monitoring of the context development, analysis and provision of recommendations.Regularly interact with the Regional Office and the Security Advisor on security issues.
- Hold final responsibility for any decision concerning security in the country.

**Accountability and quality control**

- In collaboration with the SMT is responsible to produce and submit the mission monthly activity reports.
- Continuously assess, analyse and evaluate the impact of the country program and operations, also through periodic visits to the areas of intervention, in collaboration with the Program Coordinator and MEAL.
- Ensure all the policies within INTERSOS Safeguarding Framework are respected by the staff
- Together with MEAL Department, supervise the effectiveness of a complaint feedback mechanism
- Oversee program quality and impact in line with established strategic objectives and related indicators.
- Oversee program reporting, ensuring compliance with INTERSOS policies and procedures, donor regulations and national requirements.

**Required profile and experience:**

- University degree Project management, International Affairs, Development, International Political Economy or other relevant field
- Eight years of experience in management positions in humanitarian contexts
- Experience leading humanitarian missions in active conflict zones or during rapid-onset regional escalations.
- Ability to influence donor agendas and navigate "Red Lines" with government counterparts in sensitive political environments
- Experience with major grants and international donors
- Experience of working within an insecure environment with responsibility for security planning, monitoring and management
- Essential computer literacy (word, excel and internet)
- Excellent English (written and oral)
- Strategic vision
- Good organizational and planning skills
- Leadership, team management and cooperation
- Behavioral flexibility
- Networking, negotiation skills and decision-making skills
- Diplomatic, interpersonal and good communication skills
- Ability to take initiative and work independently
- Strong analytical and practical problem-solving skills
- Commitment to INTERSOS principles

**General conditions and benefits:**

- **Salary range: 14 - 4.505€ - 5.182€ monthly gross**
- **Accommodation: House Allowance**
- **R&R: N/A**
- **Annual Leave:** 2.5 days per month
- **Medical insurance** for the staff
- **Transportation and visa:** Round-trip flights. For missions lasting at *least 9 months,* an additional flight ticket to the Country of residence and return to the mission will also be provided.
- **Induction: one week of online induction before the deployment**

jobs.title: Consultancy service to conduct a programme baseline assessment
jobs.description:
Terms of reference (TOR)

Consultancy service to conduct a programme baseline assessment

UGANDA & KENYA

· Project: Integrated Community Nutrition Management Programme (ICNMP)

· Procuring Organisation: IsraAID

· Contract Type: Consultancy

· Contract Period: October 2026 to December 2026, 75 days (Phased implementation)

· Target Start Date: Tentatively 26/10/2026

· Application Deadline: 23/10/2026

· Submission Method: EMAIL – see 'how to apply'

BACKGROUND

IsraAID is an International Humanitarian Non-Governmental Organization founded in 2001 and headquartered in Israel. It supports people and communities affected by humanitarian crises, combining rapid emergency response with longer-term recovery, resilience, and preparedness. Over the years, IsraAID has worked in more than 60 countries, responding to disasters, displacement, epidemics, and other crises. Its mission is centered on partnering closely with local communities to provide urgent assistance while helping them rebuild and strengthen their resilience to future shocks.

IsraAID is implementing a project titled Integrated Community Nutrition Management Programme (ICNMP) in Nakivale Refugee Settlement in Uganda and in Kakuma Refugee Camp in Kenya. The programme intends to improve health outcomes and reduce morbidity and mortality associated with malnutrition in vulnerable communities participating in the Program. ICNMP is designed as a regional initiative that responds to acute and chronic nutrition needs across East Africa, beginning its phase zero in Q2 of 2026, and actual implementation in September 2026. Although the immediate program launch focuses on Uganda and the emergency phase in Kenya, early 2027 will see Kenya incorporating the full package while the broader intention is to establish a model that can later expand to South Sudan as funding becomes available. The regional framing is essential, as the scale of displacement, vulnerability, and recurring shocks across these countries requires harmonized technical standards, shared learning, and coordinated supply chain approaches. The program will expand decentralized nutrition services by placing screening, early identification, and treatment within spaces that families already use daily, including schools, Child-Friendly Spaces, transit points, and primary health facilities. To be able to achieve the intended outcomes, IsraAID seeks services of a consultant to conduct a baseline upon which project progress and successes will be measured.

This Terms of Reference (ToR) sets out the background, purpose, objectives, scope of work, expected deliverables, and management arrangements for the baseline study, and invites eligible firms to submit technical and financial proposals for consideration.

PURPOSE

This assignment aims at establishing both quantitative and qualitative baseline information on access to integrated nutrition services, nutrition and food security practices and programme systems to ensure that these are addressed by programme interventions to realise the intended overall goal. The baseline will also establish baseline information on several learning areas under the OECD criteria and the IsraAID Community Resilience framework (CRF). The baseline therefore aims at obtaining verified, disaggregated benchmark values for the programme indicators, enabling precise measurement of outcomes and impacts at endline (Year 2, 2028).

OBJECTIVES OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The assignment will specifically

A. Assess the 3 programme outcome indicators

1\. Vulnerable communities — especially children under five and pregnant and lactating women (PLW) — access integrated, quality nutrition services delivered through a multi-tier workforce (community and formal system) and functional multi-sectoral pathways.

2\. Caregivers and community structures adopt improved nutritional and food security practices that prevent and protect against malnutrition.

3\. Programme systems — accountability, information, governance and supply chain, inventory management systems, logistics & distribution modalities — are functional and progressively integrated into and owned by national, district and community structures.

B. Provide baseline information on the specified Community Resilience Framework (CRF) and OECD learning questions.

SCOPE

The baseline survey will be conducted in programme’s area of implementation, covering Nakivale Refugee Settlement and its surrounding host communities in Western Uganda and Turkana West Sub-County specifically targeting Kakuma Refugee Camp, Kalobeyei settlement and its surrounding host communities in Kenya. There are several credible data sources that will benefit the project including, among others, District Information Health System (DHIS 2),

Food Security and Nutrition Assessment reports (FSNA), Demographic Health Surveys, and Population Census reports. Primary baseline information will be obtained from, among others, health facilities, schools, households, children-friendly spaces, community structures and partners engaged in nutrition interventions

METHODOLOGY

IsraAID anticipates a mixed-methods baseline design combining quantitative and qualitative approaches, consistent with the evidence requirements set out in the MEAL Plan. The final design will be proposed by the Firm and refined collaboratively with IsraAID’s MEAL team.

The baseline study should be designed so that its instruments, sampling frame, and methodology can be replicated with fidelity at endline, enabling credible before and after comparison and contribution analysis.

ETHICAL CONSIDERATIONS

The consultant will be expected to demonstrate how the assessment will be conducted in line with research ethics while protecting the human rights of the participants. It will also be the responsibility of the consultant to ensure strict adherence to IsraAID Safeguarding Policy. The consultant will also be responsible for ensuring that any persons hired, engaged, or consulted during the process are familiar with the policy and commit to abide by it during the delivery of the assignment.

EXPECTED DELIVERABLES AND TIMELINE

This assignment will last approximately 75 days from the date of signing of the contract. The consultant will provide a detailed work plan with realistic timelines to the logical conclusion of the baseline survey. The following deliverables are expected from the consultant:

The baseline assessment will be undertaken by one consultant/firm. Fieldwork will be conducted sequentially, beginning in Uganda and subsequently moving to Kenya.

1\. Inception & Evaluation Design – Week 1

Key activities

· Desk review of programme proposal, Theory of Change, Logic Model and MEAL Plan.

· Inception meetings with IsraAID.

· Refine evaluation design, sampling strategy and evaluation matrix.

Deliverables

· Inception report.

· Refined methodology and sampling plan.

· Approved work plan and evaluation/indicator matrix.

2\. Tool Development, Piloting & Field Preparation – Weeks 2–3

Key activities

· Finalize quantitative and qualitative data collection tools aligned with Indicator Reference Sheets.

· Share tools with relevant teams and incorporate feedback.

· Pilot testing and tool refinement.

· Enumerator training/orientation and field preparation.

· Ethics/safeguarding clearance preparation.

Deliverables

· Approved final data collection tools and protocols.

· Pilot findings and revisions.

· Enumerator training/orientation completed.

· Ethics/safeguarding documentation.

3\. Data Collection – Uganda – Weeks 4–5

Key activities

· Deploy quantitative and qualitative surveys/interviews with agreed respondents in Uganda.

· Conduct ongoing field-level data quality assurance.

· Hold regular field debriefs with participating stakeholders.

· Complete Uganda fieldwork and initial data quality checks.

· Provide the IsraAID team with access to data on a rolling basis as it is collected.

Deliverables

· Uganda quantitative and qualitative data.

· Field notes/transcripts.

· Data quality assurance records.

· Cleaned Uganda dataset.

3\. Transition & Data Collection – Kenya – Weeks 5–7

Key activities

· Close out any outstanding Uganda data collection activities.

· Uganda findings first draft submission

· Transition/travel from Uganda to Kenya.

· Conduct quantitative and qualitative data collection in Kenya.

· Maintain ongoing data quality assurance and stakeholder debriefs.

· Provide the IsraAID team with access to data on a rolling basis as it is collected.

· Complete Kenya fieldwork and initial data checks.

Deliverables

· Uganda fieldwork close-out and initial findings draft shared.

· Kenya quantitative and qualitative data.

· Field notes/transcripts.

· Data quality assurance records.

· Cleaned Kenya dataset.

4\. Analysis & Validation – Weeks 7–9

Key activities

· Clean, code and analyze quantitative and qualitative data.

· Triangulate findings across methods and countries.

· Develop and populate indicator baseline values.

· Prepare and conduct validation workshop with IsraAID/programme stakeholders.

Deliverables

· Analyzed datasets.

· Populated indicator baseline table.

· Draft findings.

· Validation workshop summary.

5\. Reporting & Dissemination – Weeks 9–10

Key activities

· Incorporate feedback from IsraAID.

· Finalize evaluation/baseline report.

· Prepare executive summary/brief and presentation deck.

· Present findings to relevant stakeholders.

· Hand over final datasets, tools and supporting documentation.

Deliverables

· Final report in MS Word and PDF.

· Executive summary/brief.

· Presentation deck.

· Final clean datasets and tools.

Summary of Key Milestones

· Week 1: Inception phase completed

· Week 2 & 3: Tools finalised/piloted and field preparation completed

· Week 4 & 5: Uganda fieldwork completed

· Weeks 6 & 7: Kenya fieldwork completed and initial Uganda finding draft

· Weeks 8 & 9: Analysis and validation completed; draft report ready

· Week 10: Final report, presentation and data/tools handover completed

Note: The timeline is indicative and may be adjusted in consultation with IsraAID, provided the overall 10-week period and Uganda-to-Kenya sequencing are maintained. Analysis may overlap with final data cleaning. IsraAID will want to be provided access to data on a rolling basis as it is collected, to enable ongoing data quality checks and early identification of gaps or issues.

Summary of Key Baseline Deliverables

· Inception report by the consultant within one (1) week upon signing of the consultancy contract.

· Draft Baseline Survey report with clear findings in line with the aim and outcomes of the programme, conclusion, and recommendations for review.

· Final Baseline Survey report in electronic format (MS Word as well as PDF)

· Summary of the findings in (MS PowerPoint) to be used for subsequent dissemination.

· All raw data: transcripts from In-depth Interviews, Individual Surveys, FGDs and cleaned data set used for analysis and production of the final report in an acceptable electronic format shared on a rolling basis.

KEY ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

IsraAID and the Programme Team

· Draw the contract and manage its implementation within the period.

· Coordinate the baseline study

· Share relevant documentation that are important for this assignment

· Introduction of the consultant and team to the relevant bodies within the study locations.

· Organize a validation meeting for the baseline findings.

· Review and approve the deliverables presented by the consultant.

Consultant

· Recruit, contract, remunerate, train, coordinate, and supervise data collectors, ensuring compliance with the agreed methodology, ethical standards, data quality requirements, and timelines.

· Lead consultancy assignment including data collection and analysis.

· Develop and review the data collection tools.

· Lead the development of the consultancy report and incorporate any feedback from IsraAID

· Ensure all deliverables of the assignment are accomplished and approved by IsraAID

· Present findings to the IsraAID team and relevant stakeholders for validation.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

IsraAID expects the successful consultant/firm to field a multidisciplinary team with a balance of quantitative, qualitative, and GESI expertise, complemented by strong in-country presence across ICNMP priority geographies where possible. The indicative team composition below is provided as guidance; consulting firms may propose an alternative structure provided all required competencies are demonstrated and justified.

· Team Leader / Baseline Study Lead: Advanced degree in public health, social sciences, statistics, international development, or related field; minimum 10 years’ experience leading baseline/endline evaluations for complex, multi-country development programs; demonstrated experience with forced displacement, refugee, or migration programming; strong track record managing mixed-methods research teams across multiple African countries. Excellent interpersonal and teamwork skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with the IsraAID team.

· Quantitative Research Specialist: Advanced degree in statistics, economics, or related field; expertise in survey design, sampling methodology, and quantitative data analysis (e.g., STATA, R, SPSS); experience with mobile data collection platforms (e.g., KoboToolbox, SurveyCTO, ODK).

· Qualitative Research Specialist: Advanced degree in social sciences; expertise in qualitative methods including KIIs, FGDs, and complexity-aware approaches (e.g., Outcome

· Data Management / MEL Support: Experience in data cleaning, database management, and dashboard/data visualization; familiarity with data protection standards applicable to work with protected persons.

GOVERNANCE AND REPORTING LINES

The consulting firm will report to IsraAID’s ICNMP MEAL Coordinator, who holds day-to-day responsibility for the MEAL leadership of the ICNMP programme, and will work closely with the ICNMP program teams in both Uganda and Kenya Country Offices on tool design, data quality assurance, analysis, and reporting. The ICNMP MEAL Coordinator retains overall accountability for the assignment and will review and approve the inception report and final baseline report.

PAYMENT PLAN

50% after the approval of the inception report, 50% after the approval of the final report.

APPLICATION PROCESS

Interested candidates should submit the following:

· Technical proposal outlining approach and methodology

· A financial proposal in US Dollars (USD), detailing all consultancy-related costs (operational, and logistical costs for conducting the assignment in Kenya and Uganda).

· CVs of the Lead Consultant and the entire team

· At least three relevant samples of previous similar work

· At least two (2) recommendation letters from recent clients for similar assignments.

· Copy of the company registration, Memorandum, and Articles of Association if a company/ firm is applying.

· Copy of tax compliance Certificate

· TIN Number

· VAT Number

· Any other relevant information supporting the application.

EVALUATION CRITERIA FOR SELECTION OF THE CONSULTANT/CONSULTING FIRM

Proposals from the interested bidders will be evaluated against the following criteria:

1\. Technical Approach & Understanding of the Assignment (30%): Understanding of the programme, evaluation objectives and scope; quality and appropriateness of the proposed methodology; sampling approach; quantitative and qualitative

methods; data analysis, triangulation and validation; and ethical/safeguarding considerations.

2\. Relevant Experience & Technical Capacity (25%): Demonstrated experience conducting baseline studies, evaluations or similar assignments, particularly in humanitarian, refugee, displacement and development contexts. Experience working with refugee and host communities in Uganda and/or Kenya will be an advantage. Qualifications and expertise of the proposed consultant/team will also be considered.

3\. Workplan, Fieldwork & Data Quality Approach (20%): Feasibility of the proposed workplan within the 10-week period; capacity to undertake fieldwork sequentially in Uganda and Kenya; approach to data quality assurance, data management, safeguarding and secure access to data on a rolling basis during data collection.

4\. Financial Proposal & Value for Money (25%): Completeness, clarity and reasonableness of the financial proposal, including professional fees and all logistical and operational costs required to conduct the assignment in Uganda and Kenya.

ANNEXES

1\. Program Document

2\. Program LogFrame

RESERVATION OF RIGHTS

Nothing contained in this RFP/TOR shall be construed as creating any obligation on the part of IsraAID to enter into a contract with any bidder. IsraAID reserves the unrestricted right to determine the evaluation criteria, request additional documentation, waive minor irregularities, seek clarifications, reject any or all proposals, and terminate the procurement process at its sole discretion and without prior notice.

jobs.title: Deputy Director of Finance, Ebola Response
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**BACKGROUND**

Responding to the world’s worst humanitarian crises in a great variety of roles, the International Rescue Committee’s staff is a force for humanity and hope. If you’re skilled and passionate, we’d like to add your energy to ours.

Through its Emergency Unit (EmU), the IRC is one of the world’s largest humanitarian agencies, leading rapid emergency responses that provide life-saving assistance, early recovery, and stabilization support to people affected by conflict, displacement, natural disasters, and complex emergencies across multiple contexts worldwide. We are committed to innovation, agility, and strong partnerships to deliver timely and effective humanitarian action.

On 15 May 2026, the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) officially declared the country's seventeenth Ebola virus disease (EVD) outbreak following the confirmation of cases in the health zones of Rwampara, Mongbwalu, and Bunia in Ituri Province. In the past 90 days, more than 6,700 cases have been reported with over 3,500 deaths - and more than 8,000 cases and nearly 4,000 deaths since the outbreak began, making this the fastest spreading Ebola outbreak documented. The vast majority of all cases are in Ituri province, but cases are also reported in 63 of the country’s 104 health zones, across North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uélé, Tshopo, and Bas-Uélé provinces, highlighting the scale and complexity of the response.

Active in public health, education in emergencies, livelihoods, women's empowerment, youth development, and protection and promotion of rights, we assist people from harm to home.

**RESPONSE BACKGROUND**

The Ebola outbreak is unfolding in a fragile humanitarian context characterized by protracted conflict, population displacement, weak health systems, and limited access to essential services. Health facilities remain under significant pressure, with persistent gaps in infection prevention and control (IPC), water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) infrastructure, healthcare waste management, triage capacity, and the availability of essential IPC supplies. These challenges continue to increase the risk of healthcare-associated transmission, compromise the safety of health workers and patients, and disrupt the continuity of essential health services.

In response, IRC has rapidly launched an integrated Ebola emergency response in close collaboration with the Ministry of Health, provincial and health zone authorities, and other partners. The response combines Health, Infection Prevention and Control (IPC), WASH, Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE), Protection, and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) interventions to strengthen outbreak prevention, detection, and response at both health facility and community levels.

**Position Overview**

As a member of the Emergency Response Team (EERT) Senior Management Team (SMT), the Deputy Director of Finance provides financial leadership and management necessary to ensure that the emergency response has the appropriate financial infrastructure and systems in place to support the strategic vision and mission of the organization. They will contribute to the development of the response’s strategic and operational plans and be accountable for ensuring and monitoring delivery against the financial plans through targeted and comprehensive financial analytical review. The Deputy Director of Finance is responsible for the overall policy and management for the financial and accounting management of the emergency response. Emphasis will be placed on financial management policies, practices, and systems that are compliant with local laws and US as well as adhering to donor requirements, but are also conducive to the effective implementation of country programs.

As Deputy Director Finance, they will have responsibility for all aspects of strategic and operational finance for the emergency response, acting as the principal finance business partner to the Emergency Senior Management team and the Ebola Response Director, the Emergency Unit team, as well as conforming to IRC's financial control environment and CFO standards and objectives.

Based in Bunia, the Deputy Director of Finance will have dual reporting to the Ebola Response Director and the global Director of Emergency Finance, with key coordination and technical lines of collaboration with both the Deputy Director of Operations and Deputy Director of Finance from the non-Emergency DRC Country Program.

**Major Responsibilities**

**Strategic Planning & Analysis**

- Provides financial information which supports the Response Director and EERT SMT in making business decisions in line with IRC & Country Program strategies
- Provides strategic analysis on the overall financial health of the country program to the Response Director and EERT SMT
- Contributes and provides feedback to the development of the Emergency Response Plan

**Controllership**

- Ensures that all in-country practices are in compliance with IRC and donor policies and procedures
- Establishes in-country finance procedures to supplement global policies as needed
- Closely monitors financial activities and advises the Response Director on the financial performance of the office, issues with internal controls, or financial management
- Ensures monthly balance sheet reconciliations are completed on a timely basis
- Manages the finance department activities and schedules to meet the financial reporting requirements and deadlines specified by headquarters and donors
- Identifies requirements for and develops reporting formats to aid in the management of country operations and grant expenditures
- Directs the preparation of and approves all donor financial reports in respect to accounting, legal, and contractual requirements, and ensures the review of such reports by the Response Director and Emergency Finance Director prior to submission
- Ensures in-country internal control reviews of operations are regularly undertaken.
- Facilitates external, internal, donor, or government audits
- Oversees the protection of the country’s assets (cash, inventory, fixed assets) through the enforcement of internal control policies and procedures
- Maintains current knowledge of local government requirements related to finance and complies with tax and other legal requirements
- Is the principal liaison with IRC HQ on all finance, accounting, grant budget management, and cash management

**Training & Staff Management**

- Establishes a finance department roles and responsibilities matrix; staff job descriptions are current; recruits and maintains qualified staff to perform finance functions
- Ensures comprehensive and constructive performance reviews are completed annually; career planning and development plans are in place for all finance staff
- Develops and implements a training program for the country’s finance staff
- Oversees finance training and technical support to non-finance staff for skills improvement in the areas of accounting, reporting, and internal control

**Treasury**

- Supervises all country program bank relations and bank account activities, including negotiation of fees, interest, and currency exchange rates
- Oversees the review and approval of all monthly bank account and cash reconciliations
- Maintain, on a current basis, accurate forecasts of cash requirements for meeting future spending, including commitments that obligate IRC to future spending
- Ensures that appropriate balances are maintained to facilitate grant implementation and cash held in the headquarters is drawn regularly
- Ensures the development and implementation of a plan to minimize the country’s foreign exchange exposure to currency gains and losses
- Supervises the collection of contractual and other receivables

**Budget and Forecast**

- Oversees the preparation and revision of grant proposal budgets; supports programs with guidance on costing and inputs in creating budgets for submission
- Prepares and maintains the country’s annual operating budget; ensures cost coverage for in-country operating costs and updates the operating budget regularly
- Presents and facilitates the review of actual to budget expenditures with the Country Director and program managers

**Partnerships**

- Demonstrated genuine interest in and commitment to collaboration and partnership with local actors in emergencies.
- Champion a culture of effective and respectful partnerships. Promote partner-led programming in line with IRC’s “why not partner?” and “partner as equals” approach.
- As a member of the EERT Senior Management Team (SMT), prioritize and promote IRC’s internal capacity to partner.
- Develop staffing structures with the appropriate number of staff to effectively manage partnerships and ensure quality.
- Actively contribute to the relevant sections of Partner Capacity Analysis (PCA) and the subsequent development of partner support plans.
- Manage the implementation of action items in the finance sections of partner support plans.
- Lead and/or support collaborative project and budget design with partners.
- Work collaboratively with partners to ensure that project budgets reflect fair market value.
- Ensure appropriate budget allocation for IRC to support partners in alignment with the overall response/program design.
- Actively participate in the Partnership Working Group (PWG).

**Accountability**

- Hold the Senior Management Team (SMT) accountable for outcomes related to safeguarding; regularly review progress, barriers, and enablers.
- Foster ongoing learning, honest dialogue, and reflection to strengthen safeguarding and IRC values.

**Job Requirements**

- Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Business Administration, Commerce, or Finance required; recognized professional certificate in accounting, such as CPA, or a Master’s degree in Accounting is preferred
- Extensive, senior-level experience, and a minimum of five years of managerial experience in Finance is essential
- Senior-level experience working within the Ukrainian Financial sector is an advantage
- Prior experience leading large, complex multi-donor funded programs and grants, including experience with USG, European, DFID, and UN funding streams, foreign currency and exchange management, and budget development and oversight
- Extensive experience in working with computerized accounting systems, standard spreadsheets, and database programs (SUN System, Dynamics 365, Vision, Integra, etc)
- Demonstrated skills in building strong finance teams and establishing new finance operations, including the ability to communicate and work effectively with senior management, operating, and program staff and functions
- Ability to act as a proactive member of the Senior Management Team. Proven track record of proactively identifying and communicating potential problems and proposing solutions
- Capacity to function effectively in a complex, changing work environment, setting appropriate priorities, and managing competing priorities and pressure
- Ability to carry out responsibilities independently with minimal technical support
- Excellent interpersonal communication skills and professional patience, and be able to interact, partner, and thrive in a diverse environment
- Committed to staff training, capacity building, and development, and effective at facilitation
- Cultural awareness and ability to build relationships quickly with a wide variety of people
- French and English language communications skills are required
- Commitment to ongoing learning and reflection on personal and organizational biases, and willingness to adapt practices to promote inclusion.
- Demonstrated genuine interest in and commitment to collaboration and partnership with local actors in emergencies.

***French version:***

**CONTEXTE**

En intervenant face aux pires crises humanitaires mondiales dans des rôles très variés, le personnel de l'International Rescue Committee (IRC) incarne une force au service de l'humanité et de l'espoir. Si vous possédez les compétences et la passion nécessaires, nous aimerions associer votre énergie à la nôtre.

Grâce à son Unité d'urgence (EmU), l'IRC figure parmi les plus grandes organisations humanitaires au monde ; elle pilote des interventions d'urgence rapides visant à fournir une aide vitale, ainsi qu'un soutien au relèvement précoce et à la stabilisation, aux populations touchées par des conflits, des déplacements de population, des catastrophes naturelles et des situations d'urgence complexes dans des contextes variés à travers le globe. Nous misons sur l'innovation, l'agilité et des partenariats solides pour mener une action humanitaire efficace et opportune.

Le 15 mai 2026, le gouvernement de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC) a officiellement déclaré la dix-septième épidémie de maladie à virus Ebola (MVE) du pays, suite à la confirmation de cas dans les zones de santé de Rwampara, Mongbwalu et Bunia, dans la province de l'Ituri. Au cours des 90 derniers jours, plus de 6 700 cas et plus de 3 500 décès ont été signalés ; le bilan total s'élève à plus de 8 000 cas et près de 4 000 décès depuis le début de l'épidémie, ce qui en fait l'épidémie d'Ebola à la propagation la plus rapide jamais documentée. Si la grande majorité des cas se concentre dans la province de l'Ituri, des cas ont également été signalés dans 63 des 104 zones de santé du pays — notamment dans les provinces du Nord-Kivu, du Sud-Kivu, du Haut-Uélé, de la Tshopo et du Bas-Uélé — ce qui témoigne de l'ampleur et de la complexité de la réponse.

Actifs dans les domaines de la santé publique, de l'éducation en situation d'urgence, des moyens de subsistance, de l'autonomisation des femmes, du développement de la jeunesse ainsi que de la protection et de la promotion des droits, nous accompagnons les personnes depuis les situations de danger jusqu'à leur retour à une vie stable.

**CONTEXTE DE LA RÉPONSE**

L'épidémie d'Ebola se déroule dans un contexte humanitaire fragile, marqué par des conflits prolongés, des déplacements de population, des systèmes de santé défaillants et un accès limité aux services essentiels. Les établissements de santé sont soumis à une forte pression ; des lacunes persistent en matière de prévention et de contrôle des infections (PCI), d'infrastructures d'eau, d'assainissement et d'hygiène (WASH), de gestion des déchets médicaux, de capacités de triage et de disponibilité des fournitures essentielles de PCI. Ces défis continuent d'accroître le risque de transmission au sein des structures de soins, de compromettre la sécurité du personnel soignant et des patients, et de perturber la continuité des services de santé essentiels.

En réponse, l'IRC a rapidement mis en place une intervention d'urgence intégrée contre Ebola, en étroite collaboration avec le ministère de la Santé, les autorités provinciales et celles des zones de santé, ainsi que d'autres partenaires.
