Cette réponse conjugue des interventions dans les domaines de la santé, de la prévention et du contrôle des infections (PCI), de l'eau, de l'assainissement et de l'hygiène (WASH), de la communication sur les risques et de l'engagement communautaire (RCCE), de la protection, ainsi que de la santé mentale et du soutien psychosocial (SMSPS), afin de renforcer la prévention, la détection et la réponse à l'épidémie, tant au niveau des établissements de santé qu'au sein des communautés.

**APERÇU DU POSTE**

En tant que membre de l'équipe de direction (SMT) de l'équipe d'intervention d'urgence (EERT), le directeur adjoint des finances assure le leadership et la gestion financière nécessaires pour garantir que l'intervention d'urgence dispose des infrastructures et des systèmes financiers adéquats pour soutenir la vision stratégique et la mission de l'organisation. Il contribuera à l'élaboration des plans stratégiques et opérationnels de l'intervention et sera responsable du suivi de leur exécution par rapport aux plans financiers, grâce à des analyses financières ciblées et approfondies. Le directeur adjoint des finances est responsable de la politique globale et de la gestion financière et comptable de l'intervention d'urgence. Une attention particulière sera portée aux politiques, pratiques et systèmes de gestion financière qui sont conformes aux lois locales et américaines ainsi qu'aux exigences des bailleurs de fonds, tout en favorisant la mise en œuvre efficace des programmes nationaux.

En qualité de directeur adjoint des finances, il sera responsable de tous les aspects de la gestion financière stratégique et opérationnelle de l'intervention d'urgence. Il agira en tant que principal partenaire financier auprès de l'équipe de direction de l'urgence, du directeur de l'intervention Ebola et de l'équipe de l'unité d'urgence, tout en veillant au respect du cadre de contrôle financier de l'IRC ainsi que des normes et objectifs du directeur financier (CFO).

Basé à Bunia, le directeur adjoint des finances sera placé sous la double supervision du directeur de l'intervention Ebola et du directeur mondial des finances pour les urgences (Global Director of Emergency Finance). Il entretiendra également des liens de coordination et de collaboration technique essentiels avec le directeur adjoint des opérations et le directeur adjoint des finances du programme national de l'IRC en RDC (hors urgence).

**PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILITÉS**
**Planification et analyse stratégiques**

- Fournit des informations financières qui aident le directeur de réponse et EERT SMT à prendre des décisions commerciales conformément aux stratégies de l'IRC et du programme pays.
- Fournit une analyse stratégique sur la santé financière globale du programme de pays au directeur de la réponse et à l'EERT SMT.
- Contribue et fournit des commentaires à l'élaboration du plan d'intervention d'urgence

**Contrôle**

- S'assure que toutes les pratiques dans le pays sont conformes aux politiques et procédures de l'IRC et des donateurs.
- Établit des procédures financières nationales pour compléter les politiques mondiales si nécessaire
- Surveille de près les activités financières et conseille le directeur de réponse sur la performance financière du bureau, les problèmes de contrôles internes ou de gestion financière.
- S'assure que les rapprochements mensuels des bilans sont effectués en temps opportun
- Gère les activités et les calendriers du service financier pour répondre aux exigences en matière de reporting financier et aux délais spécifiés par le siège et les donateurs.
- Identifie les exigences et développe des formats de reporting pour faciliter la gestion des opérations pays et des dépenses de subventions
- Dirige la préparation et approuve tous les rapports financiers des donateurs en ce qui concerne les exigences comptables, juridiques et contractuelles, et assure l'examen de ces rapports par le directeur de la réponse et le directeur des finances d'urgence avant leur soumission.
- Veiller à ce que des examens de contrôle interne des opérations dans le pays soient régulièrement effectués.
- Facilite les audits externes, internes, des donateurs ou du gouvernement
- Supervise la protection des actifs du pays (trésorerie, stocks, immobilisations) grâce à l'application des politiques et procédures de contrôle interne
- Maintient ses connaissances actuelles des exigences du gouvernement local liées aux finances et se conforme aux exigences fiscales et autres exigences légales
- Est le principal agent de liaison avec le siège de l'IRC pour toutes les finances, la comptabilité, la gestion du budget des subventions et la gestion de la trésorerie.

**Formation et gestion du personnel**

- Établit une matrice des rôles et responsabilités du service financier ; les descriptions de poste du personnel sont à jour ; recrute et maintient en poste du personnel qualifié pour exercer des fonctions financières
- Veiller à ce que des évaluations de performance complètes et constructives soient effectuées chaque année ; des plans de planification de carrière et de développement sont en place pour tout le personnel financier
- Élabore et met en œuvre un programme de formation pour le personnel financier du pays
- Supervise la formation financière et le soutien technique au personnel non financier pour l'amélioration des compétences dans les domaines de la comptabilité, du reporting et du contrôle interne.

**Trésorerie**

- Supervise toutes les relations bancaires et les activités des comptes bancaires du programme pays, y compris la négociation des frais, des intérêts et des taux de change.
- Supervise l'examen et l'approbation de tous les rapprochements mensuels de comptes bancaires et de trésorerie
- Maintenir, sur une base actuelle, des prévisions précises des besoins de trésorerie pour faire face aux dépenses futures, y compris les engagements qui obligent l'IRC à effectuer des dépenses futures.
- S'assure que les soldes appropriés sont maintenus pour faciliter la mise en œuvre des subventions et que les liquidités détenues au siège sont régulièrement tirées.
- Assure l’élaboration et la mise en œuvre d’un plan visant à minimiser l’exposition du pays aux gains et pertes de change
- Supervise le recouvrement des créances contractuelles et autres

**Budget et prévisions**

- Supervise la préparation et la révision des budgets des propositions de subventions ; soutient les programmes en leur fournissant des conseils sur les coûts et des contributions à la création de budgets à soumettre
- Prépare et maintient le budget de fonctionnement annuel du pays ; assure la couverture des coûts de fonctionnement dans le pays et met régulièrement à jour le budget de fonctionnement
- Présente et facilite l'examen des dépenses réelles par rapport au budget avec le directeur pays et les responsables de programme

**Partenariats**

- Démontré un réel intérêt et un engagement envers la collaboration et le partenariat avec les acteurs locaux en cas d'urgence.
- Promouvoir une culture de partenariats efficaces et respectueux. Promouvoir la programmation menée par des partenaires conformément au principe « pourquoi pas partenaire ? » de l'IRC. et une approche « partenaire sur un pied d’égalité ».
- En tant que membre de l'équipe de direction de l'EERT (SMT), prioriser et promouvoir la capacité interne de l'IRC à établir des partenariats.
- Développer des structures de dotation en personnel avec le nombre approprié d'employés pour gérer efficacement les partenariats et garantir la qualité.
- Contribuer activement aux sections pertinentes de l'analyse des capacités des partenaires (PCA) et à l'élaboration ultérieure des plans de soutien des partenaires.
- Gérer la mise en œuvre des éléments d'action dans les sections financières des plans de soutien des partenaires.
- Diriger et/ou soutenir la conception collaborative de projets et de budgets avec les partenaires.
- Travailler en collaboration avec les partenaires pour garantir que les budgets des projets reflètent la juste valeur marchande.
- Assurer une allocation budgétaire appropriée à l'IRC pour soutenir les partenaires conformément à la conception globale de la réponse/du programme.
- Participer activement au Groupe de travail sur le partenariat (PWG).
- Responsabilité
- Tenir l'équipe de direction supérieure (SMT) responsable des résultats liés à la sauvegarde ; revoir régulièrement le programme obstacles et facteurs favorisants.
- Favoriser l'apprentissage continu, le dialogue honnête et la réflexion afin de renforcer la protection des personnes et les valeurs de l'IRC.

**EXIGENCES DU POSTE**

- Licence (Bachelor) en comptabilité, administration des affaires, commerce ou finance requise ; certification professionnelle reconnue en comptabilité (ex. : CPA) ou master en comptabilité privilégié.
- Expérience approfondie à un niveau de direction et au moins cinq ans d'expérience en gestion financière.
- Une expérience de haut niveau au sein du secteur financier ukrainien constitue un atout.
- Expérience préalable dans la direction de programmes et de subventions d'envergure, complexes et financés par plusieurs bailleurs de fonds (notamment les États-Unis, l'UE, le DFID et l'ONU), incluant la gestion des devises et des taux de change ainsi que l'élaboration et le suivi budgétaires.
- Solide expérience des systèmes comptables informatisés, des tableurs courants et des logiciels de base de données (SUN System, Dynamics 365, Vision, Integra, etc.).
- Compétences avérées pour constituer des équipes financières solides et mettre en place de nouvelles opérations financières ; capacité à communiquer et à collaborer efficacement avec la haute direction ainsi qu'avec le personnel opérationnel et les équipes de programme.
- Capacité à agir en tant que membre proactif de l'équipe de direction. Expérience avérée dans l'identification et la communication proactives de problèmes potentiels ainsi que dans la proposition de solutions.
- Capacité à travailler efficacement dans un environnement complexe et en constante évolution, à définir des priorités adéquates et à gérer des priorités concurrentes ainsi que la pression.
- Capacité à assumer ses responsabilités de manière autonome, avec un soutien technique minimal.
- Excellentes compétences en communication interpersonnelle et patience professionnelle ; capacité à interagir, à nouer des partenariats et à s'épanouir dans un environnement diversifié.
- Engagement envers la formation, le renforcement des capacités et le développement du personnel ; aptitude avérée à l'animation et à la facilitation.
- Sensibilité culturelle et capacité à nouer rapidement des relations avec des personnes d'horizons très variés.
- Maîtrise du français et de l'anglais requise.
- Engagement envers l'apprentissage continu et la réflexion sur les biais personnels et organisationnels, ainsi que volonté d'adapter les pratiques pour favoriser l'inclusion.
- Intérêt sincère et engagement avéré envers la collaboration et le partenariat avec les acteurs locaux dans les situations d'urgence.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer:** Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) - We do not discriminate based on race, color, national origin, sex, disability, age, religion, or any other status.

jobs.title: Head of Support Services - Lebanon (Readvertised)
jobs.description:
**Who are we?**

DRC has been responding to various humanitarian crises in Lebanon since 2004, working with Palestinian, Iraqi and Syrian refugees. Since 2011, DRC has focused on responding to the Syrian refugee crisis in Lebanon and the resulting impact on Lebanese host community, and more recently the impact of the economic and financial crises as well as responding to the ongoing conflict. DRC Lebanon’s focus is to ensure that we are able to respond to critical emerging humanitarian needs whilst improving the living conditions of displacement-affected populations and contributing to the achievement of durable solutions. DRC is focusing its response in protection, economic recovery, shelter and site coordination and management, and humanitarian mine action across the country directly and through partners. DRC is also contributing to the broader humanitarian response through our Referral Information Management System (RIMS), utilised by 170 organisations.

**About the job**

The Head of Support Services (HoSS) is operationally and strategically responsible for Finance, Human Resources, Logistics and Procurement, Administration and/or IT. S/he oversees, develops and provides strategic direction to his/her support areas. This role has a country focus (Lebanon) and ensures compliance to DRC procedures and guidelines within the country. The role contributes to the development of country strategies, which are translated into action plans and day-to-day tasks. The role provides support and/or technical guidance to country operations while overseeing country activities.

With senior level management experience, you are expected to have demonstrable successful track record of organizational development and resource mobilization and play a leadership role in developing and implementing country-specific strategies as well as improving operational systems, processes, and policies in support of DRC’s mission and values.

**Previous experience in a Finance Manager/Director or similar role and/or a Finance-related qualification is highly recommended.**

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

**Responsibilities:**

**Staff Management**

- Lead and manage the support managers (including people planning, performance, well-being and development) whilst providing dotted technical line support to wider country support team.
- Work to build the capacity of the operational support staff throughout the operation though frequent in-service training sessions, mentoring support and frequent visits to field offices.
- Role model and lead the wider country programme against DRC values, diversity and inclusion as well as code of conduct.

**Support Services Management**

- Responsible for the strategic development, management and implementation of the support operations as per DRC operational handbook. This includes developing and improving operational approaches, compliance and systems, and support the Country Director to build and deliver effective and sustainable interventions.
- Support the Country Director and the Senior Management Team in liaising with donors and authorities, especially as relates to issues of compliance, registration, and audit
- Ensure appropriate technical support is available to programs, in line with organizational priorities
- Provide strategic guidance to the HR/Admin department to develop and implement DRCs HR policy in Lebanon. This includes providing strategic guidance for all staff management, career & development recruitment and induction process as well as appropriate stress management and care for Expatriates and National Staff.
- Lead on DRC Lebanon annual master budgets and ensuring that monthly monitoring of expenditure informs management decision making.
- Lead on the effective implementation and adherence of organization and stakeholder financial regulations.
- Overseeing the operationalization of the contextual/localized finance handbook.
- Ensure the implementation of sustainable and robust supply chain and financial system for an efficient and effective support to all DRC programs and support services.
- Ensure an efficient ICT Operating environment is in place to meet operational needs.

**Operational Management**

- Responsible for maintaining and improving operational resource management in the mission, together with SMT, identifying both short term and long-term resource needs and translate these into objectives and priorities for future DRC projects in Lebanon
- Responsible for leading the development and update of the resource management component of the Country Strategy, ensuring the Support Services facilitate the delivery of the strategy in line with DRC global policies and strategy.
- Ensure that DRC retains and continually develops its operational capacity to provide rapid emergency response in particular within its procurement and HR systems
- Ensure that Lebanon operation complies to DRC Risk Management Framework, and operational Compliance Tools and processes are duly implemented. This includes development of a risk management plan for the country that identifies the major financial and operational risks and implement a mitigation strategy
- Regular review and improvements to Country SOPs to ensure the internal control environment strengthened as well as develop policies as required where gaps are noted.
- Supervision, audits and controlling and implementation of corrective actions related to DRC’s operational standards within support area. This also includes ensuring the timely implementation of DRC’s internal audit and external audit recommendations and contextualize HQ understanding of local challenges.
- Participate as a member of the SMT in drafting project proposals, and on the use of resources according to budgets and policies.
- Together with the Head of Programs, lead the mainstreaming of Project Cycle Management and partnership best practices throughout the organization.
- Contribute to the delivery of DRC Lebanon’s localisation strategy, development and oversight of partnerships and ensure Support Services are fit for purpose to support equitable partnerships and capacity exchange.
- Ensure that all administrative and legal-related systems are accurate and maintained, and that DRC Lebanon is legally compliant with Government of Lebanon directives and processes.
- Contribute to the development and implementation of DRC’s global development initiatives
- As and when required, substitute the Country Director when is requested as such (leaves, field visits, long meetings etc)

**DRC Dynamics ERP System**

- Ensure ERP functionality is properly used by relevant staff
- Apply reports and data analytics from DRC Dynamics to improve overall performance
- Act as heavy user for most of the Projects & Finance functionalities

**About you**

To be successful in this role we expect the following:

*Required*

- Minimum 7 years’ experience in a similar role in an international NGO.
- 4 years’ experience in people management with proven leadership skills.
- Proven operational management experiences and capability, including in complex and emergency settings
- Proven significant financial, information and systems management experience as well as in procurement and tender processes
- Understanding and experience of institutional fundraising.
- Excellent communication, negotiation and problem-solving capacities; with the ability to work flexibly in a diverse team in a dynamic environment, fostering a positive working environment
- Strong capacity building, facilitation, and presentation skills with the ability to collaborate, network and negotiate in order to facilitate communication and support to staff, local partners, Governments, UN, donors & other NGOs without losing sight of the strategic objective
- Strong organizational and planning skills with the ability to effectively manage multiple competing deliverables on varying timelines
- Experience working in an ERP system, including Supply Chain, Finance and HR systems
- Full professional proficiency in English and Arabic

*Desirable*

- Strong organizational and planning skills with the ability to effectively manage multiple competing deliverables on varying timelines
- Experience working in an ERP system, including Supply Chain, Finance and HR systems

**Languages**

- Full professional proficiency in English
- Full professional proficiency in Arabic

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:

- **Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- **Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- **Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- **Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- **Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**Education**

A Master’s Degree or advanced professional qualification in Finance, Business Administration, Logistics or HR

**We offer**

- Contract length: 1 year
- Band: Management - E1
- Designation of Duty Station: Beirut - Lebanon
- Start date: ASAP

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for **national and expatriate employees.**

**DRC as an employer**
By working in DRC, you will be joining a global workforce of around 6000 employees in approximately 30 countries. We pride ourselves on our:

- Professionalism, impact & expertise
- Humanitarian approach & the work we do
- Purpose, meaningfulness & own contribution
- Culture, values & strong leadership
- Fair compensation & continuous development

DRC’s capacity to ensure the protection of and assistance to refugees, IDP’s and other persons of concern depends on the ability of our staff to uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation DRC’s values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment. DRC conducts thorough and comprehensive background checks as part of the recruitment process.

**If you have questions or are facing problems with the online application process, please visit** [**drc.ngo/jobsupport**](https://drc.ngo/jobsupport)**.**

***Danish Refugee Council is an equal opportunity employer and we consider all applicants based on individual merit and qualifications, regardless of personal characteristics or attributes. We are committed to increasing the diversity of our workforce, aiming for a 50% balance of men and women in management roles and ensuring that at least 50% of management roles are filled by national staff. We recognize that a diverse and inclusive team is crucial for achieving our organizational goals and making a positive impact on the communities we serve.***

jobs.title: Consultancy for an Inclusive Multi-Sector Needs Assessment (MSNA) in DR CONGO
jobs.description:
## **Background**

CBM (Christian Blind Mission) is an international development and humanitarian organisation dedicated to improving the quality of life of persons with disabilities in the world's poorest countries. We are providing inclusive humanitarian assistance in contexts of disasters, conflict, and displacement. CBM’s humanitarian activities aim to equally reach and actively involve persons with disabilities, addressing specific needs while promoting and facilitating full inclusion in mainstream services. We work together with our partners on programmes that are context specific, from disability-inclusive preparedness to immediate life-saving needsto resilience strengthening. CBM is based in Germany with 23 country offices in Europe, Africa, Asia and Latin America. With over 115 years of experience, CBM is considered as one of the world’s oldest organisations working in this field.
The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) faces one of the world's most complex humanitarian crises, marked by armed conflict, displacement, protection risks, epidemics, food insecurity and natural disasters. Persons with disabilities, women, children, older persons, IDPs and returnees face heightened barriers to accessing assistance and essential services.
To inform future humanitarian programming, including potential interventions under ECHO HIP 2027 and other funding opportunities, CBM seeks to conduct an Inclusive Multi-Sector Needs Assessment (MSNA) in selected crisis-affected areas. Findings will support evidence-based programme design, strategic positioning and partnership development.
CBM is seeking a qualified consultant or consulting team to lead this assessment.

## **Purpose of the Assignment**

The assessment aims to generate evidence on humanitarian needs, vulnerabilities and service gaps among crisis-affected populations, particularly persons with disabilities and other at-risk groups, to inform protection-centred, disability-inclusive and integrated humanitarian programming.

## **Objectives**

The assessment shall:

- Identify and analyse priority humanitarian needs and vulnerabilities.
- Assess barriers to accessing humanitarian assistance and essential services, particularly
for persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups.
- Assess the availability, accessibility, quality and inclusiveness of essential services.
- Examine protection risks and inclusion concerns.
- Analyse existing services, referral pathways, coverage and response gaps.
- Identify geographic areas with the highest humanitarian needs through a comparative
analysis of severity, operational feasibility and CBM's potential added value.
- Establish the priority order of needs but also of geographic areas.
- Generate recommendations on geographic focus, sectoral priorities, targeting,
partnerships and implementation modalities for future humanitarian programming,
including ECHO HIP 2027.

## **Scope of Assessment**

The assessment will focus on selected conflict-, displacement- and epidemic-affected areas in
eastern DRC and analyse:

- Needs and reintegration challenges of returnees.
- Opportunities for integrated multi-sector programming and referral pathways.
- Capacities of local actors, including OPDs, local NGOs and community-based
organisations.
- Community feedback systems, communication preferences and accountability
mechanisms.
- Humanitarian access constraints and operational feasibility.
- Community preparedness, surveillance and early warning systems.
- Environmental and climate-related risks affecting humanitarian programming.
Geographic scope :
- North Kivu (Masisi, Beni, Lubero)
- South Kivu (Kalehe)
- Mai-Ndombe (Kwamouth)

### *Thematic scope :*

The assessment should analyse current and emerging humanitarian needs, service gaps and
trends affecting programming in 2027, including:

- Humanitarian needs and vulnerabilities.
- Access barriers to services and assistance.
- Availability and functionality of services and referral mechanisms.
- Areas and population groups with the highest unmet needs.
- Implications for future ECHO and other donor-funded interventions.

### *Key minimum sectors :*

- Health (+MHPSS)
- Protection
- GBV
- Food Security
- Education
- Nutrition
- WASH
- Disaster Preparedness (+Epidemic and Health Risks)

### *Cross-cutting themes*

- Disability Inclusion
- Gender and Age
- Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP)
- Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA)
- Safeguarding and Child Safeguarding
- Protection Principles and Do No Harm
- Localisation and Community Engagement
- Humanitarian-Development-Peace Nexus

### *Priority Population Groups*

- IDPs
- Returnees
- Host Communities
- Women and Girls
- Children and Adolescents
- Older Persons
- Persons with Disabilities

## **Expected Methodology**

The consultant shall propose a mixed-method approach including:

- Secondary data review.
- Quantitative household surveys.
- KIIs.
- FGDs.
- Stakeholder consultations.
- Analysis of existing response capacities and gaps.
- Direct observation of selected services and community structures where feasible.

The methodology must ensure meaningful participation of persons with disabilities and comply
with humanitarian principles, safeguarding, confidentiality, informed consent, protection and Do
No Harm standards.

## **Expected Deliverables**

The selected consultant/team will be expected to provide:

1. Inception Report, including methodology and workplan;
2. Data collection tools and protocols;
3. Preliminary findings presentation;
4. Draft MSNA Report;
5. Final MSNA Report incorporating feedback;
6. Executive Summary;
7. Strategic recommendations for ECHO HIP 2027 and future programming, and integrated
response options.
8. Clean dataset and related assessment materials;
9. PowerPoint presentation of key findings.
10. Situational statistics on population movement (displaced or returned) in the assessment
areas

## **Duration**

The consultancy is expected to be conducted between October and December 2026.
The anticipated level of effort is approximately 40 working days.

jobs.title: Trainer for Youth Capacity Development in Conflict Analysis, Peacebuilding and Community Dialogue
jobs.description:
## 1. Background

Terre des Hommes Italia (TDH Italy) supports children, young people, families and communities in Syria through education, protection, inclusion and social cohesion programmes.

As part of its social cohesion work, TDH Italy intends to strengthen young people’s ability to understand conflict dynamics, design contextually relevant peacebuilding interventions, and plan and facilitate inclusive community dialogue. The training will combine practical knowledge with opportunities to apply skills through exercises, simulations and group work relevant to participants’ communities.

TDH Italy seeks an individual trainer to develop and deliver two complementary training programmes in Aleppo, Latakia and Idlib:

- Understanding Conflict and Designing Peacebuilding Interventions.
- Designing and Implementing Community Dialogue Processes.

## 2. Purpose of the Consultancy

The consultancy will equip participating young people with practical knowledge, skills and tools to analyse community tensions, identify opportunities for cooperation, develop conflict-sensitive peacebuilding interventions, and design and facilitate safe and inclusive community dialogue processes.

## 3. Objectives

- Strengthen participants’ understanding of conflict dynamics, causes, actors and effects.
- Develop their ability to apply conflict analysis tools to community situations.
- Support the design of realistic peacebuilding interventions informed by analysis and the principle of do no harm.
- Strengthen skills in planning, facilitating and reviewing community dialogue processes.
- Promote inclusive participation, respectful communication and constructive engagement with different perspectives.
- Enable participants to demonstrate their learning through practical group assignments and facilitation exercises.

## 4. Scope of Work and Key Tasks

### 4.1 Inception and planning

The trainer will

- Attend an inception meeting with TDH Italy to confirm participant profiles, learning needs, delivery arrangements and expected results.
- Prepare a detailed workplan covering preparation, delivery, assessment and reporting within the assignment period.
- Propose the sequence and dates of the eight courses, allowing adequate time for travel, preparation and review.
- Clarify in the technical proposal whether the two training programmes will follow a complementary approach for the same participants or be delivered as separate programmes for different target groups, specifying the rationale and any sequencing requirements.
- Agree daily training hours and accessibility requirements with TDH Italy before implementation.

### 4.2 Training design and preparation

- Develop two distinct training programmes with clear learning objectives, session plans, exercises and practical outputs.
- Prepare training materials in Arabic, including presentations, participant handouts, worksheets and assessment tools.
- Adapt language, examples and exercises to young people’s experience and the contexts of Aleppo, Latakia and Idlib.
- Design participatory activities that allow participants to practise analysis, intervention design and dialogue facilitation.
- Submit materials for TDH Italy’s review before delivery and incorporate agreed feedback.

### 4.3 Training delivery

The trainer will deliver the following courses:

- **Conflict Analysis and peacebuilding**: 2 in Aleppo, 1 in Latakia, 1 in Idleb
- **Community Dialogue:** 2 in Aleppo, 1 in Latakia, 1 in Idleb

For a total of 4 courses in Aleppo, 2 in Latakia and 2 in Idleb

Each course will accommodate approximately 20–25 participants.

The trainer will:

- Facilitate all eight courses in person.
- Use practical exercises, simulations, case studies, group work and structured reflection.
- Establish shared ground rules supporting dignity, confidentiality and respectful participation.
- Manage sensitive discussions impartially and respond appropriately to group tensions.
- Adapt delivery to participants’ learning needs while maintaining the agreed objectives.
- Coordinate with TDH Italy’s field teams on attendance, delivery arrangements and emerging concerns.

### 4.4 Assessment and learning review

- Prepare baseline and endline assessments appropriate to each programme, and conduct the assessment in coordination with TDH filed staff
- Assess practical skills through group assignments, presentations and observed simulations.
- In coordination with TDH filed staff, collect participant feedback on relevance, accessibility and training quality.
- Review learning after each course and make agreed improvements to subsequent delivery where needed.
- Document learning achievements and areas requiring further support without making unsupported claims about wider community impact.

### 4.5 Reporting and handover

- Submit a report for each course documenting delivery, participation, assessment findings, practical outputs and recommendations.
- Submit a consolidated final report in both Arabic and English covering all eight courses.
- Provide editable versions of the final training materials, tools and reports.

## 5. Minimum Technical Coverage

Applicants should propose a coherent agenda for each programme covering, at minimum, the following areas:

### 5.1 Understanding Conflict and Designing Peacebuilding Interventions

- Core concepts of conflict, peacebuilding and social cohesion.
- Conflict causes, dynamics, escalation and opportunities for constructive change.
- Practical tools for analysing conflict, stakeholders, relationships and power.
- Identification of factors that divide communities and factors that support cooperation.
- Conflict sensitivity and the interaction between interventions and their context.
- Translating analysis into realistic intervention objectives and activities.
- Participation, inclusion, risk management and do-no-harm considerations.
- Basic results chains, monitoring indicators and learning arrangements.
- Practical development and presentation of a peacebuilding intervention concept.

### 5.2 Designing and Implementing Community Dialogue Processes

- Purpose, scope and limitations of community dialogue.
- Assessing whether dialogue is appropriate for a particular issue or context.
- Stakeholder mapping and inclusive participant engagement.
- Defining dialogue objectives, structure, ground rules and facilitation arrangements.
- Active listening, questioning, respectful communication and management of disagreement.
- Managing participation imbalances, sensitive issues and challenging group dynamics.
- Safety, confidentiality, informed participation and conflict sensitivity.
- Documenting outcomes, identifying agreed actions and planning follow-up.
- Practical development of a dialogue process plan and facilitation simulations.

## 6. Expected Deliverables

1. **Inception note an detailed workplan:** Understanding of the assignment; methodology; proposed course schedule; preparation, delivery and reporting days; coordination and accessibility arrangements (timing: Before training delivery)
2. **Two complete training packages:** session plans; presentations; handouts; exercises; practical assignment templates; assessment and feedback tools (timing: Before the first delivery of each programme)
3. **Eight completed courses:** Delivery of all courses according to the approved plan, totalling training days (timing: within implementation period)
4. **Eight course reports:** Delivery summary; attendance records coordinated with TDH Italy; assessment findings; participant feedback; practical outputs; challenges and recommendations (timing: Following each course, according to the approved workplan)
5. **Consolidated final report and material handover:** Summary of delivery and learning across all locations; recommendations; final editable training materials and tools (timing: by mid-February 2027)

**Note:** All deliverables are subject to TDH Italy’s review and written acceptance. Applicants must propose delivery dates in their technical offer and confirm them in the approved workplan

## 7. Methodological and Quality Requirements

The trainer will:

- Apply a participatory approach appropriate to young people.
- Balance conceptual learning with substantial practical application.
- Use clear, respectful and non-stigmatising Arabic.
- Promote equitable participation across genders, backgrounds and abilities.
- Coordinate reasonable adaptations with TDH Italy to support participants with disabilities.
- Apply neutrality, conflict sensitivity and do-no-harm principles throughout delivery.
- Avoid requiring participants to disclose personal experiences of violence, trauma or sensitive affiliations.
- Use anonymised or fictionalised cases where disclosure could create risks.
- Distinguish training exercises from actual mediation or resolution of community disputes.
- Comply with TDH Italy’s safeguarding, code of conduct, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse, confidentiality and data protection requirements.

## 8. Management, Coordination and Responsibilities:

The trainer will report to the TDH Italy Project Manager and coordinate delivery with designated field focal points.

**TDH Italy will:**

- Arrange training venues, agreed equipment, refreshments and printing of approved materials.
- Coordinate local logistics and provide relevant information on participant needs.
- Review the workplan, materials and deliverables.
- Support attendance monitoring and communicate applicable safeguarding procedures.

**The trainer will:**

- Support with selection and mobilising participants.
- Prepare and deliver both programmes and complete the agreed assessment and reporting.
- Identify equipment and printing requirements sufficiently in advance.
- Include travel and accommodation costs required for the assignment in the financial proposal.
- Maintain regular coordination with TDH Italy and promptly report issues affecting delivery.

Changes to the agreed scope, locations, course numbers or deliverables require prior written agreement.

## 9. Duration, Location and Indicative Level of Effort

Implementation will take place from mid-October 2026 to mid-February 2027.

The contract will cover training delivery days across Aleppo, Latakia and Idlib. All preparation, coordination, assessment, reporting and travel requirements must be included in the proposed daily rate and total contract price. Applicants must submit their financial offer based on implementation days only, with no additional billable days for these tasks.

The final schedule will be agreed with TDH Italy, taking account of participant availability and operational arrangements.

## 10. Required Qualifications and Experience

Applicants should demonstrate:

- A relevant university qualification in peace and conflict studies, social sciences, community development or a related field, or equivalent relevant professional experience.
- Practical experience in conflict analysis, peacebuilding and community dialogue.
- Demonstrated experience designing and delivering participatory training for young people.
- Experience facilitating sensitive discussions and managing diverse group dynamics.
- Understanding of the Syrian context and ability to adapt training to local community realities.
- Ability to develop clear training materials and assess practical learning.
- Excellent spoken and written Arabic.
- Availability to deliver the full assignment and travel to all three governorates.

Experience in peacebuilding, inclusion, safeguarding and work with humanitarian or civil society organisations will be considered an asset.

## 11. Evaluation Criteria

- **Technical proposal:** Understanding of the assignment, quality of methodology, agendas, practical learning and assessment (30% weight)
- **Relevant experience**: Conflict analysis, peacebuilding, community dialogue and youth training (25% weight)
- **Contextual knowledge and delivery capacity:** Understanding of the Syrian context and ability to deliver in all three governorates (10% weight)
- **Qualifications and work samples:** Relevant qualifications and quality of submitted materials (5% weight)
- **Financial proposal**: Cost-effectiveness, completeness and clarity (30% weight)

## 12. Payment Schedule

Payments will be linked to the satisfactory completion and written acceptance of the following deliverables by TDH Italy. Percentages apply to the total agreed contract price.

- 20%: Acceptance of Deliverable 1 and 2: Inception note and detailed workplan and two complete training packages
- 30%: Completion and acceptance of the first four courses and their four course reports under Deliverables 3 and 4, representing 50% of the training delivery.
- 30%: Completion and acceptance of the remaining four courses and their four course reports under Deliverables 3 and 4, bringing training delivery to 100%.
- 20%: Acceptance of Deliverable 5: Consolidated final report and material handover

## 13. Ownership, Confidentiality and Ethical Obligations

- Materials and reports developed specifically under the assignment will be handed over to TDH Italy in editable formats.
- Any pre-existing or third-party materials must be identified, appropriately acknowledged and authorised for the intended use.
- The trainer must protect participants’ personal information and comply with agreed consent, confidentiality and data protection procedures.
- Participant information, photographs and training outputs may not be published or shared externally without prior authorisation.
- The trainer must sign and comply with TDH Italy’s applicable ethical and safeguarding policies.
- Revisions needed to meet the approved scope and quality requirements are included in the agreed consultancy fee.

jobs.title: Country Representative
jobs.description:
Habitat for Humanity is looking for “**Country Representative**” that serves as primary country focal point of Habitat for Humanity International (HFHI) and external representative in Jordan and is a key member of the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) leadership structure.

**1.Introduction and background:**

**Habitat for Humanity (HFH)** is an international nonprofit organization founded in 1976 as the world’s leader in addressing the housing challenges faced by vulnerable communities. Currently it operates in more than 60 countries around the world and brings people together to build more prosperous and vibrant communities by making sure everyone has a safe, affordable place to call home. Since its founding in 1976, it has helped more than 62 million people globally build their futures on their own terms through access to decent housing. HFH works alongside people of all walks of life to build, repair and finance their homes, by innovating new ways of building and financing, and by advocating for policies that make constructing and accessing housing easier for everyone.

HFHI works through a broad network of national Habitat organizations and other strategic partners, such as corporations, financial service providers, individuals, non-governmental organizations, foundations, local governments, as well as the private sector actors. HFHI supports program and project implementation by national HFH organizations and directly implements some projects and programs regionally. HFH started operating in Jordan in 1989 and has supported more than 48,000 households in 6 governorates across Jordan to improve their housing conditions in partnership with strategic local partners and community members.

**2. Position Description:**

The Country Representative (CR) reports to MENA Hub Director and supports the Director in identifying and nurturing relationships with country-based donors, local authorities, development partners, and target communities, all within the framework of HFHI’s regional and global strategies. Under the guidance of the MENA Hub Director, the CR is also responsible for leading country-level fundraising and resource mobilization efforts, while positioning HFHI as a housing thought leader in national dialogues and debates.

While the CR is also expected to deliver on standard country management tasks such as operational planning, financial and risk management, compliance, and safeguarding, our newly integrated model and structure require daily collaboration with MENA Hub staff on all the above.

The CR collaborates closely with thematic leads enabling and facilitating their technical leadership, and supports program managers in delivering against agreed objectives, embracing a people-centric approach.

**3.Scope of work and deliverables:**

**Strategic Alignment and Country Planning:**

1. Support overall strategic leadership for HFHI’s engagement in Jordan aligning country goals and plans with the MENA Strategy and HFHI global priorities.
2. Working closely with thematic leads to incorporating strategies and priorities into the overall country strategy, ensuring country plans reflect and operationalize agreed thematic approaches.
3. Support the annual country planning and budgeting process (for HFHI-funded work in-country), under the guidance of the MENA Hub Director and relevant Hub teams and monitor performance against approved plans.
4. Conduct regular country-level risk reviews, maintain a country risk register, develop mitigation plans, and escalate high/ “red” risks to the MENA Hub Director.

**Operation, Finance, Governance and Compliance:**

1. Oversee HFHI’s operational footprint in Jordan (offices, staff, contracts, and major activities), ensuring effective and efficient use of resources and compliance with HFHI standards, donor requirements and local legislation.
2. Ensure day-to-day operational compliance, local registration, and risk monitoring.
3. Provide day-to-day administrative line management for country-based staff, including leave approvals, budget oversight related to country operations, and coordination of operational support in line with HFH policies and procedures.
4. Ensure HFHI complies with all relevant registration, licensing, tax, and regulatory requirements in Jordan, working closely with the MENA Hub, Legal and Finance teams.
5. Enforce the Code of Conduct, Conflict of Interest, anti-corruption and safeguarding policies, ensuring they are understood and applied in day-to-day operations and partnerships.
6. Oversee basic financial management and internal controls for HFHI operations in-country, including oversight of budgets, expenditures, and financial reporting to the MENA Hub
7. Ensure procurement, contracting and vendor management for HFHI activities in Jordan comply with HFHI and donor policies, and that value for money, transparency and fairness are upheld.
8. Implement and oversee HFHI global safety and security standards for all HFHI staff, consultants, and visitors in-country, including maintaining country security plans, contact trees and incident protocols.
9. Ensure prompt reporting, investigation and follow-up of safeguarding and security incidents in line with HFHI policies and national law.
10. Coordinate external and internal audits related to HFHI’s country presence and support the timely closure of audit findings and implementation of management actions.

**Program Implementation Oversight, Resources mobilization and Partnership:**

1. Support local funding opportunities relevant to Jordan (institutional donors, multilaterals, private sector, foundations, etc.) and share intelligence with the MENA Hub.
2. Network and coalition building.
3. Support the development of country-level concept notes and project proposals, and support HFHI’s participation in multi-country or regional proposals that include Jordan.
4. Support the identification, scoping and design of quality projects in Jordan, aligned with HFHI’s priorities and in collaboration with the MENA Hub Subject Matter Experts (SMEs)
5. Map and engage potential donors, partners, and stakeholders in Jordan (government, private sector, financial service providers, civil society, faith organizations, academia, UN and other international actors)
6. Maintain a country partnership mapping and engagement tracker, including pipelines, contacts and agreed follow-up actions.
7. Facilitate the negotiation of country-level Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) and partnership agreements, in coordination with the MENA Hub, Legal Programs and Finance.

**Advocacy, Policy Engagement & External Representation:**

1. In coordination with the MENA Hub Director and HFHI Advocacy teams, support the development and implementation of a national advocacy and policy engagement plan aligned with regional advocacy priorities (e.g. housing policy, housing finance, urban development, resilience).
2. From an advocacy perspective, supports building and maintaining relationships with government counterparts, donors, United Nations (UN) agencies, European Union (EU) delegations, financial institutions, sector networks, civil society organizations, and other policy stakeholders at country level.
3. Represent HFHI in national forums, sector working groups, donor coordination platforms and, where appropriate, media opportunities, positioning HFHI as a credible housing and urban development actor in Jordan.
4. Support the development and implementation of a country communications approach that promotes HFHI’s brand, programs and advocacy messaging, and provides content for regional and global communications.
5. Ensuring advocacy and communication efforts are evidence-based, reflecting learning and impact from HFHI-supported programs and partnerships in Jordan.

**People Leadership, Culture and Volunteer Engagement:**

1. Provide direction, support to any HFH staff and consultants based in Jordan, fostering a culture of accountability, inclusion, learning and safeguarding.
2. In collaboration with Regional Human Resources (HR), support recruitment, onboarding, performance management and development of country-based staff and key consultants, as applicable.
3. Model and promote HFHI’s values and commitments to safeguarding, diversity, equity and inclusion in all country-level interactions and decisions.
4. Where applicable, support planning and hosting of HFHI-associated volunteer builds and events in Jordan, ensuring that they are safe, ethical, and aligned with HFHI standards and community priorities.
5. Ensure volunteer activities comply with safeguarding and duty-of-care standards, and that relevant stories and data are captured for visibility and fundraising purposes.

**4.Required Skills & Competencies:**

1. Bachelor's degree in a relevant field, combined with substantial professional experience in international development, organizational leadership, or a related area. An advanced degree is an asset.
2. Experience:
- 7-10 years of progressively responsible experience in international development, including at least 5 years in a senior leadership or management role.
- Experience with traditional and emerging institutional donors including the Gulf countries.
- Proven experience in resource mobilization including donor engagement and proposal development.
- Experience managing diverse teams remotely.
- A proven track record of both winning and executing multimillion projects.
- Extensive experience working in Jordan's international development sector, with a strong understanding of the local operating environment, stakeholder landscape, and partnership networks.
- Ability to adapt a changing environment and navigating market turbulences.
- Management of teams and experience operating in a matrix structure.
- Excellent written and spoken English and Arabic language.
- Experience working with private philanthropy is an asset.
- Previous experience in a hub structure is a plus.
3. Active support for **HFHI Values**:

**Humility** – We are part of something bigger than ourselves,

**Courage** – We do what’s right, even when it is difficult or unpopular,

**Accountability** – We take personal responsibility for Habitat’s mission),

***Safeguarding:***

*HFHI requires that all employees take seriously their ethical responsibilities to safeguarding our intended beneficiaries, their communities, and all those with whom we work*

*Managers at all levels have responsibilities to support and develop systems that create and maintain an environment that prevents harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, safeguards the rights of beneficiaries and community members (especially children), and promotes the implementation of Habitat for Humanity’s code of conduct).*

jobs.title: CGPP Indonesia Secretariat Director
jobs.description:
**Position Title**: CGPP Indonesia Secretariat Director

**Hiring Organization:** CORE, Inc. to be paid from the US

**Type of Employment:** Full-time consultancy.

**Duration of Contract:** November 1, 2026 – August 31, 2027 (with the possibility of extension)

**Duty Station:** Jakarta, Indonesia (with frequent travel to project-supported regions)

**Reports to:** CGPP Global Deputy Director

## Consultancy Purpose

The CGPP Indonesia Secretariat Director will be based in Jakarta, Indonesia and support CGPP National Program Manager and Provincial Team Leaders in operations in Indonesia to improve maternal and child health (MCH) outcomes in the selected districts of Papua and East Java provinces or any other selected CGPP work areas in Indonesia.

Serving as CGPP’s senior in-country representative, the CGPP Secretariat Director will maintain close coordination with government and the US Department of State (DOS) Foreign Assistance team.

The CGPP Indonesia Secretariat Director will provide leadership across all aspects of project planning and implementation and will maintain and strengthen CGPP's relationship with key partners and stakeholders. These include the Government of Indonesia’s Ministry of Health (and other relevant government ministries) the US Department of State (US DOS), UNICEF, STRIDES implemented by FHI 360, other Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI) partners, and Wahana Visi/ World Vision (WV) Indonesia.

In fulfilling this role, the Secretariat Director will ensure that:

- CGPP activities address stated project objectives, support national MCH and polio priorities, and are aligned with global MCH and polio objectives; and
- The needs and concerns of CGPP field teams and the communities they serve for all program related needs are effectively communicated to decisionmakers at all levels.

## Key Responsibilities

The Secretariat Director will be responsible for the following:

- **Strategic Leadership**
Provide strategic leadership for CGPP programming in Indonesia, in coordination with the CGPP global headquarters team, and CGPP National Program Manager including guiding the development of technical priorities and strategic plans that expand access to lifesaving services, strengthen routine immunization systems, and improve maternal and child health outcomes through integrated and sustainable approaches aligned with national and global priorities.
- **Government and Donor Engagement**
Lead institutional engagement with the Ministry of Health and relevant national and subnational structures, as well as with US DOS-Foreign Assistance.
- **Secretariat Leadership and Capacity Strengthening**
Provide leadership, mentorship, and oversight performance management for the CGPP National Program Manager; ensure the adequacy and quality of capacity strengthening for field-level teams and guide continuous improvement of implementation approaches.
- **Program Oversight, Quality, and Integration**
Provide oversight to the CGPP National Program Manager to effectively track progress toward CGPP MCH and polio goals, ensuring high-quality, coordinated implementation across program areas, and guide adjustments to strategies and approaches based on performance, risk analysis, and evolving context.
- **Planning, Budgeting, and Accountability**
Review, approve, and oversee implementation of the activities as per approved annual work plans and budgets, ensuring coherence, feasibility, alignment with agreed priorities, and adherence to approved budgets, with proactive identification of risks and timely course correction as needed.
- **Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning**
Oversee monitoring, evaluation, and learning activities, including planned CGPP assessments/ evaluations; ensure data quality and validation processes; guide the interpretation and use of data and evidence to inform strategic, technical, and operational decision-making; and work closely with the CGPP MEAL Officer to align workflows, strengthen MEAL capacity across secretariat and partner teams, coordinate partner support, and maintain MEAL standards in data quality and reporting across all partners.
- **Partner Coordination and Representation**
Serve as the focal point for strategic coordination and engagement with national and international stakeholders, including government counterparts, donors, and peer organizations; represent CGPP in relevant technical, policy, and coordination platforms; and sustain informal engagements with government counterparts and peer organizations, including cultivating ongoing informal communication channels to strengthen relationships, identify emerging issues, and foster trust and collaboration across stakeholders.
- **Reporting and Knowledge Management**
Ensure timely preparation and submission of required CGPP reports and briefings; validate monthly data updates, performance indicators, and partner-reported results; and oversee systematic documentation, timely synthesis, and dissemination of policy developments, coordination outcomes, and lessons learned as well as key discussions, decisions, action points, and follow-up items arising from all secretariat engagements – including technical coordination meetings, internal secretariat discussions, partner consultations, stakeholder engagements, and informal coordination touchpoints – to strengthen transparency, institutional memory, and accountability.

## Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

- **Demonstrated ability to provide strategic leadership** for complex, multi-partner initiatives, with strong analytical judgment and systems thinking to navigate ambiguity, risk, and competing priorities.
- **Exceptional relationship management and diplomatic skills**, with the ability to build trust, influence outcomes, and manage alignment across diverse stakeholders, including government counterparts, donors, implementing partners, and civil society organizations.
- **Proven ability to lead, mentor, and hold accountable senior and multidisciplinary teams**, fostering a culture of collaboration, performance, learning, and results in complex operating environments.
- **Strong executive communication and representation skills**, with demonstrated ability to synthesize complex information, brief senior decisionmakers and donors, and represent the Secretariat credibly in high-level national and international forums.
- **Demonstrated capacity to convene, align, and harmonize partners** around shared lifesaving priorities, ensuring integrated approaches and avoiding fragmentation or vertical implementation.
- **Sound judgment and decision-making capacity**, including the ability to make timely, evidence-informed decisions with significant organizational, financial, and reputational implications.

## Preferred Qualifications

- **Experience leading or supporting a secretariat or partnership platform**, including stewardship of collective decision-making processes across multiple institutions.
- **Demonstrated experience navigating complex political or institutional environments**, including managing sensitivities across government, donors, and implementing organizations.
- **Experience leading programs during periods of transition or uncertainty**, such as scale-up, funding shifts, public health emergencies, or changes in government or donor priorities.

## Required Languages

- **English** (Required): Advanced professional proficiency required, with ability to communicate effectively in meetings, presentations, and written reports with international stakeholders.
- **Bahasa Indonesia** (Required): Professional proficiency in speaking, reading, and writing.

## Travel

- Must be willing and able to travel approximately 30% to 50% of the time.

## Supervisory Responsibilities

- Will supervise staff as assigned.

## Working Relationships

- Within CGPP Indonesia (e.g., National Program Manager, MEAL Officer, Provincial Team Leaders), Wahana Visi leadership, and finance, procurement, and grants teams.
- External: Ministry of Health and relevant provincial, district, and local MOH, US DOS, GPEI partners, and others.
- CGPP Global Secretariat Team: Coordinate with the global secretariat team and Asia regional team and obtain technical guidance as needed.

## Qualifications

- Master's degree in public health or a related technical field.
- At least 12 years of progressively responsible experience, including at least five years in a senior management or leadership role, overseeing multidisciplinary teams in international and/or multicultural settings.
- Demonstrated experience providing strategic leadership and operational oversight for complex programs or initiatives.
- Demonstrated experience working with or supporting governance structures and engaging effectively with government counterparts and institutional partners.
- Proven experience in managing donor-funded programs, including compliance with donor regulations, financial accountability, audits, and high-quality reporting.
- Strong knowledge and experience in budget management and financial oversight.
- Technical expertise and demonstrated experience in maternal and child health (MCH), combined with strong familiarity with the Indonesian health system and context.
- Ability to use data, evidence, and learning to inform strategic decision-making and program improvement.
- Proficiency in standard office and data analysis software.
- Excellent leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills, with demonstrated ability to represent organizations at senior national and international levels and to build effective partnerships with donors, government, and implementing partners.

## Disclaimer

- This job description is not an exhaustive list of the skill, effort, duties, and responsibilities associated with the position.

jobs.title: Psychiatrist or Clinical Psychologist - West Africa
jobs.description:
**Position summary:**

Shelter For Life International (SFL) is anticipating a project in West Africa with a focus on managing the flow of migrants into the region. Included in the project’s objectives will be structured movement and resettlement of migrants within and outside Guinea-Bissau, while providing basic food, shelter and other humanitarian assistance.

SFL is seeking a clinical psychologist to provide mental health and social support to migrants in West Africa. The clinical psychologist will be responsible for designing and implementing a psychological and psychosocial support program for migrants who are navigating displacement and resettlement. This role involves providing direct clinical care, occasional crisis intervention, and building the capacity of local staff to ensure culturally appropriate mental health services during the resettlement process. The position will be based in Bissau, Guinea-Bissau.

**Areas of Responsibility:**

- Conduct psychological assessments and provide professional mental health support to newly arrived and transitioning migrants, with referral to in-country medical professionals if needed.
- Develop and implement support protocols for individuals experiencing stress or trauma.
- Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams, including medical staff as needed, to ensure a holistic approach to migrant well-being and basic needs.
- Conduct psychoeducational workshops to help migrants cope with acculturative stress, build resilience, and prepare for resettlement in new host countries.
- Maintain strictly confidential clinical records and monitor mental health trends within the migrant population to adapt programs and inform SFL management.

**Education and Experience Requirements:**

- Medical doctor degree (M.D., D.O., or M.B.B.S.) with Psychiatry residency, Master’s degree or Doctorate (Ph.D. or Psy.D.) in Clinical Psychology from an accredited institution.
- Valid professional license to practice clinical psychology in your home jurisdiction.
- Minimum of 3 to 5 years of post-graduate clinical experience, specifically focusing on trauma, displacement, or working with refugee/migrant populations.
- Must be fluent in English (written and spoken), with a working knowledge of Spanish. Additional language skills relevant to the demographic context (e.g., French, Portuguese) are a plus.
- Proven experience working in humanitarian emergencies, international development, or low-resource, post-conflict settings.
- Experience in cross-cultural counseling and effectively conducting clinical sessions with the assistance of language interpreters.

**Personal Skills and Abilities:**

- Exceptional cross-cultural communication skills and sensitivity to the diverse religious, cultural, and social backgrounds of multi-national migrants.
- Strong adaptability and psychological resilience, with the capacity to thrive in a dynamic and challenging physical environment with limited local amenities.
- High emotional intelligence and the ability to maintain strong professional boundaries to prevent burnout in a high-stress environment.
- Collaborative leadership style with the ability for capacity-building and empowering local staff for assistance.
- Sound judgment, strong problem-solving skills, and the ability to make rapid clinical decisions independently in the event of crises.
- Commitment to the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence, as well as the core mission of Shelter For Life International.

SFL is interested in applicants whose professional ethics, values, and determination to achieve impact are evident and aligned with organizational priorities.

Additional Notes:

- A minimum of 12 months' commitment to live and work in Guinea-Bissau is required.
- Applicants must be comfortable with travel within the project area.
- Competitive pay and benefits, including paid time off, ACA-compliant health insurance, and housing allowance.

Job description in PDF here: [https://shorturl.at/gYIwz](https://shorturl.at/gYIwz)

**About us:**

Shelter For Life International (SFL) is an international faith-based relief and development organization with over 30 years’ experience providing sustainable development and humanitarian assistance to post-conflict countries worldwide. We are currently operational in Afghanistan, The Gambia, and Ukraine, with headquarters located in Minnetonka, MN, USA. Our team provides support and assistance in the following areas:

1. Population Movement and Settlement
2. Public Infrastructure Reconstruction
3. Economic and Social Development

Our mission is to demonstrate God’s love by enabling people affected by conflict and disaster to restore their lives and rebuild their communities. To learn more about us, please visit [www.shelter.org](http://www.shelter.org/)

jobs.title: Technical Advisor I, Cash & Markets
jobs.description:
**NOTE: The Pay Range referenced in this job announcement only applies to applicants who perform the job within the US and to applicants classified by CRS as International Assignees. Staff hired on local payroll would follow the respective Country pay range. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for your anticipated work location during the candidate selection process.**

**Pay Range**
$71,349 - $88,085 Annually

**NOTE: This is a remote position, with a preference for candidates based in the LACRO and EMEA regions; CRS will also give preference to candidates who are based in countries where we have existing offices. CRS does not sponsor visas for remote employees.**

Catholic Relief Services is implementing a global emergency response initiative designed to deliver timely, lifesaving humanitarian assistance in rapidly evolving crises worldwide. Over 18 months, the program enables fast, flexible action to address urgent needs arising from sudden shocks and protracted emergencies. It supports critical humanitarian sectors through context-appropriate assistance while emphasizing operational readiness, locally led implementation, accountability to affected communities, and safe, dignified programming. The initiative strengthens the organization’s ability to respond at speed and scale in complex and resource-constrained environments, ensuring help reaches people most in need when it matters most. This role will support cash readiness efforts of Country Programs and partners, as well as provide technical support for ongoing programming, and new emergency programs, related to cash, market-based programming, and emergency food security and livelihoods.

**Job Summary:**

This position is embedded in the Humanitarian Response Department (HRD) Market-based Rapid Response and Recovery (MBRRR) Team. The HRD MBRRR Team is the agency lead for Cash & Market-based Programming and the emergency Food Security & Livelihoods Sectors. As part of this team, you will provide technical advice and support to a range of program design and implementation issues in Cash & Markets as well as Food Security & Livelihoods, in line with Catholic Relief Services (CRS) program quality principles and standards, donor guidelines, and industry best practices to Country Program (CP) teams and partners to advance the delivery of high-quality humanitarian assistance programming to the poor and vulnerable impacted by crises. Your advice, knowledge, and support will contribute to determining how effective, adaptive, and innovative CRS’ Cash and Market-based programming is across the agency.

**Roles and Key Responsibilities:**

- Support the development and contribute to the implementation of agency-wide strategies, standards, tools, and best practices in relation to Cash and Market Based Programming that effectively engage partners, donors, and governments. Help ensure a cross-sectoral approach integrating gender, protection mainstreaming, and disaster risk reduction.
- Provide programmatic and operational (including administrative and finance) technical solutions to CP teams, remotely and on-site, for strategic planning and how to best apply standards, best practices, partnership principles, tools and M&E, helping to ensure high-quality implementation.
- Contribute to, and in some cases lead, the development of the technical design for proposals. Support the process of preparation, design, submission and approval of project concepts and full-fledged proposals. As needed, act as a technical writer on proposal development teams. Advise project teams on integrating donor strategies, priorities and technical requirements into CRS’ approach.
- Support capacity strengthening initiatives in relation to Cash and Market based programming for staff and partners through helping develop learning and training strategies and agendas/curriculums, conducting trainings and workshops, and coaching.
- Collect and analyze program data, capture, and share lessons learned and best practices for specific projects to facilitate improvements in decision-making and contribute to the Cash and Market Based Programming learning agenda.
- Contribute to maintaining relationships with donors, peer organizations, research, and other institutions, participate in forums in the area of Cash and Market Based Programming to collect and share best practices and promote CRS’ work.
- Support Country Programs and partners in strengthening their cash readiness through targeted technical support, particularly in relation to developing capacities, identifying suitable cash delivery mechanisms and Financial Service Providers (FSPs), developing Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and tools, and supporting the design and implementation of pilot cash programs.

***Knowledge, Skills and Abilities***

- Strong relationship management skills with ability to influence and get buy-in from people not under direct supervision and to work with individuals in diverse geographical and cultural settings
- Good strategic, analytical, problem-solving and systems thinking skills with capacity to see the big picture and ability to make sound judgment
- Good technical writing skills
- Presentation, facilitation, training, mentoring, and coaching skills
- Proactive, resourceful and results-oriented

***Required Languages*** – English and Spanish required. French, Portuguese and Arabic highly desired.

***Travel*** - Must be willing and able to travel up to 50%, including at short notice and to emergency situations.

**Basic Qualifications**

- Bachelor's Degree in humanitarian assistance, social policy, economics or related field required.
- Minimum of five-eight years relevant work experience with progressive responsibilities, ideally with an international NGO, with minimum of two years relevant emergency response and field-based experience in cash and market-based programming, including in protracted and rapid onset crisis contexts.
- Experienced trainer in CVA Programming. Knowledge of technical principles and concepts in cash and market-based programming, including experience with multiple CVA delivery mechanisms.
- Demonstrated experience in designing CVA Programs, particularly for US Government funding, and designing and implementing Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) or sectoral cash and voucher programs related to Food Security, Livelihoods, Shelter or WASH sectors. Experience in other sectoral cash programming, such as Nutrition, DRR, and/or Protection, desirable. Experience with e-voucher platforms highly desirable.
- Knowledge of, and experience in, conducting market assessments and response analysis to inform modality decisions across different areas of programming, particularly in emergency rapid-onset humanitarian contexts.
- Experience in innovative project design for rapid response with market-based programming in a diversity of contexts.
- Experience in proposal development, for government and/or private donors.
- Knowledge of capacity strengthening and technical accompaniment best practices, with a focus on collaboration and supporting partner-led responses.
- Experience and skills in networking and relations with donors, peer organizations, and faith-based and civil society partners. Understanding of partnership principles.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Proficient in MS Office packages (Excel, Word, PowerPoint), data analytics and PowerBi.
- Master's Degree in humanitarian assistance, social policy, economics or related field is an advantage.

**Agency Competencies (for all CRS Staff):**

- **Personal Accountability** – Consistently takes responsibility for one’s own actions.
- **Acts with Integrity** - Consistently models values aligned with CRS Guiding Principles and mission. Is considered honest.
- **Builds and Maintains Trust** - Shows consistency between words and actions.
- **Collaborates with Others** – Works effectively in intercultural and diverse teams.
- **Open to Learn** – Seeks out experiences that may change perspective or provide an opportunity to learn new things.

**Agency Leadership Competencies:**

- **Lead Change** – Continually looks for ways to improve the agency through a culture of agility, openness, and innovation.
- **Develops and Recognizes Others** – Builds the capacity of staff to reach their full potential and enhance team and agency performance.
- **Strategic Mindset** – Understands role in translating, communicating, and implementing agency strategy and team priorities.

**What we offer**

CRS offers U.S. based staff a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, life insurance, vision, and a generous retirement savings plan. Benefits packages for successful candidates employed outside the U.S. are based on the country of employment/in-country office where the candidate will perform the role. CRS´ work culture is a collaborative, mission-driven culture committed to improving the lives of the poor throughout the world.
