jobs.title: Director Community Based Inclusive Development (CBID)
jobs.description:
## **About CBM**

CBM (registered as CBM Christoffel-Blindenmission Christian Blind Mission e.V.) is an international development organisation committed to improving the quality of life of persons with disabilities in the persons communities of the world. Based on our Christian values and more than 100 years of professional expertise, we address poverty as a cause and a consequence of disability. We work in partnership to create an inclusive society for all.

**About the role:**

We are looking for an experienced Director\* Community Based Inclusive Development (CBID) to lead CBM’s newly refocused CBID Initiative. In this senior leadership role, you will shape the strategic direction of Inclusive Community Support and Care, Inclusive Education, and Inclusive Livelihood, strengthen CBM’s leadership in disability-inclusive development, and drive greater impact for persons with disabilities through community-based approaches worldwide.

**This full-time position is only filled locally in one of CBM permanent established entities.** (ex: Bensheim (Germany), UK (Cambridge or remote), Nairobi (Kenya), Abuja (Nigeria), Lomé (Togo), Yaoundé (Cameroon), Lusaka (Zambia), Addis Abeba (Ethiopia), Guatemala City, Kampala (Uganda), Niamey (Niger), etc.).
**Local contractual conditions of the respective country will apply.** An expatriation is not intended

## **These are your responsibilities**

**Strategic Leadership**

- Provide overall leadership and management of the CBID Division.
- Lead, develop and inspire a globally distributed team of CBID and technical advisors.
- Manage divisional resources, people, budgets and performance to achieve organisational objectives.
- Position CBM and the CBID work in key global, regional and national processes and alliances which are related to the work of CBID.
- Develop and implement the global CBID strategy and implementation framework within CBM’s overall strategy.
- Monitor emerging sector trends and position CBM as a thought leader in community based inclusive development.
- Grow CBID within CBM as a core pillar of CBM’s strategy.
- Ensure attractiveness of CBM’s CBID work for Individual and Institutional Donors.

**Technical Leadership & Quality**

- Develop and maintain technical standards, guidance and tools for CBID programming in the areas of Inclusive. Community Support and Care (ICSC), Inclusive Education, Inclusive Livelihood.
- Provide guidance to the ICSC team and the advocacy team lead.
- Directly manage the advisors for Inclusive Livelihood and Inclusive Education.
- Bring clear approaches (definition, concepts, methods, tools) in the respective technical areas in place.
- Provide strategic oversight of programme quality.

**Resource Mobilisation & Organisational Sustainability**

- Contribute to resource mobilisation strategies and donor engagement.
- Support development of high-quality funding proposals.

## **These are your qualifications**

- Master’s degree in Business Administration, International Development, Disability Studies, Social Sciences or related field.
- Minimum 10 years of international development experience at managerial level.
- Extensive expertise in disability-inclusive development and community-based approaches.
- Ability to define and drive global strategies, translate vision into action, and align diverse stakeholders around common objectives.
- Proven capability to lead, coach, and develop multicultural and geographically dispersed teams while fostering collaboration, inclusion, and accountability.
- Professional English; German, French and/or Spanish desirable.
- Identification with Christian values and the mandate of CBM

## **What we offer**

- A meaningful position with a lot of creative freedom in the world's leading organisation in the field of Disability Inclusive Development
- A fair salary and other social benefits based on the local conditions in the country you apply for
- An approachable, agile organisation with self-reliant people in a diverse and collegial team and great team spirit

jobs.title: TCA - COORDINATEUR TERRAIN (H/F) - EST TCHAD
jobs.description:
**Que faisons nous ...**

**Date de début souhaitée :** 16/11/2026
**Durée de la mission:** 5 mois
**Localisation:** Iriba

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL** (SI) est une association d’aide humanitaire internationale qui, depuis plus de 40 ans, porte secours aux populations victimes de conflits armés et de catastrophes naturelles en répondant aux besoins vitaux, boire, manger, s’abriter. Particulièrement engagée dans le combat contre les maladies liées à l’eau insalubre, première cause de mortalité au monde, SI met en œuvre par ses interventions une expertise dans le domaine de l’accès à l’eau potable, l’assainissement et la promotion de l’hygiène mais également dans celui, essentiel, de la sécurité alimentaire et moyen d’existence. Présentes dans 26 pays, les équipes de SI - 3 200 personnes au total composées d’expatriés, de salariés nationaux, de permanents au siège, de quelques bénévoles…- interviennent avec professionnalisme et engagement dans le respect des cultures.

**La mission**

SI est présente au Tchad depuis 2008, au Cameroun depuis 2014 et en Centrafrique depuis 2007. Les missions Tchad et Cameroun ont fusionné en 2021 et la Centrafrique à rejoint cette fusion en 2025. La mission multi-pays Tchad-Cameroun-Centrafrique (TCA) est composée de 10 bases/sous-bases au total. Au Cameroun: 1 base de coordination mission à Yaoundé et 1 base opérationnelle à Maroua dans l'Extrême Nord, ainsi qu'une sous-base à Makary. Au Tchad: 1 bureau de coordination zone Tchad à Ndjaména, et 4 bases opérationnelles à Bagasola dans la province du Lac, et Adré, Iriba et Amdjarass dans l'est du pays. En RCA: 1 bureau de coordination zone RCA à Bangui, et 3 bases opérationnelles à Markounda dans le Nord-Ouest, à Bouar dans l'Ouest et à Zémio dans le Haut-Mbomou.

SI est présente au Tchad depuis 2008 et dispose actuellement de 4 bases opérationelles à Bagasola (Lac), Adré (Ouaddai), Iriba (Wadi Fira) et Amdjarass (Ennedi Est). À l’Est, la réponse de SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL a visé à améliorer l'accès des réfugiés soudanais et populations tchadiennes à l'eau potable, aux services d'assainissement et à des conditions d'hygiène améliorées, afin de prévenir la propagation des maladies diarrhéiques. Une assistance d’urgence en réponse à l’épidémie de choléra a également été mise en œuvre par les équipes au second semestre de 2025. Bailleurs : ECHO, CDCS, SDC, FHRAOC, PWC, Sida

**Descriptif de l'offre**

DIMENSIONNEMENT DE L'EQUIPE EN BASE / COORDINATION :

Est Tchad: CT, Adjoint CT Prog, Log Manager, Admin Manage, Assist log (Adré, Iriba), Assist fin (Adré, Iriba), Gestionnaire log (Iriba), Gestionnaire fin (Iriba), RP et équipes prog (Adré, Iriba, Amdjarass), chargé de liaison (Iriba uniquement)
Ndjamena : DZO, Responsable Admin Fin, Gestionnaire log, Resp Grant, Resp E&C
Yaoundé: DP, DP Adjoint Prog , Coo Techniques Prog, Coo Log, Coo Fin, Coo RH, Coo Grant

OBJECTIF GENERAL DU POSTE :

Le/la coordinateur/trice de terrain assume le rôle de chef(fe) de mission délégué(e) pour une région d’un pays dans lequel Solidarités International intervient.
Il/elle propose une stratégie régionale adaptée au contexte géopolitique et humanitaire, et veille à sa mise en œuvre une fois celle-ci validée.
Il/elle vérifie et s'assure que les projets sont menés conformément à la charte de Solidarités International, dans le respect de toutes les procédures internes et contractuelles.
Il/elle mobilise les ressources matérielles et financières nécessaires au bon déroulement des programmes et supervise la gestion des ressources.
Il/elle coordonne les équipes sur le terrain et est responsable de leur sécurité dans la zone qui lui est assignée.
Il/elle est l'interlocuteur direct et le représentant du chef de mission.

ENJEUX ET DEFIS SPECIFIQUES :

\- Contexte sécuritaire volatile avec notamment frappes de drone (Tiné, Adikong) et incursions à la frontière
\- Equipe de l'Est dispersée géographiquement
\- Fermeture base d'Abéché à finalsiée et finalisation ouverture de la nase d'Amjarass
\- Volume opérationnel important entre Adré, Iriba et Amdjarass (6 à 7 contrats)
\- Contraintes opérationelles spécifiques à l'Est qui entravent la mise en oeuvre des projets

PRIORITES SUR LES 2-3 PREMIERS MOIS :

\- Appui à la structuration des bases de l'Est (suivi carburant, suivi budgétaire, suivi paiements fournisseur)
\- Gestion de la sécurité et des mouvements et suivi de la tendance avec le conflit soudanais
\- Représentation externe auprès des autorités locales, des fora régionaux de coordination, et des autres partenaires ONGI et ONGN
\- Finalisation de la fermeture de la base d'Abéché et finalisation ouverture de la base de Amdjarass

CONTRAINTES SECURITAIRES :

Adré Iriba et Amdjarass (niveau 3) avec risque de détérioration de la situation sécuritaire (débordement du conflit soudanais avec attaques de drone). Le Coordinateur Terrain Est sera basé à Iriba mais avec des déplacements fréquents sur les bases de Adré et de Amdjarass.

**Votre profil**

DIPLÔME REQUIS : Un master en études humanitaires ou en développement, en sciences sociales, en gestion ou dans une autre discipline connexe.

EXPERIENCE DANS LE SECTEUR HUMANITAIRE : 3-4 ans

EXPERIENCE SUR POSTE EQUIVALENT : 0-2 ans

COMPETENCES TECHNIQUES :

1\. Coordination interdépartementale (suivi budgétaire, procédure d'achat, process RH)

2\. Bonne connaissance du cycle de gestion des projets

3\. Gestion de la sécurité et de l'accès

4\. Capacités de représentation externe (autorités, bailleurs, fora de coordinatin)

COMPETENCES TRANSVERSES :

1\. Leadership et management

2\. Anticipation, organisation, et suivi

3\. Réflexion et analyse stratégique

LANGUES :

1\. Français (obligatoire)

2\. Anglais (obligatoire)

3\. Arabe (un plus)

**SI vous offrira les conditions suivantes**

**Un poste salarié :** Selon l'expérience, à partir de EUR 3080 bruts par mois (2800 salaire de base + 10% d'indemnité de congé annuel versée mensuellement) et un Per Diem mensuel de 600 euros.

SI couvre également les frais de logement et les frais de déplacement entre le pays d'origine de l'expatrié et le lieu d'affectation.

**Breaks :** Pendant la mission, un système d'alternance entre travail et congés est mis en place à raison de 7 jours ouvrables tous les trois mois (avec USD 850 alloués par Solidarités International). A ces périodes de pause, s'ajoute un jour de repos supplémentaire par mois travaillé.

**Couverture sociale et médicale :** Les expatriés bénéficient d'une assurance qui rembourse tous les frais de santé (y compris les frais médicaux et chirurgicaux, les soins dentaires et ophtalmologiques, le rapatriement) et d'un système de prévoyance incluant les risques de guerre. Les frais de vaccination et de traitement antipaludéen indispensables sont remboursés.

**Condition de vie** : Iriba est classée en niveau 3. Il y a peu d'activité à faire à Iriba mais la base a été rénovée récemment avec de bonnes conditions de vie.
La liaison UNHAS avec Ndjaména a lieu 5 jours par semaine sur Abéché ou Adré (hors aléat liées à des intempéries ou des pannes) et il est également possible de rejoindre Ndjaména par la route en dernier recours.

jobs.title: Regional Human Rights Specialist, Africa
jobs.description:
**Reports To:** Director, Africa Protected Areas Management Unit (APAMU)

**Location:** Kigali, Rwanda (or another WCS Africa hub location)

**Country Program/Sector:** APAMU /Africa Program

**Position Type:** Full-time

**Scope/Capacity:** Africa-wide

**Coordinates with:** APAMU Team, Rights & Communities, Rights & Communities Regional and National Staff, Regional Leadership Teams, Country Directors, Landscape Leads, Protected Area Managers, Law Enforcement Advisors, Program Development Teams, and Technical Working Groups

**About Us**

The Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) is a private, nonprofit U.S. organization founded in 1895. Its mission is to preserve wildlife and wild places by understanding critical issues, developing science-based solutions, and taking conservation action that benefits nature and humanity. With more than a century of experience, long-term commitments in dozens of landscapes, a presence in more than 60 countries, and experience creating more than 150 protected areas worldwide, WCS has accumulated the biological knowledge, cultural understanding, and partnerships necessary to ensure that wildlife and wild places thrive alongside local communities. WCS recognizes that nature and people are intrinsically linked, and that biological and cultural diversity are interdependent, mutually reinforcing and often co-evolved. Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities frequently represent the most active defenders of nature, and we believe that respecting and protecting the rights of Indigenous Peoples and local communities reflects our global commitment to equity and justice and is our best pathway to achieving durable conservation.

**About the Africa Program**

WCS manages one of the largest conservation portfolios in Africa, supporting protected and conserved areas, community-led conservation, key biodiversity landscapes, species conservation initiatives, and wildlife law enforcement efforts across multiple countries. Globally, WCS also supports Indigenous and Traditional Territories, a growing opportunity to center guardians of nature and to secure their rights.

The Africa Protected Areas Management Unit (APAMU) seeks to ensure that conservation outcomes are achieved in a manner that applies WCS policies, principles and commitments. The Global Rights and Communities (R&C) unit provides guidance and tools across WCS countries to promote community conservation, ensure social safeguards and promote respect for human rights and positive relationships with Indigenous Peoples, local communities, and other rights holders.

This position will play an important role in coordinating and contributing to a standardized approach to human rights protection in Africa, with the guidance of APAMU, Global R&C and close collaboration with regional and country teams.

**Job Purpose**

The Regional Human Rights Specialist will lead and support the standardization of human rights integration and rights-based approaches across WCS conservation programs throughout Africa. The position will provide strategic and technical guidance to country programs and field sites to support human rights integration in conservation law enforcement, conduct human rights impact analyses, assist in investigation or fact-finding around human rights issues as requested, develop recommendations for country programs or landscapes to address human rights issues and risks, and oversee the review of rights-respecting Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for field operations.

This position reports to the Director of Africa Protected Areas Management Unit (APAMU), and will play a critical role in the APAMU team in fulfilling the needs of a human rights based approach. The position will maintain a dotted line of reporting to the Senior Human Rights Specialist in Rights & Communities Global, for final approval and review of substantive human rights products and in order to coordinate with broader WCS policy and approaches outside of Africa. The position will also coordinate closely with regional and country level human rights, law enforcement, safeguards and communities staff.

This position will require significant travel to remote field locations and sites where WCS works, and working with diverse teams from different country programs. The candidate will be expected to undertake planning and coordination as necessary with global, regional and country or site-level counterparts.

**Major Responsibilities**

**1. Human Rights Strategy and Integration**

- Work with Senior Human Rights Specialist to ensure the implementation of WCS's rights-based conservation approach across all Africa programs.
- Coordinate with Regional Social Safeguards leads to support country programs and landscapes to integrate human rights into conservation planning, project design, budgets, monitoring, and reporting.
- Provide technical guidance on international human rights standards applicable to conservation programming.
- Promote alignment between WCS sites, country and regional level management, APAMU, and Rights & Communities.
- Support the development and review of organizational guidance, tools, frameworks, and operational procedures related to human rights.

**2. Human Rights Impact Analysis and Risk Management**

- Conduct human rights impact assessments and analyses for new sites and other situations as needed.
- Identify actual and potential human rights risks associated with conservation interventions and recommend practical mitigation and management measures.
- Contribute to the development and maintenance of systems for tracking human rights risks, corrective actions, lessons learned, and emerging trends across Africa programs.

**3. Human Rights and Conservation Law Enforcement**

- Work closely with the APAMU Law Enforcement Strategist and Senior Human Rights Specialist to provide strategic guidance on the integration of human rights principles into conservation law enforcement operations.
- Support law enforcement teams, site managers, and country programs to ensure that internationally recognized human rights standards are observed, and protocols are adequate for monitoring, and training.
- Support the development, review, and implementation of rights-respecting law enforcement policies, protocols, and operational guidance.

**4. Development of Rights-Respecting SOPs**

- Review Africa-level Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) that embed human rights principles into field operations as needed together with regional safeguards leads, based on WCS institutional policies.

**5. Training and capacity building**

- Design and deliver human rights trainings with a focus on practical application of human rights protection and human rights-based approaches in the context of field implementation, community conservation and conservation law enforcement (or equivalent)

**6. Other tasks as needed**

- Review protocols and process relating to mainstreaming of gender equity, respect for the rights of Indigenous Peoples, local communities, and underrepresented groups in program design and management.
- Contribute technical content for donor reports and organizational reporting related to human rights commitments and achievements.

**Qualification Requirements**

- Advanced degree in Law or other relevant field with a specialization in human rights; a first degree with relevant experience and certificates can be accepted in lieu of an advanced degree.
- Minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible professional experience in human rights advocacy, research, policy or monitoring and reporting.
- Proven experience working directly with Indigenous Peoples, local communities, civil society organizations, and/or government stakeholders in the context of Africa.
- Fluency in English and ability to work professionally in French.

**Desirable Qualifications**

- Experience in conservation programs or issues relating to conservation.
- Experience with grassroots advocacy or human rights defenders.
- Fluency in Portuguese or African languages relevant to program areas.

**Core Competencies and Skills**

**Technical Competencies**

- Strong knowledge of international human rights standards and frameworks, and regional African frameworks
- Knowledge of both civil law and common law based systems for law enforcement.
- Understanding of human rights-based approaches to conservation and development including institutional due diligence practices.
- Demonstrated experience conducting human rights assessments and risk assessments and to develop appropriate methodologies.
- Understanding of gender integration, Indigenous Peoples rights.
- Experience developing policies, guidance documents, and operational procedures.

**Professional Skills**

- Excellent analytical and critical thinking skills.
- Effective at organization, time-management, and self-directed field work.
- Outstanding written and verbal communication skills.
- Strong stakeholder engagement and interview skills.
- Ability to work effectively across cultures and multidisciplinary teams.
- Ability to influence and support change across diverse country programs.

​​​​​**How to apply**

Interested candidates who meet the above qualifications, skills, and experience should apply through the application tab by **October 30, 2026**. We review received applications on a rolling basis.

WCS is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all employment and labor laws and regulations that prohibit discrimination in hiring and ensure that candidates from all backgrounds are fairly and consistently considered during the recruitment process. We are dedicated to hiring and supporting a diverse workforce. We are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment and looking for future team members who share that same value. The organization provides equal employment opportunities for all qualified candidates. The organization does not discriminate against employment based on age, color, disability, gender identity, national origin, race, religion, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by laws and regulations.

jobs.title: Grants Manager - Arabic speaking
jobs.description:
The MENTOR Initiative (‘MENTOR’) is a humanitarian organisation specialising in disease control and improving access to healthcare in emergency settings across countries in Africa, the Middle East and South America. MENTOR is the leading organisation dedicated to the control of malaria and other vector-borne diseases in complex, vulnerable settings.

MENTOR delivers large scale disease control interventions working with communities affected by emergencies such as conflict and natural disasters and at higher risk of diseases. We also help build the technical and operational capacity of local and international partners to incorporate medium- and long-term disease control systems into their operations and country strategy.

**Overall job purpose**

The Grants Manager (GM) will support the implementation of MENTOR’s disease control programmes through managing grant, financial and administrative activities in the country of operation, in line with regulatory and HQ systems and donor requirements. The GM will also be responsible for developing country-level finance and admin systems to ensure full compliance with relevant frameworks.

**Requirements for the role**

- Background in grant/financial management is essential. Experience of working in humanitarian or conflict settings an advantage.
- Experience working in a Middle East context an advantage.
- Extensive experience managing grants and experience with donors.
- Familiarity with NGO working environments and standard procedures.
- Highly organised with good coordination / project management skills.
- Excellent communication skills.
- Ability to work in a multicultural environment and to demonstrate gender-sensitive and non-discriminatory behaviour and attitudes.
- **Fluent in Arabic.**

**Tasks and responsibilities**

**Grant/Finance management**
- Direct grant and finance technical management with field offices:
- Continuous contact with country Finance Coordinators, their team, and the Country Director.
- Design the grant and financial management strategy in country with the Country Directors.
- Grant and programme accounting/donor reporting (for assigned country):
- Review monthly field accounts, making checks on transfers between accounts, coding of transactions to budgets, use of advance accounts, adequate descriptions, bank and cash reconciliations, and payroll.
- Receive field supporting documentation monthly and check for completion.
- Liaise with field offices to resolve questions arising from above checks, advise on necessary adjustments.
- Consolidate monthly HQ expenditure with field expenditure.
- Prepare the field budget planning for each grant.
- Prepare monthly project reports for internal accounting systems.
- Prepare periodic project financial reports for donors.
- Provide feedback to Programme Managers on expenditure including variances and burn rates.
- Work with Programme Managers to ensure narrative reports are consistent with financial reports.
- Prepare closeout documentation for donors, where applicable.
- Provide project reports and supporting detail to project auditors as required.
- Financial management and reporting
- Invoice grant donors and suppliers.
- Maintain the fixed asset register on a quarterly basis.
- Ensure thorough follow up of internal in-country audits.
- Ensure internal controls are in place and all MENTOR procedures are being properly implemented.
- Create/oversee any additional financial controls.
- Maintain and regularly update the field finance and admin guidelines.
- Cash
- Request cash from donors according to agreed schedules.
- Receive and validate requests for cash advances from the field.
- Send cash advances to the field.
- Receive copies of field bank statements and review bank reconciliations provided by the field offices.

**Grant development**
- Work with Programme Managers to review new grant opportunities and donor requests for proposals.
- Work with Programme Managers and country teams to assist them and input into the design of new grants.
- Ensure with Programme Managers that new grant budgets are designed to cover all the related costs of new programmes, and that these costs are adequately demonstrated and described in the proposal package prior to submission.
- Assign accounts codes to project budgets lines ensuring that expenditure can be aligned to suitable headings for donor reporting requirements.
- Report on cash (input/output) flow for each grant to the regional team leader.

**Human resources management and responsibilities**
- Provide technical support, advice and training as necessary to field staff, ensuring that field roles are properly understood and completed, making field visits as necessary
- Systematic follow up of emails and phone calls to teams on a regular basis
- Ensure teams produce accurate timesheets each month for review and validation
- Ensure with the Programme Manager that allocated country programmes have the requisite team structure (international and national) to meet internal minimum standards, achieve programme goals and fulfil organisational commitments to donor partners.
- Ensure the development of TORs for country team members.
- Work with HQ Recruitment team to ensure the recruitment, effective briefing and pre-departure preparation of new international consultants going to allocated country programmes, and any short-term HQ visits.
- Ensure HR management systems are in place (in line with local labour laws, performance reviews, complaints systems, local payroll).

**Logistics, procurement and IT**
- Act as primary user of field accounting software allocating access levels for other country team staff.
- Ensure systems integrity through security procedures and secure back-up.
- Oversee basic logistics procedures in relation to procurement and stock. management in the field, coordinating as necessary with the logistics team and HQ procurement officer.
- With the Programme Manager oversee the field-based logistics coordinator (for asset management, field fleet and fuel management, and communications systems management).

**Legal, security and risk management**
- Review all project contracts to ensure that MENTOR’s financial commitments are met.
- Ensure compliance with all local legal requirements.
- Ensure all contracts are in line with the programme/budget and legal (vehicle rental, services contracts, HR contracts, MoUs).

**Other**
- Support internal audits of country programmes.
- Develop HQ and field assets register.
- Manage MENTOR’s vehicle contracts, including rental contracts and monthly invoices.
- Other supportive duties as agreed with the Programme Manager and management team.

The MENTOR Initiative is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity in the organisation. We ensure the constant non-discrimination throughout the recruitment process.

The MENTOR Initiative is committed to promoting diversity and gender equality and strongly encourages candidates from under-represented backgrounds to apply.

The MENTOR Initiative applies a zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation, abuse, mistreatment or harassment, and other types of unethical behaviour including fraud.

The MENTOR Initiative will contact previous employers of applicants to determine if they have any history of violating international standards and codes of conduct relating to such matters.

jobs.title: Evaluation finale du projet « Evaluation finale EMERGENCE 2026 pour le Cameroun »
jobs.description:
Appel d'offres lancé : 08 octobre 2026
Date limite de soumission des appels d'offres : 23 octobre 2026
Lieu : Cameroun, Extrême Nord »

Les candidats doivent demander le TOR et la demande d'offres par courriel électroniquement pour obtenir ces documents via ce courriel : appels\_offres@solidaritestca.org. Doit inclure « DA-YND-00815 /EVALUATION EMERGENCE CMR-SI » dans l'objet du courriel.

À PROPOS DE SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL

Solidarités International (SI) est une organisation humanitaire française fournissant une assistance vitale aux populations touchées par des conflits armés, des catastrophes naturelles et des épidémies depuis plus de 40 ans. Indépendante de son affiliation politique ou religieuse, SI est spécialisée dans l'eau, l'assainissement et l'hygiène (WASH) ; la sécurité alimentaire et des moyens de subsistance ; l'hébergement d'urgence ; et les réponses multisectorielles intégrées. SI opère dans plus de 23 pays, avec 2 400 employés œuvrant à rétablir l'accès aux services essentiels et à renforcer la résilience communautaire.

Aperçu du projet

Depuis le 1er décembre 2022 et pour une durée de 48 mois, SI en partenariat avec l'ONG Tammounde Esperanza, bénéficie d'un financement de l'Agence Française de Développement (AFD) d’un montant de 1 000 000 euros (36% du budget global) pour la mise en œuvre du projet intitulé « Soutenir la société civile pour l'émergence des femmes et des jeunes à l’Extrême Nord du Cameroun » dont le titre simplifié est « EMERGENCE ». A partir du 1er juin 2023 et pour une durée de 41 mois, le Délégation de l’Union Européenne apporte également son soutien au travers d’un cofinancement de ce projet à hauteur de 1 738 318 euros (soit 64% du budget total), les deux financements prenant fin le 30 novembre 2026.

L’objectif global est de contribuer au renforcement de la résilience économique et sociale des populations de la région de l'Extrême Nord du Cameroun. Le projet EMERGENCE cible 6 communes réparties dans 3 départements de la région de l’Extrême Nord : Hina, Koza, Mozogo et Roua dans le département du Mayo Tsanaga, Mora dans le département du Mayo Sava et la Makary dans le département du Logone-et-Chari.

Le projet EMERGENCE ambitionne d'améliorer la gouvernance, les capacités et l'autonomisation des différents acteurs locaux (groupements, société civile et services techniques déconcentrés) pour les renforcer dans leur rôle d'acteurs du développement économique local et de l'insertion socio-économique.

Le projet vise notamment à renforcer la capacité de la société civile et des acteurs locaux dans l'atteinte de l'autonomie financière et technique des groupements agricoles, AVEC, CGPE et FCE soutenus, ainsi qu’à renforcer leur participation aux instances locales de gouvernance des ressources naturelles, notamment de l'eau. Les résultats attendus à la fin du projet sont les suivants :
Résultat 1 : L'ONG locale Tammounde est en capacité d'initier, d'appuyer et de renforcer des
groupements locaux ruraux dans l'atteinte de leur autonomie financière et technique.
Résultat 2 : Les groupements de producteurs, de jeunes et de femmes et les AVEC soutenus
par le projet sont en mesure de développer durablement leurs activités.
Résultat 3 : La participation des organisations locales, d'usagers et de producteurs, aux
instances locales de gouvernance des ressources naturelles, notamment de l'eau, est
renforcée.

LIVRABLES ET DÉLAIS DE L’EVALUATION

Période de l’évaluation

L’évaluation s'étendra sur une période de deux mois maximums, toutefois, le calendrier
définitif et la durée de la consultance seront discutés et convenus avec le consultant lors de
la signature du contrat. L’évaluation devrait débuter début novembre et prendre fin au plus
tard le 31 décembre 2026.

Production attendue

Plusieurs livrables correspondant aux exigences décrites au point 7 (LIVRABLES) ainsi qu’aux
formats exigés.
Rapport de lancement et outils proposée pour l'évaluation
Réunion et présentation des résultats clés
Rapport final détaillé (version provisoire)

PROFIL REQUIS
Dans le cadre de cette consultance externe, le Consultant devra justifier d’une :

Formation et qualification :
• Diplôme en agronomie ou génie rural, études de développement rural, en suivi
évaluation et gestion des projets et/ou dans une discipline pertinente.
Expérience professionnelle générale :
• Au moins 5 à 7 ans d'expérience dans la conduite d'évaluations de programmes SAME,
développement des OSC et gestion des ressources naturelles ;
• Avoir réalisé au moins 1 mission similaire dans le cadre de projets financés par un
bailleur européen.

jobs.title: Community Manager Uganda - Journalist Protection Program
jobs.description:
MiCT is calling for proposals for a freelance Community manager in the framework of its program “MiCT Fellowship for Critical Voices 2026-2027”, funded by the German Federal Foreign Office. This is a freelance position running from November 2026 - June 2027 to be based in Kampala, Uganda. The total number of working days will run up to 120, the exact number will depend on project implementation. MiCT invites interested and qualified persons to submit proposals by 22.10.2026.

**About MiCT**

Media in Cooperation and Transition (MiCT) is a non-profit organisation delivering expert media services in complex and challenging contexts with passion, precision, and agility.

Through collaborative work with partners, MiCT fosters transparent, inclusive, and fair dialogue supporting resilient societies. Operating across three continents and 15 countries, MiCT facilitates journalist training, media content production, research, monitoring, and supports the financial sustainability of media partners.

**About the Project:**

Since 2022, the MiCT Fellowship for Critical Voices has supported at-risk journalists and media professionals from conflict regions, enabling them to continue their essential work in safety. The programme is part of the Hannah Arendt Initiative and a member of the Journalists in Distress Network. It offers stipends, security and equipment support, (mental) health services, legal aid, relocation, and professional development through regional hubs.

**3. Description of the role**

The chosen person will undertake the following responsibilities to fulfill community management related tasks for up to 20 Fellows based in Uganda:

- Coordinate contractual engagements with the fellows
- Manage stipend transfers
- Support alumni legal and safety needs where required
- Provide logistical and technical relocation support on a needs basis
- Creation and management of safety measures for up to 20 Journalists and/or Media Makers
- Organise relocations, secure accommodations, and co-working spaces
- Organise procurement and contracting of support offers (training, expert consultations, workshops, insurance, language classes etc) in the following areas.
- Organise at least 1 community meet-up, including alumni Fellows
- Conduct regular check-ins with MiCT's Project Manager and Project Officer

**4. Application Requirements**

Interested persons should demonstrate the following:

- Proven experience in project management, particularly in media development projects.
- Established connections within the regional media landscape and community.
- Strong community management skills.
- Large network of service providers, particularly to provide integration and legal support.
- Understanding of the media landscape throughout Uganda.
- Understanding of the immigration landscape in Uganda preferred.
- Ideally based in Uganda.

jobs.title: Programme Manager - Arabic speaking
jobs.description:
The MENTOR Initiative (‘MENTOR’) is a humanitarian organisation specialising in disease control and improving access to healthcare in emergency settings currently across countries in Africa, the Middle East and South America. MENTOR is the leading organisation dedicated to the control of malaria and other vector-borne diseases in complex, vulnerable settings.

MENTOR delivers large scale disease control interventions working with communities affected by emergencies such as conflict and natural disasters and at higher risk of diseases. We also help build the technical and operational capacity of local and international partners to incorporate medium- and long-term disease control systems into their operations and country strategy.

**Requirements for the role**

- Background in public health or a related field. Post graduate qualification in public health, epidemiology or control of infectious diseases highly desirable. Experience of working in conflict and humanitarian settings is preferable.
- Experience working in the Middle East is essential.
- Extensive experience managing health/humanitarian programmes and experience with donors.
- Familiarity with NGO working environments and standard procedures.
- Highly organised with good coordination / project management skills.
- Excellent communication skills.
- Ability to work in a multicultural environment and to demonstrate gender-sensitive and non-discriminatory behaviour and attitudes.
- Fluent in Arabic.

**Overall job purpose**

The Programme Manager (PM) will support MENTOR with the overall implementation of programmes focused on delivering disease control activities in countries where we operate. The PM will be responsible for managing MENTOR programmes in specific countries ensuring on time and quality implementation of activities.

**Task and responsibilities**

**Team coordination**

- The PM will be responsible for the non-financial and non-administrative coordination areas of in country programmes including the management of Country Directors (CDs) or the officers in charge.
- Systematic follow up calls to programme teams on a regular basis to ensure adequate coordination and communication at all levels.
- Ensure all employees produce accurate timesheets each month for review and validation.
- Ensure that allocated country programmes have the requisite technical team structure (international and national) to meet internal minimum standards, achieve programme goals and fulfil organisational commitments to donor partners.
- Ensure the development of TORs for country programme technical team members.
- Work with HQ team to ensure the effective programme briefing and pre-departure preparation of new international employees going to allocated country programmes, and any short-term HQ visits.
- Follow up with CDs to ensure implementation of periodic standardised performance evaluations of programme technical employees and national team members where these have been scheduled for this period.

**Programme operations**

- The PM will support, lead discussions between in country and HQ teams and give direction to allocated country programme teams, to ensure that all programmes operate using the organisation’s existing standardised technical systems and acceptable practice.
- Guarantee programme technical establishment/set up or expansion identifying opportunities and risks and discussing them with HQ prior to decisions.
- Ensure security and safeguarding procedures and practice (adapted for local context and regularly updated and reviewed) and duly followed up in country and are regularly monitored.

**Technical support**

- The PM will support allocated country programme teams, drawing support and advice for specialist areas where needed from UK HQ, with technical advice and guidance to reinforce the quality of programme activities.
- Provide technical guidance for vector-borne disease case management delivery when applicable (diagnosis and treatment) in line with international guidelines and MENTOR experience and practice.
- Advise on, and review all job aids, training manuals and related case management tools.
- Advise on vector-borne disease case management delivery capacity building of local and international partners when needed.
- Provide technical guidance on best practice for the design and delivery of programmes across several areas mainly integrated vector management, NTDs, WASH and healthcare provision.
- Support quality improvement of activity implementation and overall programmatic management in the country supported promoting sharing of lessons learned and continuous improvement of guidelines and tools to guide technically sounds activities.
- Ensure standardisation of M&E protocols for both health and WASH related activities, guaranteeing standardisation of medically related data collection across programmes.
- Review and advise on operational research, embedded into MENTOR programmatic action and support in the design, implementation and analysis phase of potential operational research studies.

**Grant management and programme reporting**

- Ensure that all country teams provide bi-weekly technical programme reporting on a timely basis, other than in new emergency programmes.
- Ensure country teams have read all applicable grant agreements and are aware of technical narrative reporting requirements and timelines.
- Ensure that country management teams submit all requisite quarterly, annual and any other requested narrative programme progress reports in line with donor and internal requirements (normally two weeks prior to donor submission deadlines).
- Coordinate the review, technical editing and formatting of programme reports.
- Ensure the timely submission of UK HQ checked and approved (narrative) reports to donor partners in line with their specifications and schedule deadlines.

**Strategic development**

- The PM will work with the CEO, Senior Management Team (SMT) and country managers to regularly review the relevance and impact of the organisation’s ongoing operations.
- Will work with the CEO and SMT to monitor high risk VBD country situations for natural disasters, conflict, population displacement, and epidemic risk factors.
- Will research potential developing crises situations (above) where MENTOR support may be required and will develop short briefing papers to outline needs and potential responses, for the CEO, SMT and other team members to consider.
- Will investigate and identify potential donor interest and funding options for potential new MENTOR programmes (emergency responses and longer term) to help guide and inform the organisation’s decision making for new assessment missions.
- Will conduct assessment missions (normally accompanied by one other) to investigate priority settings agreed by the organisation.
- Will help to lead the development of disease control response planning, and where relevant ensure operational research issues are also considered, based on assessment and research results.
- Will assist the CEO, SMT and other team members (as needed) to develop and present concept papers, proposals and background papers to donors and country partners, to develop new funding streams for the new organisational responses proposed.
- Will work with the CEO, SMT and other team members to help lead the set-up of new programmes.

**Other**

- The PM will work with the CEO, SMT and country teams to support new technical proposal development.
- Assist in representing MENTOR at international meetings and conferences, as and when requested by the CEO.
- Assist UK HQ to provide VBD and NTD control technical advice and support to other team members who are coordinating existing programmes.
- Other supportive duties as agreed with the CEO and Management Team.

The MENTOR Initiative is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity in the organisation. We ensure the constant non-discrimination throughout the recruitment process.

The MENTOR Initiative is committed to promoting diversity and gender equality and strongly encourages candidates from under-represented backgrounds to apply.

The MENTOR Initiative applies a zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation, abuse, mistreatment or harassment, and other types of unethical behaviour including fraud.

The MENTOR Initiative will contact previous employers of applicants to determine if they have any history of violating international standards and codes of conduct relating to such matters.

jobs.title: Project Director, Chad
jobs.description:
**Role:** Full Time

**Contract Duration**: 2 Years

**Deadline for submission:** 30th October 2026

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

**About Us**

Founded in 1992, Nutrition International is a global organization dedicated to delivering proven nutrition interventions to those who need them most. Working in partnership with countries, donors and implementers, our experts conduct cutting-edge nutrition research, support critical policy formulation, and integrate nutrition into broader development programs. In more than 60 countries, primarily in Asia and Africa, Nutrition International nourishes people to nourish life.

For more than 30 years now, Nutrition International has focused on delivering low-cost, high-impact, nutrition interventions to people in need, driven by our mission to achieve a world where everyone, everywhere, is free from malnutrition and able to reach their full potential. Nutrition International’s work is guided by a dedicated and talented team of experts working globally, regionally and within countries to end malnutrition worldwide.

**About the role**

Nutrition International is supporting the Ministry of Health in Chad to implement Child Survival programming including to maintain coverage and ensure that all eligible children receive two doses of vitamin A supplementation (VAS) every six months and to preposition zinc & low-osmolarity oral rehydration salts (LO-ORS) to treat childhood diarrhea in line with WHO -recommended treatment protocols.

To ensure the supported rounds are successful, and program data is available for decision-making, Nutrition International will conduct regular post-event coverage survey (PECS) after campaigns. Doing so will ensure review data is available quickly post-event to allow course corrections in time for the next round of the vitamin A supplementation implementation. The program will also produce data and guidance that is needed to curb child deaths and maximize every dollar invested.

Nutrition International will scale up its technical assistance and advisory services to reinforce government capability and programming. Nutrition International will ensure campaigns are designed and delivered effectively and with attention paid to gender equity. This includes the application of best practices and the adaptation of global guidance to the country’s context.

The Project Director is the lead focal person for Nutrition International’s programming in Chad. The job holder will be responsible for external relationships and accountable for program delivery in Chad, in line with NI’s vision, mission and values and the VAS program design. The Job holder will also provide high-level representation of Nutrition International and oversee support to the Government at national and sub-national levels.

The Project Director will provide overall leadership of the Nutrition International Country Team and Child Survival programming in Chad, will lead the management of relations with the Government of Chad and with other key local stakeholders and oversee the work of a country team in developing, managing, monitoring and reporting on Nutrition International Child Survival programming in Chad. The Project Director will be accountable for programmatic and financial delivery and reporting against Nutrition International requirements and will also manage Nutrition International’s country operations including ongoing compliance with legal and financial regulations in the country.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**1. External Relations and Representation**

- Lead Nutrition International’s representation in Chad, building strong relationships with national and sub-national government, donors, UN agencies, NGOs, the private sector, academia and communities.
- Position Nutrition International as a key actor in nutrition and public health, including through national task forces, alliances and conferences.
- Engage in advocacy, directly and with partners, to influence government policy and partner investment in nutrition.
- Harmonise Nutrition International’s work with other partners and actively support government leadership and ownership.
- Identify opportunities to leverage and mobilise additional resources to expand Nutrition International’s work in Chad.

**2. Programme Management and Delivery**

- Be accountable for achieving agreed results, programme quality and disbursement targets within agreed timelines.
- Manage the performance of partners and sub-contractors against agreements, negotiating corrective action where needed and assessing value for money.
- Monitor progress against workplans and performance frameworks, account for variances and prepare reports for donors and stakeholders.
- Convene and participate in programme review and steering meetings with government and partners and negotiate adjustments to plans and budgets.
- Ensure vitamin A programming mainstreams gender equality in line with Nutrition International’s global strategy, including Sex and Gender Based Analysis.

**3. Financial Management**

- Working with the administrative support partner, ensure country resources are managed in line with Nutrition International policies and within approved budgets.
- Guide the team in costing, budgeting, expenditure forecasting, variance analysis and value-for-money reporting for donor purposes.

**4. Team Leadership and Country Operations**

- Lead and develop the country team of three Senior Programme Officers and a Project Officer.
- Manage country operations, including ongoing compliance with legal and financial regulations in Chad.
- Keep Nutrition International staff informed of progress and ensure contributions are recognised.

**5. Focal Point for Nutrition International Child Survival programming in Chad**

- Be the primary focal point and lead for Nutrition International Child Survival programming in the country.
- Build strong relationships with and engage regularly with senior government officials to ensure programming gaps. and needs are clearly articulated and coordinated with other partner support.
- Ensure visibility of Nutrition International’s support to national and sub-national authorities.

## **Requirements**

**Education/Professional Designations/Experience:**

- Master’s degree from a recognized university in management, international development, public health, nutrition or related area;

\- Additional post graduate certification in project or general management is desirable.

\- Certificate in research and/or monitoring and evaluation an added advantage.

- At least 10 years of experience in the management of programs in public health, nutrition, international development or a related field;
- Significant experience managing complex budgets and diverse teams in progressively more senior leadership roles;
- At least 5 years’ experience in networking at a high level with international partners and country government, desirable;
- At least 5 years’ experience of working in Chad; regional and/or global experience highly desirable;
- Previous experience as a Country Manager or Director or equivalent role in scope and responsibility for an international organization/NGO highly desirable.

**Languages Skills**

- Fluent in English and French required.
- Fluency in local Chad languages would be an asset.

## **Benefits**

Competitive market pay, comprehensive medical benefits, flexible working hours, generous annual leave, support for professional learning and development, and dedicated health and wellness allowance.

Nutrition International is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to fostering an inclusive, equitable, and accessible work environment. Applicants with special needs who require adjustments or support are encouraged to reach out during the recruitment process.

**Our Commitment to Safeguarding**

Nutrition International has zero tolerance for sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEAH), or any other form of safeguarding misconduct. We incorporate safeguarding-related questions throughout the recruitment process, including during interviews and reference checks, to ensure a safe and respectful working environment. In accordance with the Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, reference checks will include safeguarding verifications with previous employers.

**Candidate Consent**

By applying for this position, you consent to professional reference checks and appropriate background screening as part of the selection process. Any offer of employment is conditional on satisfactory completion of these checks.

jobs.title: Venezuela: Asistente de Protección y Referencias (San Fernando de Apure)
jobs.description:
La Cruz Roja Venezolana (CRV) es una organización humanitaria cuyo mandato es salvar vidas y mejorar las condiciones de las personas en situación de vulnerabilidad. Como parte del Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y la Media Luna Roja, brinda asistencia oportuna en emergencias, desastres y contextos de necesidad humanitaria.

Guiada por sus Principios Fundamentales—Humanidad, Imparcialidad, Neutralidad, Independencia, Voluntariado, Unidad y Universalidad—la CRV actúa como auxiliar de los poderes públicos en el ámbito humanitario, trabajando para reducir el sufrimiento humano sin distinción de raza, género, religión o ideología. Su labor abarca la atención médica de emergencia, el fortalecimiento de la resiliencia comunitaria, la capacitación en primeros auxilios, la respuesta a desastres y la promoción de la salud y el bienestar.

A través de una red de voluntarios altamente comprometidos, la CRV moviliza recursos de manera eficiente y eficaz para estar presente donde más se necesita, cuando más se necesita. Su labor se fundamenta en la solidaridad, el respeto a la dignidad humana y el compromiso con la protección de la vida en todas sus formas.

**Compromiso con la Salvaguarda**

La Cruz Roja Venezolana está comprometida con la creación y mantenimiento de entornos seguros y respetuosos para las comunidades, el personal y el voluntariado y con la prevención de la explotación, el abuso y el acoso sexual.

Las personas seleccionadas deberán cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas y estándares de Salvaguarda aplicables. Como parte de su proceso de contratación segura, la CRV podrá realizar verificaciones de referencias profesionales y solicitar información pertinente sobre antecedentes de conducta profesional y Salvaguarda, de acuerdo con sus procedimientos y la normativa aplicable.

**Responsabilidad general de Salvaguarda**

La persona titular del puesto deberá promover y respetar los estándares de Salvaguarda de la Cruz Roja Venezolana, cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas aplicables, mantener límites profesionales apropiados, contribuir a prevenir daños y reportar de forma inmediata cualquier preocupación de Salvaguarda a través de los mecanismos establecidos.

**Adición para puestos de riesgo elevado**

Debido a la naturaleza de sus funciones, la persona deberá identificar y mitigar activamente riesgos de Salvaguarda asociados a sus actividades, mantener estándares reforzados de conducta y límites profesionales y asegurar que su interacción con comunidades y personas en situación de vulnerabilidad se desarrolle de forma segura, digna, inclusiva y respetuosa.

Si deseas formar parte del equipo y hacer la diferencia, te invitamos a sumarte.

*¿Cómo puedes hacer la diferencia? Funciones claves / Responsabilidades*

El/La Asistente de protección y referencias tendrá como responsabilidad principal brindar apoyo en los trabajos a realizar por el Coordinador (a) local y Oficial de Protección.

Será el/la encargado(a) de:

- Realizar seguimiento de las referencias médicas realizadas por el equipo médico de la filial.
- Sensibilizar sobre el alcance de la acción humanitaria de la Cruz Roja Venezolana en materia de movilidad humana.
- Posicionar el rol auxiliar de la Cruz Roja Venezolana como un actor clave de nivel local en temas de movilidad humana.
- Reforzar la articulación con los actores gubernamentales locales sobre la importancia de proteger y promover los derechos de las personas en movilidad humana.
- Acompañar las iniciativas locales orientadas a la asistencia, protección e integración a las personas en movilidad humana.
- Influir en narrativas y actitudes públicas sobre la movilidad humana fundamentadas en las evidencias y los principios del Movimiento.
- Ser portavoz para fines de coordinación e incidencia en espacios estratégicos previamente autorizados.
- Supervisar las actividades desarrolladas en los puntos de atención para reunificación familiar bajo los lineamientos del área de protección.
- Crear una estrategia de incidencia a nivel local.
- Elaborar los informes de seguimiento, técnicos periódicos y finales y reportar al Coordinador local.

*Reporte*

El/La Asistente de protección y referencias le reportará al/la Coordinador local, al Oficial de Protección y a la Coordinación Nacional de Proyecto.

*Lugar de trabajo*

San Fernando de Apure, Estado Apure.

*Para calificar como un constructor del sistema humanitario venezolano deberás cumplir con los siguientes requisitos:*

- Título en Sociología, Educación, Trabajo Social, Enfermería, Promoción de Salud, Comunicación Social, Salud Pública.
- Al menos 1 año de experiencia como Referente de salud, promotor o profesional de incidencia. Experiencia mínima de un (1) año.
- Al menos 1 año trabajando con equipos de salud, incluyendo médicos, enfermeros, en la implementación de actividades médicas y comunitarias a nivel de salud y protección.
- Experiencia trabajando con el Movimiento de la Cruz Roja / Media Luna Roja es deseable.
- Excelentes habilidades de comunicación, capacidad para construir relaciones a todos los niveles.
- Capacidad para trabajar de forma independiente y como miembro de un equipo.
- Capacidad y acuerdo para adherirse a los Principios Fundamentales de la Cruz Roja y la Media Luna Roja.
- Capacidad de mantener la confidencialidad.
- Gran sentido de la responsabilidad y ética profesional.
- Indispensable: Residir en la ciudad de San Fernando de Apure.

La persona titular del puesto deberá promover y respetar los estándares de Salvaguarda de la Cruz Roja Venezolana, cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas aplicables, mantener límites profesionales apropiados, contribuir a prevenir daños y reportar de forma inmediata cualquier preocupación de Salvaguarda a través de los mecanismos establecidos.

**Adición para puestos de riesgo elevado**

Debido a la naturaleza de sus funciones, la persona deberá identificar y mitigar activamente riesgos de Salvaguarda asociados a sus actividades, mantener estándares reforzados de conducta y límites profesionales y asegurar que su interacción con comunidades y personas en situación de vulnerabilidad se desarrolle de forma segura, digna, inclusiva y respetuosa.

Si deseas formar parte del equipo y hacer la diferencia, te invitamos a sumarte.

***¿Cómo puedes hacer la diferencia? Funciones claves / Responsabilidades***

El/La Oficial de Salud Mental y Apoyo Psicosocial (SMAPS) es responsable de la implementación técnica y operativa de las intervenciones en salud mental y apoyo psicosocial de la Cruz Roja Venezolana, asegurando una atención segura, culturalmente apropiada, basada en evidencia y conforme a los estándares internacionales del Movimiento de la Cruz Roja y la Media Luna Roja.

Si deseas formar parte del equipo y hacer la diferencia, te invitamos a sumarte.

*¿Cómo puedes hacer la diferencia? Funciones claves / Responsabilidades*

El Auxiliar de Tesorería tiene como propósito principal proporcionar un apoyo operativo y documental esencial a la gestión de Tesorería y Finanzas de la Cruz Roja Venezolana. Este rol es fundamental para asegurar la eficiencia y transparencia en la emisión oportuna de pagos a proveedores, personal y beneficiarios, así como garantizar la correcta organización, registro y archivo de toda la documentación financiera y soporte de las transacciones. Su labor contribuye directamente a mantener la integridad y el cumplimiento de los procedimientos financieros de la institución.

*Reporte*
El/La Auxiliar de Tesorería le reportará a la Dirección de Finanzas.

*Lugar de trabajo*
Caracas (CRV Sede Central).

Funciones:

- Procesamiento, carga y validación de Órdenes de Pago: Recibir, revisar y procesar las solicitudes de pago verificando que cuenten con las debidas aprobaciones y soportes documentales, de acuerdo con las políticas de la Cruz Roja.
- Controlar, junto con las partes involucradas, de la completa documentación de cada pago emitido en la CRV.
- Emisión y Ejecución: Asistir en la preparación de pagos y archivos para bancos, donantes y socios financieros.
- Control Bancario: Realizar el seguimiento de las operaciones bancarias (depósitos, retiros y transferencias) y colaborar en la conciliación bancaria diaria y semanal, identificando y notificando cualquier discrepancia.
- Colaborar en los procedimientos de cierre de proyectos y reportes financieros de la CRV.
- Apoyar en los procesos de revisión y auditorias documentales de la CRV.
- Realizar otras tareas relacionadas con el tipo de puesto y las asignadas por sus superiores inmediatos, en función de las características y condiciones especiales del puesto, para brindar un servicio de calidad.

Responsabilidades:

1. Trabajar activamente hacia el logro de los objetivos de la Dirección Financiera de la Cruz Roja Venezolana.
2. Cumplir y trabajar de acuerdo con los principios de la Cruz Roja y la Media Luna Roja.
3. Realice cualquier otro trabajo y responsabilidades relacionadas con el soporte financiero a la Sociedad Nacional.
4. Excelentes habilidades de comunicación, capacidad para construir relaciones a todos los niveles.
5. Capacidad para trabajar de forma independiente y como miembro de un equipo.
6. Capacidad y acuerdo para adherirse a los Principios Fundamentales de la Cruz Roja y la Media Luna Roja.
7. Capacidad de mantener la confidencialidad.
8. Gran sentido de la responsabilidad y ética profesional.

jobs.title: Consultancy: Situation Analysis for the SHINE Rehabilitation Project – Kenya
jobs.description:
**CBM Christoffel-Blindenmission Christian Blind Mission e.V. (CBM) is looking for an experienced professional to conduct a Situation Analysis for a project in Kisumu, Makueni, Nyeri, Homabay, Laikipia, Kiambu and Nakuru Counties, Kenya. This assignment will be based on consultancy work for approximately 30 days in November 2026.**

**About the Project:**

SHINE Project ((Strengthening capacities for Holistic and Inclusive Need-based rehabilitative services that Empower individuals and communities in Kenya) aims to contribute to a sustainable rehabilitative healthcare and inclusive social system that enables persons with functional limitations and participation restrictions to attain the highest quality of life in Kisumu, Homa Bay, Makueni, Kiambu, Nakuru Nyeri and Laikipia Counties, Kenya. It seeks to improve delivery of quality rehabilitative services and access to assistive technology through strengthening capacity of health care system across primary (including community based rehabilitative structures and referral pathways) and secondary levels in target Counties by 2030.

The aim of the requested consultancy is to conduct comprehensive situation analysis of the proposed project of CBM in partnership with Nyabondo Centre for Persons with Disabilities, Naromoru Disabled Children's Home, and AIC CURE Children’s Hospital of Kenya toanalyze and generate robust evidence on the rehabilitation services status, capacity, accessibility, utilization, quality, and financing, as well as the unmet needs of persons with disabilities and other populations requiring rehabilitation support. It will also generate evidence on how persons with disabilities and their families currently organize support, care, and mutual aid in daily life, and how these community practices interact with, and shape uptake of, the formal rehabilitation system. The findings show county-specific gaps, priorities, opportunities and practical entry points for strengthening services

For more information, please refer to the Terms of Reference [here](http://www.cbm.org/shine-cure-nyabondo-naromoru).

jobs.title: Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Specialist
jobs.location: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.description:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**Summary:**

JOB SUMMARY
Habitat for Humanity International seeks a Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEAL) Specialist to support and advance the Terwilliger Center for Innovation in Shelter's work with small and growing businesses. The purpose of the Terwilliger Center is and always has been to influence market actors – i.e., private companies, public officials, civil society, consumers, and households – to change attitudes, behaviors, policies, business models, and products and services in ways that lead to scalable affordable housing solutions. This is the essence of the Terwilliger Center's contribution to the HFHI mission of ensuring that everyone has a decent place to live.

The Terwilliger Center supports enterprises expanding innovative and client-responsive services, products and financing so that low-income households can improve their housing more effectively and efficiently. The Terwilliger Center operates in a dynamic environment where projects are often executed using a matrix structure, leveraging cross-functional teams within the center and, at times, across the wider Habitat network to achieve success.

The MEAL Specialist will play a key role in supporting the implementation, learning, and continuous improvement of the Small and Growing Businesses (SGB) Framework, the Terwilliger Center's global approach to identifying, supporting, and learning from enterprises with solutions for affordable housing via direct support and capital mobilization. This position strengthens the systems, evidence, and coordination needed to align global strategy with regional implementation. The role will also contribute to MEAL and learning efforts connected to the Shelter Venture Fund (SVF), the Center's mechanism for deploying investment into housing SGBs, ensuring coherence between the SGB framework and investment-related evidence. The MEAL Specialist will help advance learning, insights, and network engagement that elevate the Center's ability to support SGBs, influence entrepreneurial ecosystems, and inform future program design. Specifically this role designs and implements MEAL systems for impact investment portfolios and SGB programs, ensuring evidence-based decision-making and will contribute to global learning agendas, donor reporting, and impact measurement frameworks aligned with GIIN/IRIS+ standards.

**Key Responsibilities:**

ESSENTIAL DUTIES 1) Design and implement the MEARL framework for the SGB framework.
Develop results chains/frameworks for SGB framework and Shelter Venture Fund investments.
Ensure alignment with global impact measurement standards (IRIS+, SDG indicators).
Supports SGB team in target setting for annual and multi-year projections and puts a rigorous but realistic plan in place to track and monitor against these targets.

2)Ensure Data Quality and Insight Generation to support the SGB framework and strengthen evidence of uptake.

Working with global MEARL, geographic MEARL and SGB leads, lead rigorous data collection, validation, and analysis using mixed methods. Lead stakeholder reporting requirements and ensure integrity of reporting. Produce dashboards and learning briefs for internal strategy and external stakeholders.

3)Learning and Knowledge Management.

Facilitate learning loops across regions; synthesize cross-portfolio insights. Translate evidence into actionable recommendations for the SGB framework, including investment insights and program design. Promote adaptive management. Use evidence and real-time insights to inform strategic pivots and improve program effectiveness.

4\) Capacity Building and Systems Strengthening.
Develop and maintain digital data systems (such as CRM, Airtable, PowerBI) for real-time monitoring and data visualization.
Keep up to date on industry trends and build insights into continuous improvement of MEAL systems.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

Master’s in Monitoring & Evaluation, Development Economics, Statistics, Impact Measurement, or related field.

PREFERRED REQUIREMENTS

Minimum 5 years in MEAL roles, including impact investing or enterprise development contexts.

Proven ability to design and implement MEAL systems.

**Hiring Range:**

The actual salary offered for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including location, internal equity and the candidate’s qualifications and professional experience. HFHI offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package that varies by country and typically includes vacation leave, sick leave, personal days, health insurance options, retirement plan contributions and life insurance.

For work locations in Slovakia, the minimum monthly gross pay starts at:

€3,060.00 EUR

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.
