jobs.title: Emergency Human Resources Coordinator
jobs.description:
To fulfill its mission of assistance to victims of conflicts, epidemics or natural disasters, OCG has created an Emergency Pool, whose members are experienced individuals capable of evaluating a humanitarian crisis, opening, closing and coordinating emergency projects.

The Emergency Human Resources Coordinator is a key member of this pool and reports directly to the Emergency Coordinator, as well as to the E-Cell HR Referent.

The successful candidate is expected to:

- Deploy rapidly in all contexts set by the Emergency cell
- Have the flexibility to assume different HR roles according to operational needs (HR Coordinator but also HR/Administration Manager)
- Gap fill in regular cells if required.

As a member of the Emergency Pool, the Emergency HR Coordinator must be available for deployment within 48 hours for short-term emergency interventions. You will be part of a multidisciplinary response team -including medical, paramedical, and support staff - mobilized for emergencies such as epidemics, armed conflicts, natural disasters, and other acute crises. You may also be involved in exploratory missions, short-term assignments within regular missions or gap filling in the Emergency Cell in Geneva HQ.

Job Description (but not limited to)

- Act as a strategic partner to Operations by contributing to mission planning and execution. Support the design of appropriate emergency organizational structures and ensure adequate HR capacity and sizing.
- Define, adapt, and oversee the implementation of human resources policies for emergency interventions, ensuring alignment with the operational context and challenges.
- Ensure MSF operates as a responsible employer within the mission. Oversee all HR management, administrative, and legal matters, proactively addressing HR-related risks and adapting processes to the emergency context.
- Is the technical referent for all HR and Administration related issues at Mission level (recruitment, management and development of teams, contracting and remuneration of national staff, follow up of daily workers, etc.). Coordinates the urgent recruitment of HR required for the mission. Ensures the timely deployment of critical staff in coordination with the E-Cell HR Referent.

- Monitor working conditions and staff wellbeing, with a focus on high-stress environments. In collaboration with the medical department, coordinate psychosocial support as needed.
- Design, recruit and train the HR teams at coordination and project level.
- Contribute to emergency preparedness and surge capacity planning by assessing HR risks and implementing appropriate mitigation strategies.
- Participate in exploratory missions and evaluations, upon request of the Ecell.

Your Profile

Required Skills and experience

**Field Experience**

- Minimum of 2 years in HR management in the field with MSF, gained through exposure to various contexts, including emergency contexts (population displacement, epidemic outbreaks, natural disasters and/or conflicts).
- At least one field experience with MSF in HR coordination (HR Coordinator or Deputy HR Coordinator).
- Ability to quickly evaluate an emergency on the ground and propose an adapted HR strategy.
- Experience in Finance management is an advantage.

**Strategic and Interpersonal Skills**

- Ability to work effectively in volatile and insecure environments, with strong resilience and stress management skills.
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills
- Strong people management skills.
- Strong coordination and organizational skills.
- Strong adaptability and flexibility to navigate changing priorities, dynamic operational environments, and evolving team dynamics.
- Responsible behavior that contributes to the safety and integrity of everyone - prevent, report, and refuse any abusive behavior and/or behavior that goes against MSF's values.
- Ability to thrive in a multicultural environment and demonstrate commitment and support for diversity, inclusive and non-discriminatory attitudes and behaviors.

**Language skills**

- Fluency in both French and English is highly desirable. Alternatively, candidates must demonstrate an excellent command of either language and at least B1 proficiency in the other.
- Knowledge of other mission languages is an advantage (Spanish, Portuguese, Arabic).
- Proficiency in an additional language, especially Spanish, Arabic, and/or Portuguese.

Terms of Employment

- Field-based contract. One year fixed-term contract, renewable based on operational needs and performance.
- Duration of field assignments: 4 weeks to 3 months (flexibility required according to needs).
- Accommodation and travel arrangements such as visa-related costs will be taken in charge by MSF.
- Comprehensive support and guidance will be provided by dedicated technical referents throughout the assignment.

**We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.**

**MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment.**

jobs.title: Emergency Pharmacy Coordinator
jobs.description:
To fulfill its mission of assistance to victims of conflicts, epidemics or natural disasters, MSF-Switzerland has created an emergency team, of which members are experienced individuals capable of evaluating a situation, start and coordinate the missions. The position of Emergency Pharmacy Coordinator reports to the Emergency Medical Coordinator at field level and/or to the coordination team in the capital and finally to the Emergency Desk (RMP) at headquarters level in Geneva.

The candidate is expected to 1) work in all contexts set by the emergency desk and 2) work in emergency contexts with regular cells and fill gaps in regular projects if need be.

**Duty Station**

All countries where the emergency desk opens activities, which requires an urgent response. On call, the Emergency Pharmacy Coordinator should be available within 48 hours for rapid and short interventions. He/she is part of a core group of operations, medicals, para-medicals, logisticians/supply, fin/HR responsible for responding, amongst others, to:

- Exploratory missions
- Epidemic outbreaks
- Nutritional crises
- Displaced populations and/or refugees’ camps
- Surgical emergencies
- Natural disasters

**Responsibilities**

As the emergency medical supplies representative at mission level, their priority is to ensure the continuous improvement of the medical supplies management in emergency contexts and guarantee answers, strategies and interdepartmental tools adapted to the evolution of the needs and the policies of intervention defined by the department of the operations.

The other responsibilities of the Emergency Pharmacy Coordinator include:

- During preparation phase: Surveillance system through local contact (MoH, Central Medical Store, Pharmacy Directory,) Emergency Preparedness strategy and emergency response (including stock) in place (with and without MSF presence)
- During detection phase: Emergency coordination with MSF and external actors (crisis committee)
- During response phase: Exploratory mission: preparation for rapid assessments / Intervention according to the priorities defined and the strategy.
- During evaluation phase: Evaluation of the intervention (strategy, justification, resources, results vs needs) / Modification of the Emergency Preparedness strategy if needed / Hand over to MSF or MoH or others.

**Nature and activities**

**Emergency Preparedness Strategy**

- Participate to the design of new emergency supply standards (processes, procedures, tools, etc…) according to validated strategy and support related implementations with the Emergency Supply Referent
- Participate to the definition of autonomous and decentralized e-stock content based on the market control (validation sources by Headquarter Pharmacist for medical local purchase if needed)
- Define the resources (medical needs) to respond to natural disasters and other emergency context on demand according to defined strategy.
- Define, implement and monitor internal medical supplies management in emergency contexts at all levels (field, capital, headquarters)
- Define the means, the roles, and the responsibilities in terms of pharmacy management in emergency context in interaction with the Med Supply of the MOSU
- Conceive a strategy of briefing / debriefing and training centered on three axes:
- Global medical supplies management
- Modular management by specific interventions (Hospital, Mobil Clinic, Vaccination, …)
- Management tools
- Apply the standard tools and techniques of management and information (software, workflow, monitoring, and tracking) provided by technical referent.
- Guarantee good practices in pharmacy management present on the fields and management tools used judiciously in emergency context.
- Perpetuation of the partnership with MSF Logistique
- Introduce and formalize links and operational reports (regular visits, planning and common data base, development of technical projects, conception of the emergency stock …).
- Compile all the field feedback of improvement of content of kits & modules.

**Human Resources**

- Guarantee knowledge and competencies among the mission actors (training / mentoring / coaching of medical coordinator, pharmacy manager and associated HR setup)

**Monitoring & Reporting**

- Guarantee the release and availability of weekly / monthly reports (quarterly and yearly on demand) including follow-up of indicators and corrective actions.
- Field support reports.

**Your Profile**

Required:

- Pharmacy qualification sufficient to be recognized and practice as Pharmacist in your home country
- Minimum of 12 months of field experience with MSF as Pharmacy Coordinator
- Minimum of 2 years of experience in pharmacy management in the field with MSF, gained through exposure to various contexts; as part of this experience, at least one mission in an emergency context with MSF Switzerland
- Alternatively, for candidates without MSF experience, minimum of 3 years of field experience with other NGOs in pharmacy management, gained through exposure to various contexts and including experience in emergency context
- Strong knowledge and experience in medical supply & pharmacies management
- Strong proficiency in data processing tools and advanced computer literacy
- Fluency in both French and English is highly desirable. Alternatively, candidates must demonstrate an excellent command of either language and at least B1 proficiency in the other.
- Experience in supervising, coaching and training
- Professional and personal flexibility and adaptability
- Responsible behavior that contributes to the safety and integrity of everyone - prevent, report, and refuse any abusive behavior and/or behavior that goes against MSF's values
- Ability to thrive in a multicultural environment and demonstrate commitment and support for diversity, inclusive and non-discriminatory attitudes and behaviors

**Assets**

- Experience with Isystock
- Proficiency in an additional language, especially Spanish, Arabic, and/or Portuguese

**Terms of Employment**

- Field-based contract, fixed-term for one year, renewable.
- Duration of direct interventions in the field: from 4 weeks to 3 months (certain flexibility is asked in case of needs)
- Per-diem, accommodation, travel arrangements, visa requirement will be taken in charge from MSF and in the field during your assignments.

**We encourage applications from people of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, backgrounds, religions, beliefs, abilities, and all other characteristics of diversity.**
**MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including Sexual harassment.**

**All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo reference and criminal record checks.**

jobs.title: ETHIOPIA - FIELD COORDINATOR (M/F) - TIGRAY
jobs.description:
**Desired start date: 01/12/2026**
**Duration of the mission: 6 Months**
**Location: Adwa - Tigray Region**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

PRESENTATION OF THE MISSION:

Solidarités International (SI) was registered in Ethiopia in December 2022, having previously implemented a WASH in Health intervention in Jijiga, Somali Region, in 2017. In November 2023, SI became the first humanitarian actor to operate in Mao Komo Special woreda (Benishangul-Gumuz) by rehabilitating water points in areas that had been inaccessible for three years. Currently, SI is operational in two regions of the country (In Tigray Region and Amhara Region).

In Tigray, bordering Eritrea, focusing on hard-to-reach areas in partnership with Mums for Mums (MfM) SI is implementing an emergency multisectoral humanitarian programme in Ahsea and Rama Woredas of central zone, to support communities affected by drought, conflict, and displacement. Running from September 2024 to December 2025 (which is now to be extended until end of June 2026), the project aims to improve access to safe water, health services, and nutrition support, while addressing gender-based violence and mental health needs. Key activities include rehabilitating water systems and health facilities, community-based malnutrition screening, cash assistance for vulnerable households, and capacity-building for local actors.

In Amhara region, Solidarités International (SI) and Première Urgence Internationale (PUI) are jointly implementing an integrated emergency response program in the Amhara region of Ethiopia, primarily focused on Health and Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) services. This program is part of a wider effort to address the significant humanitarian needs in the region caused by ongoing conflict and displacement.

SI has been granted cost extension (the donor contract is extended until end of June 2026 with additional fund allocation) of existing project in Tigray and is looking for a Field Coordinator to continue the project activities in the same area.

GENERAL OBJECTIVES :

The Field Coordinator is the representative of the organization at field level. He/she proposes a strategy for his/her area, according to the geopolitical and humanitarian context, and ensures its implementation once validated. He/she checks and ensures that projects are carried out in accordance with the Solidarités International charter, respecting all internal and contractual procedures. He/she mobilizes the material and financial resources necessary for programs to run smoothly and supervises resource management. He/she coordinates the teams in place and is responsible for their security in his/her assigned zone.
Representation and Internal / external communication:
The FC is the official representative of Solidarités International in his/her intervention zone for NGOs, administrative, political and local authorities and civil society. He/She participates in humanitarian forums and relevant coordination meetings
The FC Ensure that documents produced in his/her intervention zone meet deadlines and quality standards, respecting standard formats and procedures
The FC Organise regular Base meetings and Ensure that key operational information circulates properly, in his/her intervention zone and between the bases and the country coordination (sitrep).

ISSUES AND SPECIFIC CHALLENGES :

Implement activities across several woredas in a volatile and operationally constrained context, while ensuring quality, compliance and timely delivery of ongoing projects. Maintain access and programme continuity despite recurrent constraints linked to fuel availability, cash liquidity, telecommunications/network coverage, road access and market fluctuations. Maintain adequate preparedness for a potential deterioration of the security situation, including possible disruption of banking services, communications and movements.

PRIORITIES ON THE 2-3 FIRST MONTHS :

-Consolidate the base management structure and ensure clear responsibilities, delegation and reporting lines within Programme and Support teams.
-Ensure timely implementation and close monitoring of ongoing activities through updated workplans, APU/OFU/LFU and procurement plans.
-Strengthen coordination between WASH, Livelihoods, MEAL and Support departments and ensure adequate balance of management capacity between the main programme components.
-Reinforce budget forecasting and absorption monitoring.
-Maintain and strengthen coordination with local authorities, clusters, partners and other humanitarian actors to avoid duplication and identify operational synergies.
-Ensure the base is prepared for emergency scenarios through updated contingency plans, communication systems, cash/fuel contingency measures and staff preparedness, especially this year with the evolving context
-Continue effort of base development with upcoming opportunities

SECURITY CONSTRAINTS :

The security environment in Tigray remains potentially volatile and can evolve rapidly, requiring continuous monitoring and strict compliance with SI security procedures. Main operational constraints include possible access restrictions, interruptions to telecommunications and internet, fuel shortages, banking/cash limitations and disruptions to road movements. Some operational areas may have limited or no network coverage, requiring reinforced movement tracking and communication procedures. The Field Coordinator must maintain a high level of preparedness, regularly review contingency arrangements, ensure critical resources are available, and adapt programme implementation and movements according to changes in the security and access environment. Staff safety and duty of care must remain central to operational decision-making.

YOUR PROFIL :

DIPLOMAS : A master’s degree (or equivalent field experience) in Humanitarian Action, International Development, Social Sciences, Project Management, or a related field is required.

EXPERIMENT IN THE HUMANITARIAN SECTOR : more than 5 years

EXPERIMENT ON SIMILAR POSITIONS : 3-4 years

TECHNICAL SKILLS :

Relevant management skills :Operation and team management skills include leadership, communication, and problem-solving as core competencies. Other essential skills are decision-making, time management, adaptability, and organizational abilities. Including a strong understanding of finance, and logistics processes.

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS : Ability to work under pressure in a challenging and sometimes insecure environment; cultural sensitivity, adaptability, and a strong commitment to humanitarian principles and safeguarding policies (PSEA, Child Protection).

LANGUAGES : Fluency in written and spoken English is essential. Knowledge of the local language(s) (e.g., Amharic, Tigrigna) is a strong asset.

SI WILL OFFER YOU :

**A salaried position:**

**According to experience,** starting from EUR 3080 gross per month (2800 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 400.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**Living conditions:**

Guest House conditions :

\- There will be shared guesthouse both at the project and coordination during the visit.
-Internet and telephone network : Available both in Addis and Adwa
-Restaurant & social life: Restaurants are available in Addis and also Adwa :

\- Social life in Adwa is limited. All the basics food items and other are available but there is strict limitations and taxation to importation of food. Food in your luggage however is allowed and you can stock up on specials from home. Good quality chocolate, cereals and dried meat products can be hard to find and/or very expensive.

jobs.title: Spécialiste Clinique Rééducation en pédiatrie (troubles du développement) F/H
jobs.description:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

L'ouverture de ce poste est dans le cadre d'un remplacement permanent.

**Contexte**

La Fondation MSF a lancé mi 2023 un projet de développement de la rééducation au sein du mouvement MSF. Il a pour but d’amener un support et une expertise aux missions désireuses de développer leur offre de soins en rééducation dans quatre domaines (rééducation pédiatrique, en santé de la femme, en brulure et en appareillage assisté par la technologie 3D). Nous proposons pour ces différentes catégories de soins d’évaluer les besoins, de définir les objectifs, d’aider à la mise en place et au suivi de ces projets principalement sur des missions de MSF.

Dans le cadre du développement des activités de rééducation en pédiatrie, les activités du poste visent de manière non exhaustive les champs de la neuropédiatrie et des troubles du développement neuro-moteur de l’enfant dans des contextes de malnutrition et d’épidémie. Une approche transversale des autres champs de la rééducation pédiatrique est nécessaire afin de répondre à d’autres besoins terrains avec les autres spécialistes en rééducation.

Depuis 2023, les activités de rééducation pédiatrique supportées par la Fondation MSF se sont concentrées au Yemen, au Tchad et au Nigeria. D’autres projets peuvent être amenés à se développer.

**Activités principales**

Sous la responsabilité hiérarchique du Coordinateur du programme rééducation et en lien avec l’ensemble de l’équipe de La Fondation,

**Contribuer au développement opérationnel de la rééducation dans son domaine d’expertise :**

- Apporter son expertise clinique aux terrains / Coordinations pour leur permettre de prendre des décisions stratégiques opérationnelles concernant l’ensemble des projets présents et futurs en lien avec ses domaines d’expertises
- Participer à l’exploration, l’évaluation et la mise en place de projets en lien avec son expertise avec les différents terrains, coordinations et le Responsable du développement de la rééducation
- Assurer un support technique et clinique (sur le terrain ou à distance) pour répondre aux demandes du terrain dans le cadre de projet de rééducation de La Fondation MSF et de l’application des techniques qui lui sont attachées.

**Participer à la mise en place des outils et d’équipements cliniques et techniques sur le terrain pour le traitement et le suivi des patient·e·s :**

- Identifier et mettre en place les bilans et traitements standards réplicables sur le terrain permettant l’évaluation et le suivi du traitement des patient·e·s
- Identifier les équipements cliniques et techniques nécessaires à la mise en place du projet de rééducation et participer à leur commande en lien avec l’équipe de La Fondation
- Mettre en place ces équipements cliniques et techniques sur les terrains pour que les équipes locales puissent se les approprier
- Identifier et mettre en place différents outils d’organisation sur les terrains pour que les équipes locales puissent se les approprier
- Former et suivre les équipes à l’utilisation de ces outils cliniques, techniques et organisationnels (construction et animation de formation lors de visites terrain et/ou à distance).

**Assurer le suivi de qualité de soins des patient·e·s sur le terrain et à distance :**

- S’assurer que des soins de rééducation de qualité sont prodigués sur les terrains à travers la bonne application des outils techniques et cliniques
- S’assurer du suivi des patient·e·s en lien avec les équipes locales
- Être vigilant·e sur la qualité des soins de rééducation en dehors de son domaine d’expertise et alerter si nécessaire les spécialistes concernés et le Responsable du développement de la rééducation sur des besoins observés.

**Mettre en place des processus, livrables et savoirs de son activité de rééducation à MSF**

- Réaliser la veille scientifique et l’état des lieux dans son domaine de rééducation
- Définir les pratiques cliniques en lien avec ces activités avec les référents cliniques de MSF et le Responsable du développement de la rééducation
- Structurer les processus cliniques et techniques du projet (SoP, Training etc.)
- Créer de nouveau guides cliniques / techniques / Log de son activité pour permettre de la standardiser et faciliter sa réplicabilité
- Assurer un reporting mensuel de ses activités

**Participer à la collecte, l’organisation et l’analyse des données de rééducation des différents terrains :**

- Organiser la récolte et la gestion des données concernant les patients.es et leur suivi ainsi que les données propres aux projets de rééducation qui lui sont attachés.
- S’assurer avec la mission et le Responsable du développement de la rééducation de la protection de ces dernières via l’utilisation d’outils adaptés.
- Analyser les données de rééducation avec les missions et le responsable du développement de la rééducation
- Proposer et développer avec le Responsable du développement de la rééducation des projets de recherche et d’analyse.

**Participer à la mise en place de collaborations locales et internationales dans le cadre des missions ou du développement des activités de rééducation qui lui sont attachées.**

**Participer à la communication autour du projet et le promouvoir :**

- Participer à la communication interne, publique et scientifique du projet de manière orale, audio et écrite.
- Documenter le projet sur son orientation, ses méthodes, ses outils, ses équipements et plus largement sur son évolution sur les terrains.

Ce projet ayant débuté en Septembre 2023, certains éléments ont été initiés et nécessitent d’être poursuivis et réévalués au cas échéant.

Dans le cadre de l’activité pédiatrique, la/le spécialiste peut être amené à manager un profil de physiothérapeute qui aidera à la mise en place des différents projets.

**Profil recherché**

**Expérience et formation :**

- Diplôme de Kinésithérapie / physiothérapie
- Expérience de soins d’au moins 3 ans
- Expérience en ONG (expérience dans les terrains MSF est un atout)
- Expérience de soins dans le domaine des troubles du développement neuro-moteur de l’enfant.
- Diplômes Universitaires ou autres Certifications dans le domaine recherché sont un plus.

**Compétences :**

- Capacité d’adaptation et réactivité
- Esprit critique
- Capacité d’initiative / être force de proposition
- Flexibilité
- Solides compétences en communication pour la promotion de projets en interne et en externe
- Familiarité avec la documentation et l’établissement de rapports sur les activités.

**Langues :** niveau B2 minimum requis en Français et en anglais

**Aptitudes :**

- Dynamisme ; curiosité ; ingéniosité
- Organisation, autonomie, rigueur

**Conditions d'emploi**

**Statut :** CDI à temps plein. Poste cadre, idéalement basé à Paris avec déplacements sur les terrains MSF à prévoir.

**Localisation :** Le poste est idéalement basé à Paris. Toutefois, d'autres localisations pourront être étudiées en fonction des besoins du poste et du profil du/de la candidat(e).

**Rémunération et avantages (pour un poste basé à Paris) :**

- 47,8 K€ brut annuel sur 13 mois
- 22 jours de RTT par an
- Télétravail selon les règles en vigueur chez MSF (2 j/sem.)
- Mutuelle prise en charge à 100%

jobs.title: Oficial de Recuperación Económica - Medios de Vida (Caracas -Personal Nacional) - Republicado
jobs.description:
Danish Refugee Council (DRC) es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, en el marco de la respuesta de emergencia al terremoto, DRC está buscando un/a Oficial de Recuperación Económica altamente calificado/a con sede en Caracas, Venezuela.

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC administra sus operaciones en Venezuela bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela implementa actividades de monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para personas con necesidades específicas (PWSN), sesiones informativas para personas de interés (PoC), prevención de la trata de personas y seguridad alimentaria.

En el marco de la respuesta de emergencia al terremoto ocurrido en el mes de junio 2026, DRC está abriendo una nueva oficina de implementación en Caracas, independiente de la oficina de país, para atender las necesidades de las poblaciones afectadas. Para ello, busca incorporar un/a Oficial de Recuperación Económica – Medios de Vida será responsable de implementar de manera efectiva y oportuna las actividades de los programas de Recuperación Económica de DRC en Venezuela.

**Objetivo general del puesto**

Bajo la supervisión del/la Team Leader de Recuperación Económica o del Gerente de Recuperación Económica, el/la Oficial de Recuperación Económica – Medios de Vida será responsable de implementar de manera efectiva y oportuna las actividades de los programas de Recuperación Económica de DRC en Venezuela. Esto incluye el acompañamiento técnico en terreno para el fortalecimiento de emprendedores, micronegocios y otras iniciativas productivas en comunidades vulnerables, expuestas a riesgos de protección y desastres, así como el desarrollo de habilidades blandas y competencias para el emprendimiento, la empleabilidad y la generación sostenible de ingresos, promoviendo su vinculación con oportunidades de mercado y empleo.

Asimismo, el/la Oficial será responsable de facilitar procesos de orientación ocupacional, fortalecimiento de competencias para la empleabilidad, y articulación con actores del sector privado, instituciones de formación técnica y otros aliados estratégicos que contribuyan a la inserción laboral y recuperación económica de las Personas de Interés (PDI). Igualmente, facilitará la transferencia de metodologías de formación a socios locales mediante herramientas desarrolladas por DRC y garantizará la correcta recopilación de los medios de verificación necesarios para el seguimiento, monitoreo y rendición de cuentas de las actividades implementadas.

También podrá apoyar en la implementación de actividades del proyecto en terreno, principalmente en la preparación y ejecución de las jornadas de distribución de alimentos, así como en procesos logísticos, comunitarios y de documentación garantizando el cumplimiento de los procedimientos y directrices de DRC.

El/la Oficial promoverá una programación integrada y articulada con los equipos de Protección, WASH y Preparación para Desastres, asegurando intervenciones intersectoriales y de calidad en todas las etapas del proyecto. Además, será responsable de coordinar efectivamente con el equipo de Recuperación Económica, socios locales, instituciones públicas, centros de formación y empleadores potenciales, asegurando el cumplimiento del plan de acción, el logro de resultados y el fortalecimiento de la resiliencia económica de las comunidades atendidas.

**Responsabilidades:**

**Identificación de actividades propias del sector de Medios de Vida**

- Liderar diagnósticos socioeconómicos y de mercado para identificar cadenas productivas, ecosistemas de actores claves del sector público y privado, y oportunidades de inclusión financiera (instituciones, banca, sector privado) que fomenten la autosuficiencia y resiliencia de las Personas de Interés (PDI).
- Evaluar la viabilidad técnica, social, ambiental y económica de propuestas de generación de ingresos, asegurando que los proyectos de medios de vida sean sostenibles, pertinentes culturalmente y sensibles a los riesgos de protección y desastres.
- Contribuir con datos del contexto local para el ajuste y formulación de propuestas, garantizando la integración del enfoque de Recuperación Económica con otros sectores (Protección, WASH y Preparación para Desastres).
- Con el apoyo y la orientación de su supervisor y coordinación técnica, sugerir ideas innovadoras y técnicas adecuadas para las intervenciones de Recuperación Económica en función del contexto.

**Implementación técnica y logística**

- Responsable de implementar la planificación, ejecución, seguimiento y cierre técnico de las actividades de medios de vida (focalización, diagnósticos, selección, formación, entregas, encuestas PDM, líneas base/salida y gestión de bases de datos), en coordinación con el Team Leader o Gerente de Recuperación económica, y con los equipos de Logística y finanzas para asegurar el cumplimiento del plan de acción y el reporte oportuno de los indicadores propuestos.
- Diseñar e implementar procesos de formación en planes de negocios, habilidades para el empleo, orientación vocacional, habilidades blandas, planes de marketing, estructuras de costos, gestión y educación financiera. Entre las actividades se contempla la facilitación directa, la Formación a Formadores (ToT) para socios y la gestión logística/financiera necesaria para su ejecución.
- Con la orientación técnica de la coordinación de Recuperación Económica, en conjunto con la supervisión del Team Leader o Gerente de Recuperación Económica, ser el punto focal de alianzas estratégicas con actores del sector privado, público o institucional para actividades propias de medios de vida, como lo pueden ser alianzas estratégicas para emprendedores.
- Realizar planes de seguimiento a las PdI relacionados al incremento de su generación de ingresos y de medición de indicadores establecidos en el programa de Recuperación Económica.
- Identificar, coordinar y entregar apoyos en especie (como insumos productivos, herramientas, equipos, etc.) de acuerdo con las necesidades socioeconómicas y productivas identificadas, así como con los lineamientos técnicos de la coordinación y el enfoque de protección.
- Apoyar la planificación y ejecución de las jornadas de distribución y demás actividades logísticas del proyecto, incluyendo la recepción, descarga, verificación de cantidades y calidad de los insumos, la organización y acondicionamiento de los sitios de atención, el control de inventarios y materiales en terreno.
- Participar en la preparación de informes mensuales/trimestrales/anuales aportando análisis técnicos sobre el componente y las actividades realizadas, así como en la orientación técnica para elaborar presupuestos de este componente en formulaciones de proyectos.
- Transferir conocimientos, acompañar, hacer seguimiento sobre la implementación de programas de Recuperación Económica implementadas por organizaciones locales, utilizando metodologías desarrolladas por DRC. La transferencia de conocimientos y de acompañamiento incluyen las fases de focalización, formación, evaluaciones de planes de negocio, y seguimiento de la evolución de los participantes.

**Participación comunitaria**

- Facilitar procesos de información, convocatoria y participación de la comunidad que permitan el acceso y la aceptación comunitaria.
- Monitorear la participación de grupos vulnerables (mujeres, personas mayores, personas con discapacidad) y necesidades específicas para su participación
- Garantizar la calidad, participación comunitaria y mecanismos de rendición de cuentas en la ejecución de actividades.

**Monitoreo y reporte**

- Garantizar la compilación de los medios de verificación requeridos y datos cualitativos de las actividades del proyecto.
- Aplicar encuestas para el registro, línea base, PDMs, línea de salida y otras encuestas necesarias para la implementación del proyecto.
- Reportar a los supervisores, incidentes, retrasos o cualquier otro desafío o reto para la implementación de las actividades a nivel programático, logístico y/o financiero.
- Monitorear el avance de las personas beneficiarias, documentar resultados y generar lecciones aprendidas.
- Aportar a la documentación de buenas prácticas, historias de vida o casos de éxito.
- Contribuir a la elaboración de informes técnicos y narrativos según los requerimientos del proyecto.

**Experiencia y competencias:**

- 2 años de experiencia relevante en trabajo relacionado con medios de vida, especialmente con la recuperación económica de emprendimientos, empleos y fuentes de ingresos. Experiencia desarrollando estructuras de costos para pequeños negocios, planes de marketing y/o fortaleciendo habilidades blandas para emprender es valorado.
- Experiencia en trabajo articulado con proyectos de protección, preparación para desastres, WASH, trabajo social, derechos humanos u otro trabajo similar de terreno, relacionado a una ONG u otra organización sin fines de lucro.
- Experiencia de terreno y de trabajo con comunidades en zonas urbanas de difícil acceso, personas desplazadas, y/o migrantes y refugiadas.
- Experiencia en la facilitación de modelos de aprendizaje híbridos y uso de herramientas digitales (como Moodle) para la capacitación de poblaciones vulnerables es valorada.
- Experiencia y capacidad para relacionarse con las personas, interactuar con equipos multidisciplinarios, resolver conflictos y gestionar dinámicas de grupos.
- Habilidades y experiencia en capacitación y desarrollo de capacidades de personal de organizaciones sin fines de lucro con conocimiento básico o intermedio en medios de vida.
- Habilidades de redacción de informes y otros documentos de comunicación interna.
- Excelente habilidad en MS Word, Excel y PowerPoint.
- Experiencia en manejar bases de datos.

**Educación:**

Título universitario pertinente relacionado a administración de empresas, contabilidad, economía, desarrollo humano, trabajo social, psicología, mercadeo, docencia o cualificación profesional equivalente.

**Idioma:**

- Ingles (A2 Deseable)
- Español

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: 6 meses con disponibilidad de extensión según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda H.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.
- Contratación nacional.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**: actuar de acuerdo con la visión y los valores de DRC.

**Proceso de solicitud:** Todos los solicitantes deben cargar una carta de presentación (máx. 1 página) y un CV actualizado (**máx. 2 páginas, sin soportes**) en español, en la plataforma de empleo de DRC. Las solicitudes enviadas por correo electrónico no serán consideradas.

**Fecha de cierre de solicitudes**: Viernes 16 de Octubre a las 11:59 pm Hora Local. Tenga en cuenta que las solicitudes se revisarán continuamente y las entrevistas se planificarán tan pronto como se identifique a un candidat@ adecuado. DRC se reserva el derecho a cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha límite una vez se identifique a un candidato idóneo.

**Fecha de inicio:** Octubre 2026

**Nota:**

- Nos reservamos el derecho a cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha indicada de cierre de postulaciones
- Debido a una contratación de emergencia, DRC no se obliga a enviar las notificaciones de rechazo a los candidatos que no sean considerados en el proceso

jobs.title: Mission France - Médiateur.ice Interculturel.le - Basé à Dunkerque F/H
jobs.description:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

La mission France recherche un.e : Médiateur.ice Interculturel.le - Basé à Dunkerque.

**CONTEXTE**

La Mission France de MSF porte assistance aux personnes migrantes en situation de grande vulnérabilité sociale, médicale et/ou psychique sur le territoire français et mène des actions de plaidoyer pour faciliter leur accès au droit commun.

Depuis décembre 2017, la Mission France apporte une assistance aux personnes migrantes.

Elle assure la prise en charge médicale, psychologique, juridique et sociale des personnes exclues des soins de santé et plaide en faveur de l'accès aux soins des personnes étrangères vulnérables, notamment les femmes vivant dans les campements du dunkerquois.

La Mission France compte actuellement trois projets :

- En Ile-de-France. Le projet est ouvert depuis décembre 2017. Orienté dès les origines sur la prise en charge médicale, psychologique, sociale et juridique des mineurs non accompagnés en recours (accueil de jour et hébergement), il a connu une évolution importante en se spécialisant sur le public des jeunes filles en recours de reconnaissance de minorité. S’y ajoute une activité de clinique mobile animée par une équipe de bénévoles
- A Calais et sur le Littoral Nord. Ouvert à l’été 2023. Accueil de jour pour mineurs non accompagnés offrant répit et activités ; cliniques mobiles à destination du public général (adultes, familles, mineurs), incluant des activités de santé mentale. Des activités saisonnières viennent compléter les activités avec, du printemps à l’automne, une activité de maraudes littorales à destination des personnes exilées rescapées de naufrage et en hiver une activité de mise à l’abri des personnes les plus vulnérables.
- A Dunkerque. Le projet vise à répondre aux besoins croissants des femmes, jeunes filles et familles exilées vivant dans des conditions extrêmement précaires sur le Littoral Dunkerquois. En partenariat étroit avec le Refugee Women’s Centre, il se concentre sur la prise en charge médicale en santé des femmes (gynécologie, suivi de grossesse, santé sexuelle et reproductive), une prise en charge en santé mentale, un dispositif d’abri d’urgence pour les femmes seules, le renforcement de la détection et de la prise en charge des violences sexuelles, ainsi qu’un volet de documentation et plaidoyer sur les violences et l’absence de services essentiels sur le territoire.

Le volet communication et plaidoyer est central sur cette mission qui évolue dans un pays ayant les moyens d’accueillir dignement mais qui néglige volontairement les populations migrantes.

**Mission**

Soutenir la communication et l'interaction entre les bénéficiaires (migrant.es et réfugié.es) et l’équipe pluridisciplinaire, en traitant les conséquences des barrières linguistiques, des différences socioculturelles et de la discrimination, en suivant les protocoles et les procédures de MSF, afin d'améliorer l'accès à des soins de santé de qualité et à d'autres services pertinents et de permettre de mieux comprendre les déterminants socioculturels locaux.

**Responsabilités**

Faciliter la relation entre les patient.e.s et les prestataires de soins impliqués dans les consultations médicales, de soin de santé somatique et mentale ainsi qu’entre les patient.e.s et la prise en charge par l’équipe sociojuridique :

- Fournir un interprétariat de qualité entre l’équipe pluridisciplinaire et les patientes dans leur langue maternelle, en prenant en compte l’aspect interculturel, la sensibilité et la clarté de la communication entre les parties.
Aider l’équipe pluridisciplinaire et les patient.e.s à remédier aux conséquences négatives des différences socioculturelles et identifier et signaler les obstacles qui entravent l'équité et l'égalité dans l'accès aux services.
- Accompagner et suivre les patient.e.s vers les structures d'orientation (établissements de santé et de soins sociaux) si nécessaire.
- Soutenir l'intervention thérapeutique/sociale en partageant avec l’équipe pluridisciplinaire les aspects pertinents du contexte culturel du patient, en agissant en tant qu'intermédiaire culturel.le.
- Participer aux réunions pluridisciplinaires.
- En collaboration avec les autres membres de l'équipe du projet, fournir des informations aux patientes sur le fonctionnement du système de soins et des autres services de soutien (abri, nourriture, transport, soutien juridique) fournis par MSF et d'autres acteurs, dans le but de favoriser la responsabilisation et l'autonomie des patientes.

Contribuer à la compréhension du contexte et à la collecte de données sur les questions médicales et sociojuridiques, en accordant une attention particulière aux vulnérabilités, afin de fournir des informations fiables pour la prise de décisions opérationnelles :

- Assurer une traduction linguistique et interculturelle de qualité lors de la collecte de témoignages à des fins de plaidoyer et de communication.
- Apporter un soutien à la mise en oeuvre d'évaluations ou d'enquêtes, le cas échéant.
- Rapporter toutes les informations importantes exprimées par les patientes et les communautés, en garantissant la confidentialité à tout moment.
- Apporter un soutien à l'analyse des médias et à la création de contenus à des fins de communication.

**Responsabilités spécifiques à la mission France**

Sous la responsabilité de la Coordinatrice projet Dunkerque et en collaboration avec une équipe pluridisciplinaire, le.la médiateur.ice interculturel.le :

- Participe à la réflexion et l’adaptation des activités d’aller-vers mises en oeuvre par MSF sur le littoral Nord, ainsi que plus spécifiquement des activités de santé sexuelle et reproductive sur le Dunkerquois.
- Accompagne les différent.es professionnel.les (soignant.es, pyschologue.s, travailleur.seuses sociaux.les) en tant qu’intermédiaire linguistique et interculturel.le pour assurer un interprétariat en direct lors des consultations, des activités externes, des cliniques mobiles, des groupes de discussions, sensibilisation, formations, des maraudes, des activités d’allers vers et autre cas échéant et permet aux collaborateur.ices d’offrir une qualité de soins et/ou de soutien psychosocial à la hauteur des standards de l’association.
- Sensibilise le reste de l’équipe à des codes culturels qui pourraient être une barrière à l’accès aux services.
- Accompagne dans les activités pour l’identifications des besoins exprimés lors des activités.
- Participer à l’éducation à la santé des femmes et à la promotion des services en santé sexuelle et reproductive
- Tester, diffuser et animer des supports et activités de sensibilisation et d'éducation à la santé auprès des communautés.
- Apporte un soutien à l’élaboration d’outils linguistiques et communicationnels en support aux activités à destination des personnes accompagnés, en collaboration avec l’équipe pluridisciplinaire.
- Participer à l’élaboration des plans de sensibilisation et de mobilisation communautaire.
- Contribuer à l’identification des groupes cibles et des canaux de communication appropriés.
- Animer des séances de sensibilisation, causeries éducatives et campagnes communautaires.
- Assurer la promotion des bonnes pratiques de santé au sein des communautés.
- Mesurer le niveau de compréhension et l'adoption des messages clés.
- Documenter les retours, difficultés et bonnes pratiques observées.
- Participe à la formation des équipes partenaires et/ou du personnes accompagnées dans le cadre des activités sur le nord littoral et en particulier sur le Dunkerquois
- Contribue au recueil de témoignages et s’inscrit dans la démarche MSF en termes de communication et de plaidoyer concernant les enjeux humanitaires
- Participe à la collecte et la capitalisation des données individuelles de suivi des situations médico-psycho-sociales des personnes rencontrées.
- Participe aux réunions pluridisciplinaires.•Participe la communication et la coordination adéquate avec les autres organismes et institutions déployés ou consultés.
- Soutient les autres activités des projets de Calais et du Littoral Nord en cas d’absence prolongée de besoins sur le Dunkerquois.

jobs.title: Supply Chain Manager
jobs.description:
**Who we are?**

***IDA is an international independent non-governmental organization providing medical and humanitarian assistance to people affected by conflicts, natural disasters and epidemics regardless of race, religion, gender or political affiliation.***
***IDA was founded in 2012 by Syrian doctors from Aleppo in response to the healthcare and humanitarian crisis in Syria.***

***IDA Syria is the main healthcare provider in the Northern Aleppo/Syria area, working closely with 500,000 IDPs and 700,000 host community through 20 healthcare facility and other health and nutrition projects***

**During last year, IDA has provided 1.2 million services in Heath, Nutrition, WaSH and Camp Management**

Job Summary: Overseeing, directing, coordinating, and exercising control over all procurement, warehouse and logistics activities and tasks. This includes reviewing and enhancing tools, procedures, and policies in collaboration with the Operations Director. The role involves optimizing operational efficiency and ensuring the effective management of warehousing and logistics operations

***Location: Syria - Aleppo***

Main tasks and Activities Administration & Strategic Planning
• Develop and implement strategic work plans for the supply chain department, ensuring alignment with organizational goals.
• Oversee a team of multiple units (Procurement, Logistics, and Warehousing) across Syria .
• Establish and execute frameworks for capacity development in collaboration with HR to enhance team performance and capabilities.
• Foster effective communication and collaboration across departments to ensure seamless operations.
Procurement Management
• Design and implement transparent and competitive procurement processes in compliance with donor and organizational regulations.
• Formulate procurement plans for multiple projects, revise them periodically, and monitor their execution.
• Conduct market surveys to maintain updated price data, ensuring cost-effective procurement strategies.
• Develop and maintain a comprehensive supplier roster, conducting evaluations and categorizing suppliers for quality assurance.
Logistics & Fleet Management
• Establish and oversee mechanisms for fleet management, including international and local shipments, customs clearance, and tax exemption processes.
• Coordinate vehicle movement plans, manage transportation requests, and ensure compliance with security protocols.
• Optimize logistics workflows to minimize delays and maximize efficiency in the supply chain.
Warehousing & Inventory Control
• Supervise the management of warehouses ensuring systematic stock control and tracking.
• Develop online systems for managing inventory movement and consumption, ensuring accurate and timely reporting.
• Implement strategies for the storage and distribution of prepositioned goods to beneficiaries.
Assets Management
• Oversee the registration, transfer, and maintenance of assets, utilizing systematic procedures and QR-code-based tracking.
• Conduct periodic physical inspections of assets to assess conditions and maintain updated master sheets for all locations and donors.
Policy Development & Compliance
• Update and refine logistics policies, procedures, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) to enhance field operations and donor compatibility.
• Ensure compliance with all regulatory frameworks and facilitate adherence to donor standards across all operations

Requirements
• University degree (preferably in medical fields like pharmacy or medicine).
• Proficient in MS Office and relevant software.
• Minimum of 5 years of experience in NGOs.
• Stable and robust character, and team player.
• Excellent communication skills in written and spoken English, fluent in Arabic.
• Strong initiative and self-motivation, with a strong commitment to teamwork and humanitarian principles.
• Flexible, enthusiastic, and willing to learn from others.
• Ability to multitask and cope with competing demands under tight deadlines.
• Ability to cope with high workload and stress.
• Identify priority activities.
• Knowledge of the context in Syria
• Good standing and reputation in the community.
• Experience of working with local partners.
• Experience in conducting assessments and monitoring activities.

2\. Behavioural competencies :

● Planning and delivering results.
● Working with people.
● Communicating with impact and respect.
● Handling insecure environments.

***Independent Doctors Association does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, and committed to acting professionally and ethically.***
***Independent Doctors Association is zero tolerable with any SEA case, IDA is creating the best environment to make sure that all staff have understood SEA and how to report in case there is any suspected case***

jobs.title: Field engineer – FS&ERL Programs
jobs.description:
**Location**: HAMA

**Job summary**

Preparing engineering studies and detailed drawings, following up on the implementation of engineering works in accordance with technical specifications, and reviewing and analyzing engineering bids. The position also involves coordinating with the Project Manager to supervise field operations and ensure the application of quality and safety standards throughout the project.

**Qualifications and education requirements**:

- Bachelor's degree in Agricultural, Civil, or Architectural Engineering.
- A Project Management certificate is also preferred.

**Required Skills and Experience**:

- Effective communication
- Prioritization and time management
- Data analysis
- Report writing
- Advanced skills in humanitarian project management
- Technical computer skills
- Outlook
- Teams
- Word
- Excel
- PowerPoint
- OneDrive
- AutoCAD

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

- Prepare preliminary engineering studies and detailed plans necessary for the execution of engineering works
- Preparing preliminary engineering studies and detailed drawings required for the implementation of engineering works.
- Preparing estimated bills of quantities and technical specifications for project activities.
- Reviewing technical aspects of engineering bids submitted for tenders and preparing a detailed analytical assessment of the technical offers submitted by each contractor.
- Under the supervision of the Project Manager, preparing an implementation work plan for the engineering works to be carried out by ATAA, which the contractor will be required to follow.
- Conducting daily and direct field follow-up of engineering works implemented by workers previously recruited in the camps, and monitoring the quality of materials and the proper execution of works.
- Developing any engineering drawings (shop drawings) required for the work as needed.
- Maintaining close coordination with the Project Manager and providing them with all field information and updates on an ongoing basis, as well as actively participating in the preparation of the project’s weekly activity report regarding the engineering component.
- Maintaining a surveying book (paper and digital) to calculate the quantities of completed works.
- Taking responsibility for controlling, organizing, and scheduling handover and acceptance documents and paperwork, and submitting them to the Project Manager.
- Working in cooperation with the Project Manager to apply humanitarian principles and standards, and to implement protection laws for individuals and communities in general.
- Fully comply with Ata’a Association’s safeguarding policies and procedures, including policies on protection from sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment (PSEAH), and child safeguarding, ensuring the safety and well-being of beneficiaries—especially children—both psychologically and physically across all projects, offices, and facilities, and fostering a safe and supportive environment through full implementation of these policies and their annexes.

**Protection Policy:**

Ataa Association considers any type of child abuse unacceptable, as it recognizes its responsibility to protect children from harm in all areas of its work. Ataa Association confirms that it is committed to ensuring a safe environment for children and takes a strict stance against any type of child abuse and exploitation.

**Discrimination, Abuse, and Harassment Policy:**

jobs.title: Head of Operational Finance & Support Services
jobs.description:
Central African Republic | Bangui, with frequent travel to field offices

DanChurchAid (DCA) is seeking an experienced, hands-on Head of Operational Finance & Support Services (HoOFSS) to lead the day-to-day delivery of finance and support services in its Central African Republic Country Office.

Reporting to the Country Director, you will lead the finance, HR, procurement, logistics and administration teams, working closely with programme colleagues and with extended focus on field offices to ensure that staff, funds, supplies and services are available when and where they are needed.

The role centres on practical execution: translating programme plans into clear support-service priorities, maintaining reliable financial controls, resolving operational bottlenecks and following actions through to completion. You will combine team leadership with direct involvement in financial reviews, operational planning and problem-solving.

You will help teams deliver in a demanding and changing environment. We are looking for someone who remains calm under pressure, makes sound decisions, pays attention to detail and provides constructive, service-minded support to colleagues.

**Your key responsibilities**

**Operational delivery and field-office support**

- Coordinate day-to-day support services across the country office and field offices, aligning finance, HR, procurement and logistics priorities with programme delivery.
- Convert project workplans into practical support-service schedules, with clear responsibilities, deadlines and follow-up.
- Regularly review outstanding payments, procurement requests, staffing needs and other operational constraints; agree corrective actions and track their completion.
- Maintain close contact with field teams and conduct field visits to review delivery, resolve problems and strengthen working practices.
- Provide the Country Director with concise operational updates, highlighting financial pressures, delivery risks and decisions requiring escalation.

**Operational finance and financial control**

- Lead routine financial operations, ensuring timely and accurate accounting, payments, reconciliations and month-end closure in line with DCA procedures.
- Prepare and monitor cash-flow forecasts and funding requests so that country and field offices can meet approved commitments.
- Work with budget holders to prepare project budgets and forecasts, review expenditure and commitments, and address variances before they disrupt delivery.
- Monitor shared support costs, allocations and available funding, and ensure that budget revisions and project closures are completed on time.
- Review payment documentation, account balances and financial records; maintain segregation of duties and approval controls within delegated authority.
- Ensure accurate recording in DCA’s financial system, Maconomy, and complete, accessible supporting documentation for financial transactions.
- Coordinate timely donor and internal financial reporting with programme colleagues and headquarters.
- Coordinate audit preparation, respond to audit queries and ensure that agreed corrective actions are implemented.
- Ensure that financial operations follow DCA and donor requirements and applicable local legal and tax obligations, seeking specialist advice where needed.

**Procurement, logistics and administration**

- Oversee procurement planning and follow up on sourcing, purchasing and delivery schedules to meet programme needs.
- Ensure procurement decisions are documented, competitive and compliant with DCA and donor rules, with appropriate checks on costs, quality and delivery.
- Monitor suppliers, service providers and contracts; address delays and performance issues and escalate contractual risks when necessary.
- Ensure practical arrangements for transport, fleet, stock, assets, premises and IT support, including maintenance, inventories and reliable records.
- Work with field teams to improve the availability and reliability of supplies and services within access and security constraints.

**HR operations and team management**

- Oversee timely delivery of recruitment, onboarding, personnel administration, payroll inputs and staff records, in collaboration with HR colleagues.
- Ensure HR processes follow DCA policies and applicable local requirements, referring complex employment matters to the appropriate HR advisers.
- Set clear priorities for support-service managers and their teams, monitor workloads and follow up on performance and agreed deliverables.
- Coach colleagues through practical work, strengthen technical skills and ensure effective delegation and continuity during absences.
- Promote respectful working relationships, inclusive teams and high standards of conduct and accountability.

**Process improvement and accountability**

- Identify recurring delays, errors and control weaknesses and implement practical improvements to workflows, tools and documentation.
- Use regular checks and simple performance measures to monitor delivery times, financial accuracy and completion of corrective actions.
- Work closely with programme teams to ensure support services are responsive while maintaining appropriate controls.
- Apply DCA’s values, humanitarian principles and safeguarding requirements in daily work and management decisions.

**What you bring**

- A bachelor or master degree in finance or accounting,
- At least five years of relevant experience in finance and operational support within an NGO or comparable organisation, including at least two years leading teams or managing support functions.
- Strong practical experience in budgeting, cash-flow management, accounting, financial reporting and internal controls.
- Experience supporting project implementation and field operations, including coordinating finance with procurement, logistics and HR.
- A working understanding of donor compliance and internal and external audit requirements, with experience implementing corrective actions.
- Confidence using financial systems, budget tools and spreadsheets to analyse data and support operational decisions.
- Proven ability to prioritise competing needs, resolve problems and follow through on deadlines in a demanding environment.
- Effective people-management, coaching and communication skills, with a collaborative and service-minded approach.
- Fluency in written and spoken French and English.
- A commitment to equality, diversity, safeguarding and DCA’s values.

**What we offer**

- A 12-month contract with the possibility of extension.
- A generous remuneration package, with salary and benefits in accordance with the applicable DCA employment terms.
- A meaningful opportunity to improve operational delivery and support humanitarian programmes in the Central African Republic.
- Opportunities for professional development and collaboration with committed colleagues.

**How to apply**

Application deadline is 21 October 2026

Applications will be reviewed and interviews conducted on a rolling basis. DCA reserves the right to select a candidate before the closing date.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, race, religion, sexual orientation, abilities, or ethnic affiliation are encouraged to apply for the vacancy. DCA conducts an anti-terror check as part of the recruitment process. It is a prerequisite that you can pass this check and maintain this status throughout your employment with us. Everyone applying for a job with DCA must be ready to comply with our Code of Conduct, Staff Policy on Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment and our Child Safeguarding Policy.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Housing Disaster Resilience and Recovery
jobs.description:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**Summary:**

The Senior Director of Housing Disaster Resilience and Recovery will lead and coordinate efforts to strengthen the housing resilience in communities where Habitat works in the context of disasters and conflict. Where appropriate the work will be done through the implementation of Habitat’s Pathway to Permanence approach that focuses on the connection between short-term and long-term interventions. The Senior Director supervises a team of disaster risk reduction and recovery specialists and works in collaboration with global and regional departments. The role involves leading the Housing Disaster Resilience and Recovery strategy, program design, technical assistance for the network, procuring funding in coordination with other departments, and engaging with external stakeholders.

**Key Responsibilities:**

- Lead the Housing Disaster Resilience and Recovery team, including line management, performance evaluation and professional development.
- Further develop and implement the strategic plan of HDRR in alignment with Habitat’s global strategy.
- Support the organization increasing capacity in the articulation of housing resilience and recovery in disasters and conflict by developing standards, systems, guidelines and monitoring and learning mechanisms.
- Consult and contribute with US and Area Office Program teams as needed for program design and implementation, align approaches, and share knowledge.
- Collaborate with and support other departments to incorporate housing resilience, and disaster risk reduction components into long-term programs and projects.
- Provide coordination between headquarters functional units and field operation activities in the different geographies where the organization is operational. This includes, levelling, supporting fundraising, supporting reporting to donors, monitoring and evaluation, and being the spokesperson as needed.
- Lead the formation and functioning of communities of practices in areas related to this role
- Lead and collaborate in the areas of research and advocacy for housing resilience, disaster risk reduction, post-disaster interventions.
- Identify and pursue institutional and private funding opportunities in coordination with fundraising departments of HFHI.
- Oversee the management of projects and programs under the HDRR department and ensure compliance with grant requirements.
- Lead HFHI’s active engagement and leadership in disaster risk reduction and housing resilience fora, alliances and coalitions, connecting the organization to peer agencies and donor networks in the sector
- Manage the team budget.

**Minimum Requirements:**

**Education**:

- Bachelor’s in urban planning, public policy, civil engineering, environmental science or field related.
- Graduate studies in resilience planning, disaster and conflict management, international development or related discipline

**Years of Related Experience**:

- Minimum of 7 years of experience in disaster risk reduction, community resilience, housing development or related field.
- Proven track record of managing complex projects, including implementing programs or projects funded by state or multi-lateral members of the International Cooperation.
- Experience of managing projects in collaboration with partner organizations, and remote management in insecure environments.
- Experience in effectively managing and leading diverse, globally distributed leaders in a federated network in the international development/humanitarian sector.
- Minimum of 5 years working internationally in at least 2 countries in the Majority World/ Global South, and familiarity working with offices in the Global North for citizens of Majority World countries.
- Experience, knowledge and commitment integrating gender and social inclusion in programs and projects

**Knowledge, Skills & Abilities**:

- Strong understanding of resilience frameworks, housing policy frameworks, humanitarian principles and International Humanitarian Law, disaster risk reduction frameworks, and environmental regulatory frameworks
- Excellent project management skills, including budgeting, planning, and reporting.
- Ability to analyze data, assess risks, and to learn through it to develop innovative solutions.
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills, cultural-awareness, and the ability to engage diverse stakeholders.

**Active support of HFHI Values:**
\- We are part of something bigger than ourselves
\- We do what's right, even when it is difficult or unpopular
\- We take personal responsibility for Habitat's mission

**Safeguarding**
HFHI requires that all employees take seriously their ethical responsibilities to safeguarding our intended beneficiaries, their communities, and all those with whom we work. Managers at all levels have responsibilities to support and develop systems that create and maintain an environment that prevents harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, safeguards the rights of beneficiaries and community members (especially children), and promotes the implementation of Habitat for Humanity’s code of conduct.

**Hiring Range:**

The actual salary offered for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including location, internal equity and the candidate’s qualifications and professional experience. HFHI offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package that varies by country and typically includes vacation leave, sick leave, personal days, health insurance options, retirement plan contributions and life insurance. For work locations in the US, the hiring range for this position is:

$134,200.00

$199,600 USD

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.
