jobs.title: Vice President, Global Human Resources
jobs.description:
**ABOUT CHILDFUND**

**ChildFund** is a child-focused international development organization that connects children with the people, resources and institutions they need to grow up healthy, educated, skilled and safe, no matter where they are. We work directly in 23 countries, with extended reach to more than 60 countries through our global partnership network.

**ChildFund’s Values**

We aspire for every person in our organization—program participants, supporters, staff, and volunteers alike—to feel free, safe, and confident to be themselves. In our culture of connection, you will have ample opportunity to grow, learn, and lead while contributing your talents and innovations to our inspiring mission.

**ChildFund’s Commitment**

ChildFund International has a zero-tolerance policy regarding sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment (SEAH) and all other forms of harm by its staff, partners, and other representatives in the delivery of its mission and services for children. ChildFund is committed to creating a safe environment in the workplace as well as in the communities where it delivers programs and services. ChildFund expects every staff member, partner, and representative to adhere to this commitment and to ensure all organizational policies and standards are followed. This position is subject to a range of vetting checks, including a criminal records check and/or disclosure to ensure program participants are safeguarded.

**ABOUT THE ROLE**

The Vice President, Global Human Resources is a key executive leadership position in ChildFund, responsible for the critical talent strategies and infrastructure delivering the organization’s strategy, Growing Connections.

As ChildFund pursues its “bold goal” to reach 100 million children by the year 2030, the Vice President plays a pivotal role in enhancing employee experience, developing talent capacity, strengthening systems, and promoting a value-aligned and engaging work culture.

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer and serving as a member of the Executive Team and Global Leadership Team, the Vice President leads a global, matrixed Human Resources team and partners with regional leadership and Country Offices to align Global Human Resources strategies with organizational strategy and objectives. The Vice President is a key advisor to the CEO on people matters while traveling periodically and maintaining strong relationships across the organization.

An expert in HR practice, the Vice President leads organization-wide transformation initiatives while overseeing compliant, consistent service delivery and high performance of the global HR team. The Vice President coaches and mentors executives and HR professionals to support ChildFund’s culture of innovation and learning while staying current with global HR innovations and best practices in the international development sector.

**REQUIRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE**

- Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field required; Master’s degree preferred (MBA, MPA, Human Resources, or similar).
- At least 15 years of experience in the human resources function, with experience in international development strongly preferred.
- At least 10 years of experience leading teams.
- Experience leading the HR function in international organizations across multiple country locations.
- Significant experience developing and implementing people – and culture-centered, strategy-aligned HR initiatives.
- Experience advising, consulting, and influencing at the C-suite level preferred.
- Advanced knowledge of HR operations in the US; foundational knowledge of HR operations and/or labor laws in other ChildFund countries of operation is preferred but not required.
- English fluency is required; proficiency in another language is a plus.
- Impeccable integrity, judgment, and ethics.
- Excellent, demonstrated relationship-building skills.

**Please click here:** [**ChildFund International Job Description – VP, Global Human Resources.pdf**](https://pod6.app.loxo.co/redactor-files/4601?hash=65492b94955a37f9e9d762fed6dd7707114d365b9f3c3507f65241a5af152067) **for a full job description, which outlines the role’s primary responsibilities and ChildFund’s Leadership and Core competencies .**

**APPOINTMENT TERMS**

**Location: Richmond, Virginia, US**. This is a full-time hybrid position. Candidates located in Richmond, VA or willing to relocate are preferred. Candidates must have the ability to work on site in Richmond, Virginia two days per week. We are open to candidates willing to commute weekly from nearby metro areas.

**To be eligible, candidates must have current work authorization in the US.**

**Salary and Benefits:** The anticipated salary range for this position is $177,500-$225,000 per year.

**Contract length:** Permanent

jobs.description:
## **TYPOLOGIE DU POSTE**

Fondée en 2009, ALIMA est présente au Niger aux côtés de son partenaire local l’ONG nigérienne BEFEN « le Bien Être de la Femme et de l’Enfant au Niger » depuis sa création. En effet, le tout premier projet d’ALIMA a été mis en œuvre au Niger, dans le district de Mirriah, région de Zinder. ALIMA possède une grande expérience dans la réponse aux épidémies (Diphtérie, Méningite, Rougeole, Choléra et COVID-19), la nutrition, la santé primaire et maternelle, les VBG (violences basées sur le genre) ainsi que le WASH (eau, assainissement et hygiène).

Il s’agit de:

1\. Un projet en consortium avec plusieurs ONG - ALIMA/ BEFEN met en œuvre le volet Santé Nutrition, ACF met en œuvre les activités WASH ; Agriculture et sécurité alimentaire et l’ONG DIKO le volet protection).

Objectif général : Contribuer à la réduction de la morbidité et de la mortalité des populations hôtes et déplacées dans la région de Tillabéry (districts de Say, Téra et Bankilaré) par une réponse d'urgence intégrée

Dont l’objectif est : D'améliorer l'accès aux soins de santé communautaires, primaires, secondaires et nutritionnels pour les enfants de moins de cinq ans ainsi que pour les femmes enceintes et allaitantes parmi les personnes déplacées et les communautés d'accueil, touchées par la crise dans les districts de Say, Téra et Bankilaré.

2\. Un projet de Réponse d’urgence pour l’accès et l’amélioration des soins de santé des populations affectées par un choc et la contribution à la réduction de la morbi-mortalité infantile dans les régions de Tillabéry (Abala, Banibangou et Ayerou), Tahoua, Maradi et Zinder

Durée de l'action (en mois) : 36 mois

Zone d’intervention : Tillabéri : 3 HD, 5 CSI et 2 cliniques mobiles. (Abala : 1 HD, 3 CSI, et 1 clinique mobile, Ayorou : 1 HD, 2 CSI et 1 clinique mobile, Banibangou :1 HD).

LIENS FONCTIONNELS ET HIERARCHIQUES

- Il·Elle rend compte au chef ou à la cheffe de mission basé·e en coordination.
- Il·Elle encadre l’équipe de cadre du projet (par exemple le ou la Référent.e Médical·e, le ou la Responsable Administration, le ou la Responsable Logistique et le ou la Responsable des soins infirmiers) ainsi que les équipes nationales en collaboration avec ses référent·es techniques au niveau du projet.
- Il·Elle collabore avec la coordination (médicale, logistique et financière et des ressources humaines) et avec les partenaires.

## **MISSION PRINCIPALE**

Sous la supervision du Chef de Mission, le.la coordinateur.rice projet est responsable de la mise en œuvre de la stratégie opérationnelle pays dans sa zone d’intervention, en lien avec le plan stratégique et la mandat d’ALIMA.

Plus spécifiquement, il.elle est responsable de la mise en œuvre du projet et de contribuer aux résultats fixés pour le projet en fonction de l’évolution de la situation humanitaire et des besoins dans la zone d’intervention et sur la base des objectifs médico-opérationnels préfixés en collaboration avec la coordination, dans le respect des principes humanitaires et du mandat de ALIMA. Il·Elle est le garant ou la garante de la sécurité de ses équipes dans toute sa zone d’intervention. Il·Elle est responsable de l’encadrement des équipes, du suivi des indicateurs programmatiques et des indicateurs contractuels bailleurs et du suivi des dépenses du projet - avec l’appui de la coordination, et de la communication avec les acteurs gouvernementaux et non gouvernementaux en relation avec le projet.

## **ACTIVITÉS PRINCIPALES**

Le CP, avant tout, doit:

- agir en lien avec le mandat d’ALIMA, les principes humanitaires et le principe de “do no harm / ne pas nuire”.
- Respecter la stratégie opérationnelle définie avec les autres coordinateurs (collaborer avec les autres acteurs humanitaires, internationaux et gouvernementaux présents dans la zone d’intervention.

1. Définition et planification stratégique
2. Mise en oeuvre des programmes
3. Analyse des données et reporting
4. Encadrement et animation d’équipes
5. Analyse et gestion de la sécurité
6. Développement des outils informatiques

## **Expériences et Compétences**

- Expérience préalable à un poste équivalent en ONG Internationale.

- Une qualification médicale ou paramédicale ou une expérience en gestion de projets médicaux est un atout
- Expérience préalable en gestion d’équipe multiculturelle.

**COMPÉTENCES**

- Capacité d’écoute et empathie.
- Communication facile.
- Capacité d’analyse de contexte, compréhension des enjeux médicaux et humanitaires.
- Animation et motivation d’équipes.

- Capacité à définir des priorités.
- Établissement de réseaux de contacts et capacité à maintenir une posture neutre face à des acteurs opposés dans le cadre d’un même conflit armé.

- Flexibilité.
- Maîtrise de l’outil informatique (GSuite et pack office).

**Langues :**

**Conditions :**

ALIMA prend en charge :

**Duty Station** : EAST JERUSALEM

**Date Posted** : Oct 5, 2026
**Deadline** : Oct 18, 2026

**Org. Setting and Reporting**

This position is located in the Crisis Response Division (CRD) of the Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA). OCHA is the part of the United Nations Secretariat responsible for bringing together humanitarian actors to ensure a coherent response to emergencies. OCHA also ensures there is a framework within which each actor can contribute to the overall response efforts. OCHA's mission is to mobilize and coordinate effective and principled humanitarian action in partnership with national and international actors in order to alleviate human suffering in disasters and emergencies; advocate the rights of people in need; promote preparedness and prevention and facilitate sustainable solutions. This temporary job opening is being advertised for the position of Humanitarian Affairs Officer in East Jerusalem, OCHA OPT. Under the overall supervision of the Deputy Head of Office, OCHA OPT, the incumbent reports to the Head of the Access and Civil-Military Coordination Unit.

**Responsibilities**

Within delegated authority, the Humanitarian Affairs Officer will be responsible for the following duties: • Monitors, analyzes and reports on access and civil-military coordination issues, humanitarian developments, disaster relief/management or emergency situations in assigned country/area.. • Drafts and maintains access and civil-military coordination tools (HNS, AMRF, JOPs etc.) • Supports access and civil-military coordination mechanisms. • Organizes and prepares studies on humanitarian, emergency relief and related issues; organizes follow-up work, including interagency technical review meetings to support policy development work and decision-making on important issues. • Participates in large, complex projects, to include disaster assessment or other missions; assists in the coordination of international humanitarian/emergency assistance for complex emergency/disaster situations and in ensuring the necessary support (e.g. staff, funding, specialized equipment, supplies, etc.); Content Management and Workflow Coordination • Coordinate content management across different duty stations to ensure smooth collaboration and consistent workflows. Quality Control and Verification • Conduct quality control and verification of content as needed, leveraging language skills for country, regional or thematic coverage. Monitor and report any technical problems following standard operating procedures. Provide recommendations for improving the content management process, particularly in response to technological advancements. Client Service • Address client needs by efficiently resolving cases, ranging from simple to moderately complex, using empathy and sound judgment under minimal supervision. **Position:** Head of Support Services – Roster Various Countries

**Reporting Relationship:** Country Representative

**Location:** to be defined according to needs

**Deadline:** 06/11/2026

**Starting date:** according to program needs

**WHO WE ARE**

WeWorld supports people in overcoming emergencies, and it strives to guarantee that everyone can have a decent and dignified life as well as opportunities and a better future. WeWorld works in 15 countries around the world, including in Italy, with more than 120 emergency, humanitarian aid and development projects. Its activities mainly involve women, girls and young people, actors of change in every community for a fairer and more inclusive world. The organization operates in several natural and man-made crisis in various regions of the world. The emergency response, coordinated by the Humanitarian Aid Unit, is composed by multi-sectorial interventions comprising of WASH, EiE, CVA, Food Security, Protection, and others. The organization operates also in protracted crisis with provision of humanitarian aid through a prevention, emergency relief and rehabilitation approach.

**ROSTER**

WeWorld opened this Roster for Heads of Support Services with strong experience in both development and emergency settings and interested in short-notice, short-term deployments in countries where WeWorld may experience unexpected gaps.

Short-listed candidates will be contacted for an interview and selected candidates will become part of WeWorld roster list of professionals who will be contacted when needed.

Being part of the list does not guarantee any immediate of future collaborations with WeWorld. Inclusion on the roster list will be active for the ongoing year and can be renewed upon mutual agreement between WeWorld and the roster list members.

**Job description**

The Head of Support Services is responsible for the management and coordination of all country support services departments, including Finance, Human Resources, Logistics and Procurement. Working closely with the Country Representative, Head of Programmes, Project Managers and relevant headquarters and regional colleagues, the role ensures efficient, compliant and accountable support to programme implementation.

**MAIN TASKS & RESPONSIBILITIES**

- Provide leadership, line management, support and guidance to country Finance, Human Resources, Logistics and Procurement teams.
- Coordinate support services planning, priorities and departmental development in alignment with country objectives and programme needs.
- Ensure that internal policies, standard operating procedures and the Local Operational Manual are developed, updated, contextualised, disseminated and applied.
- Establish effective interdepartmental coordination mechanisms and maintain a proactive link between support services and programme teams.
- Oversee accounting, financial reporting, country budgets, project budget preparation and revisions, expenditure monitoring, cost allocation and country financial planning.
- Supervise procurement and logistics operations in accordance with WeWorld manuals and donor requirements, including assets, fleet, warehouse, stock and base management.
- Ensure compliance with employment regulations and oversee staffing analysis, payroll, insurance, employee benefits, training and capacity development for support services staff.
- Supervise the preparation and management of expenditure verifications, audits, spot checks and internal or donor assessments, ensuring effective collaboration across departments.
- Regularly review support services processes, strengthen oversight and corruption-prevention measures, mitigate operational risks and ensure improvement recommendations are implemented.
- Ensure appropriate archiving, timely delivery of reports and documentation, and effective collaboration with relevant authorities, partners, vendors, donors and other stakeholders.
- When required, support the Country Representative with emergency headcounts and the implementation of safety and security measures in WeWorld premises.

**ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS**

**Qualifications and Knowledge**

- Degree in Economics, Political Science or a related field
- Deep knowledge of the administrative rules and procurement procedures of major international donors, including ECHO, EU, UN and AICS
- Fluency in written and spoken English
- Full professional competency in Microsoft Office Suite, especially Word, Excel and Outlook

**Professional experience**

- At least four years of professional experience in similar roles
- Proven experience managing Finance, Human Resources, Logistics and Procurement functions in international cooperation or humanitarian contexts
- Experience in budgeting, financial reporting, donor compliance, procurement and audit processes

**Skills and Abilities**

- Strong management, planning, reporting, monitoring and organizational skills
- Ability to coordinate, support and train multidisciplinary teams and strengthen staff capacity
- Ability to analyse processes, identify risks and implement practical improvements
- Proactive and dynamic attitude, with the ability to work independently and prevent or resolve problems
- Ability to adapt and work under pressure in complex and multicultural contexts
- Good listening, communication and teamwork skills
- Strong commitment to the Mission of WeWorld and demonstrated integrity in relation to NGO values and ethical standards
- Cultural, gender, religious, nationality and age sensitivity and adaptability, treating all people fairly without favouritism

**DESIRABLE REQUIREMENTS**

- Previous professional experience in one or more WeWorld countries of operation or in comparable humanitarian contexts
- Fluency in Italian
- Fluency in another language relevant to WeWorld countries of operation, such as French, Arabic, Portuguese, Ukrainian, Pashto, Farsi or Swahili

**WHAT WE OFFER**

**Type of contract:** short-term or medium-term assignments, according to program needs

**Economic conditions:** according to WeWorld Expatriates Compensation Policy

Base Salary (3.190€ - 3.790€ gross monthly) + Contributions reflecting role complexity and hardship level of the duty station

**Wellbeing & Inclusion:** One day of paid menstrual leave per month. We promote a positive and inclusive work environment based on psychological safety, respect, and team empowerment

**Health insurance:** covered

**Flight ticket**: covered

**Visa/work permit:** covered

jobs.title: Request For Proposal Field Research Services for the Yegna Gize Impact Study Ethiopia October 2026
jobs.description:
**Request For Proposal**

**Field Research Services for the Yegna Gize Impact Study**

**Ethiopia**

**October 2026**

## **Procurement Summary**

**Item Details**

RFP title Field Research Services for the Yegna Gize Impact Study

Supplier type Research or data-collection agency

Contract type Framework/on-call arrangement using task orders

Geographic scope Tigray, Amhara, Oromia, Sidama, Central Ethiopia and South Ethiopia

Anticipated contract period October 2026 to September 2027

RFP issue date 5 October 2026

Proposal deadline 12 October 2026

Submission email suppliers@girleffect.org

Proposal validity 90 days

## **Who We Are**

Girl Effect is an international non-profit organization dedicated to addressing challenges faced by adolescent girls and youth in Ethiopia. Operating in the country since 2013, the organization leverages Social and Behavior Change (SBC) strategies, combining media and on-the-ground interventions to tackle various societal issues and empower young people. Girl Effect Ethiopia created the youth brand Yegna in 2014 and, since then, has reached over 10 million people through multiple products, outreach programs, girl networks, and research pieces done all for the betterment of adolescent lives.

We create safe spaces for girls, sharing facts and answering questions about health, nutrition, education, relationships, etc. And we use innovative technology so we can reach girls at scale. We arm girls with the skills to negotiate and redefine what they are told is possible, so every girl can choose to be in control of her body, her health, her learning and livelihood.

When a girl unlocks her power to make different choices that change her life, it inspires others to do so too. She starts a ripple effect that impacts her family, community, and country.

That’s the Girl Effect.

## **Background**

Yegna Gize, meaning “Our Time” in Amharic, is a Girl Effect Ethiopia programme that builds on the Yegna brand and its experience of using media, storytelling, role modelling, and community engagement to influence positive social and behavioural change among young people. Yegna Gize focuses specifically on youth economic empowerment, with an emphasis on improving young people's aspirations, mindsets, skills, access to opportunities, and pathways towards employment and entrepreneurship.

Over the programme period, Yegna Gize seeks to contribute to improved economic opportunities and livelihood outcomes for young people in Ethiopia by addressing barriers related to employment, entrepreneurship, skills development, social norms, and mindsets. The programme works with young people, schools, communities, government institutions, civil society organisations (CSOs), private-sector actors, role models, and other relevant stakeholders to create an enabling environment for youth to pursue viable economic pathways.

The programme is implemented across six regions of Ethiopia: Tigray, Oromia, Amhara, Central Ethiopia, Sidama, and South Ethiopia. Through a combination of youth-centred interventions, partnerships, capacity strengthening, communication and social and behavioural change approaches, Yegna Gize aims to strengthen young people's knowledge, skills, confidence, aspirations, networks, and access to employment and entrepreneurship opportunities.

Key areas of Yegna Gize programming include:

- Youth employment and transition to work: Supporting young people to access internships, work-based learning, employment opportunities, and other pathways into the labour market.
- Entrepreneurship and enterprise development: Strengthening entrepreneurial knowledge, business skills, growth mindsets, and access to support for young people interested in starting or growing businesses.
- Skills and mindset development: Building practical, transferable, entrepreneurial, and employability skills, alongside confidence, aspirations, resilience, and positive attitudes towards work and entrepreneurship.
- Peer-to-peer and youth support mechanisms: Establishing and strengthening youth groups and peer-support approaches that enable young people to learn from and support one another.
- Role modelling and mentorship: Connecting young people with role models, mentors, entrepreneurs, and other influential individuals who can provide inspiration, guidance, and practical exposure to different livelihood pathways.
- School-based engagement: Working with schools, teachers, students, and relevant stakeholders to promote entrepreneurship, creativity, growth mindset, career aspirations, and awareness of economic opportunities.
- Youth-centred media and social and behavioural change communication (SBC): Using Yegna's established multimedia and storytelling platforms to challenge limiting norms, promote positive attitudes towards work and entrepreneurship, and increase young people's awareness and uptake of available opportunities.
- Partnerships and systems strengthening: Working with regional and local government structures, CSOs, private-sector actors, educational institutions, and other stakeholders to strengthen the ecosystem supporting youth economic empowerment.

Girl Effect works with local partners to contextualise and implement interventions according to regional realities and the needs of young people. The programme therefore combines national-level approaches with locally relevant implementation, allowing interventions to respond to the different economic, social, cultural, and institutional contexts across the six regions.

### **Yegna Gize Programme Impact Study**

As the programme progresses, Girl Effect Ethiopia intends to commission an independent Impact Study of Yegna Gize to assess the extent to which the programme has contributed to changes in young people's knowledge, skills, attitudes, aspirations, behaviours, access to opportunities, and economic outcomes.

The study is expected to generate credible evidence on the effectiveness, relevance, and contribution of Yegna Gize interventions and to identify which approaches are working, for whom, under what conditions, and why. The findings will inform programme learning, adaptation, accountability to stakeholders and donors, and future programming and scale-up decisions.

The selected agency will therefore be expected to develop and implement a rigorous and contextually appropriate study methodology that captures both quantitative and qualitative evidence, where appropriate, and considers the diversity of young people, intervention types, implementation approaches, and regional contexts within Yegna Gize. The study should generate actionable evidence and recommendations that can strengthen the programme's contribution to sustainable youth economic empowerment in Ethiopia.

Girl Effect is looking to engage a qualified agency to recruit, train, and deploy experienced data collectors across the specified geographic scope, and to manage the full data collection cycle, from fieldwork through to data analysis and submission in line with Girl Effect Ethiopia's tools, sample design, and quality standards.

## **Who You Are**

**The ideal candidate/Agency will:**

- Have demonstrated experience managing field-based data collection for household, community, or individual-level surveys in Ethiopia, ideally on youth, gender, education, livelihoods, or social behaviour change topics.
- Maintain, or be able to rapidly build, a roster of vetted, experienced enumerators with local language coverage and cultural familiarity across some or all of the six Yegna Gize regions (Tigray, Amhara, Oromia, Sidama, Central Ethiopia, South Ethiopia), including hard-to-reach and pastoralist areas.
- Have hands-on experience with mobile data collection platforms, particularly SurveyCTO, and the ability to train enumerators on tool use ahead of each deployment.
- Demonstrate robust field supervision and data quality assurance practices — spot-checks, back-checks/call-backs, and real-time progress monitoring against a sample plan.
- Have in-house or readily available capacity for data cleaning, processing, and first-level quantitative and/or qualitative analysis, with clear documentation of methods.
- Be able to mobilize and scale data collection teams on short notice against a recurring, on-call task-order structure, without compromising quality or timeliness.
- Show a genuine commitment to Girl Effect's mission and values, with a demonstrated understanding of child/adolescent safeguarding standards appropriate to research involving youth.
- Be highly organised, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple concurrent task orders across different regions.

## **What You will do**

**2.1 Geographic Coverage**

Data collection will take place across 6 regions and 60+ woredas, including hard-to-reach and pastoralist areas. Exact woreda-level assignments will be shared with the selected agency alongside each task order, together with the corresponding sample size and tool set.

**2.2 Sourcing, Vetting, and Onboarding of Data Collectors**

The agency is responsible for building and maintaining a roster of qualified, experienced data collectors who can be deployed against Girl Effect Ethiopia's task orders. This includes:

- Recruiting data collectors with relevant prior experience in household or community-level data collection, ideally on similar topics (e.g., health, gender, youth, social behavior change).
- Ensuring appropriate local language coverage and cultural familiarity for each assigned region/woreda, including pastoralist communities.
- Verifying qualifications, references, and prior fieldwork experience before onboarding.
- Maintaining a sufficient bench of vetted collectors to meet fluctuating task-order demand without delays.
- Ensuring the data collectors are given a functioning tab and are trained on the use of survey CTO.

**2.3 Training**

The agency will organize and deliver training for all data collectors before each deployment, covering:

- Use of Girl Effect Ethiopia's data collection tools and mobile data collection platform.
- The sample design and how it translates into fieldwork assignments.
- Data quality, ethics, consent, and child/adolescent safeguarding protocols appropriate to the population being surveyed.
- Logistics, reporting lines, and escalation procedures for field issues.

Girl Effect Ethiopia will provide technical content on the tools and safeguarding standards; the agency is responsible for organizing, scheduling, and delivering the training itself, and for confirming collector competency before deployment (e.g., through a short practical assessment or pilot/pre-test).

### **2.4 Deployment**

Data collectors will be deployed per task order, which Girl Effect Ethiopia will issue for each data collection round/moment. Each task order will specify the woredas/regions, sample size, tools, timeline, and any round-specific instructions. The agency is responsible for:

- Assigning trained collectors to each task order based on location, language, and availability.
- Managing collector logistics (travel, accommodation, safety/security arrangements as applicable) within hard-to-reach and pastoralist areas.
- Providing day-to-day field supervision.

### **2.5 Data Quality and Timeliness**

The agency is accountable for the quality and timeliness of data collected under each task order, including:

- Real-time monitoring of data collection progress against the sample plan and timeline.
- Quality assurance mechanisms such as spot-checks, back-checks/call-backs, and review of flagged or inconsistent entries.
- Prompt escalation and resolution of fieldwork issues (e.g., inaccessible households, refusals, tool malfunctions) that could affect data quality or timelines.
- Regular progress reporting to Girl Effect Ethiopia (proposed: daily or weekly, to be agreed) showing completion rates by woreda/region.

**2.6 Data Analysis and Submission**

Upon completion of each round of data collection, the agency will:

- Clean and process the collected data.
- Conduct analysis as specified in the task order.
- Submit the final clean dataset (in the agreed format), any cleaning/analysis syntax or code, and a summary report to Girl Effect Ethiopia within the timeline specified in the task order.

## **Responsibilities**

The Hiring Organization and the selected Consultant/agency will have the following division of roles:

**Activity Girl Effect Ethiopia Contracted Agency**

Data collection tools & sampling frame Provides (already designed) Reviews & confirms understanding

Data collector recruitment Sets qualification criteria; final sign-off Sources, screens candidates

Training Provides technical/content input; approves training plan Organizes and delivers logistics

Task orders Issues task order per round/moment Deploys collectors against task order

Fieldwork supervision Spot-checks and technical backstopping Day-to-day field supervision

Data quality assurance Defines quality standards; conducts audits Implements real-time QA checks

Timeliness tracking Reviews progress dashboards Reports daily/weekly progress against timeline

Data cleaning & analysis Reviews and validates Cleans, processes, and produces first-level analysis

Submission Receives final dataset & report Submits clean dataset, syntax/code, and summary report

## **Deliverables**

Specific deliverables for the duration of the engagement will include:-

1. Roster of vetted, trained data collectors, updated and available on an ongoing basis.
2. Training plan and completion records for each deployment.
3. Field deployment plan per task order (collector-to-woreda assignment).
4. Data collection progress reports (per agreed frequency) per task order.
5. Quality assurance reports (back-check/spot-check findings and resolutions).
6. Clean, validated datasets with accompanying documentation.
7. First-level analysis and summary report per task order.

Deliverables will be accepted when they meet the applicable task order, agreed quality standards and Girl Effect’s written feedback.

The agency must correct substantiated quality issues attributable to its work at no additional fee.

## **Expected Commitment**

This engagement is structured as a framework/on-call arrangement: the agency will be expected to mobilize data collectors on a per-task-order basis over the contract period between October 2026 and September 2027, with the frequency and scale of rounds varying according to program needs. Each task order will specify its own scope, sample, and timeline.

## **Management**

The Consultant will have a primary point of contact within the Evidence & Insight team.

## **Procurement Timeline**

- Terms of Reference Published: **Oct 5, 2026**
- Deadline for Proposal Submission: **Oct 12, 2026**

## **Proposal Submission**

### Interested Consultant/agency should submit a maximum 10-page proposal that includes the following:

- ### **Technical Proposal**

- A CV or organizational profile outlining previous work and experience relevant to field data collection, enumerator training and management, and data analysis, particularly within the Ethiopian context and specifically highlighting experience across the Tigray, Amhara, Oromia, Sidama, Central Ethiopia, and/or South Ethiopia regions, including hard-to-reach or pastoralist areas where applicable.
- A brief overview of your understanding of Girl Effect's mission and the objectives of this assignment, and your proposed methodology — covering enumerator sourcing and vetting, training approach, field supervision structure, data quality assurance mechanisms (e.g., spot-checks, back-checks), and your approach to data cleaning and first-level analysis.
- Examples of at least two to three previous data collection and/or analysis assignments completed within the specified regions, demonstrating comparable scale, topic area, and quality outcomes.
- Reference — Provide at least three references for similar contracts with a description of the service provided, the value of the contract, and the contract periods of performance.
- **Financial Proposal**
- Please provide your proposed fee in **ETB**, including the total cost for impact the study assignment, along with a detailed breakdown by deliverable, aligned with the activities outlined in the Scope of Work for the region(s) you are applying to cover. Ensure that all applicable taxes are clearly itemized in your proposal.

## **Evaluation Criteria**

Evaluation will follow three stages:

- Pre-screening
- Technical evaluation
- Financial evaluation
- ### **Technical Evaluation – 70%**

**No. Technical Evaluation Criterion Weight**

1\. **Relevant Organizational Experience in Impact Evaluation, Research and Data Collection 15%**

2\. **Understanding of Yegna Gize Programme and Assignment / TOR 10%**

3\. **Proposed Research Methodology and Impact Evaluation Approach 20%**

4\. **Sampling, Fieldwork and Data Collection Strategy 10%**

5\. **Technical Capacity, Quality Assurance, Team Expertise and Operational Feasibility 15%**

**Total Technical Score 70%**

- **Value for Money / Financial Competitiveness – 30%**

The financial scoring is based on the **total evaluated cost**, while also checking whether the proposed budget is sufficiently detailed and realistic across key cost categories such as personnel, training, fieldwork, travel/logistics, data management, analysis and reporting.

GE is not liable for any cost incurred during the award/contract preparation, submission, or negotiation of the award/contract. All submitted documentation and/or materials shall become and remain the property of GE, and Technical & Financial proposals will need to be submitted as a separate document.

Girl Effect may request clarifications, interviews, presentations, reference checks, due diligence or best-and-final offers.

The lowest-priced proposal will not necessarily be selected.

## **General and Commercial Terms**

- **Framework and task orders:** The successful agency will sign Girl Effect’s applicable framework agreement. Work may begin only after an authorised task order has been issued. The framework does not guarantee any minimum volume or value of work.
- **Contracting and Payment:** The successful agency will sign Girl Effect’s applicable agreement. Payments will be linked to the satisfactory delivery and written acceptance of agreed milestones and receipt of a correct invoice. Girl Effect may withhold acceptance pending correction of material quality issues.
- **Pricing, taxes and expenses:** Prices must be quoted in Ethiopian Birr and remain firm during the proposal-validity period. Taxes and approved reimbursable expenses must be itemised separately. Girl Effect will deduct or account for taxes as required by Ethiopian law. Unapproved costs will not be reimbursed.
- **Intellectual property and data ownership:** Subject to the final agreement, Girl Effect will own the commissioned outputs, research data, instruments, documentation and analysis produced under the engagement. The agency may not reuse, publish or disclose these materials without Girl Effect’s prior written approval.
- **Confidentiality and data protection:** The agency must use personal and confidential information only for this assignment, apply appropriate technical and organisational safeguards, promptly report incidents and securely return or delete data when instructed.
- **Safeguarding, ethics and conduct:** The agency and all assigned personnel must comply with Girl Effect’s safeguarding, informed-consent, ethical research, anti-fraud, information-security and supplier-conduct requirements. Required checks and training must be completed before deployment.
- **Personnel and subcontracting:** Changes to key personnel and the use of subcontractors require Girl Effect’s prior written approval. The agency will remain responsible for the quality, conduct and performance of all subcontracted work.
- **Conflicts of interest:** Bidders must disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest.
- **Equal opportunity:** Girl Effect is committed to equal opportunity and encourages submissions from organisations with strong local knowledge and diverse professional and cultural backgrounds.
- **Right to award:** Girl Effect may seek clarification, negotiate, amend or cancel the process, reject any or all proposals, award all or part of the requirement, appoint more than one agency or make no award. Girl Effect will not reimburse proposal-preparation or negotiation costs.
- **Proposal validity:** Proposals must remain valid for 90 days from the submission deadline.

jobs.title: Consultancy to support development of NORCAP Expert Reporting System
jobs.description:
## Introduction to NORCAP

NORCAP is part of Norwegian Refugee council (NRC), and has a mission is to improve aid to protect and empower people affected by crises and climate change. With expertise in the humanitarian, development, and peacebuilding sectors, we collaborate with local, national, and international partners on finding solutions that meet the needs of people at risk.

## Context of the assignment

NORCAP is working on development of an internal expert reporting system (ERS) that will tie together reporting sources within one MS Fabric workspace. In the first phase of the project we have worked on collecting, analysing and prioritizing our requirements, designed the data architecture and created user profiles.

This assignment will support the second phase of the project, where we will create a data architecture within MS Fabric, and develop and test a minimum viable product of the system.

## Objective of the assignment

This assignment will support the NORCAP in:

- Organizing the MS Fabric workspace for the reporting system, integration of data sources from various NRC /NORCAP systems, creation of relevant data flows and semantic models.
- Piloting solutions (MVP) for surveying and data analysis, testing, collecting and integrating feedback.
- Creating and piloting relevant analytical tools and dashboards.
- Piloting AI powered search for data sorting and RAG within the expert reporting system.
- Documenting processes for users and admins in an ERS manual.

## Scope of work for the assignment

Please see the Terms of Reference attached for the scope of work.

## Expected Outputs and Timeline

Key deliverables of the assignment:

- Updated architecture and data model document
- Operational Fabric workspace with a working survey pipeline
- Operational analytics model (dashboards/business analytics)
- AI assistant MVP capable of semantic search and summarization of qualitative variables/fields in reports
- User documentation – admin and user guides

Please see the detailed list of expected outputs in the attached Terms of Reference document.

The schedule will be agreed upon with the consultant(s). The timeframe for the work is between October and December 2026. The estimated time for the assignment is 50 days. NORCAP reserves the right to make changes to the schedule.

## Required Qualifications for the Consultant(s):

- At least 5 years of relevant professional experience:
- Demonstrated experience integrating enterprise source systems, including HR, CRM, ERP, ITSM, and survey platforms, into cloud-based data platforms. Experience with Oracle HR systems, Freshworks/Freshdesk, Microsoft 365/SharePoint, and Kobo Toolbox is considered an advantage.
- Experience with Azure Data Factory / MS Fabric
- Demonstrated experience designing and developing Power BI semantic models, dashboards and reports.
- Experience creating testing and documenting copilot AI agents
- Extensive experience with reporting in international humanitarian and development sector
- Experience in data management and knowledge management approaches
- Experience in communication, facilitating workshops, and collecting inputs from users and stakeholders.
- Knowledge of NRC and/or NORCAP ICT systems is an asset.

**About Prosper Global**

Barely enough is not enough for anyone. Prosper Global is a humanitarian organization working alongside communities facing conflict, climate change, and economic hardship to meet urgent needs and create the conditions for lasting progress. Today's challenges demand new solutions, so we pair local knowledge with global resources to help communities build what's needed, test what's possible, and scale what's proven so that people everywhere can pursue a full life on their own terms. In 2026, we changed our name from Mercy Corps to Prosper Global, to reflect our belief that when every community can prosper, all of humanity moves forward.

## **The Department**

The People Team ensures that Prosper Global has the people, strategies and learning that will enable it to be a world-class, cutting edge, humanitarian organization, creating transformational change in the world. We do this through the recruitment, retention and development of the best global talent. Our aim is to drive strategic thinking and planning at all levels of the organization; create a robust body of research to guide us internally and externally and steward the organizational culture. To achieve this, we align conversations on learning; keep the organization focused on what has the greatest impact; leverage our comparative advantages in the crowded and competitive international relief and development landscape; and assure we are constantly learning from our work and the external environment.

## **The Position**

The Senior Compensation and Benefits Advisor – Europe & Strategic Initiatives designs and delivers compensation, benefits, and performance management frameworks that support a diverse workforce across European markets and globally.

This role develops and implements total rewards strategies that enhance the organization’s ability to attract, retain, and incentivize top talent from the private sector, impact investing, and tech sectors. With a strong emphasis on performance management and value creation, the role ensures that compensation and benefits structures are aligned with organizational outcomes and impact objectives. They partner closely with global teams, regional leadership, and HR team members to ensure that compensation and benefits frameworks are market-relevant and performance-driven.

Working closely with senior leadership, the role drives the design and execution of compensation and benefits frameworks and tools. They build global HR capacity and provide strategic advisory support. A strong focus is placed on data-driven decision-making, pay equity, and continuous improvement in line with evolving business and investment priorities.

The position serves as a strategic partner, strengthening cross-functional collaboration and ensuring that total rewards approaches are aligned, performance-oriented, and scalable across global operations.

## **Essential Responsibilities**

**Strategy, Planning & Continuous Improvement**

- Champion and operationalize the organization’s People Strategy, ensuring alignment between pay practices and innovation objectives.
- Partner with leadership to define and execute a forward-looking total rewards and performance management strategy, linking compensation to financial, operational, and impact performance.
- Drive continuous improvement initiatives by identifying gaps, inefficiencies, and opportunities across compensation and benefits programs and processes.
- Influence organizational and regional strategies through data-driven compensation insights that support growth, equity, and impact.
- Lead the design and implementation of scalable, globally consistent compensation and benefits frameworks and tools.
- Build and maintain strategic external partnerships.

**Compensation, Benefits & Performance Advisory**

- Familiar with different compensation structures and statutory benefits across Europe, bring working knowledge and practical experience.
- Design, implement, and refine global salary structures, grading frameworks, and pay policies aligned with market competitiveness and organizational goals.
- Lead regular market benchmarking and salary analysis to ensure competitive, equitable, and compliant pay practices.
- Drive improvements in job evaluation, role architecture, and pay-for-performance methodologies.
- Integrate compensation frameworks with performance management systems, ensuring clear links between individual performance, growth outcomes, and reward.
- Develop and harmonize benefits strategies across European jurisdictions, ensuring competitiveness, compliance, and employee well-being.
- Stay on top of employment law in European countries with Prosper Global presence, so the organization can proactively adapt.
- Provide strategic advisory support to leadership on compensation, performance calibration, workforce planning, and organizational design.

**Strategic Improvement Projects**

- Design and implement key improvement initiatives that align Prosper Global's compensation and benefits with the organization’s strategic direction, including:
- Partner with Prosper Global Europe HR and Talent Acquisition to support strategies to attract and retain high-performing professionals across Europe from private sector and impact investing backgrounds.
- Develop performance-related pay principles and establish incentive structures to align with organizational growth and impact metrics.
- Support operationalizing the organization’s framework to global mobility to ensure compliance, employee retention, and equitable compensation decisions. Own and implement the organization’s global mobility workstream, including reviewing and advising on requests, with executive, HR, and legal input.
- Develop metrics, dashboards, and reporting frameworks to track performance, inform decisions, and support continuous improvement.

**Communication, Influence & Stakeholder Engagement**

- Communicate compensation and benefits initiatives clearly to internal stakeholders, strengthening understanding and engagement.
- Partner with innovations teams, HR, and leadership to ensure alignment between talent, performance and reward strategies.
- Build internal capability through coaching and guidance on compensation, benefits, and performance management best practices.
- Collaborate with Talent Acquisition to position total rewards as a competitive advantage in attracting top-tier talent in private markets.

**Personal Leadership & Organizational Values**

- Demonstrate resilience, adaptability, and professionalism in complex and dynamic environments.
- Promote innovation by encouraging new approaches to problem-solving within organizational frameworks.
- Foster a high-performing, inclusive team culture focused on learning, accountability, and innovation.
- Uphold high ethical standards and model organizational values in all interactions.

**Safeguarding Responsibilities**

● Actively learns about safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work.

● Practices the values of Prosper Global including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members.

● Encourages openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options.

### **Supervisory Responsibility**

None.

### **Accountability**

**Reports Directly To:** Global Compensation and Benefits Director

**Works Directly With:** People Team, Europe HR, Talent Acquisition, and global and regional leadership

### **Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders**

Prosper Global team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.

### **Minimum Qualification & Transferable Skills**

- 5+ years of experience managing total rewards or compensation and benefits programs at a private sector company, investment firm, or development bank.
- Familiar with different compensation structures and statutory benefits across Europe, bringing working knowledge and practical experience.
- Experience managing global programs and designing performance-related pay structures is highly preferred.
- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in Human Resources, Business Administration or related field, preferred.
- English proficiency required.
- Project management skills including the ability to create and execute plans within established deadlines. Strong problem-solving skills, interpersonal skills, and written and verbal communication.
- Strong analytical skills and a thorough knowledge of compensation and benefit plan designs. Ability to understand how to leverage compensation and benefits programs to align with industry best practices

### **Success Factors**

The successful team member will be an avid learner, self-directed, innovative and action orientated. Furthermore, they must have the ability to work independently, employ effective time management skills, handle frequent interruptions and shift priorities, exhibit effective customer service skills and work effectively with a wide variety of individuals including team members based overseas.

They will be able to work onsite and collaborate with team members, deliver compelling designs within the guidelines of specific project objectives and interact professionally and productively with HQ and other global staff. Additionally, the individual will thrive in a fast-paced environment prone to rapid change and be willing to increase his/her responsibility level in the assigned areas.

The most successful Prosper Global team members have a positive approach, a strong commitment to teamwork and personal accountability, and the ability to be flexible and ensure effective communication is a priority in all situations.

### **Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions**

The position is based in UK or Netherlands and may require occasional travel to support country programs, which may include travel to insecure locations where freedom of movement is limited and areas where amenities are limited.

### **Ongoing Learning**

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development

### **Team Engagement and Effectiveness**

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

Prosper Global is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law.

**Safeguarding and Ethics**

Prosper Global is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC **and have signed on to** [**the Interagency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme**](https://www.schr.info/the-misconduct-disclosure-scheme). We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to [Prosper Global Code of Conduct Policies](https://www.mercycorps.org/who-we-are/ethics-policies) and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct elearning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Prosper Global Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@prosperglobal.org).

jobs.title: Community Conservation Coordinator – Gabon
jobs.description:
**Report to:** Technical Director
**Location:** Libreville, Gabon
**Country Program**: Gabon
**Position Type**: Full-Time
**Collaborators:** Regional Right and Communities team, Community and Conservation Team, MEL Teams, Environment and Social Safeguards Team, relevant departments of institutional partners, notably the ANPN and the Ministry of Water and Forests, Finance, Logistics, Human Resources, and Administration departments
**Expected Travels:** WCS project sites in Gabon (national parks: Ivindo, Lopé, Mayumba, Loango, and other sites depending on the projects)

**Job Summary**

The Community Conservation Coordinator is responsible for defining, implementing, and monitoring WCS Gabon’s community conservation strategy.

As part of WCS’s broader Rights and Communities team, he or she ensures that conservation initiatives are grounded in human rights-based approaches and aligned with WCS strategies, policies, and standards at the national, regional, and global levels.

The incumbent coordinates community activities at WCS project sites, supervises field teams, and builds strong relationships with local communities and institutional partners to foster active and inclusive participation in conservation efforts.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Development and implementation of the community conservation strategy:**

- Develop and adapt WCS Gabon’s national community conservation strategy to the local context.
- Support the development and implementation of community strategies at the site level.
- Identify priorities for community engagement and promote initiatives that strengthen community support for conservation goals.
- Contribute to the revitalization and operation of the Community-Based Local Management Committees (CCGL).
- Ensure coordination with the ANPN to guarantee alignment with national guidelines.
- Ensure consistency between community activities and other program components (biomonitoring, law enforcement, tourism, etc.).

**Coordination and Supervision of Field Teams**

- Supervise technical assistants, project managers, research assistants, and field teams involved in community activities.
- Plan and monitor the implementation of field activities.
- Monitor the implementation of activities by partners and contractors.
- Provide technical support to the teams and resolve operational challenges.

**Training and capacity building**

- Train field teams in community-based conservation approaches and outreach methods.
- Develop appropriate educational tools and materials.
- Strengthen the teams’ skills and performance through regular monitoring.

**Engagement and Community Relations**

- Build and maintain trusting relationships with local communities, community leaders, and local authorities.
- Promote inclusive and respectful community participation in conservation initiatives.
- Ensure adherence to ethical principles of respect for individuals, benevolence, and justice.
- Ensure that free, prior, and informed consent is systematically sought for any activity involving communities.
- Ensure the quality of community activities (local governance, livelihoods, environmental education).
- Ensure that community feedback is taken into account, particularly through complaint management mechanisms.

**Monitoring, Evaluation, and Reporting**

- Ensure that activities comply with WCS’s community conservation standards and national regulations.
- Contribute to the implementation of tools for monitoring and controlling activities.
- Support the design and implementation of socioeconomic studies and data collection activities.
- Produce regular reports on activities.
- Help draft funding proposals and document best practices.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

- Master’s degree or equivalent in social sciences, rural development, conservation, natural resource management, anthropology, sociology, or a related field.
- At least 7 years of relevant professional experience, including at least 3 years in roles involving coordination, team supervision, or program/project management.
- Substantial experience in designing and implementing community-based conservation approaches, local development, or community-based natural resource governance.
- Proven experience working directly with rural communities and Indigenous peoples, including in facilitating participatory processes and multi-stakeholder consultations.
- Experience in operational planning, monitoring work plans and indicators, and supervising teams and/or implementing partners.
- A solid understanding, backed by practical experience, of rights-based approaches, inclusive participation, and the principles of FPIC, social safeguards, and grievance mechanisms.
- Experience collaborating with government agencies, civil society organizations, and/or international organizations.

**Skills and Qualities**

- Strong skills in managing, coordinating, and supporting teams, including remotely.
- Ability to translate a strategy into priorities, work plans, and operational results at the site level.
- Excellent facilitation, communication, negotiation, and constructive conflict management skills.
- Ability to analyze and synthesize information, particularly socio-economic data and information relevant to program planning.
- Very strong writing and reporting skills.
- Fluency in French; ability to work in English strongly preferred.
- Willingness to travel frequently to WCS sites in Gabon.

**Strengths**

- Professional experience in Gabon or Central Africa.
- Knowledge of protected area governance issues and community representation/consultation mechanisms.
- Experience with projects funded by international donors.
- Experience contributing to the design of projects or funding proposals.

jobs.title: Point of Care Ultrasound Advisor W/M
jobs.description:
Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organization created in 1971 that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters.

The advisor helps shape medical and operational policies and strategy by contributing expertise in their specialty and providing support for their implementation.

**General context**

The vision of Point-of-Care Ultrasound (POCUS) integration in MSF is to ensure that clinicians, both locally hired and international mobile staff, have the knowledge, guidance, and access to proper and selective use of this diagnostic tool as part of the comprehensive management of patients, in remote and low-resource settings. There are currently POCUS Regional Managers in DRC, Yemen, Bangladesh, CAR, and South Sudan – who work intersectionally to cover POCUS needs for those regions.

Following the POCUS TIC, which focused on the expansion, scale-up, and integration of Point-of-Care Ultrasound (POCUS) into MSF operations - particularly by engaging national clinical staff - MSF France has decided to continue this initiative by recruiting a dedicated focal point within the Medical Department. This position will provide high-quality hands-on training, support ongoing POCUS implementation, and focus on strengthening local capacity within OCP projects, with possible support to other Operational Centres as needed and feasible.

To realize these ambitions, the POCUS advisor will continue to work closely with the MSF OCP medical referents, operational cells, the projects, and the other intersectional POCUS advisors and regional managers to support POCUS implementation. The advisor will develop POCUS strategies adapted to the mission needs and coordinate section-wide POCUS needs.

**I. PLACE IN THE ORGANISATION**

The POCUS advisor is hierarchically accountable to the Head of the Diagnostic Pole and is functionally accountable to the Clinical Integration & Innovation Coordinator (POCUS Project Coordinator) and OCP Dep-DirMed. S(He) works in close collaboration with the clinical referents in the medical department working on improvement of clinical reasoning. S(He) will coordinate with the POCUS program within the Diagnostic Imaging Working Group, through the Clinical Integration & Innovation Coordinator.

While in the field, the advisor operates under a matrix system: hierarchical and functional accountability remain at headquarter level, with operational coordination and contextual alignment ensured with the mission management team. Technical guidance remains under the responsibility of the Medical Department.

**II. OBJECTIVES OF THE POSITION**

The OCP POCUS advisor will:

- Develop, execute, and evaluate implementation of ongoing POCUS training programs within OCP, with specific strategies for building of local POCUS teaching capacity.
- To act as the Ultrasound advisor in the medical department and for project staff in the Operational Center Paris, with a general knowledge on the principles of POCUS within MSF and be able to educate members of the OC regarding the program philosophy and setup.
- To collaborate with the Diagnostic Image Working Group, the POCUS project team, medical department and other sections to improve POCUS usage and impact.
- Global oversight of all POCUS activities for MSF France and support intersectional coordination with the larger POCUS program team.
- Serve as MSF France ultrasound referent for relevant work with MSF Logistique, OCP Biomeds, and OCP Telemedicine cases, in coordination with the POCUS Team.

**III. MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Technical Referent FOR POCUS**: Provide OCP specific and intersectional coordination and support as a technical referent. Main tasks include annual Strategy Mapping, budgeting, point person for MSF Logistique/Biomed/MedRef/Cells/Telemedicine/Medical supervisors as first contact.

- Promote best practices in ultrasound use and strengthen clinical reasoning to ensure appropriate indication, interpretation, and integration of POCUS findings into patient management.
- Serve as a technical referent of all ultrasound-related telemedicine cases within OCP projects. Liaise with the experts on telemedicine, as well as the Clinical Case Coordinators, regarding specific ultrasound cases within OCP. Actively feedback to MSF and telemedicine the necessary changes needed to improve the program.
- Advocate with local medical teams for appropriate usage of telemedicine platform and where appropriate, provides training to clinicians on how to use MSF telemedicine platform for ultrasound cases.
- Directly advise and oversee ultrasound equipment validation, procurement, maintenance, daily use, and repair/replacement with international supply centers, biomed teams, and field teams for all relevant MSF projects in OCP
- Identify solutions and improvements in MSF supply, procurement, and biomedical support as pertains to ultrasound equipment, through ultrasound device reviews, direct feedback to the Biomed WG, development of educational material, and training of relevant staff.
- Serve as an OCP consultant on POCUS. Sit in internal medical or operations meetings as relevant, and liaise with key stakeholders in that OC (medical units, cell, referents, BioMed, HR, etc)
- Provide Quarterly updates on OCP POCUS activities for relevant training partners, platforms, and line managers to ensure integration across the MSF movement with other clinical training programs and priorities.

**POCUS Implementation**: Analyze new/ongoing training requests, organizing training, briefing, and supporting external POCUS trainers and IMS staff in the field, close collaboration with existing field POCUS users, quality control, and longitudinal follow up.

- Throughout the year, the MSF OCP POCUS Advisor will have a highly mobile role, with frequent field visits dedicated to hands-on POCUS training and capacity-building activities. The objective is to provide POCUS training to new OCP projects, consolidate existing skills through multiple training cycles in projects with ongoing POCUS implementation, and place particular emphasis on developing local POCUS facilitation capacity in regions with limited access.
- Provide hands-on field implementations whenever feasible – combining technical ultrasound expertise (image acquisition and interpretation) with medical/clinical expertise (development of appropriate clinical care based on ultrasound results).
- Directly evaluate suitability of POCUS implementation in MSF projects, advise teams on training scope, tailor and develop a project-appropriate curriculum, and then coordinate the context specific field-based deployment itself.
- Serve as technical mentor for any POCUS facilitators deployed in field sites under their responsibility, including technical briefing, ongoing support, and debriefing
- Liaise with POCUS Pool manager for facilitator recruitment, matching, and planning

**Quality, Integration, Sustainability**: The advisor has a role in evaluating the quality of POCUS use in MSF, it’s integration into clinical care, and the sustainability of POCUS within OCP projects. Identifying, developing, and mentoring future leaders, superusers, and facilitators is a core component of the role.

- The advisor has a role in creating local and regional POCUS facilitation capacity. Main tasks include identifying key clinicians for Training of Facilitators, co-facilitation, in-project superusers; and working with POCUS-trained sites on creating teaching opportunities for these clinicians. Eventually, development of POCUS Country Managers and decentralized leadership opportunities should be prioritized.
- Develop in project POCUS Focal Points, and support them in daily clinical use of POCUS in MSF OCP Projects, identifying and mitigating challenges.
- Advise and support medical coordinators and project teams towards longitudinal, sustainable, and responsible integration of high-quality POCUS utilization in all relevant MSF projects in OCP, including budgetary and training planning annually.
- Directly support, advise, and supervise field teams in the clinical management effected by ultrasound use. This includes direct feedback for management of complex clinical cases, linking with external Telemedicine experts, and ensuring additional context-specific POCUS training with longitudinal implementation for all OC within the region of responsibility.
- Contribute to the evolving ultrasound program within MSF including integrating POCUS appropriately into clinical guidelines and providing evidence-based updated information for clinical care WGs in MSF. To serve as liaison for the pediatric WG.
- Oversee the transformational impact of POCUS through high-quality implementation of ultrasound to change clinical care on a project, regional and international level, and identify areas for improvement

**Profile**

**Education**

Certified licensed Medical doctor

POCUS competency certificate from recognized academic institution (or MSF comparable certificate) is required.

**Experience**

Minimum 3 years working experience with extensive experience in performing and reporting/interpreting ultrasound of both children and adults. Experience teaching Point-of-Care-Ultrasound to clinicians.

Clinical experience in several of the following areas: paediatrics, obstetrics, adult and infectious disease (TB/HIV)

Baseline expertise in module-specific ultrasound in several areas (cardiac, pulmonary, OB), with willingness to learn/achieve competency in multiple other modules as needed

**Languages**

Fluency in either English/French essential, minimum level = B2 in both languages. Proficiency in another language is desirable, particularly one related to the countries involved in the project.

**General skills**

- Essential computer literacy (word, excel and ppt);
- Excellent networking and communication skills
- Demonstrated experience and excellence in teaching and training MSF
- Clinical Guidelines,
- Point-of-Care-Ultrasound Advanced competency
- Ability to motivate and lead medical colleagues and to translate strategy and
- policy into operational practice in the field
- Flexibility to travel and to spend up to 50% or more of time on work related
- travel to project sites
- Enthusiastic, motivated and independent; able to work with minimal
- supervision in challenging contexts
- Experience working in resource limited settings with MSF or with equivalent
- humanitarian organization
- Good written and oral communication skills
- Prior research experience is desirable

**Conditions**

**Status:** 12 month fixed-term contract part-time (50%). Management position based in Paris requiring frequent travel to the field and to other MSF medical departments. Remote work in accordance with MSF’s current policies (2 days/week).

**Conditions:** €56,1k gross annual salary paid over 13 months (pro-rated for part-time). Supplementary health insurance fully covered by Doctors Without Borders. Meal vouchers with a face value of €12 (60% covered by Doctors Without Borders). 50% coverage of public transportation subscription.

**Position available:** as soon as possible

Job Title: Human Resources Officer (HR Officer)

Department: Human Resources Department

Line Manager: HR Manager

Work Location: Syria - Aleppo

Contract Type: Full-Time

## About Amal Organization For Relief& Development

Amal is a non-profit Syrian non-governmental organization established and registered in Turkey on 6/6/2014, to provide life-saving aid and services to the most vulnerable people, strengthening their resilience, advocating for their basic rights, and also contributing to providing recovery and revitalization programs for societies that war turned

**Job Summary**

The HR Officer is responsible for managing and executing day-to-day personnel and recruitment operations within the organization, ensuring full compliance with internal policies and applicable labor laws. The role holder contributes to talent acquisition, maintains employee data efficiently with strict confidentiality, and supports the implementation of safeguarding and dignity-at-work policies within the humanitarian context.

**Key Responsibilities**

Personnel & Record Management

- Establish and maintain up-to-date, structured, and secure physical and digital personnel files for all personnel categories (full-time staff, contractors, volunteers, and daily workers).
- Track and manage monthly attendance, leave requests, and absences, ensuring thorough verification before submission to the Finance/Payroll department.
- Verify that all required onboarding documentation, credentials, and reference check forms are completed by new hires prior to contract signing.

**Recruitment & Selection**

- Organize and facilitate interview panels and technical assessments, managing all candidate communications professionally.
- Conduct background and reference checks for selected candidates.

**Onboarding & Capacity Building**

- Coordinate induction and onboarding programs for new hires to facilitate smooth integration and promote understanding of organizational policies.
- Collaborate with the Protection/Safeguarding team to ensure all new staff sign the Code of Conduct and Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) policies.

**Employee Relations & Reporting**

- Provide daily HR support to staff members, responding to queries regarding policies, leave entitlements, and benefits.
- Submit regular (weekly/monthly) operational reports to the HR Manager covering recruitment progress, staffing movements, and operational challenges.
- Maintain strict confidentiality regarding all personal, financial, and administrative data belonging to the organization and its employees.
- Perform any other job-related duties assigned by the Line Manager within the scope of work.

**Qualifications & Experience**

Academic Background:

- Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Human Resources, Social Sciences, or a related field.

Work Experience:

- 2 to 4 years of progressive experience in Human Resources (experience within local or international NGOs is strongly preferred).

**Skills & Competencies**

- Technical Knowledge: Strong understanding of HR principles, labor regulations, and operational practices relevant to the humanitarian sector.
- Data Management & Confidentiality: High capacity to handle sensitive information with discretion and manage secure archiving systems.
- Technical Proficiency: Advanced skills in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook).
- Languages: Fluency in Arabic and English (advanced written and spoken proficiency).
- Adaptability: Ability to perform under pressure within fast-paced emergency response environments.

### **EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES AND NON-DISCRIMINATION:**

Amal is dedicated to promoting equal opportunities in our recruitment practices so maintaining equal opportunities and nondiscrimination is a foundational principle:

Discrimination based on race, color, religion, gender, age, disability, social status, origin, pregnancy, genetic characteristics, or any other grounds is strictly prohibited across all aspects of employment, organizational practices, work arrangements, salary, dismissal, and service provision.

Preference among employees or candidates for employment may be granted based on objective criteria and qualifications essential for the job, and such preferences do not constitute discrimination.

In instances where specific provisions apply to contracting concerning gender, qualifications, working conditions, or contract type (daily, weekly, seasonal), rights and responsibilities remain equitable

**PROTECTION FROM HARASSMENT AND SEXUAL EXPLOITATION:**

Amal Organization is dedicated to fostering a secure and respectful environment for employees and those they interact with in the course of their work. The recruitment, retention, and promotion of staff are inherently tied to maintaining high ethical standards and a commendable reputation. Amal Organization unequivocally prohibits and will not tolerate (zero tolerate) any form of discrimination, abuse, harassment (whether sexual or otherwise), based on race, ethnicity, religion, national origin, gender, age, sexual orientation, marital status, citizenship status, disability, or military status. Employees and associated personnel must strictly refrain from engaging in any discriminatory, harassing, or abusive behavior, whether physical, sexual, verbal, or otherwise, both within and outside the Amal organization.

**CHILD SAFEGUARDING:**

Amal Organization recognizes that ensuring a secure environment for children begins with the recruitment of qualified employees equipped with the necessary competencies and skills to perform their duties effectively, safely, and reliably. This commitment is geared towards safeguarding children from all forms of exploitation, labor, or potential harm.

In our dedication to children's safety, our selection process incorporates comprehensive background checks, underscoring our unwavering commitment to preventing abuse and ensuring the well-being of children.

**SAFEGUARDING EMPLOYEE RELATIONS:**

In line with our commitment to fostering a secure and respectful work environment, the post holder is required to adhere to Amal's anti-harassment policy. This policy underscores our dedication to safeguarding the well-being of our staff by promoting a workplace culture characterized by mutual respect and professionalism. The role holder plays a vital part in this commitment, ensuring a supportive atmosphere and actively contributing to the safeguarding of their colleagues through the promotion of positive employee relations.
