jobs.description:
- **Do you want to do work that really matters? Help us end avoidable blindness.**
- **Full time, Fixed Term Role based in Mombasa, Kenya.**
- **Closing Date: Friday, 16th October 2026.**

**ABOUT THE FRED HOLLOWS FOUNDATION**

The Fred Hollows Foundation is an international development organisation working to prevent blindness and restore sight. We continue to carry on the legacy of Professor Fred Hollows, who believed every person had the right to quality eye care, no matter where they live. The Foundation is known around the world as an organisation that works with purpose and determination. With a reputation for excellence, we are well known for making change happen.

The Foundation has grown to work in more than 25+ countries throughout Africa, South Asia, Southeast Asia, the Middle East and the Pacific, as well as Australia. The Foundation has restored sight to more than 3 million people worldwide. We have an ambitious five-year strategic plan that aims to take us even closer to realising our vision of a world in which no person is needlessly blind, or vision impaired and Indigenous Australians exercise their right to sight and good health. To find out more about our work, please visit our website [https://www.hollows.org](https://www.hollows.org/)

**THE OPPORTUNITY**

The Regional Coordinator (RC) is the area programme manager for Kenya’s Coast Region and a senior member of the Kenya Country Office. The role leads the planning, coordination and delivery of The Fred Hollows Foundation’s integrated eye health programme across Mombasa, Taita Taveta, Kilifi and Kwale counties, including partner private eye hospitals. In line with The Foundation’s strategy, the coordinator works with governments and other stakeholders to improve eye care services, strengthen the workforce, support data-informed decisions, enhance sector coordination and advance eye health as a social and economic priority.

The RC oversees the day-to-day work of a multidisciplinary programme, finance and operations team, including resource allocation, team cohesion, partnership management, effective communication and compliance with donor and organisational requirements.

The role is accountable for regional team performance, operational outcomes and delivery of multiyear partnership commitments across the four counties.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**The Regional Coordinator will own the outcomes of:**

1. **Project Delivery, design and alignment: The coordinator will:**

- Lead the implementation of FHF Kenya program at the regional and county level.
- Ensure integration of FHF Projects to attain seamless reporting, M&E and engagement for partners.
- Coordinate technical support from Nairobi Managers, Advisors and team to ensure seamless support
- Execute one plan that encompasses all FHF supported initiatives and with delegated budget and administrative responsibility for his/her area.
- Coordinate work plans, fund transfers, and budget alignment to meet project targets and ensure accountability by the partners and various project teams.
- Mobilize the regional team to co-design with partners relevant eye health projects in line with country strategy in collaboration with Nairobi teams.

1. **Coast Region Eye Health Leadership and Advocacy; Stakeholder Engagement and Representation:** Lead the Foundation’s regional engagement with county governments, particularly Departments of Health, and represent it at key eye health forums. Build partnerships across executive, technical and community levels, strengthen regional visibility, monitor sector developments, and engage health management teams and other stakeholders to improve eye care, expand equitable access and reduce avoidable blindness in Kenya.
2. **Team leadership:** Plan regional activities, coordinate technical and operational support with Nairobi teams, foster teamwork, and manage delegated budgets and procurement within agreed thresholds. Lead project reviews and manage, motivate, coach and mentor Coast Region staff through capacity development aligned with FHF policies and strategy.
3. **Service Efficiency:** Develop tools to track project results and milestones, support partners to use surgical outcomes data for continuous quality improvement, and promote equitable access and participation for women, people with disabilities and other marginalised groups.
4. **Technical Support and Learning:** Facilitate the implementation of technical support activities to the partners supporting the implementation of the integrated projects in collaboration with national MOH and other county-level health service departments and units.
5. **Partnerships:** Develop and enhance partnerships at regional level among key stakeholders and supports capacity building among local partners and health professionals for common approaches and synergy towards impact.

**WHAT YOU’LL NEED TO SUCCEED**

- Bachelor’s degree in Public Health, Social Sciences, International Development or Health Systems.
- At least 5–6 years’ experience managing health programmes in an INGO context.
- Experience in strengthening public health service delivery programs, Innovation in health service delivery, partner technical support and capacity building, advocacy, health systems performance and eye health programming.
- Excellent knowledge of; national/county/community-level issues impacting health services.
- Experience in project management and collaboration with ministries of health in one or more areas of health systems.
- Experience with devolved health sector and working with County Government; experience working with Coastal counties is and added advantage.
- Demonstrated capacity to build and maintain productive working relationships with a wide network of partners and stakeholders.
- Considerable experience in leading the delivery of donor-funded programmes and working with donor organizations and development partners.
- Experience managing staff and working and collaborating in a matrix organisation.
- Superior presentation skills (both written and oral) and ability to communicate technical materials to a mix of audiences using print, electronic, and presentation media.

***Please Note: The Foundation does not provide relocation support for this position. The successful candidate must be based in the Coast Region by the role’s start date.***

**How we recognise your contribution**

Through our internal programs and employee benefits we aim to create an environment where you will feel supported and empowered. Whether your focus is on continuous learning, professional development or finding an environment which enables you to thrive while balancing family or personal commitments, we have a range of programs in place to support you.

[To find out more about our benefits click here](https://www.hollows.org/au/careers)

jobs.title: Countering the Financing of Terrorism Expert (Remote)
jobs.description:
**Mission and objectives**

The United Nations Office of Counter-Terrorism (UNOCT) was established by the General Assembly in June 2017. The Office has five main functions: (a) provide leadership on the General Assembly counter-terrorism mandates across the United Nations System; (b) enhance coordination and coherence across the 43 Global Counter-Terrorism Coordination Compact entities to ensure the balanced implementation of the four pillars of the Strategy; (c) strengthen the delivery of United Nations counter-terrorism capacity-building assistance to Member States; (d) improve visibility, advocacy and resource mobilization for United Nations counter-terrorism efforts; and (e) ensure that due priority is given to counter-terrorism across the United Nations System and that the important work on preventing violent extremism is firmly rooted in the Strategy.

**Context**

The United Nations Office of Counter-Terrorism (UNOCT), through its Global Coordinated Programme on Detecting, Preventing and Countering the Financing of Terrorism (CFT Programme), supports Member States in strengthening their capacities to prevent and counter the financing of terrorism in line with relevant United Nations resolutions, international obligations and applicable international standards. Within this framework, UNOCT provides specialized technical assistance, policy support and capacity-building to strengthen legal, regulatory, institutional and operational frameworks relevant to countering the financing of terrorism, including support for the effective implementation of Financial Action Task Force (FATF) standards. In Turkmenistan/Uzbekistan, UNOCT is supporting national efforts to strengthen implementation of the revised FATF Recommendation 8 concerning the protection of non-profit organizations (NPOs) from potential abuse for terrorist financing purposes. The initiative responds to identified gaps related to the assessment of terrorist financing risks affecting the NPO sector, the application of targeted, proportionate and risk-based approaches to supervision and oversight, the adequacy of relevant legal and regulatory frameworks, inter-agency coordination, and practical engagement with the NPO sector. The project will support a targeted review of relevant legal, regulatory and institutional frameworks and provide technical assistance to a sector-specific assessment of terrorist financing risks affecting NPOs. This will include support to the development and application of risk criteria and analytical approaches, review and analysis of relevant information and data, identification of key vulnerabilities and risk factors, and preparation of substantive findings and recommendations for national consideration. The initiative will further support the development of practical guidance on risk-based and proportionate supervision of the NPO sector, including approaches to identifying different levels of risk, applying proportionate supervisory measures and periodically reviewing the adequacy of relevant measures. It will also include targeted consultations, capacity-building activities and technical workshops with competent national authorities and other relevant stakeholders, with a view to strengthening national understanding, coordination and practical implementation of the revised Recommendation 8. The UN Volunteer will serve as a substantive Expert within the project and will be expected to provide high-level technical and analytical expertise across these workstreams. The assignment will require strong professional knowledge of FATF Recommendation 8 and terrorist financing risks affecting the NPO sector, demonstrated experience with risk-based regulatory and supervisory approaches, strong analytical and drafting capabilities, and the ability to engage effectively with senior and technical government counterparts, subject-matter experts and other relevant stakeholders. The assignment will be implemented in close coordination with relevant national counterparts and in cooperation with the Eurasian Group on Combating Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism (EAG) Secretariat and the United Nations Regional Centre for Preventive Diplomacy for Central Asia (UNRCCA), in line with the approved project framework and relevant international standards.

**Task description**

Under the direct supervision of the Programme Management Officer, the UN Volunteer will serve as a substantive Expert and provide specialized technical and analytical expertise for the implementation of the project “Strengthening the Implementation of FATF Recommendation 8 in Turkmenistan/Uzbekistan”. The Expert will contribute to the effective delivery of project activities, with particular emphasis on the assessment of terrorist financing risks affecting the non-profit organization (NPO) sector, risk-based and proportionate approaches, relevant legal, regulatory and institutional frameworks, and the development of practical guidance and targeted capacity-building. The Expert will contribute to substantive research and analysis, technical inputs to the NPO-sector terrorist financing risk assessment, review of relevant legal and regulatory frameworks, development of practical guidance and analytical products, preparation and delivery of capacity-building activities, and the formulation of practical recommendations to support national follow-up. In particular, the UN Volunteer will undertake the following tasks:

• Conduct substantive research and analysis on FATF Recommendation 8, terrorist financing risks affecting the NPO sector, risk-based and proportionate approaches, and relevant international and regional standards, guidance and good practices, and translate analytical findings into practical inputs for project implementation.

• Provide specialized technical inputs to the assessment of terrorist financing risks affecting the NPO sector, including the development and application of appropriate risk criteria and analytical methodology; collection, review and analysis of relevant qualitative and quantitative information; identification of vulnerabilities, risk factors and differentiated levels of risk; and preparation of substantive findings and practical recommendations.

• Conduct and substantively contribute to the review of legal, regulatory and institutional frameworks relevant to the implementation of FATF Recommendation 8 in Turkmenistan/Uzbekistan, including analysis of existing measures against the requirements of the revised Recommendation 8 and identification of areas where risk-based and proportionate approaches could be further strengthened.

• Prepare high-quality analytical and technical products, including background papers, briefing notes, comparative analyses, technical inputs, presentations, talking points, substantive meeting materials, findings and recommendations related to the implementation of FATF Recommendation 8.

• Contribute substantively to the development of practical guidance and methodological materials for competent national authorities on risk-based and proportionate approaches to the NPO sector, including the identification of different levels of terrorist financing risk, application of proportionate risk-mitigation and supervisory measures, and periodic review of the adequacy of such measures.

• Provide substantive expertise for the preparation and delivery of consultations, technical meetings, workshops and capacity-building activities for competent national authorities and other relevant stakeholders, including the development of training materials, case-based exercises and technical presentations, and delivery or co-facilitation of substantive sessions, as appropriate.

• Engage with relevant national authorities, subject-matter experts, representatives of the NPO sector and other relevant stakeholders to support the collection and validation of information, facilitate substantive technical exchanges and ensure that project outputs are informed by relevant national context and international standards.

• Review and provide substantive comments on technical documents, analytical products and other materials prepared in the context of the project, and ensure the quality, consistency and technical accuracy of relevant project outputs within the Expert’s area of expertise.

• Support the formulation of practical, evidence-based recommendations for national consideration, drawing on the findings of the risk assessment, legal and regulatory analysis, consultations and capacity-building activities, and taking into account the need for measures to be targeted, proportionate and risk-based.

• Contribute to substantive coordination with the Eurasian Group on Combating Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism (EAG) Secretariat, the United Nations Regional Centre for Preventive Diplomacy for Central Asia (UNRCCA), relevant national counterparts and other partners, as required for the implementation of project activities.

• Prepare substantive records and follow-up documentation arising from consultations, workshops and technical meetings, and contribute to monitoring and documenting progress, results, lessons learned and recommendations relevant to project implementation.

• Perform other related substantive duties within the scope of the assignment, as required.

**Qualification Requirements**

• Master's degree in law, economics, finance, international relations, security studies, public policy, criminal justice, or another field directly relevant to anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT).

• At least 7 years of progressively responsible professional experience in anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT), with substantial experience specifically related to CFT, FATF standards, financial integrity, or related regulatory and policy frameworks.

• Demonstrated professional experience in the implementation and practical application of FATF standards, including FATF Recommendation 8 and risk-based and proportionate approaches to protecting NPOs from terrorist financing abuse.

• Demonstrated experience in conducting or substantively supporting terrorist financing risk assessments, sectoral risk assessments or comparable analytical exercises, including the development or application of risk assessment methodologies, analysis of qualitative and quantitative information, identification of vulnerabilities and risk factors, and formulation of risk-based recommendations.

• Demonstrated experience conducting legal, regulatory, policy or institutional analysis in the AML/CFT field, including the review of relevant frameworks and the development of practical recommendations, guidance or methodological tools.

• Demonstrated experience providing specialized technical assistance and substantive advice to government authorities, financial intelligence units, regulators, law enforcement bodies and/or other competent national authorities on AML/CFT-related matters.

• Experience designing, developing and delivering specialized capacity-building activities, technical workshops, consultations or training for government officials and other professional audiences.

• Proven experience drafting, reviewing and quality-assuring high-quality technical and analytical products, including policy papers, legal or regulatory analyses, risk assessment products, practical guidance, methodological materials, technical reports, recommendations and training materials.

• Strong knowledge of terrorist financing risks affecting the NPO sector and of targeted, proportionate and risk-based approaches under the revised FATF Recommendation 8.

• Excellent analytical, research, drafting, editing and reporting skills, including the ability to translate complex technical and regulatory issues into clear, practical and actionable recommendations.

• Demonstrated ability to engage effectively with senior and technical government counterparts, subject-matter experts and other relevant stakeholders in a multicultural and politically sensitive environment.

• Fluency in English and Russian is required, including excellent drafting and communication skills in English and the ability to conduct substantive professional exchanges in Russian.

• Ability to work independently, exercise sound professional judgement, manage multiple substantive workstreams and deliver high-quality outputs within agreed deadlines.

• Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and virtual collaboration tools.

UN Volunteer entitlements and allowances:

The purpose of the allowances and entitlements paid to UN Volunteers is to enable them to sustain a secure standard of living in line with United Nations standards without incurring personal costs. The allowances are in no way to be understood as compensation, reward, or salary in exchange for the UN Volunteer’s service. Contingent on specific eligibility criteria, location of the volunteer, and contractual type and category, the payment of allowances will begin from the date of Commencement of Service.

For information specific to your assignment, please see below:

\- Monthly Living Allowance (Remote Arrangement): USD 1,200 (global average, per month). The final amount will be calculated based on the selected candidate’s country of residence using the UNV Allowance Calculator: [https://app.unv.org/calculator](https://app.unv.org/calculator).

\- Entry lump sum (one-time payment): USD 200

\- Medical and life insurance: Cigna Private Insurance

\- Annual leave: 2.5 days accrued per calendar month

\- Certified and Uncertified Sick Leave in accordance with UNV Conditions of Service

jobs.title: Consultant national – Enquêteur / Collecteur de données temporaire
Finanzsachbearbeitung Projektabrechnung (m/w/d)
jobs.description:
Als **Deutsches Rotes Kreuz (DRK)** ist es unsere Aufgabe, für die Menschen da zu sein und ihnen zu helfen – allein nach dem Maß der Not. Schon seit mehr als 150 Jahren leistet die Rotkreuz- und Rothalbmond-Bewegung umfassend Hilfe für Menschen. Egal was wir tun und wo wir tätig sind, immer sind unsere sieben Rotkreuzgrundsätze: Menschlichkeit, Unparteilichkeit, Neutralität, Unabhängigkeit, Freiwilligkeit, Einheit und Universalität handlungsleitend.

Im **DRK-Generalsekretariat in Berlin** gestalten Sie die zukünftige Ausrichtung des DRK e.V. als nationaler Rotkreuz-Gesellschaft und Spitzenverband der Freien Wohlfahrtspflege mit. Sie tragen täglich dazu bei, dass Menschen in Deutschland und weltweit Hilfe erhalten – allein nach dem Maß der Not.

## Finanzsachbearbeitung Projektabrechnung (m/w/d)

Zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt suchen wir Sie als **Finanzsachbearbeitung Projektabrechnung (m/w/d).**

Die Stelle ist im Bereich Internationale Zusammenarbeit des DRK-Generalsekretariates verankert und dem Team Strategisches Engagement zugeordnet.

Die Beschäftigung erfolgt in Vollzeit (39h/wöchentlich). Das Beschäftigungsangebot ist auf 2 Jahre befristet.

### Ihre Aufgaben:

Finanztechnische Bearbeitung von DRK-Projekten im Bereich „Internationalen Zusammenarbeit“, das bedeutet im Einzelnen:

- Mitwirkung bei Budgeterstellung und Budgetmonitoring der Auslandsprojekte
- Erstellung von Mittelanforderungen beim Zuwendungsgeber und Kontrolle der Zahlungseingänge
- Überweisung von Vorschüssen an die Auslandsdelegationen, Abrechnung von Auslandskassen, Kassenbelegablage und -archivierung
- Enge Kommunikation mit den Finanzdelegierten in den DRK-Auslandsdelegationen, zum Teil in englischer Sprache
- Führen der Projektstammakte, Rechnungsbearbeitung sowie das Anfertigen von Zahlungs- und Buchungsanweisungen
- Abrechnung der Projekte, Erstellung von Zwischen- und Verwendungsnachweisen unter Beachtung geberspezifischer Vorgaben (AA, ECHO, BMZ, GIZ, KfW und weiteren Zuwendungsgebern)
- Begleitung interner und externer Prüfungen
- Mitwirkung an vorbereitenden Jahresabschlussarbeiten für den Bereich Internationale Zusammenarbeit

### Wir erwarten:

- Erfolgreich abgeschlossene kaufmännische/verwaltungstechnische Ausbildung oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation
- Erfahrung in der Abrechnung drittmittelfinanzierter Projekte (AA, ECHO, BMZ, GIZ, KfW und weiteren Zuwendungsgebern)
- Fundierte Buchhaltungskenntnisse
- Kenntnisse im Zuwendungsrecht
- Beherrschung einer Finanzbuchhaltungssoftware, z.B. SAP und/oder Microsoft Dynamics 365
- Routinierter Umgang mit Office 365 und vertiefte Kenntnisse in Excel
- Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift
- Eigenverantwortliches und selbstständiges Arbeiten, Teamfähigkeit
- Identifikation mit den Grundsätzen des Roten Kreuzes

### Wir bieten:

- Eine verantwortungsvolle und vielseitige Tätigkeit im Zeichen der Menschlichkeit
- Raum für Ihre berufliche und persönliche Entwicklung in einem erfahrenen und engagierten Team
- Faire Arbeitsbedingungen gemäß DRK-Reformtarifvertrag
- Vergütung nach Entgeltgruppe 9b
- 30 Urlaubstage im Jahr und Heiligabend und Silvester arbeitsfrei
- Eine attraktive betriebliche Altersvorsorge (VBL)
- Flexible Arbeitszeitmodelle, um die Vereinbarkeit von Beruf und Familie zu gewährleisten
- Mobiles Arbeiten (bei Vollzeit bis zu zehn Arbeitstage monatlich) mit Präsenz am Standort Berlin je nach Arbeitsanforderung
- Urban Sports Club, Headspace, Babbel und weitere individuelle Angebote zur Gesundheitsförderung und Weiterentwicklung

Arbeitsort ist das DRK Generalsekretariat, Carstennstr. 58, 12205 Berlin.

jobs.title: Chef de la délégation régionale Tchad/Cameroun (H/F/X)
jobs.description:
**ENVIRONNEMENT DU POSTE**

**Tchad**

La Croix-Rouge française (CRF) a mené des actions au Tchad à partir des années 1970, et dispose d’une délégation permanente sur place depuis 1998. De 2001 à 2009, les premiers programmes menés par la CRF portaient sur l’accès à l’eau et l’assainissement dans la ville de N’Djamena, puis ce programme s’est étendu à partir de 2004 dans la région du Logone Occidental.

En 2010, la CRF a monté une intervention pour lutter contre la malnutrition dans la région du Batha. A partir de 2012, elle a ré-axé son approche en intégrant des éléments pour une amélioration de la sécurité alimentaire et de la santé maternelle et infantile.

Aujourd’hui, la CRF est présente dans les régions du Mayo Kebbi-Est et dans la ville de N’Djamena, en étroite collaboration avec la CRT et les services déconcentrés de l’Etat.

**Cameroun**

La délégation de la Croix-Rouge française (CRF) au Cameroun accompagne la Croix-Rouge camerounaise (CRC) de manière permanente depuis 2011 sur demande de la CRC comme le prévoient les principes du Mouvement CRCR. Le renforcement des capacités de la CRC est au cœur de son mandat : c’est la raison et la condition de sa présence et de toutes ses actions sur le territoire. La première collaboration entre la CRF et la CRC a été établie en 1967 avec l’ouverture d’une délégation permanente de la CRF au Cameroun, à Yaoundé en 2009.

Actuellement, la CRF intervient dans les régions de l’Extrême Nord et de l’Est dans les domaines de la santé/nutrition, la GRC, le soutien au développement de la société nationale, la cohésion sociale. Elle dispose d’un bureau de coordination à Yaoundé (Région du Centre), d’une sous-délégation à Maroua et d’une base à Batouri.

**FINALITÉ DU POSTE** :

*Le/la chef.fe de délégation est chargé.e de la création et de la mise à jour d’une stratégie adéquate aux besoins humanitaires et politiques de financements et en ligne avec les expertises de la CRF et des Sociétés nationales hôtes (SNH). S’assure que les différents coordinateurs sous sa responsabilité mettent en place les plans d’action y relatifs, en priorisant l’appropriation des projets et des procédures de gestion de ces projets par les SNH. La CRF doit pouvoir se retirer des opérations au profit des SNH, et jouer un rôle d’assistance technique à moyen terme.*

**MISSIONS ET ACTIVITÉS DU POSTE**

- **Élabore une stratégie adéquate au contexte et orchestre sa mise en oeuvre auprès des coordinateurs, et en lien étroit avec les SNH:**
- Déploie la stratégie de la CRf
- S’assure de la mise en œuvre effective des opérations
- **Assurer la disponibilité des moyens pour que chaque position clé atteigne ses objectif:**
- S’assure de la bonne gestion des moyens financiers et logistiques de la délégation
- Assure une gestion des ressources humaines constructive, positive et respectueuse de la loi
- Assure une communication efficace et un reporting régulier et de qualité
- Assure la sécurité du personnel et des marchandises sur sa délégation
- Veille à la capitalisation des connaissances, méthodes, outils liées aux programmes et contexte d’intervention
- **Soutenir le Développement des Sociétés Nationales et leur autonomisation progressive en gestion administrative et financière (CRT et CRC)**
- Met en place une feuille de route NSD claire et temporalisée avec les SNH sur trois ans
- Assure la direction et l’animation efficace et dynamique de la délégation, en lien avec celles des SNH

**ENVIRONNEMENT DU POSTE**

MANAGEMENT HIÉRARCHIQUE **:** ***oui***

MANAGEMENT FONCTIONNEL **:** ***oui***

INTERLOCUTEURS PRINCIPAUX **:**

- Interne CRf **:** ***Desk, Coordinateurs.trices et responsables des différents départements support et techniques, chef.fe de sous-délégation / de base et chef.fe de projet, services supports du siège***
- Externe CRf : ***SG des Croix-Rouge du Cameroun et du Tchad (lien important dans le cadre du renforcement des capacités) et autres membres de la gouvernance, les autres acteurs du Mouvement, les autorités locales administratives, les bailleurs des projets en cours, les partenaires techniques et financiers de tout type…***

## **Profil recherché**

**COMPÉTENCES**

- Expérience significative en renforcement de capacités des partenaires et en transfert de compétences
- Expérience dans des contextes de sécurité volatile
- Expérience de l’encadrement d’équipe
- Expérience ou connaissance du Mouvement Croix-Rouge obligatoire
- Maitrise du français et de l’anglais (oral et écrit)

**PROFIL**

- Bac+5 en gestion de projet humanitaire ou formation équivalente
- Master 2, de type Bioforce

### **Informations pratiques**

**Conditions d’emploi**

- **Type de statut** : expatrié
- **Type de contrat** : CDD de droit français/prime de précarité versé en fin de contrat
- **Prime de fin d’année** : équivalent à un 13ème mois au pro-rata au temps de présence
- **Perdiem** : perdiem journalier qui varie en fonction du pays
- **Congés** : 5 semaines de congés payés/an et 21 jours de récupération – Billet d’avion pris en charge à 100% par la CRf pour trajet domicile/mission pour les congés à 6 mois
- **Couverture santé** : CFE + Mutuelle MSH (couverte 100%) – pris en charge à 75% par la CRf
- **Assurance MedEvac/rapatriation** : OUI
- **Autres assurances** : prévoyance (décès-invalidité)

**Résumé**

- **Localisation :** N'Djamena (Tchad) avec déplacements réguliers sur les différents bureaux et bases du Tchad et du Cameroun
- **Durée:** 12 mois
- **A pourvoir** : Décembre 2026

La Croix-Rouge française se réserve la possibilité de clore un recrutement avant la date d’échéance de l’annonce et de dépôt des candidatures. Merci de votre compréhension.

Sans autre contact de notre part dans un délai de 3 semaines, veuillez considérer que nous ne donnons pas de suite favorable à votre candidature.

Candidatures féminines encouragées.

**Formations en ligne :**

Pour mieux connaître le Mouvement Croix-Rouge, nous vous invitons à suivre deux formations en ligne, gratuites et accessibles à tous. La réalisation de ces formations constitue un plus dans votre candidature : W.O.R.C. (World of Red Cross and Red Crescent) : cette formation aborde des sujets tels que l'origine et l'histoire du Mouvement, ses principes fondamentaux, l'emblème, la Fédération internationale, le CICR et les sociétés nationales. Stay Safe, quant à elle, a pour objectif de développer une culture commune de la gestion de la sécurité au sein du Mouvement. Vous trouverez ces cours sur la Plate-forme d’apprentissage de la Fédération Internationale: [https://ifrc.csod.com/client/ifrc/default.aspx](https://ifrc.csod.com/client/ifrc/default.aspx)

jobs.title: Human Resources Advisor - HQ
jobs.description:
**Organisation Background**

Founded in 2011, the International NGO Safety Organisation (INSO) is an international non-governmental organisation that supports humanitarian aid workers by establishing safety coordination platforms in insecure contexts. INSO provides registered NGOs with a range of free services, including real-time incident tracking, analytical reports, safety-related data and mapping, crisis management support, staff orientations and training.

INSO provides daily support to more than 1,500 NGOs operating in 24 of the world’s most insecure countries. INSO is registered in the Netherlands, with its headquarters located in The Hague, a city renowned for its international focus on peace and justice.

**Job Summary**

We are looking for a Human Resources Advisor (HRA) experienced in the humanitarian sector to support a portfolio of Country Offices in West Africa, Latin America, the Middle East, and Southeast Asia.

This role offers the opportunity to combine strategic HR thinking with real operational impact, influence HR practice across diverse contexts, build the capacity of colleagues, and contribute to a stronger, more consistent global HR function.

Based in The Hague, Netherlands, you will be a trusted HR partner to Country Office leadership and HR teams, providing strategic and technical HR advice, strengthening local HR capacity and helping ensure consistent, compliant and effective HR practices. This is an advisory role, combining HR expertise, coaching, problem-solving and collaboration. During exceptional and time-bound situations such as start-ups, emergencies or crises, the HRA also provides hands-on operational support and carries out HR activities. The role requires frequent travel to Country Offices.

**Main Responsibilities**

- Advise and support Country Offices in workforce and organizational planning, including workforce requirements, succession and capacity needs.
- Strengthening HR capacity by coaching managers and HR focal points in applying INSO’s HR policies, procedures and practices.
- Champion compliance, helping Country Offices navigate local labour legislation, INSO policies and donor and audit requirements.
- Monitor data quality in HR systems, and report on trends and identify risks to facilitate decision-making.
- Identify workforce, organizational and people-related risks, trends and opportunities and contribute to global HR projects, policies and organizational improvements.
- Support safeguarding, employee relations and duty of care, working closely with specialist colleagues.
- Visit Country Offices to provide targeted advice, oversight and capacity building.

**Requirements**

- 5+ years of progressive HR experience in an INGO or humanitarian environment, including experience supporting a country office.
- 3+ years of advisory expertise supporting the employment lifecycle, including workforce planning, recruitment, performance management, employee relations, and organizational change.
- Demonstrated experience partnering with managers on workforce, organizational and people-related challenges, translating needs into practical HR solutions..
- Sound knowledge of labour laws, HR compliance and risk management with experience working with donor/audit requirements.
- Ability to analyze HR and workforce data, identify trends and risks, and translate insights into practical recommendations for management
- Experience in reporting using HR systems.
- Confidence and credibility to coach and advise constructively managers and HR colleagues across cultures and at different levels of seniority.
- Fluency in **English**. Good working knowledge of at least another language such as **French, Spanish or Arabic**, required.
- Willingness to travel to Country Offices.

**Nice to Have**

- Master's in HR, Business Administration, or related field.
- Experience working in West Africa, Latin America or Southeast Asia
- CIPD/SHRM or equivalent professional certification.
- Experience in duty of care and psychosocial support frameworks.
- Familiarity with INSO’s vision, mission and values.

**Personal Competencies**

- Initiative – Takes proactive action, anticipates needs, and identifies practical solutions.
- Strategic – Connects strategic thinking with strong operational understanding to support effective decision-making.
- Resilience – Remains effective under pressure, manages competing priorities, and maintains performance in demanding situations.
- Communication – Builds strong relationships and communicates clearly and effectively across multicultural environments.
- Integrity – Demonstrates accountability and commitment to INSO values, safeguarding, confidentiality, and ethical conduct.

**INSO’s Safeguarding Policy**

INSO is fully committed to safe recruitment, selection and vetting of all potential new staff, trustees and volunteers. We ensure rigorous compliance with our Code of Conduct and Safeguarding Policy throughout the recruitment process. INSO is a member of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, and the selected candidate will be required to undergo the relevant misconduct disclosure checks as part of the final hiring steps.

**Terms & Conditions**

Fixed-term (renewable) contract based in The Hague, Netherlands, EUR 5,610 per month plus 8% vacation pay (vakantiegeld), 2.5 days annual leave per month. INSO provides Basic Premium ONVZ health insurance for staff members and their dependents. **The right to live and work in the Netherlands is required for this position**. Be aware that INSO’s employment terms do not include transport and pension benefits.

jobs.title: Malawi Farmer Behavior & Extension Design Lead
jobs.description:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Malawi program, founded in 2016, provides more than 670,000 farmers with quality farm supplies and training. Our office in Malawi is located in Zomba, in the country’s south. One Acre Fund works in Malawi’s southern region, which has the highest concentration of smallholder farmers in the country.

## **About the Role**

The Agronomy & Extension Lead will own the implementation of Malawi’s extension strategy, using HCD and SBC approaches to translate agronomic recommendations into simple, practical and adoptable support for farmers. The role will strengthen extension delivery, training and communication content, and use farmer feedback and impact data to continuously improve our approaches. They will work closely with Field Operations and Innovations to turn validated research into scalable farmer-facing solutions.

## **Responsibilities**

The role combines technical agronomy leadership with the design and management of a practical, farmer-centered extension system.

Own Malawi's agronomy and extension strategy

- Co-design and maintain a multi-year strategy aligned with Malawi’s impact priorities and farmers’ needs.
- Turn the strategy into annual OKRs, budgets, seasonal plans and clear ownership across teams.

Embed extension in Field Operations execution

- Build agronomy and extension priorities into the Field Operations seasonal calendar, training cascade, field tools and performance routines.
- Strengthen the technical capability of Field Managers, Field Officers and other delivery partners through training-of-trainers, coaching and practical support.
- Create clear feedback and support channels so field teams receive timely technical answers and can share implementation challenges and farmer responses.

Own the process of qualitative technical agronomic recommendations

- Use Human-Centred Design, farmer feedback and impact data to develop, test and refine agronomic recommendations.
- Work with Innovations, MEL and global technical teams to assess recommendations against local evidence, farmers’ realities and government guidance before they are scaled.
- Conduct formative research to understand farmers’ needs, behaviours and barriers to adoption.

Design farmer-centered extension and behavior-change interventions

- Translate technical recommendations into simple, memorable and actionable guidance for field teams and farmers.
- Develop extension approaches that use the right mix of group training, demonstrations, coaching and digital channels.
- Use the findings to design, test and improve extension approaches and communication content.
- Apply adult-learning, behavior-change and human-centered design approaches to understand barriers to adoption and ensure content works for different farmer profiles.

Monitor adoption, learning and impact

- Analyze results across farmer groups, locations and delivery channels to identify where recommendations or delivery approaches need to change.
- Lead seasonal learning reviews and maintain clear records of lessons and decisions to continue, adapt or stop interventions or crop offerings.

Build and manage a high-performing team

- Set clear goals, roles and decision-making responsibilities, and hold the team accountable for timely, high-quality delivery.
- Coach direct reports, strengthen the team’s technical expertise and support staff to take on greater ownership.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

Technical Expertise

- A bachelor's degree in Agronomy, Crop Science, Agricultural Systems, Agricultural Extension, Sociology, Anthropology, Design or a related field;
- Experience working in the agricultural sector, ideally with smallholder farmers, is strongly preferred.
- At least 5+ years of relevant professional experience in Agricultural Extension, Human-Centred Design, Social Behaviour Change Campaigns, or Rural Marketing, with experience applying these approaches in the agricultural sector
- Demonstrated experience developing, testing or scaling agronomic recommendations or rural extension interventions.
- Experience using adult-learning, instructional-design, SBCC or human-centered design approaches is strongly preferred

Core skills

- Technical judgment: Able to assess agronomic evidence, identify limitations and translate it into responsible recommendations.
- Farmer-centered design: Able to understand farmer constraints and create practical interventions that improve understanding and adoption.
- Data and learning: Comfortable using qualitative and quantitative evidence to make decisions; strong Excel skills required, with R or Stata as an advantage.
- Strategy and project management: Able to prioritize, build critical paths and keep multiple seasonal workstreams on track.
- Communication: Able to make complex technical information simple and persuasive for field teams, farmers, leaders and external partners.
- Collaboration and influence: Able to work across Field Operations, Innovations, MEL and government-facing teams without relying solely on formal authority.

jobs.title: Caseworker
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.

**Job Overview:** The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to recently arrived refugees and other qualified immigrants to meet basic needs and support client achievement of self-sufficiency. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs, engaging a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements. The Caseworker is expected to follow guidelines and standard practices, connecting clients to services that support wellbeing.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure each client has living essentials such as housing, food, medical care, access to transportation and community orientation
- Purchase necessary items, conduct housing set-ups, airport pick-ups, home visits, grocery orientation, bus orientation and other field-based services related to the immediate needs of newcomers. Lift, transport, drive and move items as needed for program delivery.
- Conduct intake to assess needs. Develop self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with each client. Provide individualized support through direct services, referrals, and advocacy.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals. Address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- Collaborate with colleagues across grants and programs, ensuring that clients access services for which they are eligible. Complete program quality assurance activities to ensure appropriate use of funds.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in social work or related field of study preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- Prior experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations required, including casework and/or pre-arrival services
- Prior experience navigating program eligibility and program requirements; ensuring services are provided and appropriately documented

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build relationships with clients, colleagues and collaborators
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluent in spoken and written English. Proficiency in language(s) spoken by client group strongly desired.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research and problem-solving purposes.
- Ability to transport, lift and move items as needed to set up homes and otherwise support new arrivals. Lifting and carrying of items 50+ lbs, including larger items such as furniture
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.
- Ability to drive a large van or other passenger vehicles, as needed to conduct work.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities. Typically, this position is based at the office 4 days/week and remotely 1 day/week, with potential field work all days.
- Requires schedule flexibility to perform weekend and/or evening work, including but not limited to airport pick-ups.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $26.80/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.description:
**Logistics and Management Services for ITCILO Digitalization of Artificial Intelligence Training of Trainers Event**

In Erbil, Iraq

1 - 5 November 20261

## Background and purpose / Objective for this Service:

### Credit Analysis for MoLSA Staff

The promotion of the Development of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) plays a central role in fostering inclusive economic growth, job creation, and resilience in Iraq. In partnership with the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (MoLSA) and with financial support from KfW, the International Labour Organization (ILO) is implementing the Promotion of the Development of SMEs in Iraq Project.

As part of these efforts, strengthening the capacity of national trainers is important to support digital transformation engagement with SMEs in the context of SME financing and related programmes. The project tailored a TOT training in close coordination with the ITCILO. The ITCILO proposes to adapt its existing Digitalization and AI for Small and Medium Enterprises – Training of Trainers programme to the context of the Promotion of the Development of SMEs project in Iraq. The existing course equips trainers and enterprise support professionals to help SMEs use digitalization and AI to improve productivity, competitiveness and decision-making. Its approach is deliberately business focused, responsible and people-centred: participants first examine business processes, data, skills and organizational readiness before considering AI applications. The course also prepares them to provide training, coaching and advisory services to SMEs.

For Iraq, we recommend retaining this core learning logic while adapting the format, language, cases and tools. The proposed pathway would comprise ten in-country training days delivered through two five-day missions, separated by a supervised field roll-out period:

- Mission 1: five-day intensive Arabic-language ToT, leading to Level 1 certification.
- Field application: trainers pilot the methodology with real SMEs, with remote ITCILO support.
- Mission 2: five-day consolidation, troubleshooting and quality-assurance mission, leading to Level 2 certification for trainers who successfully complete the field application.

This split format allows trainers to test the methodology in real conditions and makes the second mission responsive to actual implementation challenges rather than repeating theoretical content. ITCILO’s engagement would conclude by the end of February 2027, following completion of the final assessment, issuance of Level 2 certificates and handover of the Arabic-language materials, trainer registry and implementation tools to the project. Continued deployment and support of certified trainers would thereafter be managed directly by the project.

### Coordination

jobs.title: Director, Finance
jobs.company: International Centre for Diarrhoeal Disease Research
jobs.description:
icddr,b is an international health research institute based in Bangladesh. Policymakers and practitioners utilise our evidence and expertise to improve health outcomes and prevent premature death and disability worldwide. In recognition of its scientific and humanitarian contributions, icddr,b has received numerous international and national awards, including

- **Gates Award for Global Health (2001):** For its pioneering contributions to global health, including the development of oral rehydration therapy.
- **Independence Award (2005):** For services rendered to the people of Bangladesh.
- **Conrad N. Hilton Humanitarian Prize (2017):** For innovative approaches to addressing health challenges in underserved communities

Since its establishment in 1960, icddr,b’s research focus has expanded beyond cholera and diarrhoeal diseases to encompass a broad range of public-health challenges in Bangladesh and globally.

Our research priorities are organised around nine public-health goals:

- Address health risks related to climate change;
- Address health risks related to gender and sexual and reproductive health and rights;
- Prevent and manage non-communicable diseases;
- Improve healthcare in urban populations and achieve universal health coverage;
- Prevent and control infectious diseases;
- Improve maternal and newborn health;
- Reduce maternal, adolescent and childhood malnutrition;
- Enhance laboratory services and support genomics research; and
- Improve hospital services and clinical research.

## **The Opportunity**

We seek an accomplished, strategic and collaborative Director, Finance to provide leadership and oversight of icddr,b’s financial strategy, operations and governance.

Reporting directly to the Deputy Executive Director, the Director, Finance will lead a multidisciplinary finance team and work closely with the Senior Leadership Team, Division Directors, Principal Investigators and donors to ensure sound financial stewardship and long-term organisational sustainability.

The successful candidate will combine strong professional expertise with integrity, sound judgement and inclusive leadership. The position will ensure effective financial planning, transparent reporting, robust internal controls and adherence to sound financial governance and applicable regulatory requirements.

## **Key Responsibilities**

**Strategic Planning and Development**

- Provide strategic leadership and overall direction for icddr,b’s Finance function, ensuring that financial strategy, resource allocation and financial management are aligned with icddr,b’s mission, research priorities and long-term institutional sustainability.
- Serve as a trusted financial adviser to the Executive Director, Deputy Executive Director, Senior Leadership Team, Finance & Audit Committee (FAC) and Board of Trustees (BOT), providing independent advice and constructive challenge on financial performance, sustainability, funding, investment, risk and major institutional decisions.
- Lead the development and implementation of icddr,b’s long-term financial strategy, multi-year financial plans, annual budgets, forecasts and scenario analyses, translating institutional and research priorities into sustainable financial plans and resource-allocation decisions.
- Provide financial leadership on major research initiatives, institutional programmes, partnerships and funding opportunities, assessing their financial implications, affordability, risks and long-term sustainability.
- Analyse funding patterns, expenditure trends and cost structures to inform strategic decisions and strengthen cost recovery.
- Anticipate changes in the research, donor funding and operating environment and advise leadership on their implications for icddr,b’s financial resilience, funding model, cost structure and future resource requirements.

**Financial Planning and Analysis**

- Lead the preparation of annual budgets, multi-year financial plans, cash-flow forecasts and scenario analyses.
- Lead organisation-wide financial planning and performance management, ensuring effective alignment of resources with icddr,b’s research, programme and institutional priorities.
- Establish consistent budgeting assumptions, guidelines and monitoring arrangements across the organisation.
- Provide financial insight and constructive challenge to Division Directors, Principal Investigators and programme leadership to strengthen resource allocation, financial planning and organisational performance.
- Establish appropriate financial performance measures and provide timely, forward-looking analysis of financial results, funding, expenditure, cost structures, cost recovery and resource utilisation to support management, FAC and BOT decision-making.
- Hold overall accountability for the financial health, integrity and stewardship of icddr,b, ensuring that financial resources are managed effectively, transparently and in accordance with approved strategy and governance arrangements.

**Financial Operations Management and Reporting**

- Oversee accounting, financial reporting, accounts payable and receivable, project finance and related financial operations.
- Ensure that financial information and management reporting provide reliable, timely and decision-useful information for management and governance oversight.
- Provide strategic leadership of icddr,b’s financial governance and control environment, ensuring appropriate policies, delegated authorities, accountability mechanisms and internal controls are established and operating effectively.
- Ensure that accounting policies, financial reporting and practices remain aligned with applicable international standards, including IPSAS, as well as relevant laws, regulatory requirements, donor obligations and icddr,b policies.
- Provide timely financial reports and analysis to the Deputy Executive Director, Executive Director, Division Directors, Board of Trustees and donors, in accordance with established reporting arrangements.
- Promote efficient, responsive and service-oriented financial support across the organisation.

**Financial Systems and Process Improvement**

- Lead the strategic evolution and modernisation of the Finance function, ensuring that its operating model, capabilities, systems and processes remain fit for icddr,b’s evolving research, funding and institutional environment.
- Set the strategic direction for Finance systems, digitalisation, automation, data and management information, ensuring these enable effective financial management, strong controls and informed organisational decision-making.
- Provide strategic oversight of icddr,b’s financial reporting framework and accounting architecture, including the effective application of IPSAS and adaptation to evolving accounting and reporting requirements.
- Sponsor and oversee major Finance transformation and continuous-improvement initiatives, ensuring that investments in systems, processes and capabilities deliver sustainable improvements in efficiency, transparency, control and service quality.
- Ensure that ERP and other financial systems provide integrated, reliable and decision-ready information across icddr,b and support effective financial governance and performance management.

**Project Fund Management**

- Provide strategic oversight of grants, contracts and collaborative research agreements, working with Principal Investigators, Division Directors and programme leadership to ensure sound financial stewardship, appropriate cost allocation and recovery, effective financial management and compliance with donor and contractual requirements.
- Support Principal Investigators and programme teams in proposal budgeting, expenditure planning, financial monitoring and project close-out.
- Ensure appropriate cost allocation, indirect-cost recovery and compliance with donor-specific financial requirements.
- Review and approve project budgets and financial transactions within delegated authority.
- Ensure timely and accurate donor financial reporting and resolve escalated financial and contractual issues.
- Promote constructive collaboration between Finance, research teams, donors and partner institutions.

**Risk Management**

- Oversee material financial risks relating to research funding, institutional sustainability, liquidity, foreign exchange, investments, financial reporting, fraud, compliance and donor obligations, ensuring significant risks are identified, escalated and appropriately managed.
- Maintain appropriate controls to prevent and detect fraud, misuse of funds and material financial misstatement.
- Ensure effective segregation of duties and compliance with delegated financial authorities.
- Oversee financial due diligence on relevant banking institutions, service providers and partners.
- Promote financial accountability, ethical conduct and risk awareness across the organisation.

**Audit and Compliance**

- Provide executive oversight of statutory, external and donor audits and work closely with Internal Oversight, while respecting its independence, to strengthen assurance and ensure timely resolution of material findings and agreed recommendations.
- Support internal audit and assurance activities while respecting the independence of the Internal Oversight function.
- Ensure timely implementation and monitoring of agreed audit recommendations.
- Maintain effective relationships with auditors, donors and relevant regulatory authorities.
- Maintain effective senior relationships with donors, auditors, regulators, financial institutions and other key external stakeholders on significant financial, contractual and regulatory matters.
- Ensure compliance with applicable taxation, regulatory and contractual obligations.

**Treasury Management**

- Oversee cash-flow forecasting, liquidity management, banking relationships and foreign-exchange exposure.
- Oversee liquidity, reserves, investments and other institutional financial resources, ensuring an appropriate balance between financial resilience, risk, return and icddr,b’s strategic priorities.
- Develop and review treasury and investment policies within approved governance arrangements.
- Oversee the prudent management of surplus funds, reserves, endowments and separation funds.
- Report regularly on liquidity, investment performance and treasury risks.

**Leadership and Team Development**

- Lead and develop the Finance function through its management structure, establishing clear accountability and performance expectations across its respective units and ensuring effective integration and collaboration across the function.
- Build a high-performing Finance leadership team with the professional capability, managerial strength and succession depth required to support icddr,b’s evolving strategic and operational needs.
- Foster a culture of integrity, accountability, collaboration, service excellence and continuous improvement across Finance.
- Position Finance as a strategic business partner to icddr,b’s scientific, research, programme and corporate leadership, providing insight, advice and constructive challenge to strengthen organisational performance, research delivery and financial sustainability.
- Lead significant organisational change within Finance and ensure the function continuously develops its capabilities in response to changing technologies, accounting standards, funding models and institutional priorities.
- Represent the Finance function at senior institutional and external forums and contribute to icddr,b-wide strategy, performance, risk and institutional decisions.

## **Qualifications and Experience:**

**Essential Requirements**

- A master’s degree in Accounting, Finance or a related discipline.
- At least 15 years of progressively responsible experience in accounting, finance or financial management, including at least five years in a senior financial leadership role with substantial responsibility for financial strategy, operations, governance and team management.
- Fellowship of a recognised professional accountancy body, FCA, FCCA, FCMA, FCPA is mandatory. Candidates must hold at least one of these designations and maintain current membership in good standing with the awarding professional body.
- Demonstrated experience managing complex, multi-million-dollar budgets and multiple funding sources in an international, donor-funded or comparably complex organisation.
- Substantial experience in financial planning and analysis, accounting, management reporting, treasury, audit, internal controls and financial risk management.
- Demonstrated experience in grant and contract financial management, including donor compliance, cost recovery and financial reporting.
- Strong working knowledge of internationally recognised accounting standards, including IPSAS and/or IFRS.
- Proven experience leading financial process improvement, organisational change and the implementation or optimisation of ERP systems.
- Demonstrated ability to advise executive leadership and communicate financial performance, risks and recommendations to governing bodies or equivalent senior decision-makers.
- Proven ability to lead and develop diverse teams and collaborate effectively with financial and non-financial stakeholders.
- Excellent written and spoken English.

**Desirable Requirements**

- Experience in an international health research institution, university, development organisation, public-health organisation or other not-for-profit institution.
- Formal training or certification in IPSAS and practical experience implementing or transitioning to an international accounting framework.
- Experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365, SAP, Oracle Financials or a comparable ERP platform.
- Experience managing endowments, institutional reserves and investment portfolios.
- Knowledge of Bangladesh’s financial, taxation and regulatory environment.
- Experience working across multiple countries, cultures or regulatory environments.

## **Key Skills**

- Analytical rigour – translates complex financial data into clear, actionable insight for financial and non-financial audiences alike;
- Sound, independent judgement – comfortable making high-stakes financial calls under time pressure or incomplete information;
- Integrity under scrutiny – upholds rigorous controls and ethical standards even under programme or donor pressure;
- Systems thinking – understands how financial decisions ripple across research operations, HR, IT and institutional risk;
- Cross-functional communication – builds trust and negotiates effectively with donors, auditors, regulators, scientists and field teams alike;
- Change leadership – drives adoption of new systems and processes (e.g. ERP, IPSAS) with genuine staff buy-in rather than top-down mandate;
- Coaching and talent development – builds bench strength and succession within the finance function itself;
- Resilience under resource constraint – sustains service quality and team morale through funding volatility or donor-driven change;
- Diplomatic acumen – navigates competing priorities between the Board, donors and scientific leadership without compromising financial discipline; and
- Hands-on digital fluency – works directly and confidently with financial systems, dashboards and data-analytics tools, not just through others.

## **Compensation**

This internationally recruited position offers a competitive salary paid in US Dollars.

The successful candidate will receive an initial three-year contract, including a one-year probationary period. Contract renewal will be subject to satisfactory performance and funding availability.

This role is open to suitably qualified Papua New Guinean National candidates only.

**Program Background**

DT Global is engaged by the Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) to manage Australia’s investment in strengthening the delivery of law and justice services in Papua New Guinea for a 4-year period to 31 December 2027.

APLJ seeks to contribute to PNG’s law and justice sector capacity to provide inclusive, safe, secure and accountable law and justice foundations for peaceful and prosperous communities, equitable economic development and private sector growth.

The program aligns with the Government of Papua New Guinea’s (GoPNG) law and justice sector goal of ‘building peaceful and prosperous communities together’. APLJ will focus on three End of Program Outcomes (EOPOs):

- **EOPO 1 – Community Safety and Access to Justice at the Local Level:** Communities in target locations, especially women, children, persons with disabilities, vulnerable people and those accused of sorcery, have improved access to selected justice and support services.
- **EOPO 2 – Law and Justice Services Supply:** Responsible law and justice sector agencies increasingly provide selected inclusive, responsive, and accountable essential law and justice services in target locations.
- **EOPO 3 – Leadership, Coordination and Accountability:** Responsible law and justice mechanisms demonstrate improved sectoral leadership and coordination of national and subnational law and justice services and improved sector integrity systems.

APLJ has a strong focus on addressing gender equality, disability equity and social inclusion (GEDSI): this includes continued and strengthened attention to Gender Based Violence1 (GBV) and strengthened opportunities for women in leadership, as well as increased focus on the engagement of persons with a disability and other particularly marginalised populations.

The program will continue Australia’s support to law and justice development in up to nine demonstration provinces across Papua New Guinea, including the Autonomous Region of Bougainville (ARoB).

At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact.

For more information, please see [www.dt-global.com](http://www.dt-global.com/)
