jobs.title: Regional Programme and Data Management Associate [Open to Tier 1 & 2 Applicants Only]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The Regional Programme Management Support Unit (RPMSU) at the UNDP Bangkok Regional Hub (BRH) plays a central role in supporting the effective management, oversight, quality assurance, compliance, and performance monitoring of the Regional Programme (RP) and Regional Projects throughout the project lifecycle. RPMSU works closely with programme and project teams to ensure that regional initiatives are designed, implemented, monitored, and reported in accordance with UNDP Programme and Project Management (PPM) standards and corporate compliance requirement while promoting high-quality programme implementation and results delivery.

As BRH enters the implementation phase of the Regional Programme 2026–2029, there is an increasing need to strengthen evidence-based management, portfolio oversight, and proactive performance monitoring. At the same time, corporate requirements related to project transparency, data quality, risk management, quality assurance, results reporting, and audit readiness continue to expand, requiring greater consistency and accuracy in project data management and programme monitoring practices.

In responding to these needs, PMSU has led a series of initiatives under the Project Managers Peer Learning Network and the Regional Programme Digitalization and Automation Initiative to strengthen project management practices, improve access to programme management knowledge, and modernize RP monitoring systems. A key milestone of these efforts has been the development of the Regional Programme Performance Dashboard, which provides an integrated platform for monitoring regional programme delivery, pipeline management, portfolio performance, and management analytics through automated data integration and visualization tools.

To ensure sustainability and continuous improvement of these digital solutions, PMSU seeks a Regional Programme and Data Management Associate to support dashboard management, project data quality, transparency compliance, programme and project quality assurance, and regional project risk monitoring. The incumbent will work closely with Regional Project Managers and Programme Teams to strengthen Programme and Project Management and data management practices in corporate systems. The position will also support PMSU Programme Specialists in conducting RP compliance monitoring, programme and project quality assurance reviews, risk management exercises, and annual results reporting.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Regional Programme and Data Management Associate will work under the direct supervision of the Regional Programme Management Specialist. On the day-to-day basis, the incumbent will work closely with RBM Specialist and PA Coordinator as well as regional project team members and relevant Project Assistants / Associates to strengthen compliance with Programme and Project Management (PPM) requirements, improve data quality and transparency, support portfolio-level risk and quality reviews, and continuously enhance the effectiveness of the Regional Programme Performance Platform (RP³) as a management and decision-support tool.

Under the direct supervision of the Regional Programme Management Specialist, the Regional Programme and Data Management Associate will support PMSU in strengthening Regional Programme performance monitoring, project quality assurance, compliance oversight, and digitalization initiatives through the management of the Regional Programme Performance Dashboard and related data management systems.

The incumbent will perform the following functions:

A. Regional Programme and Project Database Management and Enhancement

- Serve as the focal point for the day-to-day management and maintenance of the Regional Programme Performance Dashboard;

- Monitor dashboard functionality, data synchronization, accessibility, and user experience to ensure reliable and timely performance reporting;

- Coordinate with ICT teams, data warehouse focal points, dashboard developers, and corporate system administrators to troubleshoot technical issues and improve dashboard functionality;

- Monitor project compliance with mandatory project setup and data management requirements reflected in the corporate Transparency Dashboard;

- Conduct periodic testing, validation, and quality reviews of dashboard data and analytics;

- Develop a set of data management guidelines (data governance) for both physical and electronic data including protocols for data entry, storage, security, and sharing, among others, to ensure data integrity and security;

- Develop a Data Quality Assessment (DQA) plan that sets the standards for data accuracy, consistency, and completeness—setting benchmarks and criteria for evaluating the quality of data;

- Develop data and digital products including, but not limited to, collection tools, dashboards, and reports, that are critical for accountability, transparency, and learning.

B. Regional Programme and Project (RP) Compliance, Risk Management and Quality Assurance

- Support RPMSU in monitoring compliance with UNDP Programme and Project Management (PPM) standards and procedures across the Regional Programme and Projects (RPs);

- Conduct regular RP compliance reviews and identify emerging compliance risks and implementation challenges;

- Monitor and track high-quality completion of project setup in Quantum in responding to PPM standards and corporate requirements;

- Support PMSU Programme Specialists in conducting programme and project quality assurance exercises throughout the project lifecycle;

- Review project management documentation and provide recommendations to improve compliance, project design quality, implementation effectiveness, and results reporting;

- Support PMSU in strengthening regional project risk management practices;

- Monitor regional projects risk treatments using the Regional Programme Risk Dashboard and other corporate systems;

- Conduct periodic reviews of regional project risk logs to assess quality, completeness and updated risk treatment measures.

C. RP Management and Implementation Support

- Support the management and improvement of digital technology solutions, including POCOMAS and relevant web- based project results management platforms, to enhance scalability and sustainability in line with UNDP digital standards;

- Support the regional programme and project evaluations and results monitoring as assigned;

- Provide administrative support to assigned projects and GPN thematic areas by maintaining internal expenditure systems, reviewing technical reports and payments for quality assurance, coordinating follow-up with relevant units, and ensuring timely corrective actions;

- Make preparations for external and internal programme / project audits, and support implementation of audit recommendations.

D. Capacity Development and Knowledge Management

- Provide day-to-day guidance and capacity-building support to regional project teams on: Use of the Regional Programme Performance Dashboard Transparency Dashboard requirements Project data quality management Programme and Project Management standards Risk management practices Quality assurance requirements Develop guidance notes, SOPs, FAQs, job aids, and training materials related to project compliance, data quality, risk management, and performance monitoring.

- Support PMSU learning initiatives, including the Project Managers Peer Learning Network and Digitalization and Automation Community of Practice;

- Document lessons learned and good practices from dashboard implementation, programme monitoring, compliance reviews, and quality assurance exercises.

Competencies

Core Competencies:

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline.

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible.

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident.

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships.

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination.

Cross-Functional & Technical Competencies:

Business Development

- Knowledge Generation: Ability to research and turn information into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need.

Business Management

- Project Management: Ability to plan, organize and control resource, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals.

- Digital Awareness and Literacy: Ability to monitor new and emerging technologies, as well as understand their usage, potential, limitations, impact, and added value. Ability to rapidly and readily adopt and use new technologies in professional activities, and to empower others to use them as needed. Knowledge of the usage of digital technologies and emerging trends.

- Working with Evidence and Data: Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions and supporting decision-making.

Digital & Innovation

- Data strategy and management: Knowledge to draft or execute a data strategy or a data management framework.

- Digital product management: Ability to design and lead digital product development including testing, ongoing product iteration, product strategy and delivery.

- Data governance: Knowledge of data science, skills to develop data management tools, organize and maintain databases and operate data visualization technologies.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Secondary education is required. OR,

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in Business, Public Administration, Law, Economics, Finance, Accounting, Political Science, International development, International Relations and Social Sciences or a relevant related field will be given due consideration but not a requirement.

Experience:

- Minimum 7 years (with secondary education), or 4 years (with Bachelor’s degree) of experience in project management, administration and financial management or closely related field is required.

Required skills and competencies:

- Experience in the usage of computers and office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.), database packages, and web-based management system such as ERP is required;

- Proven experiences in project management, knowledge-sharing and/or capacity building sessions particularly in the areas related data management and compliance assurance is required.

Desired additional skills and competencies:

- Experience in implementation support to development projects;

- Good knowledge of UNDP’s policies, procedures and practice including familiarity of ERP e.g. Quantum and Quantum+;

- Experience working with international organizations.

Required Language(s) (at working level):

- Fluency in English and Thai is required.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

jobs.title: Programme Coordination Specialist - [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

BACKGROUND

The UN SDG Action Campaign is a special initiative of the UN Secretary-General hosted by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and based in Bonn, Germany. To bring us closer to a just, inclusive and sustainable future, the UN SDG Action Campaign elevates unheard communities, nurtures changemakers, and leverages creativity to inspire hope and bold action.

The Campaign’s Advocacy for Change approach aims at systemic transformation by rethinking, recalibrating, and reimagining economies and societies so that they serve people and the planet, while inspiring SDG action and sending a message of hope and possibilities.

The UN SDG Action Campaign facilitates convening spaces and supports the engagement of civil society organizations and other key stakeholders in relevant dialogues and processes, with a focus in the areas of financing for development, gender equality, climate action, sustainable food systems and justice and peace. Additionally, the Campaign leverages art and creativity to inspire action and tap into humanity’s creative power for good. And the UN SDG Action Awards programme, the Campaign’s flagship initiative, serves to identify and recognize exceptional changemakers and initiatives that are making a difference towards the 2030 Agenda.

DUTIES AND RESPONSABILITIES

Under the overall guidance of the UN SDG Action Campaign Global Director and direct supervision of the Deputy Director, the Programme Coordination Specialist is responsible for coordinating the Campaign’s main initiatives, including overseeing the planning and implementation of the Heroes of Tomorrow: UN SDG Awards Programme. The incumbent will also provide support with the management of the Global Director’s office.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Coordinate planning and project management for the main events and activities of the UN SDG Action Campaign

- Coordinate the overall planning of the Campaign’s main events and activities, working in collaboration with relevant team members across workstreams to ensure that plans are clear, timelines are monitored and follow-up actions are captured.

- Liaise proactively with team members across workstreams to support alignment, flag gaps or bottlenecks, and help ensure that no key planning or coordination elements fall through the cracks.

- Coordinate planning meetings and working groups for relevant project workstreams as required.

- Identify gaps in project planning and coordination and activate corrective measures in consultation with Campaign leadership and relevant team members.

- Coordinate the overall planning of the Heroes of Tomorrow: UN SDG Action Awards, ensuring that each phase of the process is clearly mapped, sequenced and completed in line with agreed timelines.

- Maintain oversight across all relevant Awards workstreams and areas of work, including outreach, applications, selection processes, communications, event planning, logistics and follow-up, ensuring coherence and timely progress across the full process.

- Liaise with relevant internal and external stakeholders involved in the Awards process to support effective coordination, information flow and issue resolution throughout the planning and delivery cycle.

- Build and manage relationships with partners as necessary, in coordination with Campaign leadership and the relevant workstream leads.

Coordinate ways of working and information management for the UN SDG Action Campaign

- Coordinate the Campaign’s ways of working portfolio, including the development, maintenance and implementation of internal protocols, tools and working methods that support effective collaboration, information flow and team coordination.

- Support the effective use and maintenance of key internal platforms and systems, including Salesforce, SharePoint and Microsoft Teams, ensuring that information is organized, up to date and accessible to relevant team members.

- Identify opportunities to improve internal workflows, information management and digital collaboration, and support the implementation of agreed improvements in coordination with Campaign leadership and team members.

- Contribute to knowledge management and information sharing by documenting lessons learned, good practices and relevant resources linked to the Campaign’s activities and priorities.

- Support onboarding and practical guidance for team members and consultants on the Campaign’s key tools, protocols and ways of working, as required.

Provide executive support to the Global Director of the Campaign

- Coordinate the scheduling and management of events and speaking engagements of the Global Director, in coordination with relevant team members.

- Manage the agenda of the Global Director, including maintaining the Director’s calendar and contacts with high-ranking visitors and partners, and arranging appointments and meetings.

Ensure provision of top quality advisory services and facilitation of knowledge building and management.

- Identify policy-driven issues; and identify and synthesize best practices and lessons learned directly linked to programme goals.

- Establish/strengthen national and international advocacy networks. Implement relevant, high -impact advocacy with key partners.

- Coordinate and ensure integrated support in development of policies and institutions to address country problems and needs in collaboration with strategic partners.

- Support policy advisory services that contribute to inclusive societal digital transformation and take digital technology risks and opportunities or futures signals into account.

- Provide sound contributions to knowledge networks, communities of practice, and digital knowledge platforms.

- Organize and deliver training for the operations/ projects staff on programme related matters.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities:

N/A

COMPETENCIES

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

People Management

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

CROSS-FUNCTIONAL & TECHNICAL COMPETENCIES

Business Management

- Working with Evidence and Data : Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions and supporting decision-making

- Portfolio Management: Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity. Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment. Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management.

- Monitoring and Evaluation: Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programmes, and activities with a view to make sure that they are being implemented effectively; Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback and reporting on the consistency or discrepancy between planned activities and programme management and results. Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming. Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools. Ability to make an independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

Business Direction and Strategy

- System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

External Relations and Advocacy

- Event planning and execution: Ability to plan, manage and execute of public and private events to ensure that they support and amplify individual communications and advocacy initiatives, as well as UNDP's overall brand and mandate

Procurement

- Procurement Management: The ability to acquire goods, services or works from an outside external source.

Partnership Management

- Relationship Management: Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding

QUALIFICATIONS

Education:

- Advance university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Political Affairs, Development Studies, Business Administration, International Relations or related fields is required OR

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The nexus of security-humanitarian-development issues around Lake Chad has given rise to an intractable extremist insurgency that has left tens of thousands of people dead, approximately 2.5 million displaced, and more than 10 million people in the region affected and in need. While robust national and multi-national military operations have re-taken territory previously controlled by Boko Haram, UNDP recognizes that a new approach is required to consolidate these gains and establish the conditions necessary to transition from military to civilian responsibility for security, and from the provision of humanitarian assistance to the resumption of stalled development processes. In this context, the UNDP Regional Stabilization Facility is intended to provide a new approach, calibrated to respond to the need for a step-change in the scale and nature of intervention, improvement in speed of response, increased territorial coverage, and improved regional cooperation.

The UNDP Stabilization Facility aims to enhance civil-military cooperation to design and implement Joint Action Plans for the immediate stabilization of specific target areas, to increase security and the rule of law as well as provide infrastructure, basic services and livelihood opportunities as a rapid-response package. The Facility will underwrite the Lake Chad Basin Commission (LCBC) and the African Union implementation of the LCBC Regional Stabilization Strategy, strengthening coherence and coordination of response to the Lake Chad crisis, and establishing the mechanism and process required to operationalise the New Way of Working and a transition from provision of humanitarian assistance to development and resilience.

The Stabilization Facility Service Centre in Nigeria, established under the UNDP Regional Stabilization Facility, aims to ensure that immediate national stabilization efforts are well targeted, calibrated and fully owned by relevant stakeholders; and is set-up to provide the dedicated operational support necessary for timely implementation.

Reporting Structure and Partners

The Stabilization Facility Service Centre is composed of finance, procurement, human resources and project management /administration functions, led by the Operations Specialist with delegated authority as Manager Level 2 in the UNDP Nigeria office.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Position Purpose

The Operations Specialist will lead the operations of the UNDP Stabilization Facility Service Centre Nigeria under the direct supervision of the Head of Stabilization and matrix reporting to DRR-O, ensure full compliance with the Internal Control Framework and UNDP rules and regulations.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Operations Specialist will be responsible and contribute directly to the effective and efficient operations of the UNDP Stabilization Facility Service Centre Nigeria. He/she will liaise directly with the relevant staff to ensure coordination of delivery as appropriate. To this extent the Operations Specialist will be responsible for the following functions:

Ensure Oversight of operations of the Facility Service Centre implementation for optimization of delivery:

- Develops appropriate tools to deliver on operational services within the required time frame.

- Sets up appropriate monitoring system(s) in order to excel in client orientation and ensure timely delivery of results in accordance with the established work plan.

- Ensures frequent communication with programme staff, as main clients, on progress with respect to service requests.

- Operates at Manager level 2 approval level in Quantum.

- Identifies bottlenecks and operational solutions to operational obstacles.

- Oversees operations (procurement, human resources, finance, logistics, administration etc.) processes to ensure that they are performed consistently and in accordance with the corporate standards.

- Performs the function of Audit focal point for the Service Centre

- Collaborates closely with respective Operations Units of UNDP Nigeria CO as relevant.

Oversee application of operational policies for operations support pertaining to project implementation and management

- Works closely with the relevant Regional Stabilization Facility Nigeria staff to develop sound operational and procurement work plans/budgets and implementation plans, which match expected outputs.

- Clears agreements for working with partners, before signature by Senior Management of the Country Office.

- Reviews operational policies and advises on policies and SOPs which will ensure accountability and speed of implementation, with high client satisfaction.

- Oversees effective delivery of client-oriented administrative support to UNDP staff and project personnel on human resources, procurement, finance, logistics, administration and transactional issues.

Ensure Effective and accurate financial resource and efficient procurement management

- Implements effective internal controls such as maintenance of the internal expenditures control system, financial recording/reporting system.

- Ensures proper planning and expenditure tracking of financial resources and monitoring of financial delivery against work plans and preparation of relevant periodic reports.

- Prepares procurement strategies including sourcing strategy, supplier selection and evaluation, and quality management in line with UNDP rules and regulations.

- Reviews terms of reference to ensure the quality of inputs to be procured.

- Prepares annual procurement plans, with an indicative list of goods and services as identified in the annual work plan, in collaboration with the procurement team. Proper management of assets and timely handover where required.

- As part of a longer-term capacity building strategy, builds the capacity of counterparts and Service Centre national staff.

Ensure Strategic human resource management

- Prepares timely recruitment strategies and elaborates job descriptions for required staffing in line with UNDP rules and regulations.

- Supports recruitment processes and works closely with the HR unit of the UNDP Nigeria office to ensure timely recruitment of Regional Stabilization Facility Nigeria staff.

- Ensures overall management of administrative issues with administration officer of the Service Centre.

Ensure other tasks related to operations management and lead knowledge building and sharing

- Provide support to staff capacity development as requested.

- Participate in Task Forces and other ad-hoc internal working groups as requested.

- Perform any other tasks as required by the Head of Stabilization and/or Deputy Resident Representative-Operations.

- Leads processes to facilitate and promote staff learning and engagement.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: Supervises Service Centre/Operations staff

Competencies

Core Competencies

Achieve Results - LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively - LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously - LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility - LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination - LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

Engage and Partner - LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

Enable Diversity and Inclusion - LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

People Management

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Partnership Management - Relationship Management: Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust, and mutual understanding.

Business Direction & Strategy - System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Business Management - Portfolio Management: Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity. Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment. Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management

Business Management - Risk Management: Ability to identify and organize action around mitigating and proactively managing risks

Business Management - Results-based Management: Ability to manage programmes and projects with a focus on improved performance and demonstrable results.

Business Development - Knowledge Generation: Ability to research and turn information into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need.

Business Management - Communication: Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced University Degree (Masters or equivalent) in Business Administration, Operations Management, Procurement, Social Sciences, International Development, Economics or related fields. Or

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- A minimum of 5 years (with master’s degree) or 7 years (with bachelor’s degree) relevant work experience, at least 5 of which involve similar senior experience of operational management of projects or programmes.

- At least 2 years of relevant experience in crisis/post conflict countries is required?

- Experience of sustaining high level professional relations with Government officials is desired .

- Substantive project operational management experience, including detailed working knowledge of human resources, procurement, ICT, finance, project management, asset management and logistics is required

- Extensive expertise in procurement is of specific importance is desired.

- A sound track record of experience in an international setting with the UN or with international organisations, or similar context is desired.

- Experience in the Africa region is an advantage.

- Good knowledge of UNDP ERP system (Quantum) is desirable.

- Practical familiarity with UNDP project management principles and practices is desired

Language:

Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Descripción de la oficina/unidad/proyecto

El PNUD es la principal organización de las Naciones Unidas en la lucha para poner fin a la injusticia de la pobreza, la desigualdad y el cambio climático. Trabajando con nuestra amplia red de expertos y socios en 170 países, ayudamos a las naciones a construir soluciones integradas y duraderas para las personas y el planeta.

Desde hace 50 años, el Programa de las Naciones Unidas (PNUD) ha sido un aliado estratégico de Panamá, centrándose en soluciones integradas y alineadas con las prioridades nacionales, apoyando la gestión, implementación y ejecución de programas y proyectos en beneficio de las personas.

El PNUD en Panamá está organizado en tres grupos programáticos que coordinan más de 40 proyectos en todo el territorio nacional:

- Igualdad e inclusión social, económica y ambiental

- Gobernabilidad, paz y derechos humanos

- Cambio climático, gestión integral ambiental y reducción de riesgos y desastres

En el PNUD, la gestión basada en resultados, la igualdad de género, los derechos humanos, el enfoque multidimensional, el desarrollo territorial, la innovación, digitalización y el uso de nuevas tecnologías son transversales en todas nuestras áreas de trabajo y proyectos.

El proyecto 1005035 “Instituto de Formación Profesional y Capacitación para el desarrollo Humano INADEH 4.0: Formación para la Competitividad y el desarrollo”, busca contribuir al posicionamiento del INADEH como rector de la formación profesional, al fortalecimiento institucional, a la mejora de la calidad de la oferta educativa de hoy y del futuro, y a la mejora de la gestión operativa.

De esta manera, la acción del PNUD se centra en apoyar en la generación de una visión del sistema de formación técnica profesional con alternativas diferenciadas que sirvan a las personas, a la economía y a la sociedad. Organizar la gobernanza de la formación técnica y profesional, la vinculación educación – empleo, superar la sexta frontera, y poner el talento y capacidad de las y los panameños en reactivar nuestra economía y desarrollar la estrategia del cambio del proyecto definida como “Formación profesional como instrumento para fortalecer competencias, asegurar medios de vida y hacer una economía competitiva”.

La Oficina de Proyectos del INADEH es la instancia principal de comunicación y gestión de proyectos que ejecuta el INADEH con diversos organismos e instituciones, por lo que su rol principal es brindar estrecho seguimiento a la ejecución de los proyectos que se ejecutan como aquellos que se proyectan ejecutar en la institución, tanto en el corto como en el mediano plazo.

Alcance del trabajo

El/la Asistente en Programación de Informática fortalecerá la gestión de la Oficina de Informática del INADEH, brindando apoyo técnico en el análisis, diseño, desarrollo, validación, documentación y mantenimiento de programas y soluciones informáticas, de acuerdo con las necesidades institucionales y los requerimientos establecidos.

Las actividades específicas incluyen el apoyo en:

- Análisis, diseño y desarrollo de programas y soluciones informáticas Apoyar en el levantamiento, análisis y documentación de las necesidades de los usuarios y de los datos requeridos para el desarrollo o mejora de programas y soluciones informáticas. Desarrollar y actualizar programas, aplicaciones o componentes informáticos, utilizando los lenguajes de programación y las herramientas tecnológicas definidas para cada solución. Diseñar los pasos lógicos requeridos para el desarrollo de programas individuales o que formen parte de sistemas informáticos, incluyendo la preparación de flujogramas y la codificación correspondiente. Interpretar y procesar información relacionada con las actividades de su área de trabajo, utilizando los medios y herramientas tecnológicas requeridas, de acuerdo con los procedimientos técnicos aplicables.

- Validación, mantenimiento y documentación de programas Ejecutar pruebas funcionales de los programas, aplicaciones o componentes desarrollados, identificar posibles errores y realizar los ajustes requeridos dentro de su ámbito de competencia. Revisar y comprobar las listas de validación de los programas elaborados. Documentar los programas desarrollados y preparar las instrucciones necesarias para su operación y utilización. Mantener organizada y actualizada la documentación y los archivos relacionados con los programas y soluciones informáticas bajo su responsabilidad. Proponer mejoras a los métodos y procesos de trabajo relacionados con las funciones del puesto, cuando corresponda.

- Asistencia técnica, seguimiento e informes Atender consultas y brindar asistencia técnica, dentro de su ámbito de competencia, al personal de la institución y a terceros, cuando corresponda, de acuerdo con los procedimientos establecidos. Apoyar en la preparación de informes periódicos sobre las actividades desarrolladas, avances y resultados de los trabajos asignados.

- Apoyar la generación y el intercambio de conocimientos, así como el fortalecimiento de capacidades en el marco del proyecto. Participar en actividades de capacitación y organizar sesiones informativas sobre procedimientos internos para el personal del proyecto. Brindar apoyo a otras iniciativas de fortalecimiento de capacidades, incluyendo el diseño y la elaboración de herramientas, materiales para talleres o plataformas que aprovechen la inteligencia colectiva de las comunidades y movilicen la acción. Apoyar la difusión y el intercambio de datos relevantes y lecciones aprendidas. Mantenerse al tanto de las mejores prácticas emergentes —a nivel nacional, regional e internacional— relacionadas con la labor del proyecto. Realizar aportes valiosos a redes de conocimiento y comunidades de práctica. Apoyar la recopilación y sistematización de los conocimientos, productos y herramientas del proyecto, así como su amplia difusión entre los socios.

El titular desempeña otras funciones dentro de su perfil funcional que se consideren necesarias para el funcionamiento eficiente del Proyecto, la Oficina y la Organización.

Acuerdo Institucional

- Supervisión: El/la Asistente en Programación de Informática trabajará bajo la supervisión general del/de la Coordinador/a del Proyecto y del/de la Director/a del Proyecto. Sus servicios tendrán alcance nacional y se prestarán en el marco del Proyecto 01005035, “Instituto Nacional de Formación Profesional y Capacitación para el Desarrollo Humano (INADEH) 4.0: Formación profesional para la competitividad y el desarrollo humano”. La relación contractual se establecerá directamente con la Oficina de País del Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD), en coordinación con el equipo del Proyecto, el Clúster de Igualdad e Inclusión Social, Económica y Ambiental y el Instituto Nacional de Formación Profesional y Capacitación para el Desarrollo Humano (INADEH).

- Lugar de trabajo: El/la Asistente en Programación de Informática estará asignado/a a la Oficina de Proyectos de Transformación y Mejora Integral del INADEH, sin perjuicio de los desplazamientos a otros centros o sedes institucionales que sean requeridos para el cumplimiento de las funciones establecidas en estos Términos de Referencia.

- Horario: El/la profesional deberá laborar en horario regular de lunes a viernes. Cuando las necesidades del Proyecto lo requieran, deberá tener disponibilidad para laborar en horario extendido.

- Movilización: Los gastos de movilización, alojamiento y alimentación derivados de misiones oficiales o actividades previamente autorizadas, conforme a los requerimientos del Proyecto, serán cubiertos por este, de acuerdo con las normas y procedimientos aplicables.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Competencias

Competencias Básicas

1. Logro de Resultados

Nivel 1: Planifica y supervisa su propio trabajo, presta atención a los detalles, entrega un trabajo de calidad antes de la fecha límite.

2. Piensa de manera innovadora

Nivel 1: Abierto a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, es pragmático solucionador de problemas, hace mejoras.

Nivel 1: De mente abierta y curiosa, comparte conocimientos, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación

4. Se adapta con agilidad

Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja constructivamente la ambiguedad/incertidumbre, es flexible.

5. Actúa con determinación

Nivel 1: Muestra impulso y motivación, capaz de rendir con calma frente a la adversidad confiado.

6. Compromiso y Asociación

Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión, comprensión hacia los demás, establece relaciones positivas.

7. Diversidad e Inclusión

Nivel 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, es consciente de los prejuicios inconscientes, confronta la discriminación

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Office/Unit/Project Description

UNDP’s Rule of Law Programme in Pakistan is working to strengthen the rule of law and to ensure equal access to justice and security services, particularly for women and marginalized groups across Pakistan in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) including the merged districts (MDs), Balochistan, and Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT). In close collaboration with a range of government, rule of law and justice sector institutions, the overall Programme aims to enhance and sustain peace and stability for the longer-term in Pakistan.

The Programme activities and interventions therefore directly correspond with the government of Pakistan’s strategies and commitments to rule of law and justice reforms, as well as improving the efficiency and effectiveness of institutions to deliver accountable and affordable security and justice services to the public.

The Rule of Law Programme implementation is guided by the following four strategic objectives:

- Policy, legal and regulatory frameworks strengthened to warrant people-centered, equitable, timely, affordable justice and security delivery to all people with an emphasis on women, marginalized and vulnerable groups, and digital technologies.

- Capacity of justice and security stakeholders (duty bearers) enhanced to deliver inclusive, timely, and accessible services to all people with an emphasis on women and digital technologies.

- Capacity of women, and the most vulnerable and marginalized (rights holders) strengthened to access referral pathways to justice and security.

- Justice and security sector institutional facilities enhanced to deliver inclusive, timely, and accessible justice and security services, through women friendly and gender-responsive infrastructure development support with an emphasis on flood resilience and green energy.

Against this backdrop, UNDP actions and interventions are aimed at restoring public confidence and service delivery in the formal justice and rule of law sectors through a range of initiatives i.e. policy development and reform, fostering justice and security sector governance, as well as oversight and accountability at an institutional level with emphasis on inclusive and gender-responsive programming. The overall engagement strategy, therefore, involves both federal and local levels. The Programme is implemented in partnership with the Judiciary, Police, Prosecution, Prisons, Probation and Reclamation, Bar Associations, Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and the academia both at federal and provincial levels.

The Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting Analyst will provide technical leadership and support for programme monitoring, evaluation, results measurement, data management, learning and reporting. The Analyst will establish and maintain robust systems to track progress against programme results frameworks, strengthen data quality and evidence use, support evaluations and assessments, and ensure timely, accurate and evidence-based reporting.

The Analyst will work with relevant institutional counterparts and designated other team members to strengthen monitoring arrangements, results-based management and learning, including appropriate disaggregation and attention to gender equality and vulnerable populations.

Scope of Work

The Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting Analyst will report directly to the Team Lead – Programme Specialist. The Analyst will provide technical leadership, advice and quality assurance for monitoring, evaluation, results measurement, data management, learning and reporting under the Rule of Law Programme.

The Analyst will lead the development and implementation of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, indicators, baselines, targets, data-flow systems and reporting arrangements; strengthen data quality and analysis; and support the use of evidence for adaptive management and decision-making. S/he will coordinate evaluations, assessments, surveys and research assignments and ensure that programme reporting is timely, accurate, analytical and results-focused.

The Analyst will promote gender-responsive monitoring and evaluation, including systematic collection and analysis of appropriately disaggregated data and evidence on the experiences and results of women and vulnerable populations. S/he will maintain effective engagement with relevant institutional counterparts, research and evaluation service providers, and designated other team members to support coherent results measurement and learning.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams and projects in multidisciplinary teams to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Key Duties and Responsibilities

1.Lead monitoring, evaluation and results measurement for the Rule of Law Programme.

- Design and implement an integrated Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) plan to ensure effective implementation and achievement of programme results; monitor the implementation of the plan including measurement of programme indicators, design of monitoring tools and establishment of data flow systems.

- Operationalise, maintain and, where required, support the refinement of key performance indicators (KPIs) in accordance with approved programme results frameworks and annual workplans; assess progress against agreed indicators and targets and work with programme colleagues to identify evidence-based course corrections where gaps or implementation issues arise.

- Establish and maintain appropriate databases and data-management systems for the programme results framework and, in collaboration with programme focal persons, identify data sources and agree on data-collection methods, responsibilities, frequency, disaggregation requirements, quality-assurance standards and reporting arrangements.

- Conduct and manage quality assurance activities, develop strategies for course correction and update M&E frameworks as required.

- Oversee collection and validation of data to support any change that might be required in the programme activities; and undertake field M&E activities as required.

- Develop and maintain appropriate data-visualisation tools, dashboards and analytical products to support results monitoring, management decision-making and communication of programme performance.

2.Lead programme reporting, results analysis and performance information management.

- Lead the preparation and coordination of periodic, annual and other programme and donor reports, in accordance with applicable reporting requirements and agreed timelines.

- Coordinate and provide results-based inputs to relevant corporate reporting processes, including the Results-Oriented Annual Report (ROAR) and Annual Programme Report (APR), as applicable, ensuring consistency with corporate standards and programme results.

- Maintain and update relevant programme results information in UNDP corporate systems, including Quantum, in accordance with applicable corporate requirements and approved results frameworks.

- Coordinate and ensure timely updating of programme results information in applicable donor reporting systems, including EU OPSYS, in accordance with agreed reporting requirements.

- Provide analytical and evidence-based inputs to programme planning, implementation reviews and strategic decision-making, drawing on monitoring, evaluation, research and programme data to support achievement of agreed results and targets.

- Support the synthesis and use of monitoring, evaluation, research and assessment findings to identify trends, lessons, implementation issues and emerging priorities, and facilitate their use in programme learning and adaptive management.

- Provide results-based planning and performance information to support work planning, implementation reviews, resource planning, management discussions, briefings and other internal and external reporting requirements.

- Engage with programme staff and consultants to facilitate communication of information and assist in generating a strong understanding of project activities, M&E framework, and related issues; conduct field visits as required.

- Support consistency and consolidation of results information for joint or programme-level reporting through coordination with relevant counterparts, where required.

3.Strengthen data quality, results-based management and institutional monitoring practices and knowledge sharing

- Develop and apply appropriate data-quality assurance mechanisms to assess the accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness and reliability of programme monitoring and reporting information.

- Conduct periodic reviews and verification of programme results data, including source documentation, institutional records and other means of verification, and recommend corrective measures where data-quality issues are identified.

- Provide technical guidance and capacity-development support to designated other team members and relevant partners on results-based management, indicator measurement, monitoring tools, data collection, data quality, analysis and use of evidence.

- Support relevant institutional partners in strengthening monitoring, data-management and results-reporting practices, where appropriate, to improve the availability and quality of evidence supporting programme results.

- Promote consistent application of monitoring standards, methodologies, definitions and reporting practices across programme interventions to strengthen comparability and reliability of results information.

- Identify monitoring and evaluation risks, data gaps and evidence limitations and recommend practical measures to address them.

4.Coordinate evaluations, assessments, surveys and research for programme learning and accountability.

- Provide technical leadership and coordination for programme evaluations, assessments, surveys, studies and other evidence-generation initiatives in accordance with programme requirements and applicable UNDP standards.

- Prepare and/or review terms of reference, methodologies, data-collection tools, sampling approaches, analytical frameworks and other technical documentation for monitoring, evaluation, survey and research assignments.

- Provide technical oversight and quality assurance for consultants, research organisations and service providers engaged for specialised monitoring, evaluation, assessment, survey and research assignments.

- Review evaluation, assessment and research deliverables to ensure methodological rigour, appropriate use of evidence, analytical quality and consistency with agreed requirements.

- Facilitate appropriate management responses, follow-up and use of evaluation and assessment findings and recommendations to strengthen programme performance and accountability.

- Promote gender-responsive and inclusive evaluation and research approaches, including appropriate disaggregation of evidence and consideration of differential results and experiences among women and vulnerable and marginalised populations.

5.Ensure M&E quality assurance and contribute to programme planning and management.

- Provide technical advice to the Chief Technical Advisor on programme performance, results achievement, evidence gaps, monitoring risks and areas requiring management attention or course correction.

- Review relevant programme workplans, results frameworks, technical documents and implementation arrangements from a monitoring and results perspective and provide recommendations to strengthen measurability and results orientation.

- Provide M&E and results-based inputs to programme planning, reviews, management meetings, briefing notes, presentations and other programme documentation, as required.

- Support the establishment and periodic review of appropriate monitoring arrangements for programme interventions to ensure that expected results can be credibly measured and reported.

- Maintain organised and accessible monitoring, evaluation and reporting records, datasets, evidence and supporting documentation to facilitate programme management, reporting, reviews, evaluations and assurance processes.

- Capture and promote lessons from programme monitoring and evaluation to strengthen implementation quality, institutional learning and future programming.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Rule of Law Programme is placed within the Democratic Governance Unit of the UNDP Country Office in Pakistan, and the Analyst will work under the supervision of the Team Lead – Programme Specialist and coordinate with designated other team members and relevant Country Office colleagues.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan.

Within the GPN, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policy and guidance to support the results of UNDP's Strategic Plan. BPPS's staff provides technical advice to Country Offices, advocates for UNDP corporate messages, represents UNDP at multi-stakeholder fora including public-private dialogues, government and civil society dialogues, and engages in UN inter-agency coordination in specific thematic areas. BPPS works closely with UNDP's Crisis Bureau (CB) to support emergency and crisis response. BPPS ensures that issues of risk are fully integrated into UNDP's development programmes. BPPS assists UNDP and partners to achieve higher quality development results through an integrated approach that links results-based management and performance monitoring with more effective and new ways of working. BPPS supports UNDP and partners to be more innovative, knowledge and data driven including in its programme support efforts.

The newly established UNDP Planet Hub will drive UNDP’s vision of a world where economies and ecosystems thrive together — where energy systems are clean and accessible, nature is protected and restored, communities are resilient to climate impacts, and pollution is minimized. By 2030, the Hub seeks to help countries achieve this vision through systemic change that aligns policy, finance, integrated solutions, and societal ownership to advance sustainable human development. Backed by diverse partnerships and funding sources, the Planet Hub combines thought leadership, technical expertise, and strategic collaboration to help countries advance their environmental and economic goals.

The Planet Hub will build on UNDP’s existing portfolio of over USD 5 billion in over 140 countries, as well as on key offers across UNDP. The Planet Hub’s theory of change rests on five mutually reinforcing service lines that together enable systemic transformation:

- Intergovernmental and UN System Coherence and Support

- National Policies, Strategies, and Planning

- Innovative and Integrated Solutions

- Scaled-up Finance

- Insights, Modeling, and Data

The Planet Hub will be made up of eight interconnected pillars, covering strategic areas of work to deliver its core objective, as well as a set of integrated functions and support that cut across pillars and help ensure cohesive offers and delivery of the Planet Hub. One critical component of the Planet Hub is the portfolio of support to countries on Climate and Nature Policy. The Climate and Nature Policy Pillar provides strategic leadership on integrated climate and nature policy development, implementation, and advocacy, supporting countries to address interconnected environmental challenges while advancing sustainable development objectives. The Pillar brings together expertise on climate policy, biodiversity policy, environmental governance, integrated planning frameworks, Multilateral Environmental Agreements, and science-policy interfaces. Working across all Planet Hub pillars and in close collaboration with governments, UN entities, international organizations, research institutions, and development partners, the Pillar promotes policy coherence, strengthens implementation of global environmental commitments, and supports countries in developing integrated approaches to climate action, biodiversity conservation, ecosystem resilience, and sustainable development.

Climate Transparency and implementation of Paris Agreement’s Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF) are paramount to the vision of the Policies pillar, under the Planet Hub. UNDP has extensive experience supporting developing countries to meet international climate reporting requirements and works closely with UNFCCC, UNEP, GEF and other partners in this area.

The Climate Transparency - Global Support Programme Phase III (GSP III) will be jointly implemented by UNDP and United Nations Environment Programme UNEP (through UNEP United Nations Environment Programme

(CCC)), with project management and coordination responsibilities shared between UNDP and UNEP. Effective delivery therefore requires close day-to-day collaboration between the UNDP and UNEP teams, as well as coordinated engagement with the project's governance bodies, regional networks and technical partners.

In this context, UNDP is recruiting a Programme Analyst -Transparency Global Support Programme who will maintain and analyze the project's data and monitoring systems, track and report on programme results with particular attention to gender-responsive and youth-inclusive implementation, manage information flow between the global team and the project's regional networks, and prepare knowledge products and communication materials for the UNDP stream of GSP III.

Position Purpose

Under the direct supervision of the Global Support Programme Project Manager, and in close collaboration with the Chief Technical Lead and the Regional Network Coordinators, the Programme Analyst will maintain and analyze the project's data and monitoring systems; track and report on programme results, with particular attention to gender-responsive and youth-inclusive implementation; manage information flow between the global team and the project's regional networks; prepare knowledge products and communication materials in line with the project's Gender Action Plan and Stakeholder Engagement Plan; and provide analytical, documentation and administrative support to the project team.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

1.Ensure Data, Knowledge and Information Management

• Compile, structure and analyze project data, and prepare tables, charts and dashboards to support programme monitoring

• Support the development, updating, and dissemination of technical guidance, knowledge products, sectoral guidance documents, manuals, toolkits, catalogues, communication materials and other project outputs for global and regional audiences.

• Support the development and maintenance of project knowledge repositories, stakeholder databases, document management systems and digital archives, ensuring effective version control, accessibility and compliance with project partners’ information management standards.

• Apply standardized templates and agreed review procedures across knowledge products and communication materials to ensure consistency and coherence across project outputs.

• Assist in maintaining and updating the roster of local, regional and international experts supporting programme implementation.

• Support lessons learned exercises and prepare knowledge capture and synthesis notes across programme components

2. Monitoring, Results Tracking and Reporting

• Support implementation of the programme’s Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) framework through systematic data collection, validation, analysis and reporting.

• Maintain and update indicator-tracking and results-monitoring tools, ensuring that reported information is complete, traceable and supported by appropriate evidence.

• Contribute to the preparation of annual work plans, Project Steering Committee documentation, progress reports, Project Implementation Reports (PIRs), and other corporate reporting requirements.

• Support preparation and organization of documentation and evidence for mid-term review and terminal evaluation.

• Support systematic tracking of gender-responsive implementation and results in programme reporting, in line with the project's Gender Action Plan and UNDP's gender-marker requirements.

3. Promote Communications and Outreach

• Support the development and coordination of communication materials, outreach packages, newsletters, presentations, web content, promotional materials and dissemination products to increase the visibility and impact of programme results.

• Support implementation of the programme's communication and branding strategy, ensuring consistency of messaging, visual identity and positioning across all products and events.

• Provide communication and documentation support for global and regional events, workshops, technical exchanges, COP and SB sessions, Global Transparency Forum and other external engagements

• Support the preparation, dissemination and analysis of project surveys and communication products to strengthen stakeholder engagement and knowledge sharing.

• Coordinate the preparation of the yearly event planner, supporting coherence of messaging and communication priorities across project events.

4. Provide Programme Coordination Support

• Support internal team coordination, including documentation, drafting and dissemination of meeting summaries, communication workflows and internal updates.

• Support the delivery of technical and in-country assistance activities in coordination with the RNCs and thematic experts

• Prepare background documentation, analytical materials, technical templates and briefing notes for country missions

• Support the preparation of presentations, guidance notes, training materials and learning resources, and contribute to capacity needs assessments and regional training plans

• Support the exchange of country-level experience, lessons and knowledge products between UNDP's wider GEF Enabling Activities and CBIT portfolio and GSP III, and flag potential duplication to the Global Support Programme Project Manager

• Perform other related technical and programme support duties as required to ensure the effective implementation of the Climate Transparency Global Support Programme III.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: None

Competencies

- Core Competencies

Achieve  Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline.

Think  Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

Adapt  with  Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible.

Act  with  Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident.

Engage  and  Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships.

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination.

- Cross-Functional & Technical Competencies

Business Direction and Strategy & System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

2030 Planet-Agenda & Climate: Climate Change Adaptation: Climate-Resilient Infrastructure.

Business Management & Portfolio Management:

- Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity

- Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment

- Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management

Business Management & Communication:

- Ability to communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience

- Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels

Business Management & Monitoring & Evaluation:

- Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programmes, and activities with a view to make sure that they are being implemented effectively;

- Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback and reporting on the consistency or discrepancy between planned activities and programme management and results.

- Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming.

- Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools.

- Ability to make an independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks.

- Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

Business Management & Digital Awareness and Literacy:

- Ability to monitor new and emerging technologies, as well as understand their usage, potential, limitations, impact, and added value.

- Ability to rapidly and readily adopt and use new technologies in professional activities, and to empower others to use them as needed.

- Knowledge of the usage of digital technologies and emerging trends.

Business Management & Working with Evidence and Data: Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions and supporting decision-making.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Environmental Management, International Development, Social Sciences, Communications, or a related field is required. Or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor's degree) in the areas stated above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum 2 years (with a master's degree) or 4 years (with a bachelor's degree) of relevant professional experience in data analysis, monitoring and reporting, or knowledge management, in climate transparency, climate policy or international development programmes, is required.

- Demonstrated experience in international project/programme management and/or oversight, preferably in climate policy, transparency, and/or international development contexts is required.

- Prior working experience with UN agencies, multilateral fund projects or multi-country technical programmes is required.

- Demonstrated experience supporting monitoring, evaluation and reporting for UN agencies, multilateral funds projects or multi-country programmes, including progress reporting, mid-term reviews or terminal evaluations, is required.

- Experience in data handling and analysis, including data collection, structuring, quality checks, documentation and version control, is required.

- Experience with collaborative platforms and data visualization tools (e.g. SharePoint, Teams, Power BI) is required.

- Experience in knowledge management, communications or stakeholder engagement in climate change or international development context is required.

- Experience in preparing communication products, managing knowledge platforms or supporting event communications in international programmes is desirable.

- Experience working with developing-country institutions, capacity-building programmes or climate transparency networks is desirable.

- Experience supporting gender-responsive programming, monitoring or reporting is desirable.

- Work experience in GEF- funded programming is a strong asset.

- Relevant professional training or certification in climate change, climate transparency or related climate policy areas is an asset.

- Proven experience and sound understanding of climate transparency frameworks and ETF/MRV reporting requirements is desired.

- Strong writing, editing and analytical skills, with demonstrated ability to present complex technical information clearly for different audiences is desired.

Languages:

- Fluency in English is required.

- Fluency in other UN language is desirable.

jobs.title: ICT Associate [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Background

With offices in Copenhagen, Kuala Lumpur, Dakar, Amman, Panama City and Istanbul, the Global Shared Services Centre (GSSC) services over 180 countries, 40,000 personnel and more than 40 other UN Agencies and Organizations. Through its functional service lines, GSSC ensures high quality and timely delivery of human resources, financial and procurement services as well as information and innovative tools to its various clients and stakeholders. The GSSC is led by the Director, who reports to the Director of Bureau for Management Services (BMS).

Under the guidance and direct supervision of the ICT Analyst, the ICT Associate provides ICT services, support the management of ICT systems, provides daily tier 2 technical support to users of information management tools and technology infrastructure. The ICT Associate promotes a client-oriented approach.

The ICT Associate works in close collaboration with the Directorate, GSSC and non-GSSC teams, and UNDP HQ staff for resolving ICT-related issues, collaborates with other ICT Staff.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Support ICT Operations and Service Delivery

Ensure effective ICT service delivery and operational support across the GSSC environment through:

- Managing day-to-day ICT operations and support services.

Ensure that the desktop and network resources are protected from malicious virus attacks and deploy countermeasures in the event of the attacks

Lead automation initiatives that improve operational efficiency and user productivity through:

- Designing, developing, and maintaining business process automation solutions using Microsoft Power Automate.

- Developing Power Apps applications to streamline manual and repetitive processes.

- Integrating business systems and workflows to improve operational effectiveness.

- Identifying opportunities for automation and digital transformation across functional units.

- Supporting workflow redesign and process optimization initiatives.

- Creating dashboards, reports, and analytical tools using Microsoft Power Platform and related technologies.

- Developing proof-of-concepts and innovative technology solutions aligned with business needs.

4. Knowledge Management and Team Collaboration

Promote knowledge sharing and organizational learning through:

- Identification and promotion of different systems and applications for optimal content management, knowledge management and sharing, information provision;

- Sharing expertise on emerging technologies and automation solutions.

- Facilitating skills development initiatives within the ICT function.

- Supporting cross-functional projects and organizational transformation initiatives.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.
