Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategies. Look for ways to add value beyond clients' immediate requests. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

jobs.title: Programme Analyst
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Myanmar continues to face a complex operating environment characterized by protracted conflict, economic contraction, disrupted essential services, and heightened vulnerability across communities. Since 2021, the country has experienced sustained institutional and market disruptions, large-scale population displacement, and recurrent natural hazards, including the March 2025 earthquake, compounding existing fragilities.

In this context, UNDP’s programming prioritizes ‘community first’ that strengthens community resilience. Interventions are designed to remain responsive to evolving conditions, grounded in local realities, and sequenced to link immediate recovery with longer-term resilience. UNDP’s support spans community governance, local economic recovery and resilience, and climate resilience and natural resource management, with a consistent focus on reaching those most exposed to vulnerability, exclusion, and repeated shocks.

Position Purpose

The Programme Analyst supports UNDP’s commitment to accountable, risk-informed, and results-oriented programme delivery by strengthening quality assurance, compliance, monitoring, and learning across the programme portfolio. The role focuses on second-line assurance, complementing programme management and operations functions, and enabling senior management to make informed decisions based on timely evidence and risk analysis. The position also provides technical leadership and quality assurance for UNDP’s programming priorities in the areas of community governance, and local economic recovery and and resilience, ensuring coherence, technical soundness, and facilitating linkages within and across these priority areas.

The Programme Analyst reports to the Deputy Resident Representative and works in close collaboration with all programme teams, project management units, field offices, and operations units across the Country Office. The role supports a whole-of-office approach to programme quality, risk management, and performance, providing independent assurance while enabling teams to deliver effectively in a complex operating environment.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

UNDP Myanmar is committed to achieving 50/50 gender balance in its staff. Female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply for this position.

Duties and Responsibilities

- Ensure programme assurance, quality control, and risk-informed oversight of the UNDP programme, with a focus on assigned programme priorities and projects:

- Reviews programme and project design to ensure robust articulation of Theories of Change, results frameworks, and alignment between inputs, outputs, outcomes, and indicators.

- Provides independent quality assurance inputs to programme and project documents, including Integrated Work Plans, project documents, revisions, and results reporting.

- Reviews the integration of political, social, economic, climate, and risk analysis into programme documents, policy briefs, and planning instruments.

- Assesses the alignment of proposed programme and project interventions with UNDP strategic priorities, country needs, and donor requirements, from assurance, feasibility and positioning perspectives.

- Supports identification, tracking, and mitigation of programme and project-level risks, including fiduciary, delivery, partner, and reputational risks.

- Flags emerging risks, bottlenecks, or quality concerns to senior management and supports project teams in identifying corrective actions.

- Ensures that UNDP Enterprise Risk Management frameworks are applied across the assigned portfolio, and verifies compliance with Social and Environmental Standards and safeguard requirements

- Ensures that gender equality and women’s empowerment commitments are systematically integrated into programme and project design, results frameworks, budgets, risk analysis, and safeguards, in line with UNDP Gender Equality Strategy and corporate standards.

- Reviews all documentation prior to final approval by Senior Management to ensure completeness, quality and alignment with requirements.

- Contributes to preparing and conducting programme and project governance meetings, and management decision-making processes.

- Support strategic positioning, partnerships, and resource mobilization with a focus on assigned programme priorities and projects:

- Provides ongoing analysis of contextual and programmatic signals related to assigned programme priorities to inform strategic positioning and decision-making.

- Maintains regular discussions with donors and partners to support alignment of priorities, and effective partnerships.

- Analyzes partnership and funding landscapes, including donor priorities, financing instruments, and implementation modalities, to identify emerging opportunities.

- Conducts horizon scanning on financing and partnership trends, identifying implications for programme quality, delivery risks, and future pipeline development.

- Provides independent assurance inputs to concept notes, project proposals, and financing agreements related to, assessing strategic fit, quality, risk mitigation measures, and implementation feasibility.

- Reviews partnership and pipeline development processes to assess readiness, credibility, and alignment with donor requirements and UNDP strategic priorities.

- Verifies the quality, consistency, and timeliness of donor reporting and compliance with partnership agreements, flagging risks that may affect institutional credibility, future funding, or strategic relationships.

- Assesses whether partnership arrangements, financing instruments, and pipeline proposals adequately reflect gender equality commitments and donor gender requirements.

- Promote Integration, Communications and Facilitate Knowledge Management:

- Maximizes communication to ensure that stakeholders (development partners, bilateral and multilateral donors, private sector, civil society, UN agencies and Government agencies) have one consistent UNDP counterpart.

- Ensures internal communication and coordination across the programme and effective and proactive communication between relevant CO units and projects to maintain consistent approaches and messaging.

- Provides sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice relating to assigned programme priorities and project, including capturing lessons and good practices to inform programme assurance and adaptive management.

- Ensures that development results are effectively monitored, reported and communicated to meet internal and external M&E and reporting expectations and requirements.

- Facilitates coherent programme implementation by ensuring consistent information flow across CO units, field teams and projects and promote alignment across thematic workstreams.

4.Provides strategic, technical advice and capacity-development on Country Programme priorities

- Provides technical advice to programme and projects, to assess needs and identify appropriate strategies and interventions, with a particular focus on (but not limited to) community governance, and economic resilience and recovery, while ensuring alignment with UNDP programme assurance standards and quality requirements.

- Works closely with Project Managers, Project Management Units and Technical Specialists to provide advice and technical support as required including adherence to programming principles, safeguards, risk management, monitoring and evaluation, and assurance processes.

- Identifies capacity needs, and supports capacity development of UNDP personnel on programme assurance functions, including quality assurance processes, risk management, compliance with POPP and donor requirements, results-based management, and documentation standards across the project cycle.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities:

The Programme Analyst works under the overall supervision of the Deputy Resident Representative and collaborates closely with Programme personnel, Project Managers and Project Management Units, Operations units, and Field Offices.

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results:

LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively:

LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously

LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility

LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination

LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner

LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion

LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Business Development

UNDP Representation

Effectively represent and advocate for UNDP, its values, mission, work, and positions with various constituencies/audiences, shares UNDP knowledge and activities.

Business Management

Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies

Business

Ability to select, prioritize and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity Ability to

balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment. Knowledge and understanding of key

principles of project, programme, and portfolio management

solutions and create ‘win-win’ situations.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced University Degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in Development Studies, Public Administration, Economics, Social Sciences, or a related field is required. Or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree

Experience:

- Minimum of 2 years (with master’s degee) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant professional experience in programme management, programme assurance, monitoring and evaluation, compliance, risk management, or related areas within development, humanitarian, or public sector contexts.

- Demonstrated experience supporting quality assurance, results-based management, monitoring and reporting of development programmes or projects is required.

- Experience working with UN agencies, international organizations, or donor-funded programmes is an asset.

- Technical experience in one oft he following areas is an advantage: Community mobilization and empowerment; gender equality; governance; livelihoods; economic recovery is desired.

- Experience and sound knowledge of programme/project cycles and processes is desired.

- Familiarity with internal control frameworks, including application of corporate policies and procedures is desired.

- Fluency in English and Burmese is required.

Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

jobs.title: Assistant Public Information Officer-UNOCHA-(Nationals Only)
jobs.description:
Open to Ukrainian nationals only

Background

This position is located in the Operations and Advocacy Division (OAD), in the Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA). OCHA is part of the United Nations Secretariat responsible for bringing together humanitarian actors to ensure a coherent response to emergencies. OCHA also ensures there is a framework within which each actor can contribute to the overall response efforts. OCHA's mission is to mobilize and coordinate effective and principled humanitarian action in partnership with national and international actors in order to alleviate human suffering in disasters and emergencies; advocate the rights of people in need; promote preparedness and prevention; and facilitate sustainable solutions.

The position of Assistant Public Information Officer/Reporting is based in Kyiv, Ukraine. Under the overall supervision of the Deputy Head of Office, the incumbent (s) reports to the Public Information Officer/Head of Unit.

Key Duties and Responsibilities

Under the guidance of the Public Information Officer/Head of Unit, the Assistant Public Information Officer /Reporting will support the implementation of public information programs to publicize priority issues and/or major events. He/She will focus on the following sets of activities:

- Media monitoring,

- Supports humanitarian emergency response and preparedness,

- Develops national humanitarian information networks, and

- Contributes to initiating and sustaining professional relationships with key constituencies.

Within limits of delegated authority and depending on location, the Assistant Public Information Officer/Reporting at this level may be responsible for the following duties:

- Contributes to implementation of public information programs to publicize priority issues and/or major events, to include drafting information strategies, coordinating efforts, monitoring and reporting on progress, taking appropriate follow-up action, and analyzing the outcome.

- Conducts comprehensive monitoring of relevant news, current events, public opinion, and press from a broad scope of sources (English, Ukrainian, and Russian) - print, TV, electronic, internet, etc., and identifies issues and trends.

- Promotes media coverage of priority issues and/or major events by arranging press briefings/interviews, disseminating materials such as photo and video content of vulnerable communities and consulting with press on approach/story angle and other information requests, undertaking appropriate follow-up action, analyzing and reporting on the impact of coverage.

- Assists in creation of information communications products (e.g. press kits, press releases, feature articles, backgrounders, audio-visual materials, and other print/web products), develops information campaigns, including proposing topics, undertaking research, determining appropriate medium and target audience; prepares production plans, writing drafts, obtaining clearances and finalizing texts, editing copy, and coordinating design approval, printing procedures and distribution.

- Ensures that the social media platforms are updated daily, and programs and activities are properly reflected through social media platforms.

- Initiates and sustains professional relationships with key constituencies, liaises with national and international media representatives, and undertakes activities to promote media coverage and media outreach of priority issues and/or major events.

- Acts as focal point on specific issues, monitoring and reporting on developments, responding to inquiries, etc.

- Assists in the day-to-day operation of the Public Information Office.

- Supports translation services with proofreading

- Performs other duties as required.

Work implies frequent interaction with the following:

- Deputy Head of Office, Public Information Officer/Head of unit and Humanitarian Affairs Officer/ Head of Humanitarian Funds, and other Humanitarian Affairs Officers, and managers throughout the UN and in other UN organizations and missions.

- Regional UN agencies

- International and national NGOs.

- Relevant authorities and official departments.

Impact of Results

The key results have an impact on the effectiveness of OCHA Ukraine’s communication efforts and perception of existing humanitarian needs and the ongoing response.

Competencies:

Professionalism: Knowledge of different aspects of public information and communication approaches, tools, and methodologies essential to planning and executing effective campaign strategies and programmes. Ability to address a range of issues in the context of political developments, public attitudes and local conditions. Ability to conceptualize, design and implement major information campaigns. Ability to rapidly analyze and integrate diverse information from varied sources. Ability to diplomatically handle sensitive situations with target audiences and cultivate productive relationships. Ability to produce a variety of written communications products in a clear, concise style. Ability to deliver oral and visual presentations to various audiences. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work.

Planning and organizing: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies. Identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required. Allocates an appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work. Foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning. Monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary. Uses time efficiently.

Communication: Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately; asks questions to clarify, and exhibits interest in having two-way communication; tailors language, tone, style and format to match audience

Teamwork: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others’ ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with a final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings.

Education:

- Master's degree or equivalent in communication, journalism, international relations, public administration, social sciences or related field is required.

- A bachelor’s degree in combination with an additional two (2) years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Applicants with a master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field of study are not required to have professional work experience. Applicants with a Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) are required to have a minimum of two (2) years of progressively responsible experience in public information, journalism, international relations, public administration, or a related field is required.

- Experience in drafting, editing, and producing communication and information products is required.

- Experience in collecting information from multiple sources for communication and reporting purposes is required.

- Experience in graphic design, photo and/or video editing is desirable.

- Experience with social media platforms is desirable.

- High-quality translation of information and reporting materials into Ukrainian and English is desirable.

- Experience in a public information context within the UN Common System or other comparable international organization is desirable.

Language:

- Fluency in English and Ukrainian is required.

- Knowledge of other UN languages is desirable.

jobs.description:
1. Position Information

Office/Unit/Project

UNDP Türkiye Country Office / Programme / Preparedness, Response and Resilience Programme / Social Cohesion and Inclusion Support for Refugees in Türkiye

Title

Technical Project Associate

Level

NPSA 6

Duty station (City and Country)

Ankara, Türkiye

Type (Regular or Short term)

Regular

Office- or Home-based

Office-based (Premises of the Presidency of Migration Management - PMM)

Expected starting date

December 2026

Expected Duration

1 year with possible extension based on performance and availability of funds.

Position Number

00138782

2. Office/Unit/Project Description

UNDP is committed to achieving workforce diversity in terms of gender, nationality, and culture. Individuals from minority groups, indigenous groups and persons with disabilities are equally encouraged to apply. All applications will be treated with the strictest confidence.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

UNDP is the leading United Nations organization in fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations to build integrated, lasting solutions for people and planet. Learn more at undp.org or follow at @UNDP

The project aims to strengthen social cohesion in Türkiye by supporting the effective implementation of the national harmonization strategy. It enhances opportunities for meaningful participation in social, economic, and civic life, with a particular focus on women. Through a combination of institutional support, community-based initiatives, and targeted services, the project contributes to a more harmonious society and improves well-being for Syrians under Temporary Protection (SuTP), International Protection Status Holders and Applicants (IPSHA), and Turkish Citizens.

To expand access to decent employment, the project reinforces institutional coordination, regulatory frameworks, and labour governance systems while facilitating work permits and labour mobility across regions. It provides market-oriented vocational training, counselling, and job-matching services—especially in the green and digital sectors—and introduces tailored measures to increase women’s employability, including addressing care-related barriers. In parallel, the project supports voluntary relocation by delivering comprehensive resettlement and integration packages that help SuTP and IPSHA settle in new locations and participate effectively in local labour markets and community life.

The project also enhances language proficiency by scaling up accessible language and literacy programmes, with dedicated support for women and girls through enabling measures such as child-care provision. Additionally, it strengthens social cohesion by addressing cultural and social barriers, discrimination, and misinformation that hinder the participation of SuTP, IPSHA in Turkish society. These combined efforts foster mutual understanding, reduce tensions, and create an enabling environment for sustainable integration and cohesive development.

3. Scope of Work

Support the technical coordination and follow-up of project activities carried out within PMM and ensure the regular and timely flow of technical information, needs and inputs among PMM, UNDP and relevant institutions.

- Coordinate the planning, implementation and follow-up of activities carried out within PMM in line with the Project Document and annual work plans, and follow up the flow of technical information and inputs between relevant PMM units and the UNDP project team.

- Contribute to ensuring that project activities are carried out in alignment with PMM’s institutional priorities, relevant policy documents and strategies, and the work programmes of its central and provincial structures.

- Coordinate technical matters among PMM central units, provincial directorates of migration management, the UNDP project team and relevant institutions, and follow up the timely communication and resolution of technical requests, institutional views and decisions.

- Collect and consolidate technical inputs from relevant units for project outputs requiring PMM review or approval, and follow up the alignment of reports, guidelines, tools, presentations and other technical documents with PMM needs and institutional priorities.

- Contribute to the review of technical deliverables prepared by experts, responsible parties and service providers against PMM needs and the agreed technical scope, and share follow-up actions with the UNDP Project Manager and relevant PMM units.

- Collect, clarify and prioritize technical and operational needs raised by PMM units and provincial directorates, ensure their timely communication to the UNDP project team, and follow up the exchange of information required for their reflection in activity plans.

- Provide administrative and operational support to project activities organized in cooperation with PMM and relevant stakeholders, including meetings, workshops, consultations, trainings, field visits, missions and other events.

- Ensure that project-related documentation, correspondence, meeting records, approvals and supporting documents are properly filed, regularly updated and maintained in line with institutional procedures.

- Support the secure storage and archiving of project records containing personal data, sensitive information or information intended for internal use, in line with applicable legislation, institutional rules and confidentiality principles.

Support PMM’s social cohesion activities at central and provincial levels.

- Support PMM in the design, implementation, follow-up and evaluation of social cohesion activities carried out under the project.

- Contribute to the regular and systematic monitoring of social cohesion activities carried out by PMM central units and provincial directorates, and to the compilation and reporting of their results.

- Contribute to the development and maintenance of up-to-date tracking tools covering implementation status, participant profiles, level of outreach, challenges encountered, emerging needs and issues requiring follow-up in relation to activities carried out at central and provincial levels.

Reinforce PMM’s field presence through research, outreach, monitoring and analytical reporting.

- Develop and keep up to date integrated tracking tools covering project activities, decisions taken, identified risks, follow-up actions, responsible parties and target dates.

Support inter-institutional coordination, partnerships and stakeholder engagement.

- Establish and maintain regular communication channels with relevant public institutions, PMM units, labour market institutions, local authorities, UN agencies, civil society organizations, service providers and other project stakeholders.

- Support coordination with institutions relevant to foreign nationals’ access to formal employment, including labour market actors and public institutions responsible for employment, vocational training, work permits and social security.

- Coordinate the preparation of agendas and technical inputs for technical coordination meetings, consultations and working groups among PMM, UNDP and relevant institutions; record decisions, actions, responsible parties and target dates; and follow up their implementation.

- Support the collection, consolidation and follow-up of feedback, views and recommendations received from PMM, provincial institutions, project partners, stakeholders and beneficiaries.

- Contribute to the coordination of social cohesion-related activities among PMM central units, provincial directorates, local authorities, civil society organizations and other relevant stakeholders.

Support data collection, data management, analysis and evidence-based decision-making.

- Support implementation of the project monitoring system in alignment with its Monitoring and Evaluation framework to ensure effective information sharing, provision of feedback and preparation of high-quality progress reports.

- Monitor existing and emerging technical, operational and field-level risks identified on the PMM side, communicate updated risk information to the UNDP project team, and follow up mitigation measures and actions agreed by the relevant parties.

Support project-related knowledge generation, knowledge sharing and capacity development.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Office/Unit/Project Description

UNDP’s Rule of Law Programme in Pakistan is working to strengthen the rule of law and to ensure equal access to justice and security services, particularly for women and marginalized groups across Pakistan in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) including the merged districts (MDs), Balochistan, and Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT). In close collaboration with a range of government, rule of law and justice sector institutions, the overall Programme aims to enhance and sustain peace and stability for the longer-term in Pakistan.

The Programme activities and interventions therefore directly correspond with the government of Pakistan’s strategies and commitments to rule of law and justice reforms, as well as improving the efficiency and effectiveness of institutions to deliver accountable and affordable security and justice services to the public.

The Rule of Law Programme implementation is guided by the following four strategic objectives:

- Policy, legal and regulatory frameworks strengthened to warrant people-centered, equitable, timely, affordable justice and security delivery to all people with an emphasis on women, marginalized and vulnerable groups, and digital technologies.

- Capacity of justice and security stakeholders (duty bearers) enhanced to deliver inclusive, timely, and accessible services to all people with an emphasis on women and digital technologies.

- Capacity of women, and the most vulnerable and marginalized (rights holders) strengthened to access referral pathways to justice and security.

- Justice and security sector institutional facilities enhanced to deliver inclusive, timely, and accessible justice and security services, through women friendly and gender-responsive infrastructure development support with an emphasis on flood resilience and green energy.

Against this backdrop, UNDP actions and interventions are aimed at restoring public confidence and service delivery in the formal justice and rule of law sectors through a range of initiatives i.e. policy development and reform, fostering justice and security sector governance, as well as oversight and accountability at an institutional level with emphasis on inclusive and gender-responsive programming. The overall engagement strategy, therefore, involves both federal and local levels. The Programme is implemented in partnership with the Judiciary, Police, Prosecution, Prisons, Probation and Reclamation, Bar Associations, Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and the academia both at federal and provincial levels.

The Project Travel and Logistics Associate will provide dedicated travel, mission, event-logistics and related administrative support for Rule of Law Programme activities. The Associate will facilitate timely and efficient arrangements for official travel, field missions, trainings, workshops, consultations, conferences and other programme activities in accordance with applicable UNDP policies and procedures.

The Associate will support travel planning and processing, logistical arrangements, travel documentation and claims, participant coordination, service-provider liaison and maintenance of accurate administrative records. S/he will contribute to smooth programme implementation by ensuring that travel and logistical requirements are anticipated, coordinated and followed through in a timely, accurate and service-oriented manner.

Scope of Work

Under the supervision of the Team Lead – Programme Specialist, the Travel and Logistics Associate will provide day-to-day travel, mission and event-logistics support for programme activities. The Associate will coordinate closely with programme personnel, operations colleagues, institutional counterparts and service providers to ensure timely, accurate and compliant arrangements.

The Associate will be responsible for the following functions:

a) Coordinate travel and mission arrangements.

- Process and coordinate official travel arrangements for programme personnel, consultants and other authorised travelers in accordance with UNDP travel policies and procedures.

- Support preparation and processing of travel requests, travel plans, itineraries, tickets, accommodation, terminal arrangements and other required travel documentation.

- Liaise with authorised travel service providers and relevant UNDP units to obtain appropriate travel options and facilitate timely issuance and amendment of travel arrangements.

- Support coordination of security-related travel requirements and ensure that required traveler and mission information is provided to the relevant focal points in a timely manner.

- Maintain an up-to-date travel and mission calendar and follow up on pending approvals, documentation and arrangements that may affect planned travel.

- Provide travelers with relevant administrative and logistical information before missions and support resolution of travel-related issues during implementation, as required.

b) Support travel claims, documentation and financial follow-up.

- Support travelers in completing required post-travel documentation and travel claims and check submissions for completeness before further processing.

- Maintain organised records of travel authorisations, itineraries, tickets, boarding passes, claims and other required supporting documentation in accordance with applicable record-management requirements.

- Coordinate with the Operations & Finance Analyst on travel budgets, advances, claims, reconciliations and other financial matters related to missions and programme travel.

- Follow up on outstanding travel documentation, advances and claims and support timely closure of completed travel actions.

- Maintain travel trackers and provide periodic information on travel status, costs, pending actions and completed missions for programme monitoring and planning.

c) Coordinate logistics for programme events and activities.

- Coordinate logistical arrangements for programme workshops, trainings, consultations, conferences, meetings and other events in collaboration with programme colleagues and institutional counterparts.

- Arrange venues, accommodation, local transportation, participant travel, interpretation, audiovisual equipment, printing, catering and other logistical services, as required and in accordance with applicable procedures.

- Support participant registration, attendance records, travel information, logistical communications and other administrative requirements for programme events.

- Coordinate logistical requirements with designated other team members while ensuring clear sequencing between substantive event planning and logistical arrangements.

- Liaise with vendors and service providers on approved logistical requirements and monitor timely delivery of agreed services, escalating issues to the responsible colleagues where necessary.

- Provide on-site logistical support during programme events and missions and facilitate timely resolution of practical and administrative issues.

d) Provide logistical and administrative support to programme implementation.

- Support arrangements for programme meetings, field visits, delegations and official visits, including schedules, transportation, accommodation and related logistics.

- Coordinate vehicle and transportation requirements for programme missions and activities with relevant UNDP service providers and administrative units.

- Support receipt, dispatch and movement of programme materials, documents and equipment associated with missions and events, as required.

- Maintain organised logistical records, service-provider information, contact lists and other administrative documentation needed for programme implementation.

- Support designated other team members with routine administrative coordination related to missions, events and field activities and ensure timely follow-up on agreed actions.

- Contribute to practical contingency arrangements for missions and events, particularly where travel conditions, security requirements or operational constraints may affect implementation.

e) Ensure compliance, coordination, service quality and effective records management.

- Ensure travel and logistical arrangements are processed in accordance with UNDP policies, procedures, applicable entitlements and approved programme budgets.

- Coordinate with designated other team members and relevant Country Office operations and administrative units to ensure appropriate sequencing, documentation and timely completion of travel and logistics actions.

- Provide relevant specifications, schedules and service information where procurement action is required for travel or logistical services.

- Monitor the quality and timeliness of travel and logistics services and promptly flag recurring service issues, operational risks or delays requiring attention.

- Provide travel and logistics information for programme workplans, implementation reviews, reports and management updates, as required.

- Keep abreast of relevant changes in UNDP travel and administrative procedures and support their consistent application within the Programme.

f) Support knowledge building, knowledge sharing and capacity building relevant to the project.

- Participate in training and organize briefings on internal procedures for the project personnel. Provide support to other capacity building activities, including to the design and delivery of tools, materials for workshops, or platforms that tap into the collective intelligence of communities and mobilize action.

- Provide support in the dissemination and sharing of relevant data and lessons learned within the CO and regionally. Keep pulse on emerging best practices nationally, regionally, and internationally that relate to the work of the project.

- Make sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice. Support compiling and systematizing project knowledge, products and tools as well as their wide distribution to partners.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Travel and Logistics Associate will be based in the UNDP Pakistan Country Office in Islamabad, with travel to programme implementation locations, particularly Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, as required.

Under the supervision of the Team Lead – Programme Specialist, the Associate will provide dedicated travel, mission, event-logistics and related administrative support for programme activities.

The Associate will work closely with programme colleagues, including technical specialists, provincial teams, as well as relevant UNDP Country Office operations and administrative units and approved service providers, to ensure timely, efficient and compliant travel and logistical arrangements.

Learn Continuously

LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

travel policy, the Staff Rules, administrative circulars and

financial regulations and rules on travel-related matters.

- A minimum of 7 years (with secondary education) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience in travel administration, logistics, event support, programme administration or related areas is required.

jobs.title: Project Management and Coordination Analyst [Open to internal and external applicant]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

As the lead United Nations agency on international development, UNDP works in 170 countries and territories to eradicate poverty and reduce inequality. We help countries develop policies, leadership skills, partnerships and institutional capabilities to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals.

As outlined in the UNDP Strategic Plan 2026-2029, UNDP’s work is guided by four strategic objectives that together define our contribution to human development: expanding prosperity for all, strengthening effective governance, safeguarding a healthy planet and building crisis resilience. These objectives are enabled by three accelerators that drive transformative impact across our portfolio: digital and AI innovation, gender equality and sustainable finance. Through this integrated approach, UNDP supports countries to deliver tangible improvements in people’s lives and to advance sustainable development at scale.

UNDP, through its Sustainable Finance Hub (https://sdgfinance.undp.org/), supports partners in promoting financing for the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). As an accelerator of the UNDP Strategic Plan, sustainable finance strengthens countries’ ability to mobilize, align and deploy finance at scale for national priorities. UNDP supports international and country level policy reform as a catalyst for system-wide change, stronger policy environments, better-functioning markets and more coherent financing strategies for sustainable development.

UNDP hosts the Secretariat of the Better Than Cash Alliance. The Better Than Cash Alliance, established in 2012, is an 80+ member partnership, including governments, corporates, industry bodies, international and regional organizations, partnering to promote the transition from cash to responsible digital payments thereby enabling meaningful financial inclusion, in order to reduce poverty, drive inclusive growth and accelerate the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals. The Alliance Secretariat delivers advisory services, supports advocacy, facilitates knowledge generation and exchanges across members, or partners, to advance equitable access to responsible digital payments and other financial services.

Billions of dollars in cash payments and transfers are made daily in emerging and developing economies, including payment of salaries, social welfare and relief, payments to suppliers, remittances, etc. The problems with these cash payments include a lack of transparency, accountability, and security, as well as inefficiency. Furthermore, the individuals who receive the cash payments are often part of the 1.3 billion excluded from the formal financial sector. This means they are excluded from access to a range of appropriate and affordable financial services to help them save safely, take advantage of economic opportunities, and reduce their vulnerability to risk.

Shifting these payments from cash to digital has the potential to improve livelihoods, particularly for women -who are twice as likely to be excluded from the financial system, providing them with more control over family finances, increasing personal security, and improving economic opportunities. The change to responsible digital payments, as an alternative to cash, further gives governments, development organizations, and the private sector a more transparent, time and cost efficient, and often safer means of disbursing payments.

The Better Than Cash Alliance Secretariat is hosted by UNDP with a globally distributed team based in Africa, Asia, and Latin America. The Alliance Management Support Team provides overall management of all operational, HR, and financial aspects of the Better Than Cash Alliance Secretariat work in full compliance with UNDP rules and regulations. The Team works to enhance the institutional effectiveness of the Alliance Secretariat in its core functional areas of accounts and finance, admin, and travel as well as operations and procurement.

Under the direct supervision of the Managing Director of the Alliance Secretariat, the Project Management and Coordination Analyst is responsible for contributing to project, financial, HR, and operations management, promoting a client-focused, quality, and results-oriented approach, working in close collaboration with the Secretariat’s Program Administrative Analyst, and the Program and Partnerships Specialist, as well as across the entire Alliance Secretariat team, and with UNDP HQ corporate operations, and UNDO Country and Regional Offices, where required. The position is strategically based with location in Kigali, Rwanda, as the Managing Director as direct supervisor, and the Head of Africa, leading the biggest budget of the Alliance’s work with 70% of resources allocated to work in Africa, are based in the same duty station.

Scope of Work

Reporting directly to the Managing Director, the Project Management and Coordination Analyst will ensure project support and day-to-day operations and will be responsible for the performance of the following duties and responsibilities:

Ensure effective project management and coordination in compliance with UNDP administrative requirements:

- Contribute to the corporate planning, monitoring, and reporting exercises;

- Contribute to the preparation of key program documents, such as the Project Document, Multi-year and annual Workplans, and further project reports, including narrative and financial reporting;

- Responsible for preparing, monitoring, and updating the program budget, including on Quantum, and constantly reviewing project revenue and expenditures, monitor budget implementation, prepare, and enter project budget revisions as may be needed. This further includes;

- Regular reporting and consultations on program delivery and budget execution with the Alliance Secretariat Global and Regional Implementation teams;

- Prepare of budgets/financial reports and other related inputs for stakeholder meetings such as the Executive Committee, and other required donor/partner reporting;

- Prepare financial authorizations to enable financial transfers/allocations, or other actions as needed to ensure smooth allocation/funds deployment processes, with close focus on any existing Letter of Agreements (LOAs);

- Review project accounts and initiate corrective actions and resolve issues on exceptional transactions, including budget errors;

- Ensure timely preparation and submission of requests for payment while coordinating inputs into the Payment tracker and full alignment with the existing Contracts;

- Contribute/respond to audit requests, program evaluation activities, as well as risk assessment procedures such as HACT (Micro Assessments, Spot Checks, Audits) and UNDP Private Sector Risk Assessment;

- Contribute to Human Resource processes for hiring, contract extensions, and other related activities, including supporting the drafting of position descriptions, hiring strategies, etc.

Ensure partnerships and coordination:

- Support in strengthening partnerships across UNDP/BPPS and especially the Sustainable Finance Hub, and with UNDP Country and Regional Offices and other UN agencies, where the Alliance Team requires support and coordinated efforts, especially regarding the organization and execution of activities on the ground in country;

- Contribute to the drafting, clearing and signing of contribution agreements with resource partners, and others such as Letters of Interest/Agreement, including managing agreements on the Quantum platform, and monitoring reporting requirements/timelines;

- Research and prepare, as needed, the Team updates on the use of any new tools/portals while ensuring full support and guidance throughout the roll out and implementation;

- Work in coordination with Project Management and Operations Analyst), and the rest of the team.

Facilitate knowledge building, knowledge sharing, and stakeholder guidance:

- Ensure facilitation of knowledge building and knowledge sharing, and provide guidance to stakeholders on financial matters;

- Synthesize lessons learned and good practices in programme and project finance;

- Contribute actively to knowledge networks and communities of practice.

The incumbent may also perform other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

Project Management and Coordination Analyst will report directly to the Managing Director (Program Manager).

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results : LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pay attention to details, deliver quality work by the deadline;

- Think Innovatively : LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements;

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback;

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible;

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident;

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships;

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination.

Cross-Functional/Technical competencies

Business Management

- Project Management Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals.

- Operations Management Ability to effectively plan, organize and oversee different parts of corporate operations, simultaneously and in an integrated way, in order to convert the organization's assets into the best results in the most efficient way. Knowledge of relevant concepts and mechanisms.

Finance

- Financial planning and budgeting Ability to create and manage processes to achieve UNDP's long and short-term financial goals, including through planning, budgeting, forecasting, analyzing and reporting.

- Budget management Ability to support budgetary aspects of work planning process, drawing and management of team budgets

- Financial reporting and analysis Understands changes in regulatory, legal and ethical frameworks and standards for financial reporting in the public sector; Ability to extract, evaluate financial data, derive relevant findings and present them in a meaningful and coherent manner to facilitate effective decision making and performance monitoring; Understands the benefits of integrated reporting, including non-financial resources such as human, social and intellectual capital, and environmental and governance performance.

Business Direction and Strategy

- System Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Partnership Management

- Relationship management Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding.

Required Skills and Experience

Education

- Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Business Administration, Public Administration, Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field is required. Or:

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the above-mentioned fields of study, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience

- Minimum of two (2) years (with master's degree) or four (4) years (with bachelor's degree) of relevant professional experience in finance, accounting, project management, programme management support or other closely related area is required.

Required skills

- Demonstrated experience in budget preparation, monitoring, expenditure analysis and financial reporting in line with donor and organizational requirements is required;

- Experience in financial reporting, quality assurance, and compliance, with established regulations, policies, or standards is required;

- Demonstrated experience using an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system for financial transaction processing and reporting is required.

Desired skills

- Demonstrated experience in developing and supporting the implementation of donor contribution and partnership agreements is desirable;

- Experience in overall operations for projects or programmes is desirable;

- Previous programme/project experience with UN is desired;

- Experience with the implementation of the UNDP HACT framework and supporting project audit exercises is desirable;

- Experience providing guidance to project personnel on budget and finance matters is desirable;

- Experience and knowledge of UN/UNDP financial rules, regulations, policies and procedures is desirable;

- Experience working in global or geographically distributed virtual teams is an asset;

- Experience and knowledge of IPSAS and/or IFRS is an asset.

Languages

- Fluency in written and spoken English is required

Professional Certificates

- Professional certification in accounting, finance or project management from a recognized international institution — such as ACCA, CPA, CIMA, CIPFA, PRINCE2 or PMP — is an advantage.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

Data Privacy

jobs.title: Asociado/a de Proyecto: Especialista en Fortalecimiento Democrático y Cooperación Parlamentaria
jobs.description:
Uruguay ha sido tradicionalmente reconocido como una de las democracias más estables de la región y continúa ubicándose entre las democracias plenas a nivel mundial. Sin embargo, sostener y profundizar la calidad democrática requiere fortalecer de manera permanente la participación cívica y política, la confianza en las instituciones y la capacidad del sistema democrático para responder a nuevas demandas y transformaciones.

El Documento de Programa de País (CPD) 2026–2030 del PNUD en Uruguay busca contribuir a un desarrollo sostenible, justo, inclusivo y resiliente, en línea con la Agenda 2030 y las prioridades nacionales, desde un enfoque transformador de género, basado en derechos humanos e interseccional. Su Outcome 3 está orientado a fortalecer una gobernanza democrática centrada en las personas que contribuya al bienestar equitativo y al desarrollo inclusivo. En particular, el Output 3.3 apunta a alcanzar: «Instituciones públicas y un Parlamento con capacidades técnicas fortalecidas para promover una gobernanza colaborativa y deliberativa que mejore la calidad de las políticas públicas mediante la transparencia, el uso de evidencia y la innovación; articule el diálogo interinstitucional; garantice la paridad y una democracia inclusiva y abierta; y cuente con sistemas robustos de monitoreo, evaluación, rendición de cuentas y prospectiva».

El Informe Regional sobre Democracia y Desarrollo del PNUD 2026 documenta un momento de presión inédita sobre las instituciones democráticas de la región, marcado por la erosión de la confianza ciudadana y la dificultad de los sistemas representativos para responder a demandas cada vez más complejas. Ello representa una oportunidad para renovar el contrato democrático desde sus cimientos institucionales y desde PNUD se está impulsando la iniciativa Instituciones Democráticas para el Futuro, que pretende promover el fortalecimiento de capacidades para anticipar el cambio, ampliar la participación y la colaboración, sostener una esfera pública plural y confiable, y aprovechar las transformaciones digitales al servicio de las personas y de la democracia.

En línea con estas prioridades, desde 2023 la Oficina del PNUD en Uruguay ha venido consolidando una agenda de trabajo orientada al fortalecimiento democrático, combinando el desarrollo de capacidades institucionales con la generación de nuevos espacios de participación, diálogo e innovación.

Como parte de esta estrategia, el PNUD en Uruguay ha venido colaborando con el Parlamento como una contraparte central para, además de contribuir a su fortalecimiento institucional, ampliar los vínculos entre representación política y ciudadanía y generar espacios de articulación entre actores políticos, sociales e institucionales. Adicionalmente, el trabajo con juventudes políticas se ha consolidado como una línea relevante para ampliar y renovar la participación democrática a través del acompañamiento al fortalecimiento de la Juventud Interpartidaria. De manera complementaria, tanto a nivel nacional como regional, desde PNUD se ha venido impulsando una agenda de democracia paritaria orientada a promover la participación política de las mujeres y el posicionamiento de la agenda de igualdad en el quehacer parlamentario. Asimismo, la integridad de la información forma parte de esta agenda de fortalecimiento democrático y de la esfera pública.

En este marco, se pretende profundizar y articular estas líneas de trabajo mediante un enfoque sistémico de fortalecimiento de la gobernabilidad democrática, fortaleciendo las capacidades de las instituciones democráticas con un enfoque de futuros, ampliando la cooperación con el Parlamento y consolidando iniciativas en materia de participación ciudadana, integridad de la información, juventudes políticas, diálogo intergeneracional, democracia paritaria, gobernanza anticipatoria, transformación digital de la democracia e innovaciones democráticas, entre otras.

Alcance del trabajo

El/la Asociado/a de Proyecto en Fortalecimiento Democrático y Cooperación Parlamentaria trabajará bajo la supervisión directa del/de la Analista de Programa – Gobernabilidad Democrática y Efectiva de PNUD Uruguay, en coordinación con las demás áreas programáticas y operativas de la Oficina País, instituciones contraparte, socios estratégicos y otros actores relevantes. La posición brindará apoyo sustantivo, técnico-operativo y de coordinación para la formulación, implementación, seguimiento y gestión del conocimiento de proyectos e iniciativas vinculadas al fortalecimiento democrático, la cooperación parlamentaria, la participación ciudadana, la integridad de la información, las juventudes políticas, la gobernanza anticipatoria, la democracia paritaria, la transformación digital y la innovación democrática.

Sus principales funciones y responsabilidades serán las siguientes:

- Apoyar la formulación, planificación y desarrollo sustantivo de iniciativas de fortalecimiento democrático y cooperación parlamentaria.

- Apoyar el diseño, formulación y planificación de proyectos e iniciativas vinculadas al fortalecimiento democrático y la cooperación parlamentaria, incluyendo participación ciudadana, integridad de la información, juventudes políticas, democracia paritaria, gobernanza anticipatoria, transformación digital e innovaciones democráticas.

- Preparar insumos analíticos, antecedentes, notas conceptuales, propuestas, planes de trabajo, marcos de resultados, presupuestos y arreglos de implementación para consideración de la supervisión y de los equipos responsables.

- Contribuir al diseño y revisión de documentos de proyecto, acuerdos, propuestas de cooperación, términos de referencia y otros instrumentos programáticos, asegurando coherencia con el Programa País, los estándares corporativos del PNUD y los enfoques de derechos humanos, género, generaciones e interseccionalidad.

- Acompañar procesos de participación, diálogo, consulta y co-creación entre instituciones públicas, actores políticos, sociedad civil, academia, juventudes y ciudadanía, incluyendo espacios interpartidarios, intergeneracionales y multiactor.

- Promover la incorporación de metodologías, herramientas y enfoques de innovación democrática, gobernanza anticipatoria, generación de evidencia, análisis de tendencias y uso responsable de tecnologías emergentes en las iniciativas bajo su ámbito de trabajo.

- Identificar oportunidades de articulación, complementariedad y sinergia entre proyectos e iniciativas del Programa País, especialmente en aquellas áreas donde el fortalecimiento democrático, la participación, la inclusión y la innovación institucional puedan agregar valor transversal.

- Sistematizar información relevante sobre tendencias nacionales, regionales e internacionales en materia de democracia, gobernanza, participación, Parlamento abierto, integridad de la información y transformación digital, a fin de alimentar la formulación de nuevas iniciativas y la toma de decisiones programáticas.

- Contribuir a la implementación, seguimiento técnico-operativo y reporte de proyectos e iniciativas asignadas.

- Apoyar la planificación operativa anual, la programación de actividades, la elaboración de cronogramas y el seguimiento de productos, hitos, indicadores, riesgos, supuestos, compromisos de socios y utilización de recursos de los proyectos e iniciativas asignadas.

- Dar seguimiento a la implementación de actividades, identificando avances, alertas, cuellos de botella programáticos u operativos y posibles medidas de mitigación, para consideración de la supervisión y de los equipos responsables.

- Coordinar insumos y preparar borradores de informes de avance, informes corporativos, reportes a donantes, revisiones de cartera, comités de proyecto, auditorías, evaluaciones y ejercicios de cierre, según corresponda.

- Revisar la calidad, consistencia y oportunidad de la documentación programática y de gestión preparada para los proyectos e iniciativas bajo su ámbito de trabajo, proponiendo ajustes antes de su elevación.

- Mantener una articulación periódica con contrapartes, socios, consultores/as, proveedores y equipos internos, facilitando la coordinación de actividades y el flujo oportuno de información para la implementación.

- Preparar y dar seguimiento a términos de referencia, solicitudes de contratación, adquisiciones, viajes, pagos, acuerdos y otros procesos operativos necesarios para la ejecución de las iniciativas, en coordinación con Operaciones y conforme a las normas y procedimientos del PNUD.

- Apoyar la revisión de productos elaborados por consultores/as, instituciones socias o proveedores, verificando su consistencia con los términos de referencia, los resultados esperados y los estándares de calidad acordados.

- Contribuir a la aplicación de herramientas de gestión basada en resultados, gestión de riesgos, HACT, salvaguardas, seguimiento financiero, monitoreo y cierre de proyectos, de acuerdo con las orientaciones institucionales.

- Brindar apoyo técnico-operativo, logístico y de coordinación a misiones, reuniones, talleres, consultas, diálogos, procesos participativos, actividades de formación y otros espacios vinculados a los proyectos e iniciativas asignadas.

- Contribuir al desarrollo de alianzas, movilización de recursos, comunicación estratégica y gestión del conocimiento.

- Preparar análisis, mapeos de actores, perfiles de socios, notas de antecedentes y otros insumos sustantivos que contribuyan al desarrollo de alianzas estratégicas y oportunidades de cooperación en materia de fortalecimiento democrático y cooperación parlamentaria.

- Identificar oportunidades de financiamiento, cooperación técnica y alianzas con instituciones públicas, Parlamento, partidos políticos, sociedad civil, academia, organismos internacionales, sector privado y otros actores relevantes, para consideración de la supervisión.

- Contribuir a la elaboración de ideas de proyecto, conceptos, propuestas y documentos de movilización de recursos, asegurando coherencia con el CPD, las prioridades nacionales, el enfoque de gestión basada en resultados y los requisitos corporativos.

- Participar en reuniones técnicas con contrapartes y socios, presentar información sobre avances, necesidades y oportunidades, y facilitar acuerdos de trabajo dentro de su ámbito funcional y bajo la orientación correspondiente.

- Sistematizar buenas prácticas, innovaciones, metodologías, resultados, aprendizajes y desafíos derivados de los proyectos e iniciativas, contribuyendo a la generación de evidencia y al posicionamiento del PNUD como socio estratégico en la agenda democrática.

- Preparar notas conceptuales, minutas, informes, presentaciones, insumos de comunicación, productos de conocimiento y otros materiales dirigidos a distintas audiencias internas y externas.

- Contribuir a la difusión de experiencias, metodologías y aprendizajes en redes, comunidades de práctica, espacios de formación, intercambios regionales y actividades externas relacionadas con las líneas de trabajo bajo su responsabilidad.

- Apoyar la implementación de estrategias de comunicación de los proyectos e iniciativas, en coordinación con los equipos responsables, asegurando mensajes claros, inclusivos y consistentes con el posicionamiento institucional del PNUD.

La persona contratada estará bajo la supervisión directa del/de la Analista de Programa – Gobernabilidad Democrática y Efectiva de PNUD Uruguay. Trabajará en coordinación con la gerencia de la oficina (RR/DRR), las demás áreas programáticas y operativas de la oficina, así como con las principales contrapartes relacionadas con los temas asignados.

Competencias esenciales

Obtener resultados:

NIVEL 1: Planifica y supervisa su propio trabajo, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajos de calidad dentro del plazo establecido.

Pensar de forma innovadora:

NIVEL 1: Abierto a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, es pragmático en la resolución de problemas, realiza mejoras

Aprender continuamente:

NIVEL 1: Mente abierta y curiosa, comparte conocimientos, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con agilidad:

NIVEL 1: Se adapta a los cambios, gestiona de forma constructiva la ambigüedad y la incertidumbre, es flexible.

Actuar con determinación:

NIVEL 1: Muestra empuje y motivación, capaz de actuar con calma ante la adversidad, seguro de sí mismo

Participar y asociarse:

NIVEL 1: Demuestra compasión/comprensión hacia los demás, establece relaciones positivas.

Fomentar la diversidad y la inclusión:

NIVEL 1: Apreciar/respetar las diferencias, ser consciente de los prejuicios inconscientes, enfrentarse ante la discriminación.

Gestión de personas

La posición no tendrá responsabilidades de supervisión de personal.

Competencias transversales y técnicas (insertar hasta 7 competencias)

Área temática

Nombre

Definición

Gestión institucional

Gestión basada en resultados

Capacidad para gestionar programas y proyectos con un enfoque en la mejora del rendimiento y resultados demostrables. Conocimiento y comprensión de las teorías, los conceptos, las metodologías, los instrumentos y las herramientas relevantes.

Gestión institucional

Gestión de proyectos

Capacidad para planificar, organizar, priorizar y controlar recursos, procedimientos y protocolos para lograr objetivos específicos.

Gestión empresarial

Trabajar con pruebas y datos

• Capacidad para inspeccionar, depurar, transformar y modelar datos con el objetivo de descubrir información útil, fundamentar conclusiones y apoyar la toma de decisiones.

Gestión empresarial

Concienciación y alfabetización digital

• Capacidad e inclinación para adoptar rápidamente nuevas tecnologías, ya sea dominando su uso o comprendiendo su impacto y capacitando a otros para utilizarlas según sea necesario

Gestión empresarial

Comunicación

• Capacidad para comunicarse de forma clara, concisa y sin ambigüedades, tanto por escrito como verbalmente; para adaptar los mensajes y elegir los métodos de comunicación en función de la audiencia. Capacidad para gestionar las comunicaciones internas y externas, a través de los medios de comunicación, las redes sociales y otros canales adecuados

Desarrollo de negocios

Generación de conocimiento

Habilidad para investigar y transformar información en conocimiento útil, relevante para el contexto o que dé respuesta a las necesidades establecidas.

Gestión de redes y alianzas
