Background

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan.

Within the GPN, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policy and guidance to support the results of UNDP's Strategic Plan. BPPS's staff provides technical advice to Country Offices, advocates for UNDP corporate messages, represents UNDP at multi-stakeholder fora including public-private dialogues, government and civil society dialogues, and engages in UN inter-agency coordination in specific thematic areas. BPPS works closely with UNDP's Crisis Bureau (CB) to support emergency and crisis response. BPPS ensures that issues of risk are fully integrated into UNDP's development programmes. BPPS assists UNDP and partners to achieve higher quality development results through an integrated approach that links results-based management and performance monitoring with more effective and new ways of working. BPPS supports UNDP and partners to be more innovative, knowledge and data driven including in its programme support efforts.

The newly established UNDP Planet Hub will drive UNDP’s vision of a world where economies and ecosystems thrive together — where energy systems are clean and accessible, nature is protected and restored, communities are resilient to climate impacts, and pollution is minimized. By 2030, the Hub seeks to help countries achieve this vision through systemic change that aligns policy, finance, integrated solutions, and societal ownership to advance sustainable human development. Backed by diverse partnerships and funding sources, the Planet Hub combines thought leadership, technical expertise, and strategic collaboration to help countries advance their environmental and economic goals.

The Planet Hub will build on UNDP’s existing portfolio of over USD 5 billion in over 140 countries, as well as on key offers across UNDP. The Planet Hub’s theory of change rests on five mutually reinforcing service lines that together enable systemic transformation:

- Intergovernmental and UN System Coherence and Support

- National Policies, Strategies, and Planning

- Innovative and Integrated Solutions

- Scaled-up Finance

- Insights, Modeling, and Data

The Planet Hub will be made up of eight interconnected pillars, covering strategic areas of work to deliver its core objective, as well as a set of integrated functions and support that cut across pillars and help ensure cohesive offers and delivery of the Planet Hub. One critical component of the Planet Hub is the portfolio of support to countries on Forests, Land Use and Food Systems. The Forests, Land Use and Food Systems Pillar advances integrated approaches to sustainable land management, forest conservation and restoration, sustainable food systems, and resilient landscapes, recognizing their critical role in addressing climate change, biodiversity loss, environmental degradation, and sustainable development challenges. The Pillar brings together UNDP’s work on forests, land use planning, sustainable agriculture, food systems transformation, ecosystem restoration, nature-positive development, and landscape approaches, while supporting countries to achieve climate, biodiversity, and land degradation objectives under relevant Multilateral Environmental Agreements. Working across the Planet Hub and in collaboration with governments, local communities, Indigenous Peoples, development partners, and the private sector, the Pillar promotes integrated solutions that enhance environmental sustainability, strengthen livelihoods, improve food security, and contribute to resilient and inclusive development pathways.

The Head of Forests, Land Use & Food Systems will be based in Bonn, Germany and will report to the Director of the Planet Hub.

Position Purpose

To help support UNDP’s Strategic Plan, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) established the post of Head of Forests, Land Use & Food Systems in the Planet Hub. As the leader of this portfolio, the incumbent will directly support the Planet Hub’s goals by playing a leading role in coordinating the delivery of the Hub’s strategy across different areas of policy and programming. This includes overseeing the Forests, Land Use & Food Systems portfolio.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

Substantive Leadership and Management

- Provide substantive leadership of UNDP’s Forests, Land Use & Food Systems, ensuring coherent and effective support to regional bureaux and countries.

- Ensure effective coordination and integrated ways of working across the Planet Hub, including with other pillars and functional teams.

- Substantively guide the Forests, Land Use & Food Systems Pillar to achieve and maintain coherent development policies and programming frameworks in support of the implementation of the Strategic Plan.

- Exercises overall responsibility and accountability for planning, implementation, management, monitoring, and coordination and ensure appropriate tracking and substantive reporting of the Forests, Land Use & Food Systems portfolio for timely and efficient delivery of portfolio outputs and products leading to the achievement of expected results.

- Provide supervision and guidance to Forests, Land Use & Food Systems team leads and other other senior advisors in leading their teams to provide substantive services to country offices related to Forests, Land Use & Food Systems and Planet more broadly.

- Promotes collaboration and establishes effective working relationships with internal stakeholders (project teams, Regional Bureaux, Country Offices, GPN, etc.) and external stakeholders (donors, partners, civils society).

- Establish and oversees a monitoring system of the global impacts and achievements of the Forests, Land Use & Food Systems across projects and programmes.

- Provide substantive and managerial oversight of relevant Hub staff at the global and regional levels; and

- Participate as part of the Planet Hub Leadership Team, sharing information across pillars and informing strategic direction and decisions for the Hub as it relates to Forests, Land Use & Food Systems.

Integrated Policy Formulation and Programme Support

- Oversee and coordinate the corporate UNDP policy positions in relation to Forests, Land Use & Food Systems, drawing on expertise within the pillar, across the Planet Hub and across the organization.

- Promote collaboration across the GPN on Forests, Land Use & Food Systems, including across the new BPPS (e.g. Governance and Rule of Law Hub, Prosperity Hub, Sustainable Finance Hub, Hub, Gender Team, Digital, AI and Innovation Hub, Quality and Impact Hub) as well as Crisis Bureau (e.g. Crisis Readiness, Response and Recovery Team, Research, Analytics, Learning and Innovation Team, and Strategic Partnerships and Communications Team).

- Lead integrated technical support related to Forests, Land Use & Food Systems, by activating the broad network of UNDP expertise related to this thematic area so as to ensure relevant and timely support to Country Offices and partners.

- Oversee the implementation of programming and operational management of the Forests, Land Use & Food Systems portfolio, including being custodian of quality assurance and second tier oversight (delegated as appropriate), in accordance with UNDP Programme Operations Policies and Procedures (POPP), UN Frameworks and project strategy documents.

- Support integrated pipeline development in coordination with the other teams and thematic hubs, including the Sustainable Finance Hub and the Quality and Impact Hub, based on consultations with Senior Technical Advisors, Regional Team Leads.

- Collaborate with other thematic team leads within and beyond the Planet Hub and the Strategic Innovation Unit on the design of integrated portfolios to address complex issues at the country, regional and global levels; and

- Manage efficiently the financial resources of the Forests, Land Use & Food Systems portfolio, including budgeting and budget revisions, as well as expenditure tracking and reporting as needed including in support of the Planet Hub.

Thought Leadership and Positioning and Lead Cross-Organization Knowledge and Learning

- Keep abreast of the impact and effectiveness of UNDP’s portfolios related to Forests, Land Use & Food Systems and connect that knowledge and lessons learned to future development and improvement.

- Liaise closely with Regional Bureaux, BERA and other parts of the GPN to identify regional/global priorities, opportunities and needs that could be supported/engaged by the Planet Hub, with a focus on Forests, Land Use & Food Systems.

- Lead cross-organization knowledge and learning in Forests, Land Use & Food Systems related domains, grounded in the UNDP knowledge strategy, with a view to leveraging all-of-house knowledge in UNDP and in external networks, within which meaningful south-south exchange should be a priority.

- Lead and promote capturing knowledge emerging from the development and implementation of programmes at global, regional and country level.

- Identify and develop ways of integrating and analysing data and intelligence from both internal and external sources that connect UNDP’s partnership performance with larger political, economic and development cooperation trends.

- Lead and contribute to global knowledge management and practice networks to position UNDP as a thought leader on Forests, Land Use and Food Systems, promoting the dissemination of knowledge, evidence, innovations, and lessons learned related to sustainable landscapes, ecosystem restoration, sustainable agriculture, food systems transformation, biodiversity conservation, and climate-resilient land-use practices.

- Analyse global economic and political trends and provide strategic forward-looking analysis of UNDP’s positioning related to Forests, Land Use & Food Systems with key partners, and advise on how best to leverage its external relations opportunities and minimize risks for the organization; and

- Scan the horizon, particularly from a political and economic perspective, and assess implications for UNDP’s role as a major multilateral development partner. Monitor the strategic positioning of UNDP with bilateral, UN, and other multilateral institutions, to identify key risks and opportunities.

Resource Mobilization, Advocacy and Communications

- Support the Planet Hub Director on hub-wide resource mobilization, strategic communication and partnership and programme development to enable delivery of the Planet Hub strategy.

- Develop strategies and carry out mobilization of resources related to <Pillar>, in coordination with other teams across the Planet Hub, and ensure effective utilization of resources in the context of meeting the Hub’s objectives.

- Coordinate and work closely with units within the Planet Hub and across the GPN on developing new approaches and strategies for resource mobilization.

- Communicate the value and results of UNDP’s work to contributors and constituents to advocate for meeting the needs of SDGs and national development priorities; and

- Coordinate with BERA and Regional Bureaux to leverage expertise, networks, and channels around Forests, Land Use & Food Systems and broader Planet issues, including promoting results and sharing information, while also developing external branding, and inspiring people into action.

Develop Strategic Partnerships, Representation and Engagement

- Develop strategic partnerships, working with the Planet pillars and Sustainable Finance Hub, the Regional and Central Bureaux, to ensure the development of a global portfolio on Forests, Land Use & Food Systems, that draws on all available sources of funding.

- Maintain and develop strong partnerships with key donors of UNDP’s work on Planet, to ensure continued support and explore opportunities for future support.

- Mobilize, foster and strengthen strategic partnerships with UN Agencies and Funds, particularly UNEP, FAO, WMO, SE4ALL, IFAD, ILO, UN-HABITAT, and the secretariats of GEF, GCF, UNFCCC, UN CBD, UNCCD; and other agencies within the UN.

- Forge key partnerships with governments and CSOs; encourage South-South partnerships.

- Expand partnerships with IFIs, Multilateral development Banks, OECD/DAC, Impact Investors and the Private Sector.

- Oversee partnerships relevant to Forests, Land Use & Food Systems, with strategic external partners, such as World Bank, Multilateral Development Banks, research institutions and Foundations, and other partnerships.

- Represent UNDP in interagency coordination and in other fora to engage partners in advancing the strategic agenda of Forests, Land Use & Food Systemsand sustainable development; and

- Represent UNDP at international conferences and seminars, contribute to research, communications and op-eds to advocate the importance of Forests, Land Use & Food Systems in contributing to the sustainable development goals.

- Identify and spearhead opportunities for large-scale innovation in UNDP's partnership strategies, particularly around <Pillar>, to advance the Planet Hub and deliver on the Strategic Plan.

- Lead corporate discussions on identifying strategic opportunities for engagement and advocacy around Forests, Land Use & Food Systems, and be accountable for distilling key messages through consultative processes.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: Supervision, management, performance management, and development of global staff and consultants will be required.

The Head of Forests, Land Use and Food Systems will supervise a globally distributed team of personnel across Bonn, New York and other locations, including direct reports at the global level and secondary reporting personnel, including Regional Specialists supporting forests, sustainable landscapes, land restoration, sustainable agriculture, and food systems portfolios across UNDP Regional Bureaux.

Competencies

- Core Competencies:

Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact.

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems.

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences.

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands.

Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results.

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration.

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity.

- People Management

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

- Cross Functional and Technical Competencies:

2030 Agenda - planet - Nature:

- Ecosystems and Biodiversity: Access and benefit sharing of biodiversity, land, forests and oceans.

- Ecosystems and Biodiversity Programme: Protected and Conservation Areas and Systems.

Business Direction and Strategy - System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Business Management:

- Partnerships Management: Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies.

- Result-based Management: Ability to manage the implementation of strategies, programmes, and projects with a focus at improved performance and demonstrable results. Knowledge and understanding of relevant theories, concepts, methodologies, instruments, and tools.

- Portfolio Management: Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity. Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment. Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management.

Business Development - UNDP Representation: Effectively represent and advocate for UNDP, its values, mission, work, and positions with various constituencies/audiences, shares UNDP knowledge and activities.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced University Degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Natural Sciences, Environmental Management, International Development, Economics, Public Administration, or a closely related field. Or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum of 10 years (with master’s degree) or 12 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant progressively responsible experience on Forests, Land Use and Food Systems at the international level is required;

- Demonstrated experience in designing and managing complex programmes and strategies to support the implementation of global initiatives related to Forests, Land Use and Food Systems is an asset;

- Extensive field-level experience in sustainable land management, forest conservation and restoration, landscape approaches, sustainable agriculture, food systems transformation, biodiversity conservation, ecosystem management, and/or nature-based solutions in developing country contexts is required;

- Substantive knowledge and practical application of forests, land use planning, food systems, sustainable agriculture, climate-land-food nexus, and relevant policy frameworks and Multilateral Environmental Agreements, including the UNFCCC, UNCBD, and UNCCD are required;

- Experience and solid understanding of Multilateral Environmental Agreements, including UNFCCC, UNCBD and UNCCD among others, and its relevant technical and policy areas is required;

- A strong track record in overseeing and managing large-scale programmes and portfolios; demonstrated thought leadership in areas such as sustainable landscapes, sustainable agriculture, food systems transformation, and/or climate-resilient land-use planning is required;

- Solid and demonstrable understanding of the capacity-building needs to strengthen technical and institutional capacities in the forest, land use and food systems sectors at country or regional level is an asset;

- Working experience in developing country contexts including extensive experience advising national and subnational governments on forest governance, sustainable land management, food systems policies, sustainable agriculture, land-use planning, and implementation of national commitments under relevant environmental agreements and frameworks is an asset;

- A strong record of progressively responsible, substantive and results-oriented experience at the international level, including in policy and programming, resource mobilization and advocacy is an asset;

- Established professional networks of international organizations, think tanks and/or advocacy organizations in areas related to Forests, Land Use and Food Systems, sustainable development, finance and other relevant areas are an asset;

- Experience in business systems, human resources management and budgeting is required;

- Experience in management of disbursed teams, and budgeting of complex programmes and/or portfolios is an asset;

- Proven track record of resource mobilization from public and/or private sources is an asset;

- Extensive working experience in international organizations, especially in UN organizations is desirable;

- Excellent communications skills with public speaking experience are required.

Language:

- Fluency in English, both written and oral is required.

- Fluency in other UN languages is an asset.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Probation

For all new UNDP fixed term appointments (FTA), including for staff members being transferred or seconded to UNDP under the Inter-Organization Agreement concerning Transfer, Secondment or Loan of Staff, on an appointment of more than one year, continuation of the appointment beyond the initial 12 months is contingent upon the successful completion of a probationary period.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

jobs.title: Asociado(a) en Comunicación Estratégica
jobs.description:
Descripción de Proyecto:

México impulsa el cambio de política industrial más significativo en tres décadas a través del Plan México, bajo la premisa de que la acción climática y el desarrollo económico equitativo son objetivos que se refuerzan mutuamente. Esta política industrial verde busca relocalizar cadenas de valor estratégicas, fortalecer la capacidad productiva nacional y movilizar una inversión estimada en 277,000 millones de dólares en cinco años, a través de dos instrumentos: el Decreto de estímulos fiscales del 21 de enero de 2025, y los Polos de Desarrollo Económico para el Bienestar (PODECOBI)[1].

La implementación de los PODECOBI se coordina a través del Comité Intersecretarial de Promoción, presidido por la Subsecretaría de Industria y Comercio (SIC) de la Secretaría de Economía, con participación de dependencias de la Administración Pública Federal. La Subsecretaría de Industria y Comercio es responsable de operacionalizar las condicionalidades de ambos instrumentos y de promover su adopción entre el sector productivo y los gobiernos estatales.

Con el acompañamiento del PNUD, la SIC implementa un Plan de Iniciación de 18 meses con un equipo técnico especializado en evaluación de proyectos, análisis financiero, sostenibilidad y economía circular, desarrollo social y coordinación regional, orientado a pilotear el monitoreo de las condicionalidades verdes, explorar esquemas de financiamiento mixto e institucionalizar herramientas para una transición industrial más sostenible. La intervención se alinea con el Efecto 5 del Marco de Cooperación de las Naciones Unidas 2026-2031 y el Output 2.1 del Documento de Programa País del PNUD México (indicador 2.1.1).

[1]Zonas delimitadas en entidades federativas que combinan incentivos fiscales y facilidades administrativas con condicionalidades climáticas, ambientales y de viabilidad social. A la fecha existen 14 PODECOBI declarados en 14 entidades federativas.

Alcance de Trabajo:

Sus funciones principales incluirán:

1.- Apoyar en la estrategia de comunicación para informar sobre el avance /o resultados del Plan de Iniciación

- Elaborar piezas de comunicación, como presentaciones, infografías y demás materiales gráficos que respalden la difusión de resultados ante tomadores de decisión.

- Preparar y proporcionar materiales de comunicación estratégica, como informes ejecutivos, presentaciones y notas de resultados, orientados a tomadores de decisión.

- Compilar y estructurar los avances del proyecto para su difusión ante la SIC, el PNUD

- Examinar que los productos de comunicación reflejen con precisión la contribución del proyecto a los objetivos de empleo digno, integración productiva regional y sostenibilidad de los PODECOBI.

- Preparar y estructurar materiales visuales, como presentaciones, infografías y piezas gráficas, que comuniquen los avances y resultados del Plan de Iniciación.

- Apoyar el análisis del posicionamiento institucional del proyecto entre actores estratégicos, generando insumos para fortalecer la estrategia de comunicación y difusión de resultados.

- Proponer acciones de mejora en la estrategia de comunicación y diseño de materiales del proyecto.

2.- Diseñar y producir materiales visuales estratégicos

- Colaborar en el diseño de materiales visuales que traduzcan sus avances técnicos en productos claros y accesibles

- Ejecutar la producción de piezas gráficas para informes técnicos, reportes institucionales y espacios de difusión del proyecto.

- Revisar la calidad visual y la consistencia de imagen de los materiales generados para el proyecto.

3. Apoyar la creación, el intercambio y el desarrollo de capacidades relevantes para el proyecto.

- Compilar el Informe de Documentación de Aprendizajes y los materiales visuales de comunicación necesarios para el PRODOC.

- Participar en capacitaciones y organizar sesiones informativas sobre procedimientos internos para el personal del proyecto.

- Apoyar otras actividades de desarrollo de capacidades, incluyendo el diseño y la entrega de herramientas, materiales para talleres o plataformas que aprovechen la inteligencia colectiva de las comunidades y promuevan la acción.

- Apoyar la difusión y el intercambio de datos relevantes y lecciones aprendidas dentro del proyecto.

- Mantenerse al tanto de las mejores prácticas emergentes a nivel nacional, regional e internacional relacionadas con el trabajo del proyecto asignado.

- Apoyar la recopilación y sistematización del conocimiento, los productos y las herramientas del proyecto, así como su amplia distribución a los socios.

Desempeñar otras funciones dentro de su perfil funcional que se consideren necesarias para el funcionamiento eficiente de la Oficina y la Organización.

Acuerdo institucional:

El/la Asociado(a) en Comunicación Estratégica estará bajo la supervisión directa de la titular de la Unidad de Desarrollo Social.

Competencias Esenciales:

Logro de Resultados: Nivel 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

Pensar Innovadoramente: Nivel 1: Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente: Nivel 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agilidad: Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre de manera constructiva, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación: Nivel 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

Participar y Asociarse: Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión:Nivel 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación.

Requisitos Académicos Mínimos:

- Educación secundaria (certificado de preparatoria) completa es requerida.

- Título universitario (Licenciatura) en Comunicación, Diseño Gráfico, Comunicación Visual, Mercadotecnia, Diseño Digital o áreas afines se dará debida consideración, pero no es requisito.

Años Mínimos de Experiencia Reqerida:

- Se requiere de mínimo 6 seis años (con educación secundaria) o 3 años con (estudios universitarios de primer nivel) de experiencia profesional relevante en elaboración de materiales de comunicación estratégica orientados a tomadores de decisión. Así como en diseño y producción de materiales visuales (presentaciones, infografías, reportes gráficos) para audiencias institucionales .

Habilidades Requeridas:

- Experiencia en la elaboración de materiales de comunicación estratégica orientados a tomadores de decisión.

- Experiencia en el manejo de herramientas de diseño gráfico y edición visual (p. ej. Adobe Creative Suite, Canva, PowerPoint avanzado u otras).

- Experiencia en el manejo de herramientas de visualización de datos, como Power BI, para la construcción de tableros e indicadores.

Habildiades Deseadas:

- Experiencia en la sistematización y difusión de resultados e impacto de proyectos o políticas públicas.

- Experiencia en proyectos de comunicación institucional con gobiernos subnacionales u organismos internacionales.

- Experiencia en el manejo de instrumentos de política industrial o de desarrollo regional.

Idiomas Requeridos:

- Fluidez en español es requisito.

- Nivel básico de inglés, no es requisito pero se dará debida consideración.

Al ser una contratación nacional al aplicante debe ser ciudadana/o mexicana/o en pleno ejercicio de sus derechos, o extranjera/o, cuya condición migratoria permita la función a desarrollar

jobs.title: Project Analyst, Digitalization of the Visa Issuance System [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP Montenegro has a longstanding partnership with the Government of Montenegro in advancing digital transformation, focusing on digital government infrastructure, e-services, interoperability, institutional capacities and digital skills. This support is aligned with national priorities and Montenegro’s EU accession process, helping institutions strengthen their ability to meet evolving EU standards and deliver more efficient, accessible and citizen-centred public services. A particular focus has been placed on using digital technologies to make public services more accessible, efficient and responsive to the needs of general population. UNDP has supported the development of key digital government infrastructure, as well as the development of increasingly sophisticated electronic services. These interventions aim to improve interoperability across public administration, shorten administrative procedures, reduce administrative burdens and enable faster and more user-centred delivery of public services.

Digital transformation is increasingly important to Montenegro’s EU accession, supporting stronger interoperability, data management, transparency and institutional efficiency. Within the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, this is particularly relevant to the continued modernisation of the national visa issuance system. Alignment with the EU visa and Schengen acquis requires not only procedural and policy adjustments, but also secure, interoperable and sustainable digital systems and the institutional capacity to manage evolving technical requirements.

Building on its cooperation with the Ministry, UNDP will support the modernisation of the Montenegro Visa Information System and the related technical infrastructure. The intervention will combine system development, infrastructure upgrades, capacity building, training and technical assistance ensuring continuity of services while strengthening the Ministry’s readiness to respond to future EU requirements.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the oversight of the Team Leader for Governance and Responsive Institutions and direct supervision of the Programme Analyst for Digital Governance Acceleration in the UNDP Office in Montenegro, the Project Analyst will support the day-to-day coordination and implementation of the intervention, working across project management, policy and technical areas. Through close coordination with the Ministry and technical specialists, the position will help ensure that system development, infrastructure, capacity building and stakeholder engagement are implemented coherently and on time, contributing to more efficient, secure and sustainable visa-related services.

The Project Analyst will ensure effective and efficient implementation of relevant project activities and delivery of the results as per the annual workplans, and in line with the prevailing UNDP rules and procedures, as well as with due compliance with the UNDP Internal Control Framework. The Project Analyst will execute duties and responsibilities outlined below in the following functional areas:

Support partnerships and advocacy activities at project level:

- Manage and implement project activities in a gender-sensitive and inclusive manner, while ensuring effective coordination of technically complex activities related to the digitalisation and modernization of Montenegro’s visa issuance system, including the development and deployment of the new Visa Information System and supporting technical infrastructure

- Contribute to the further development of the project through its promotion and partnership-building with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, relevant national institutions, diplomatic and consular missions, international partners, EU stakeholders, and technical service providers involved in visa management, digital transformation, interoperability, and EU accession

- Coordinate resource mobilization activities and engage in dialogue with donors for activities within the project framework

- Maintain regular communication with donors and actively participate in the design and development of follow-up and complementary projects

- Contribute to the formulation and development of new projects and strategic plans aligned with UNDP’s strategic focus, national priorities, Montenegro’s EU accession commitments, and gender equality objectives, drawing on lessons learned from the implementation of technically and operationally demanding digital transformation interventions

- Advise UNDP on strategic and technical matters related to the digitalisation of visa services, EU visa policy and the Schengen acquis, interoperability, data exchange, biometric systems, cybersecurity, data protection, digital public services, and institutional readiness

- Monitor implementation progress and ensure quality, accuracy, and timeliness of reporting to donors and project partners, and internally within UNDP

- Maintain regular communication with other UN Agencies, CSOs, international organizations, EU institutions and partners, and relevant stakeholders interested in supporting digital transformation

- Identify and develop new interventions aligned with national priorities and Montenegro’s EU accession trajectory, building on UNDP Montenegro’s existing portfolio and practical implementation experience, including opportunities to further strengthen the Ministry of Foreign Affairs’ digital and institutional capacities and to scale up or replicate interoperable, secure, and user-centred digital solutions across relevant public administration services

Ensure management of the project and implementing activities, in accordance with the UNDP policies and procedures:

- Assist in identifying and mobilizing relevant technical expertise required for project and activity implementation, including specialized inputs related to information systems development, business-process analysis, system architecture, interoperability, cybersecurity, biometric technologies, ICT infrastructure, testing, deployment, and quality assurance

- Advise the respective Programme Analyst and Team Leader on potential adjustments of actions, sequencing, and procedures, considering evolving implementation requirements, operational constraints, risks, EU accession requirements, changes in EU visa-related systems and standards, and technical or institutional considerations affecting the project implementation

- Maintain regular communication and provide advisory and implementation support to identified institutional partners, particularly the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and relevant diplomatic and consular missions

- Organize and manage project teamwork in line with the Project Document

- Supervise and coordinate consultants and vendors - prepare and assign tasks, monitor progress, and ensure effective coordination across technical and operational functions. Ensure their timely coordination and recruitment, including profiles with strong technical, ICT, information systems, cybersecurity, data management, interoperability, and digital transformation backgrounds, in line with UNDP procedures and gender-sensitive recruitment principles

- Ensure that project work plans are prepared and updated in a timely manner and accurately reflect project objectives, outputs, implementation phases, system development and deployment activities, procurement processes, capacity-building activities, and delivery milestones as defined in the Results and Resources Framework

- Ensure that procurement of goods and services under the project is undertaken in an optimal, timely, and quality-assured manner, in compliance with UNDP rules and relevant technical, information-security, data-protection, and operational standards

- Identify, assess, and manage potential project and reputational risks, and propose appropriate mitigation measures in coordination with the Programme Analyst for Digital Governance Acceleration

- In cooperation with the Project Assistant, support the maintenance of complete and accurate financial and accounting records for all project activities (budget, commitments, expenditures, income), ensuring proper follow-up on expenditures, approvals, and financial reporting

- Be responsible for the title transfer and proper registration of all assets procured and used under the project, including ICT equipment and other technical assets provided to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and its relevant diplomatic and consular network

- Monitor use of project resources, including approval of requisitions in Quantum (UNDP’s ERP system) and certification/confirmation of receipt of goods and services

- Ensure that outputs and results produced by the project are adequately documented and communicated, in coordination with relevant institutions and donors, including progress and results related to the development, testing, deployment, and operationalization of the Visa Information System, supporting infrastructure, institutional capacity-building, and alignment with EU requirements

- Regularly monitor relevant developments, events, and topics in local, regional, and international media related to the project’s thematic scope.

Ensure implementation of knowledge management activities:

- Capture lessons learnt during project implementation and support development of case studies and storytelling for portfolio results, with particular focus on the digitalization of national platforms, institutional capacity-building, and alignment with evolving EU requirements

- Facilitate strategic innovation processes using established frameworks, applying systems thinking and portfolio approaches to digital transformation and modernization of national platforms

- Ensure regular exchange of information/experience with other projects, cross-learning and sharing results and good practices, particularly in relation to digital public services, information systems, interoperability, cybersecurity, biometric technologies, and EU accession-related digital transformation

- Contribute to the learning and knowledge sharing within UNDP and among external partners at the country, regional and global levels

- Participate in regular internal meetings, training events, communities of practice, and other relevant knowledge-sharing and learning activities.

Ensure gender mainstreaming:

jobs.description:

Background

The Information and Communication Technology Section (ICTS) serves as a strategic enabler and innovation partner for the United Nations Volunteers (UNV), supporting digital transformation across the organization. ICTS provides and evolves cloud platforms, business applications, enterprise data services, cybersecurity capabilities, service management, automation, AI-enabled solutions, and a modern digital workspace for UNV.

The ICTS Data Team enables evidence-based decision-making by developing and maintaining enterprise data pipelines, data models, analytics products, governance practices, and business intelligence solutions. The role provides seasoned technical and advisory support to strengthen UNV's enterprise data platform, ensuring that data from volunteer management, HR, finance, programme, ERP, and external sources is integrated, governed, documented, monitored, and made available for reliable reporting, analytics, and emerging AI/ML use cases.

Scope of Work

The ICT Specialist - Data Engineering will provide seasoned technical leadership, subject matter expertise, platform modernization, data governance, DataOps, and analytics enablement support to UNV ICTS. The role functions as a lead technical resource for enterprise data engineering and related platform capabilities, providing technical authority through architecture guidance, engineering standards, quality assurance, and expert advisory services rather than through direct supervision of UNV personnel.

Duties and Responsibilities

A. Technical leadership, subject matter expertise, and enterprise data platform architecture

- Act as a technical authority for UNV ICTS Data Teams's enterprise data engineering function, providing expert guidance on enterprise data architecture, platform design, data integration strategies, governance frameworks, and engineering standards.

- Serve as UNV ICTS Data Team's technical subject matter expert for enterprise data engineering and data platform architecture, providing authoritative technical guidance for the design, evolution, modernization, and optimization of UNV's enterprise data platform, including cloud-native data pipelines, data stores, transformation frameworks, governance capabilities, and analytics enablement.

- Exercise independent technical judgment, establish technical best practices, influence technology direction, and provide authoritative advice to management, stakeholders, and external service providers on matters relating to enterprise data platforms, analytics capabilities, and data governance.

- Establish and maintain technical standards, architectural principles, reusable engineering patterns, and best practices to support organizational reporting, analytics, AI-enabled solutions, and data-driven decision-making.

B. Data integration, transformation, and engineering delivery

- Design, develop, and optimize scalable ETL/ELT workflows to ingest, cleanse, transform, and load structured and semi-structured data from UNV source systems and external APIs into governed data stores.

- Develop reusable transformation frameworks using Azure Data Factory, Databricks, PySpark/Python, SQL, Delta Lake, and related tools to ensure repeatable, idempotent, version-controlled, and performant data processing.

- Implement reliable data-processing logic for batch and, where applicable, near-real-time data flows, ensuring that pipelines are resilient to source-system changes and operational interruptions.

C. Data modelling, semantic layer, and analytics enablement

- Lead the design and enhancement of dimensional, normalized, and semantic data models that support operational reporting, self-service analytics, enterprise dashboards, and advanced analytical workloads.

- Collaborate with business analysts, BI developers, and stakeholders to translate business requirements into trusted data products that are usable, performant, and aligned with UNV reporting needs.

- Support optimization of Power BI semantic models, DAX measures, data refresh processes, and model performance in collaboration with BI colleagues.

D. Data quality, governance, lineage, and compliance

- Design and implement data validation frameworks, quality checks, anomaly detection, lineage documentation, technical metadata repositories, and catalog entries to improve data reliability and transparency.

- Advise on practical implementation of data governance principles, access patterns, documentation standards, and compliance-oriented controls in data engineering solutions.

- Document business rules, data definitions, transformation logic, dependencies, known limitations, and data-quality thresholds for critical datasets.

E. DataOps, automation, CI/CD, and observability

- Develop and maintain CI/CD pipelines for data engineering code using Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions, or similar tooling.

- Implement automated testing, validation, and deployment practices across development, staging, and production environments.

- Establish monitoring, alerting, and logging using appropriate observability tools to support reliable operations, incident analysis, and continuous improvement.

F. Business intelligence, reporting, and decision support

- Support the design, development, optimization, and lifecycle management of Power BI reports, dashboards, data models, measures, and analytical products.

- Ensure BI solutions are grounded in reliable, well-governed data and are documented through functional specifications, business rules, data model diagrams, measures, deployment pipelines, and UAT criteria.

- Contribute to improved data accessibility and usability for management reporting, operational monitoring, and evidence-based decision-making.

G. Stakeholder engagement, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement

- Work with ICTS teams, business sections, data consumers, and stakeholders to identify data needs, define data-product requirements, resolve data-quality issues, and promote a data-driven culture.

- Produce and maintain pipeline architecture diagrams, data dictionaries, runbooks, deployment guides, and knowledge materials.

- Participate in code reviews, peer testing, engineering best-practice discussions, and continuous improvement activities.

- Perform other duties within the functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The NPSA holder will work under the direct supervision of the Team Lead of the UNV ICTS Data Team. The incumbent will serve as a lead technical resource and subject matter expert for enterprise data engineering and related platform capabilities within UNV. The role provides technical leadership through architecture guidance, engineering standards, quality assurance, and expert advisory services.

While the position has no formal supervisory responsibility over UNV personnel, the incumbent will be expected to coordinate, guide, review, and manage the work of external vendor consultants, contractors, and technical resources engaged by UNV for data engineering, analytics, reporting, and related digital initiatives. The incumbent will provide technical direction, prioritize deliverables, review outputs, ensure quality standards, and support acceptance of vendor-delivered solutions.

The role is home-based and will work collaboratively with ICTS colleagues, data engineers, BI developers, business analysts, and business stakeholders using agreed ICTS work-management, version-control, sprint, documentation, and deployment practices.

Core Competencies

Achieve Results

- Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Learn Continuously

- Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Adapt with Agility

- Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Act with Determination

- Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

Engage and Partner

- Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

Enable Diversity and Inclusion

- Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

People Management: The position has no direct supervisory responsibilities. The role is intended to provide technical leadership and vendor/resource oversight through subject matter expertise, architecture guidance, quality assurance, and management of vendor-delivered outputs, not through line management of UNV staff.

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Data Engineering

- Ability in programming languages such as SQL, Python; ability to work with warehousing solutions and ETL tools; and understanding of basic machine learning and algorithms.

Data strategy and management

- Knowledge to draft or execute a data strategy or data management framework.

Data governance

- Knowledge of data science and skills to develop data management tools, organize and maintain databases, and operate data visualization technologies.

Data analysis

- Ability to extract, analyse, and visualize data to form meaningful insights and aid effective business decision-making.

Data Management & Analytics

- Knowledge in data management and data sciences; ability to structure data, develop dashboards and visualization, and design data warehouses, data lakes, or data-platform concepts.

Solutions Architecture

- Ability to design and manage information-system architecture supporting corporate business processes and integration strategies across applications and services.

Working with Evidence and Data

- Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform, and model data to discover useful information, inform conclusions, and support decision-making.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in Computer Science, Data Engineering, Information Technology, Information Systems, Engineering (any), Mathematics, Statistics, Data Science, or a related discipline is required; or

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor's degree or equivalent) in the same areas in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

Required skills:

- Hands-on experience with Azure Data Factory or equivalent ETL/ELT tools;

- Experience with Databricks, Delta Lake, Azure SQL, data lakes, warehouses, or lakehouse architecture;

- Experience implementing data quality, validation, metadata, lineage, and governance practices;

- Experience with CI/CD and version control for data solutions;

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section:

- Experience with monitoring/observability tools such as Azure Monitor or Application Insights;

- Experience with AI/ML data pipelines, feature engineering, or analytics enablement;

- Experience producing architecture diagrams, runbooks, data dictionaries, and functional specifications.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in Sierra Leone supports the United Nations system through its integrated offer, using a people-first approach centred on the ‘leave no one behind’ principle, and a human rights- and area-based development strategy. In alignment with the 2030 Agenda, National Development Plan, United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework, the African Union Agenda 2063, the programme seeks to reduce multidimensional poverty and enhance justice, peace, social cohesion, and resilience with its focus on two pillars: (a) People-centred sustainable development and resilience, prioritising people’s well-being and planetary health and (b) Inclusive governance, peace, and prosperity, embodying harmonious development, effective resource management, and equitable governance. Furthermore, the UNDP comparative advantage includes leveraging global and regional partnerships, working across economic, social, and environmental goals, strengthening good governance, and providing technical and policy-oriented support, all while ensuring national ownership for sustainable outcomes.

In 2025, UNDP signed an agreement with the United Nations Multi‑Partner Trust Fund Office (MPTFO) to implement the project activities under Spotlight Initiative 2.0 in Sierra Leone. Within this framework, UNDP serves as the hosting agency for the Programme Coordination Team, which is embedded in UNDP and supported administratively by the Country Office. The team consists of a Programme Coordinator, an M&E and Knowledge Management Specialist, a CSO and Advocacy Analyst, and Operations Analyst (Finance and Administration).

To ensure the timely implementation of project activities and maintain the highest standards of accountability, the UNDP Spotlight team requires dedicated financial and administrative support. He/she will will provide essential operational, logistical, and administrative support regarding managing financial and administrative processes, while each Reciepient UN Agency for the Spotlight Programme follows its financial regulations and ensures compliance, the Analyst will coordinate common financial planning and monitoring of financial delivery. Additionally, the Analyst will undertake administrative tasks, including coordinating meetings, maintaining documentation, and supporting procurement processes.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the overall supervision of the Spotlight Programme Coordinator and in coordination with the Spotlight Program coordination team and the UNDP operations unit, the Operations Analyst (Finance and Administration)will perform the following functions:

Ensure Financial Management and Administrative Coordination

- Provide financial and administrative support for the effective implementation of Spotlight Programme coordination activities in accordance with UNDP rules, regulations, policies, and procedures.

- Monitor the Spotlight Programme budgets, expenditures, and delivery rates, ensuring proper utilization of resources and timely identification of financial discrepancies or implementation delays across the four UN agencies.

- Review the Spotlight Programme coordination related payment requests, invoices, supporting documentation, and financial records for completeness, accuracy, and compliance prior to submission for processing.

- Support the four UN agencies in budget planning, expenditure forecasting, and preparation of budget revisions and financial projections as required.

- Maintain and oversee financial and administrative filing systems, ensuring accurate record keeping, traceability, and accessibility of documentation for the Spotlight programme coordination activities.

- Monitor deadlines related to payments, contracts, reporting, and operational processes, and proactively follow up on pending actions.

- Support the organization of missions, meetings, workshops, and events, including administrative and financial coordination arrangements.

Ensure procurement, contracts, and operational support

- Support procurement and contract management processes in compliance with UNDP procurement policies and procedures.

- Prepare, review, and maintain procurement, contractual, and administrative documentation, ensuring completeness and compliance with audit and operational requirements.

- Monitor procurement plans, contract implementation status, vendor documentation, and payment schedules to support timely project delivery.

- Review vendor invoices and supporting documents against contractual terms, deliverables, and approved budgets before payment processing.

- Coordinate with suppliers, service providers, consultants, and relevant stakeholders to resolve administrative and operational issues in a timely manner.

- Contribute to the preparation of terms of reference, requests for quotations, evaluation documentation, and administrative justifications related to procurement and contracting actions.

- Support asset and inventory tracking related to project implementation and ensure proper documentation and record management.

- Contribute to improving operational workflows, administrative tracking tools, and filing systems to strengthen efficiency and accountability.

Reporting compliance, project support and facilitating knowledge management

- Contribute to the preparation of financial, operational, and administrative reports by compiling, reviewing, and validating supporting documentation and expenditure data.

- Support compliance with UNDP financial, administrative, and operational procedures through regular monitoring and verification of project records and transactions.

- Coordinate the organization and maintenance of documentation for audits, evaluations, monitoring missions, and verification exercises.

- Identify financial or administrative issues and escalate them to the supervisor with proposed corrective actions and follow-up recommendations.

- Provide administrative and operational support for implementation of annual work plans, procurement plans, and project reporting requirements.

- Support knowledge management and documentation of operational processes, lessons learned, and best practices related to project implementation.

- Ensure confidentiality, transparency, accuracy, and integrity in the management of project financial and administrative information and documentation.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation.

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline.

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

- Monitoring & Evaluation Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programmes, and activities with a view to make sure that they are being implemented effectively; Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback and reporting on the consistency or discrepancy between planned activities and programme management and results; Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming; Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools; Ability to make an independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks; Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.
