jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP Moldova supports the Government of the Republic of Moldova in strengthening public finance management, domestic resource mobilization, and development financing systems so that public resources are mobilized, allocated, and used more effectively in support of national development priorities and the Sustainable Development Goals. This work is closely linked to Moldova’s EU accession process and implementation of the EU-Moldova Growth Plan, which place increasing demands on fiscal governance, expenditure efficiency, public investment management, revenue mobilization, institutional capacity, and the effective implementation of reforms.

In this context, UNDP works closely with the Ministry of Finance, the State Tax Service, line ministries, and other national institutions to strengthen the analytical and institutional foundations of fiscal policymaking. The approach combines support to public finance reforms with applied policy analysis, institutional capacity development, knowledge exchange, and access to regional and global expertise. Particular emphasis is placed on ensuring that reforms are embedded in government systems and processes rather than implemented as stand-alone interventions.

Public Finance for Development in Moldova

Since 2009, the Ministry of Finance of the Slovak Republic, in partnership with UNDP, has supported Moldova in modernizing its public finance management system. Over successive phases, the cooperation has evolved from support to programme-based budgeting and analytical reporting towards a broader public finance agenda focused on expenditure efficiency, fiscal analysis, domestic resource mobilization, and stronger institutional capacities for evidence-based decision-making.

The current Public Finance for Development in Moldova project is implemented under Component 1 of the regional Public and Private Finance for Development (PPFD) programme, financed by the Ministry of Finance of the Slovak Republic. The project builds on previous cooperation between UNDP and the Government and supports implementation of the Public Finance Management Development Strategy 2023-2030, while contributing to broader reforms associated with Moldova’s EU accession and economic governance agenda.

The project aims to strengthen the institutional, regulatory, and analytical capacities of the Government to improve the quality of public finance management and better align fiscal policies and public expenditure with national development priorities and the SDGs. It supports the transition from individual analytical exercises towards sustainable government functions, methodologies, and institutional practices that can be applied systematically across sectors.

A central area of intervention is the continued development and institutionalization of spending reviews as a regular instrument of public expenditure management. UNDP supports the Ministry of Finance and relevant line ministries in applying the national Spending Review Methodology, strengthening analytical capacity, assessing the efficiency and effectiveness of public programmes, and improving the use of evidence in budget preparation and medium-term expenditure planning. The objective is not limited to identifying potential savings, but also to support better prioritization of public resources, improve value for money, and strengthen the link between policy objectives, programme performance, and budget decisions.

This work builds on earlier spending reviews in priority sectors and on the progressive establishment of the legal, methodological, and institutional framework required for spending reviews to become a permanent government function. The reform is particularly relevant as Moldova faces growing investment and reform needs while fiscal space remains constrained, increasing the importance of ensuring that existing public resources generate stronger development results.

A second major area of engagement is domestic resource mobilization and tax policy. Through the Tax for SDGs initiative, UNDP supports the Ministry of Finance and the State Tax Service in strengthening the analytical basis for tax policy decisions and in using taxation not only as a revenue instrument, but also as a tool to advance broader development objectives. Areas of support include health-related and environmental taxation, analysis of tax expenditures, assessment of fiscal and distributional implications of tax policy options, and institutional capacity development. Analytical work under the initiative helps national counterparts assess trade-offs between revenue, competitiveness, social outcomes, and behavioral effects and supports more evidence-based approaches to tax reform.

Complementing this work, Moldova participates in the Tax Inspectors Without Borders (TIWB) initiative implemented jointly by UNDP and OECD. TIWB provides specialized technical assistance to strengthen tax audit capacities, including in areas such as transfer pricing and international taxation. The initiative contributes to protecting the national tax base, improving the effectiveness of tax administration, and strengthening national capacity to address increasingly complex cross-border tax issues.

The project also supports broader analytical and policy work related to development finance, including the use of fiscal instruments to support national priorities, the assessment of financing needs and policy options, and the integration of public finance considerations into wider development planning. This builds on earlier UNDP-supported work, including the Development Finance Assessment, which helped map Moldova’s public and private financing landscape and identify opportunities to improve the alignment of financing flows with national development objectives.

Biodiversity Finance

UNDP Moldova also implements the GEF8 Umbrella Programme to Design a National Biodiversity Finance Plan, which supports the Republic of Moldova in developing a systematic approach to identifying biodiversity financing needs, expenditure patterns, financing mechanisms and opportunities for mobilizing and improving the effectiveness of financial resources for biodiversity.

The project forms part of the global Biodiversity Finance Initiative (BIOFIN) and supports implementation of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, including through development of Moldova’s first national Biodiversity Finance Plan. Technical implementation is undertaken in close cooperation with national counterparts, the UNDP Climate Change, Environment and Energy Cluster and relevant regional and global BIOFIN expertise.

Within the present assignment, the Project Manager will support the effective administrative, operational and financial management of the BIOFIN project, including planning, contracting, monitoring, reporting and coordination of project implementation. Substantive and technical leadership for biodiversity policy and biodiversity finance will be provided by the Climate Change, Environment and Energy Cluster and the relevant Green Finance Specialist(s).

Strategic relevance

The project is implemented at a time when Moldova’s public finance system is assuming an increasingly important role in the country’s EU accession process and implementation of the Growth Plan. Public finance management is closely connected to the Government’s capacity to plan and execute investments, absorb external financing, manage fiscal risks, improve public services, and demonstrate credible implementation of reform commitments.

Current reform priorities include expenditure efficiency, medium-term fiscal planning, public investment management, tax policy modernization, revenue administration, digitalization of public finance systems, and stronger alignment with EU economic governance requirements. The effectiveness of these reforms increasingly depends not only on policy design, but also on the ability of institutions to implement, monitor, and sustain them over time.

Recent engagement with international financial institutions has similarly highlighted implementation capacity, expenditure efficiency, fiscal sustainability, and institutional effectiveness as important elements of Moldova’s reform trajectory. This reinforces the relevance of practical support that combines policy analysis with institutional strengthening and effective implementation.

Through the Public Finance for Development project, UNDP therefore provides a platform for sustained cooperation with the Ministry of Finance, State Tax Service, line ministries, and other national institutions on public finance reform. The project also facilitates access to Slovak, regional, and international expertise through the UNDP Istanbul Regional Hub and relevant global initiatives, supporting peer learning and the adaptation of international good practices to Moldova’s institutional and EU accession context.

The project forms part of UNDP Moldova’s broader effective governance and development financing work, helping strengthen the connection between fiscal policy, institutional performance, and development outcomes. Its implementation is based on close partnership with national institutions, evidence-informed policymaking, national ownership, and the progressive integration of new analytical approaches into regular government processes.

Duties and Responsibilities

Summary of key functions:

The Project Manager- SDG Finance will work under the direct supervision of the UNDP Moldova Policy Specialist and in close coordination with the Effective Governance and CCEE Cluster Leads. The incumbent will ensure the effective implementation of the Public Finance for Development project and contribute substantive and analytical support to UNDP Moldova’s work on public finance management, taxation and development finance.

The Project Manager will also support the operational, administrative and financial management of the GEF8 Biodiversity Finance (BIOFIN) project, working in close coordination with the Climate Change, Environment and Energy Cluster, which will provide substantive and technical leadership for biodiversity-related work.

The Project Manager will combine project planning and implementation responsibilities with technical coordination, quality assurance, partnership management, monitoring and knowledge development. The incumbent will work closely with the Ministry of Finance, the State Tax Service, relevant line ministries, the UNDP Istanbul Regional Hub, and other national and international partners engaged in public finance reform.

More specifically, the SDG Finance Project Manager will be responsible for:

Project planning, management and implementation

- Coordinate the operational and financial planning of assigned projects’ activities, including annual work plans, procurement, recruitment, budgeting and implementation schedules, in line with strategic direction provided by the Policy Specialist and the Country Office.

- Manage the day-to-day implementation of projects’ activities, ensuring timely delivery of outputs, efficient use of resources and compliance with UNDP rules, procedures and agreed work plans.

- Coordinate the work of the Project Associate, consultants, service providers and technical experts engaged under the assigned projects, provide operational and substantive guidance as appropriate, and facilitate effective interaction with national counterparts and partners.

- Monitor projects’ risks and implementation challenges and propose appropriate corrective or adaptive measures.

- Ensure effective coordination between project activities related to spending reviews, taxation, domestic resource mobilization and broader public finance reform.

Technical coordination and quality assurance

- Guide and support the technical coordination of Public Finance for Development project activities related to public finance management, expenditure efficiency, taxation and development finance, including implementation of project-supported spending reviews.

- Support implementation of the Tax for SDGs initiative and Tax Inspectors Without Borders activities, including coordination with the Ministry of Finance, State Tax Service, line ministries, UNDP, OECD and relevant technical experts.

- Review analytical studies, technical reports, methodologies, policy notes and other project deliverables, and coordinate revisions to ensure consistency with agreed objectives and quality standards.

- Undertake background research and analytical work and contribute to policy briefs, analytical summaries, presentations, briefing materials and talking points.

- Coordinate with relevant UNDP regional and global initiatives to facilitate access to technical expertise, methodological guidance and international experience.

Partnership building, resource mobilization and policy coordination

- Maintain effective working-level coordination with the Ministry of Finance, State Tax Service, relevant line ministries and other national institutions involved in project implementation.

- Support the substantive preparation and organization of policy consultations, technical meetings, workshops, missions and other project-related engagements.

- Maintain regular coordination with the UNDP Istanbul Regional Hub and contribute to engagement with development partners, international financial institutions and other stakeholders active in public finance reform.

- Support the Policy Specialist and Effective Governance and CCEE Cluster Lead in identifying emerging priorities, partnerships and potential areas for further UNDP engagement, including through substantive inputs to concept notes, project proposals and resource mobilization initiatives

Monitoring and reporting

- Monitor implementation of the assigned projects against approved work plans, results frameworks, indicators and agreed milestones, and ensure systematic collection of information and evidence required for reporting.

- Coordinate the preparation of project progress updates, narrative reports and other required reporting for UNDP, national counterparts, donors and relevant regional or global programmes, in consultation with the respective substantive programme leads.

- Monitor the assigned projects’ financial delivery, commitments and expenditure in coordination with relevant programme and operations colleagues.

- Support progress reviews, risk assessments, project assurance processes and timely operational and financial closure of activities.

Knowledge management and capacity development

- Document lessons, good practices and implementation experiences and support their dissemination within UNDP and among national and regional partners.

- Support national counterparts in strengthening institutional and analytical capacities through technical workshops, peer learning, practical guidance and experience exchange.

- Facilitate knowledge transfer from Slovak, regional and international public finance experience to national counterparts and support adaptation to Moldova’s institutional context.

- Contribute to knowledge, communication and visibility products and to broader Country Office analytical and programme work on public finance management, taxation and development finance.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangements:

The Project Manager -SDG Finance will work under the direct supervision of the UNDP Moldova Policy Specialist and in close coordination with the Effective Governance and CCEE Cluster Leads. The incumbent will oversee the day-to-day work of the Project Associate and coordinate the work of consultants and technical experts engaged under the assigned projects, as applicable.

The Project Manager will work in close cooperation with relevant UNDP Moldova Country Office teams and with the UNDP Istanbul Regional Hub, including the Regional Programme Specialist for Public Finance for SDGs, to support effective project implementation, ensure alignment with regional and global approaches, facilitate access to technical expertise, and contribute to timely resolution of substantive and operational issues. This coordination will be particularly relevant for activities related to public finance management, Tax for SDGs, Tax Inspectors Without Borders and broader SDG finance work.

The incumbent will maintain regular coordination with national counterparts, including the Ministry of Finance, the State Tax Service and other relevant public institutions, as well as with development partners and technical stakeholders engaged in public finance management, taxation and development finance.

For the GEF8 Biodiversity Finance project, the Project Manager will be responsible primarily for operational, administrative and financial coordination, including work planning, procurement and contracting processes, financial monitoring, reporting and implementation follow-up. The Climate Change, Environment and Energy Cluster, under the guidance of the Programme Specialist, will provide substantive and technical leadership for biodiversity policy, BIOFIN methodology and related technical outputs.

The Project Manager will also contribute to knowledge exchange and coordination between country-level activities and relevant regional and global initiatives, including by sharing implementation experience, analytical findings and lessons that may inform broader Public Finance for SDGs work.

Background:

Suriname's mangrove ecosystems are among the country's most valuable natural assets. Covering nearly 86,000 hectares and accounting for approximately 0.6% of the world's mangrove area (SBB, 2023; FAO, 2023), they provide critical habitat for biodiversity, support fisheries, strengthen climate resilience, and sustain coastal livelihoods and community well-being in areas where nearly 90% of the country's population resides (ABS, 2024). They also provide a foundation for sustainable economic opportunities through tourism, research, education, and other nature-based sectors.

UNDP has been a key development partner of the Surinamese Government and its people since 1994 and continues to support Suriname through its three broad programmatic areas: Democratic Governance, Social Development, Environment, Climate Change and Natural Resource Management. The three programmatic areas are interlinked, integrating nature-based solutions, justice and social services with the engagement of stakeholders that are relevant to all three programmatic areas.

UNDP in partnership with the European Union has been supporting Suriname in preservation and conservation of mangrove forests, especially through the two phases of the Global Climate Change Alliance (GCCA+) programmes; phase one: from March 2016 to August 2019 and phase 2: 2020- 2023. In 2024, UNDP and EU launched a new initiative Protection, Restoration, and Sustainable Use of Mangrove Forest (PRSUMF) project (2024 to 2027).

The PRSUMF project builds on the results achieved in strengthening mangrove protection and conservation by the GCCA+ programme. The PRSUMF project aims to support Suriname in building the resilience of target coastal communities through inclusive, gender-responsive coastal zone management, mangroves conservation, and sustainable use.

SBB. 2023. Mangrove Monitoring System: Total Mangrove Forest Area per District in Suriname (2023).

FAO. 2023. The World's Mangroves 2000-2020.

ABS. 2024. Population and Housing Census (Census 9), population distribution by district.

The project aims to achieve this objective:

a) By strengthening coordination, legal and strategic frameworks, for integrated coastal zone management, water management, coastal defense, and governance.

b) By enhancing the meaningful participation of local communities in the co-management of mangroves and Multiple Use Management Areas (MUMAs) and

c) By increasing sustainable income generation with a focus on women and youth, from mangrove-based value chains such as honey, fisheries, and mangrove ecosystem based-tourism.

Through the above approach, the project aims to support mitigation of rising sea levels impact, frequent flooding, and support the country’s population to adapt to climate change by playing a central role in mangrove protection, restoration and sustainable use through nature positive economic activities.

The project is implemented through a Project Management Unit (PMU) headed by the Project Manager. The Communications Associate will be part of the project management unit.

Scope of Work:

The incumbent will contribute to stakeholder engagement, knowledge sharing, visibility, and public awareness efforts that support achievement of project outputs and donor communication requirements. S/He will work under the direct supervision of the Project Manager, and the overall guidance of the Deputy Resident Representative of UNDP Suriname. The Communications Associate will also work in close collaboration with the Technical Officer of the PRSUMF project.

The Communication Associate will design and implement specific targeted public relations (PR) and media activities highlighting project activities, results and accomplishments, including related products and articles for social media distribution.

Key functions and responsibilities of the Communication Associate include:

a. Implement and revise the Media/Communication and Visibility Plan as needed:

- Monitor implementation of and periodically update the Project Communication and Visibility Plan based on emerging communication needs, project progress, and donor requirements.

- Based on the Communication and Visibility and Communications Plan, develop a Media/Communication Action Plan and relevant budget in close collaboration with the Project Manager and supporting PMU members.

- Develop graphic designs for third party production (audiovisual and or print) in support of project branding communication and visibility, in line with UNDP and EU communication guidelines and requirements.

- Maintain and expand the network of project stakeholders and media and maintain regular contact with and provide information to media on project activities and project progress.

- Ensure and monitor visibility through the proper and correct use of logo’s during events, in photo-, audio-, and video productions and on all publication materials, equipment, materials and goods financed by the project as agreed with donors.

b. Lead knowledge management and dissemination:

- Liaise with specific sector specialists and technical resource persons for the development of folders, brochures and presentations and other communication material on climate change, mangrove conservation, sustainable use of mangroves for economic development.

- Develop and maintain a repository of communication, visibility, and knowledge products, ensuring accessibility and institutional memory for the project.

c. Support awareness and training activities of the project:

jobs.title: National Technical Specialist Roster - Sustainable human development
jobs.description:
1. Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) China Country Office is part of UNDP—the United Nations' global development network. UNDP works in about 170 countries and territories, helping to end poverty, reduce inequalities and exclusion, as well as protect the planet, in line with the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Together, these efforts aim to ensure that improvements in human wellbeing remain within ecological boundaries. We also help countries to develop policies, leadership skills, partnering abilities and institutional capabilities, as well as build resilience, in order to achieve the SDGs.

UNDP China has been working in China over the past four decades, partnering to advance various phases of China’s development outlined in the Government of China’s Five-Year Plans. UNDP assists China in integrating the SDGs into development decisions, promotes the transition to an inclusive, low-carbon economy and a sustainable society, protects biodiversity, and informs China’s international development cooperation engagement to advance global progress on the SDGs and the global climate agendas. In addition, UNDP leverages its global network and South-South Cooperation (SSC) to facilitate mutual knowledge and experience sharing between China and partner countries on best practices and lessons learned to advance the SDGs.

UNDP China’s implementation modalities currently engage more than 15 Ministries and government representatives at the national and sub-national levels in 28 provinces. UNDP China also actively engages the United Nations development system, multilateral and regional institutions, the private sector, philanthropic foundations, academia and think tanks, intergovernmental bodies, and the media to accelerate the SDGs and global climate agendas in China.

The incumbent works with the other project experts and counterparts of the Government as well as engages with other national institutions, international organizations, and other relevant actors.

Roster validity:

Successful candidates will be included in the UNDP China technical Roster for a period of one (1) year, with possibility of extensions.

However, inclusion on the roster does not guarantee any active assignment and financial commitment during its validity. The actual engagement will be structured on an on-demand basis and remuneration will be calculated based on the actual amount of services rendered as requested by the UNDP China.

When a request for services arises, UNDP China will contact the individuals categorized under the specific area of expertise, providing the assignment description, location, and dates, and seeking confirmation of availability.

Partnership Management - Multi-stakeholder engagement and funding Knowledge and ability to forge multi-stakeholder partnerships, and remove any obstacles to resource mobilization and multi-stakeholder funding platforms.

jobs.title: National Field Coordinator (Nationals Only)
jobs.description:
Organization Setting and Reporting Relationships:

The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) is the part of the United Nations Secretariat responsible for bringing together humanitarian actors to ensure a coherent response to emergencies.

OCHA’s mission is to:

- Mobilize and coordinate effective and principled humanitarian action in partnership with national and international actors to alleviate human suffering in disasters and emergencies.

- Advocate for the rights of people in need.

- Promote preparedness and prevention.

- Facilitate sustainable solutions.

OCHA provides support to the Humanitarian Coordinator (HC) and the Humanitarian Country Team (HCT) in Sudan. Working with the entire humanitarian community, OCHA looks to foster a conducive operating environment that facilitates the effective delivery of humanitarian assistance.

OCHA also promotes compliance with humanitarian principles in the humanitarian response. This is an essential element of effective humanitarian coordination and is central to establishing and maintaining access to affected people, particularly in conflict-affected areas of Sudan.

Responsibilities: Under the immediate supervision of the Head of Access Unit in Khartoum, and under the overall supervision and direction of the Deputy Head of Office and Head of Office, the incumbent is expected to perform the following: will be responsible for the following

• Supports the Deputy Head of Office, Head of Office and sub-offices in implementing an access strategy for the Sudan context, including actor mapping and context analysis of access dynamics.

• Monitors, analyses, and reports on humanitarian developments, disaster relief/management or emergency situations.

• Reviews and provides advice on humanitarian access, safeguarding humanitarian principles and ensuring effective delivery of humanitarian assistance; organizes and supports follow-up work, including inter-agency technical review meetings to support access work and decision-making on important issues.

• Drafts and prepares regular access papers/reports highlighting relevant policy and operational factors affecting access, the humanitarian situation, and response efforts.

• Supports the maintenance of an access database, including access monitoring, reporting and analysis, providing timely analysis and updates to various coordination key stakeholders.

• Organizes and prepares studies on humanitarian, emergency relief and related issues; organizes follow-up work, including inter-agency technical review meetings to support policy development work and decision-making on important issues.

• Partners with other humanitarian agencies to plan and evaluate humanitarian and emergency assistance programmes and help ensure that latest findings, lessons learned, policy guidelines, etc. are incorporated into these activities, including gender-related considerations.

• Provides substantial support to sector/cluster working groups as required and facilitate exchange on humanitarian access.

• Supports negotiations with relevant stakeholders to establish/maintain humanitarian access and resolves any arising constraints, while working to promote a principled, coordinated approach to access, and shares best practice with partners to ensure effective and coordinated humanitarian access strategies across the country.

• Undertakes and provides support to technical assistance and field missions, e.g., participates in field trips to undertake in-depth reviews of specific humanitarian access issues. Organizes and participates in working groups, meetings, conferences, consultations with other agencies and partners on humanitarian access-related matters.

• Prepares or contributes to the preparation of various written reports, documents and communications, e.g., drafts sections of studies, background papers, policy guidelines, parliamentary documents, briefings, case studies, presentations, correspondence, etc.

• Establishes and maintains contacts with government officials, other UN agencies, non- governmental organizations, diplomatic missions, media, etc. Supports access advocacy initiatives on issues impacting humanitarian needs and response efforts through the collection of information, liaison with humanitarian partners, government officials, etc.

• Establishes and maintains contacts with government officials, other UN agencies, non- governmental organizations.

• Supports field offices and provides advice and technical assistance on engagement with government bodies.

• Participates in formulating and communicating OCHA positions on government-related matters on humanitarian issues, providing suggestions for briefing notes, talking points and issues papers for relevant discussions with the Government.

• Responds to queries from government Officials, NGOs, individuals, etc. and provides the information required or appropriately refers the queries elsewhere.

• Supports OCHA Sudan staff in meetings with government officials and facilitate conversations for smooth representation of OCHA.

• Participates in any relevant meetings and conferences organized by authorities.

- Performs other duties as required.

Results Expected:

Support humanitarian access operations in Sudan through access analysis, stakeholder engagement, coordination, reporting, and advocacy. Monitor humanitarian developments, maintain access information systems, support negotiations and engagement with government authorities and partners, prepare reports and briefing materials, provide technical support to field offices, and contribute to coordinated humanitarian response efforts to ensure effective and principled delivery of assistance.

Competencies:

- Professionalism: Knowledge of a range of humanitarian assistance, emergency relief and related human rights issues, including approaches and techniques to address difficult problems. Analytical capacity and in particular the ability to analyze and articulate the humanitarian dimension of issues which require a coordinated UN response. Ability to identify issues and judgment in applying technical expertise to resolve a wide range of problems. Ability to conduct research, including ability to evaluate and integrate information from a variety of sources and assess impact on the humanitarian rights situation in assigned country/area. Ability to work under extreme pressure, on occasion in a highly stressful environment (e.g. civil strife, natural disasters and human misery); ability to provide guidance to new/junior staff. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. Able to analyze and interpret data in support of decision-making and convey resulting information to management.

- Communication : Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately; asks questions to clarify, and exhibits interest in having two-way communication; tailors language, tone, style and format to match audience; demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping people informed.

- Teamwork : Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others’ ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings.

- Planning& Organizing : Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently.

- Client Orientation : Considers all those to whom services are provided to be “clients” and seeks to see things from clients’ point of view; establishes and maintains productive partnerships with clients by gaining their trust and respect; identifies clients’ needs and matches them to appropriate solutions; monitors ongoing developments inside and outside the clients’ environment to keep informed and anticipate problems; keeps clients informed of progress or setbacks in projects; meets timeline for delivery of products or services to client.

Required Education, Experience, Skills and Competencies

Minimum Education requirements:

Master’s Degree preferably in Political or Social Science, Law, international studies, Public Administration, or another relevant Field

OR

Bachelor’s degree with two additional qualifying years in above fields may be accepted in lieu of the Masters.

Minimum years of relevant work experience:

A minimum of 5 years (with a master’s degree) or 7 years (with Bachelor’s degree) of relevant progressively responsible experience in humanitarian affairs, emergency preparedness, crisis/emergency relief management or other related areas, preferably with at least two years with a UN organization or an NGO.

Required skills

- Humanitarian experience in the field (actual setting where a mission and/or project is being implemented) in emergencies (complex emergency or natural disaster) is required.

- At least 3 years of humanitarian access and government liaison work in a UN or INGO are required.

- Experience in McCord, including understanding principles, mechanisms, and engagement with military and security bodies, is required.

- Excellent knowledge of government structures and dynamics, including the cultural, political, and economic dimensions, is required.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

- Ability to relate humanitarian affairs issues and perspectives to political, economic, social and human rights is desired.

- Strong negotiation and diplomatic skills are desired.

- Ability to work under pressure, on occasion in a highly stressful environment is desired.

- Excellent knowledge of institutional mandates, policies and guidelines about humanitarian affairs – particularly on humanitarian access, bureaucratic and administrative procedures, regulatory environment, and government policies is desired.

- Excellent knowledge of the institutions of the UN system and inter-agency coordination is desired.

- Excellent knowledge of humanitarian access issues is desired.

- Excellent writing skills are required.

- Fluency in English and Arabic is required

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

OFFICE/UNIT/PROJECT DESCRIPTION

For six decades, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has shaped advances in human development, providing large-scale, integrated support to improve the lives of millions of people worldwide. As part of its Strategic Plan 2026-2029, UNDP will continue to support countries' progress towards high-level human development while protecting the planet. Its strategic direction is defined by four strategic goals—prosperity for all, effective governance, resilience to crises, and a healthy planet—supported by three accelerators: digital transformation and AI, gender equality, and sustainable finance. All are reinforced by a commitment to human rights and a determination to leave no one behind.

In Gabon, UNDP contributes to the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF, 2023-2027) with national partners through its interventions in the areas of inclusive governance; the environment and climate change; the reduction of poverty and inequality; and the promotion of gender equality.

In 2024, the Government of Gabon and UNDP agreed on the implementation of UNDP’s flagship Programme d’Urgence et de Développement Communautaire (PUDC) in Gabon over the 2025-2027 period. The PUDC’s main objective is to boost the economic and social development of rural areas by improving basic infrastructure and providing economic opportunities for local populations. The Programme aims to reduce poverty, promote social inclusion, and strengthen the resilience of rural communities by investing in key sectors such as health, education, water and energy infrastructure.

In order to accelerate the implementation of the infrastructure projects under the PUDC, UNDP Gabon is recruiting a Chief Engineering Specialist. He/she will lead on the design, implementation, monitoring and quality assurance of infrastructure projects under the PUDC Programme. He/she will supervise his/her team members, oversee vendors, manage financial resources and maintain partnerships for the timely delivery of engineering projects to national counterparts.

SCOPE OF WORK

Lead on the implementation of engineering projects, focusing on the achievement of the following results:

- Lead, coordinate and manage the PUDC team of engineers in delivering on engineering projects

- Contribute to the development and periodic review of the PUDC Programme’s Workplans and Budgets in order to ensure that engineering projects are completed on time and within budget

- Engage with technical counterparts within Government at Ministerial and decentralised Government level to achieve consensus on engineering project design and planning- related issues

- Analyse technical documents and studies provided to UNDP by the various ministries and national entities involved in the Programme

- Co-ordinate planning visits to project sites; verify technical studies against realities on the ground; ensure adequate documentation of findings from site visits and their incorporation in project specifications

- Oversee engineering (civil, electrical, water and energy) from preliminary site preparation to commissioning, final completion and handover to national counterparts.

- Contribute to the PUDC Programme narrative and financial reports, both for internal and external use

- Help ensure that the PUDC Programme is managed and implemented in accordance with UNDP’s Programme and Project Management requirements as well as financial rules and regulations

Contribute to PUDC procurement processes for the selection of vendors / contractors, focusing on the achievement of the following results:

- Contribute to the development and implementation of the Programme’s Procurement plan

- Contribute to the design and implementation of procurement strategies to ensure value for money for engineering projects

- Develop terms of reference for vendors and/or contractors for engineering projects

- Review and validate tender documents before publication for engineering projects

- Review and validate bills of quantities for engineering works

- Participate in bidder selection processes such as site visits and bid evaluation panels

- Participate in negotiation processes to ensure value for money for engineering projects

Lead on engineering projects monitoring, quality assurance and risk management, focusing on the achievement of the following results:

- Contribute to the development and implementation of the Programme’s Monitoring and Evaluation plan and related Travel plan

- Ensure that findings from site visits to engineering projects are adequately documented, disseminated and that corrective measures are taken on time by contractors

- Ensure that the engineering projects are fully compliant with UNDP’s project quality assurance system as well as UNDP’s social and environmental standards monitoring system

- Coordinate the identification, registration, mitigation and regular monitoring of risks identified related to engineering projects under the PUDC

- Act as the contractors’ primary point of contact for supervision purposes

- Review and validate technical attachments to invoices submitted by contractors

- Lead on inspection visits to completed engineering projects; ensure that UNDP specifications, requirements and safety standards are fully met

- Contribute significantly to contractor management processes, including contract amendments, payment, and performance assessment.

- Manage infrastructure project handover processes in line with UNDP policies and procedures

Contribute to developing and sustaining effective partnerships around the PUDC programme, focusing on the achievement of the following results:

- Contribute to the development and implementation of a PUDC programme stakeholders’ engagement strategy

- Ensure meaningful consultation and involvement of stakeholders at key stages of infrastructure project implementation, including community members, local, provincial, national authorities as well as civil society

- Participate in programme and/or partnerships discussions with Government, International Financial Institutions, Bilateral and Multilateral donors, and the UN system

- Help mobilise additional resources for the PUDC and other related programmes or projects

Contribute to the gathering and dissemination of knowledge generated under the PUDC programme, focusing on the achievement of the following results:

- Contribute to the development and implementation of the PUDC programme’s knowledge management and communications strategy

- Help inform the design, production and dissemination of communication products; support efforts towards the visibility of project results, best practices and lessons learned

- Help ensure that knowledge generated through site visits and progress reports are adequately documented and communicated to policy and decision-makers

- Assist in identifying and addressing opportunities for capacity development either through training or systems development, in particular at decentralised level

The incumbent will perform other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities:

- Responsible for the supervision and performance management of Engineers and support staff in PUDC project management team.

INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENT

The Chief Engineering Specialist will work under the direct supervision of the PUDC Programme Manager. He/she will also liaise with the Team Leader : Governance & Poverty Reduction on programme oversight-related matters, the Oversight Unit as well as the Operations Team.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

COMPETENCIES

Core competencies

Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Knowledge and understanding of the operational frameworks in the organization and ability to make good judgments and quick decisions within such frameworks.

Business Development - Collective Intelligence Design: Ability to bring together diverse groups of people, data, information or ideas, and technology to design services or solutions.

Business Management - Risk Management: Ability to identify and organize action around mitigating and proactively managing risks.

Business Management - Monitoring: Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback on the consistency or discrepancy between planned and actual activities and programme performance and results.

2030 Agenda: Prosperity - Inclusive Growth: Urban Community Infrastructure /Assets.

Business Direction & Strategy - Systems Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Business Management - Portfolio Management: Ability to select, prioritize and control the organization’s programmes and projects, in line with its strategic objectives and capacity; ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives and the maintenance of business-as-usual, while optimizing return on investment.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS OF THE SUCCESSFUL IPSA

Min. Education requirements

• Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in engineering, preferably in civil/infrastructure engineering and/or electrical engineering, hydraulics and agronomy, or related field is required, or

• A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the above fields combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Min. years of relevant work experience

• Minimum of 7 years (with master’s degree) or 9 years (with bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible experience at the national or international level in managing the construction of large-scale infrastructure projects, including buildings, road infrastructure, electricity (off-grid renewables), drilling, value chains, and agricultural equipment, is required.

Required experience and skills

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Solomon Islands has a predominantly rural population, with approximately 600,000 people (74% of the population) living in rural areas and relying largely on subsistence agriculture. Most households engage in small-scale farming primarily for food security, with limited surplus sales. Livestock ownership is widespread, particularly pigs and poultry, across approximately 80,000 households distributed over 350 islands. Organic waste management remains largely informal and unregulated.

Access to modern energy services is limited, especially in rural areas. Fuelwood and other biomass remain the dominant cooking fuels, while electricity supply is scarce and grid access does not reach the majority of rural communities. Electricity tariffs are among the highest in the Pacific region. The country’s Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) identifies the energy sector as the main contributor to greenhouse gas emissions (95% of total emissions), underscoring the importance of renewable energy solutions for climate mitigation and sustainable development.

Biogas technology presents a viable opportunity to convert livestock manure and organic waste into clean energy for cooking and power generation, reducing reliance on fossil fuels and traditional biomass while mitigating environmental and health impacts. However, biogas systems in Solomon Islands remain underdeveloped.

The SENBIOSIS project is a nationwide programme supporting biogas investments to transform organic waste into energy, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and improve rural livelihoods. Its objectives are to strengthen farmers’ capacity to manage biogas systems and establish sustainable financing mechanisms to support initial capital investments.

In this context, UNDP is recruiting a Project Associate to support procurement and administrative functions of the SENBIOSIS project.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Project Associate will be under the direct supervision of the Project Coordinator.

UNDP retains intellectual property and other proprietary rights over all materials that have a direct relation to the project.

Under the overall supervision of the Project Coordinator, the Project Associate will manage and oversee all procurement activities related to the construction of biogas systems and the acquisition of project goods and services and provide integrated administrative and operational support under the Solomon Islands Biogas Project (SENBIOSIS – Sustainable Energy from BIOgas in Solomon Islands).

1. Lead and manage end-to-end procurement processes

- Ensure all procurement activities are in accordance with UNDP Procurement Rules, donor requirements, and national regulations

- Conduct procurement planning

- Preparation and solicitate procurement documents

- Manage the bidding processes

- Provide support to evaluation committees

- Award contracts

- Monitor the performance of suppliers

- Conduct contract closure

2. Ensure effective supplier and contract management

- Liaise with suppliers, contractors, and project staff to secure timely delivery of goods and services

- Conduct basic supplier performance monitoring

- Document lessons learned

- Ensure transparency, fairness, and value for money in all procurement activities

3. Coordinate international and local logistics processes

- Oversee all related importation, shipping, customs clearance, insurance, and sustainability compliance for biogas equipment and other project-related goods.

4. Provide administrative and operational support to the project

- Manage travel authorizations and field missions logistics

- Oversee office operations, workshops and stakeholder meetings logistics

- Conduct asset tracking

- Provide day-to-day support to technical experts and project staff

5. Support financial and HR administration

- Prepare and file documentations

- Assist with budget monitoring and expenditure tracking

- Provide administrative inputs to financial and donor reports

- Document related revolving funds

- Coordinate with financial institutions

6. Ensure proper records management and reporting

- Maintain organized electronic and physical filing systems in line with UNDP standard

- Draft outline correspondence and operational reports

- Contribute and provide procurement and administrative inputs to the annual, mid-term, and final reports

7. Strengthen compliance, internal controls, and risk management

- Ensure adherence to UNDP policies and audit requirements

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is a UN agency that works in about 170 countries and territories, helping eradicate poverty, reduce inequalities and exclusion, and build resilience. It thereby helps them sustain progress and achieve Sustainable Development Goals. In Ukraine, UNDP operates with three programme priorities: Democratic Governance and Inclusive Social Fabric, Inclusive and Sustainable Economic Recovery and Growth, and Sustainable Environment and Energy Transformation.

Since the start of the hostilities in 2014 and the full-scale invasion in 2022, UNDP in Ukraine has been present on the ground, through its hubs around the country, supporting regional and local authorities and civil society partners in their emergency response and crisis management efforts.

Lessons from the past years informed the development of UNDP’s Country Programme Document (2025-2029) and the scale-up of the Area-Based Recovery (ABR) Framework. The Framework’s programmatic pillars of Reconstruction, Returns, Resilience, and Reforms are focused on ensuring community recovery and creating conditions for the return to a development pathway in Ukraine.

The Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) Analyst will support the design, implementation, coordination and monitoring of MHPSS initiatives under the Area-Based Recovery Framework, with a particular focus on strengthening community-based MHPSS systems and services.

The incumbent will promote UNDP's mandate as a gender-responsive organization with zero tolerance to discriminatory and abusive behaviour, including sexual harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse.

Duties and Responsibilities

1) Contribute to the design and implementation of MHPSS initiatives under the ABR Framework:

• Contributing to the integration of MHPSS considerations into relevant ABR interventions, including community recovery, social services, healthcare, veteran reintegration and support to vulnerable population groups.

2) Support implementation of community-based MHPSS system strengthening initiatives:

• Providing technical support to projects implemented with partners aimed at assessing and strengthening MHPSS systems at community level.

• Supporting the planning and implementation of community-level assessments, including mapping of MHPSS services and stakeholders, identification of needs, service gaps, barriers to access and opportunities for strengthening local MHPSS systems.

• Providing technical and programmatic support to initiatives aimed at strengthening referral pathways, case management, multidisciplinary cooperation and intersectoral coordination at community level.

• Facilitating engagement and coordination with local authorities, healthcare and social service providers, civil society organizations and other relevant stakeholders to support implementation of community-based MHPSS initiatives.

• Supporting the development and implementation of practical recommendations and locally appropriate solutions aimed at improving accessibility, coordination, continuity and quality of MHPSS services.

• Providing technical inputs to procurement processes related to the establishment or strengthening of MHPSS services and infrastructure, including preparation and review of technical specifications and requirements.

3) Ensure coordination and implementation of MHPSS projects and activities:

• Coordinating implementation of assigned MHPSS activities with implementing partners and other relevant stakeholders.

• Monitoring implementation progress and following up with partners on agreed activities, deliverables, timelines and expected results.

• Reviewing technical and programme deliverables submitted by implementing partners and providing inputs and recommendations, as appropriate.

• Identifying implementation challenges and contributing to the development of practical solutions and adjustments in coordination with relevant programme colleagues and partners.

• Participating in relevant MHPSS coordination mechanisms, as appropriate, and contributing to coordination, collaboration and information exchange with relevant partners and stakeholders.

4) Contribute to monitoring, reporting, capacity development and knowledge management:

• Monitoring and analysing results of MHPSS interventions and contributing to programme-level monitoring and reporting.

• Collecting, analysing and systematizing information on implementation progress, results, challenges and lessons learned.

• Contributing to the preparation of programme reports, analytical materials, presentations, briefs and other MHPSS-related documentation.

• Supporting the design and implementation of capacity-development activities based on identified needs and gaps, including trainings, workshops, consultations, conferences and knowledge-sharing events.

• Identifying and documenting lessons learned, good practices and approaches that may inform further development and replication of MHPSS interventions.

• Contributing to knowledge sharing on MHPSS within the ABR portfolio and with relevant partners and stakeholders.

5) Promote Gender Equality and a Safe, Inclusive Workplace

• Demonstrate leadership and personal accountability in fostering an organizational culture of gender equality and zero tolerance for any form of sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment.

• Respect and promote diversity and inclusion by ensuring all team members, partners, and vendors are treated equally and fairly, regardless of gender, race, sexual orientation, ethnicity, ability, or other identity markers.

• Model respectful professional behavior by identifying and addressing sexism, gender discrimination, and other forms of bias in internal and external interactions.

• Ensure all personnel and partners are informed of, and adhere to, corporate policies on sexual harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, and codes of conduct.

• Support work-life balance and care responsibilities by recognizing the caregiving roles of both women and men, and encouraging the use of family-friendly policies, flexible work arrangements, and inclusive facilities.

Timor-Leste, as a developing nation in Southeast Asia, has made significant strides in promoting digital transformation across various sectors of governance. In line with this, the Government of Timor-Leste has recognized the need to accelerate the digitization of its public services and enhance digital literacy across its population, particularly in remote and underserved areas. The Dalan Digital Project aims to strengthen the digital infrastructure and services in Timor-Leste, promoting digital citizenship and enhancing the government's capacity to deliver public services digitally. The project's overarching goal is to contribute to the creation of a more digitally empowered society, where citizens can access essential services through innovative, efficient, and secure digital platforms. In this regard, Dalan Digital will focus on promoting digital inclusion, improving the quality of public services, and enhancing transparency in government processes.

The project aligns with Timor-Leste’s national strategies, including the Timor Digital 2032 Vision, which sets a roadmap for leveraging digital technologies to foster economic development, social inclusion, and governance reforms. The Dalan Digital Project also complements ongoing initiatives under the Ministry of Transport and Communications, the Ministry of State Administration and the Ministry of Justice to bring public services closer to citizens and improve institutional capacity in the public sector.

In addition to fostering digital transformation within the government, Dalan Digital aims to strengthen public-private partnerships, foster collaboration with international development partners, and support the development of a digital ecosystem that empowers youth, women, and marginalized communities to fully participate in the digital economy.

By advancing digital literacy, creating digital public services, and establishing the necessary governance frameworks, the Dalan Digital Project will contribute to a more connected and transparent society, where citizens are empowered to actively engage with government and access services with ease.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Country Office in the Kingdom of Bahrain operates within the context of a high-income, net-contributing country, where UNDP engagement is fully funded through government cost-sharing and aligned with national development priorities. Bahrain is implementing an ambitious national reform agenda under Bahrain Vision 2030 and the Government Programme (2023–2026), with a strong focus on economic diversification, fiscal sustainability, effective governance, environmental resilience, digital transformation, and inclusive human development. As a net contributor country, UNDP Bahrain maintains a lean operational footprint while delivering high-value technical assistance, policy advisory services, and innovation-driven solutions in support of national priorities.

UNDP Bahrain’s programme is guided by the Country Programme Document (CPD) 2025–2029, approved by the UNDP Executive Board in January 2025, and is fully aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) 2025–2029. The financial envelope for the 2025–2029 Country Programme Document (CPD) is structured around a total estimated cost of US 2.5 million for Economic Prosperity (Outcome 1) and US 5 million for Environmental Sustainability (Outcome 3). As of late 2025, the Country Office manages seven ongoing projects with a total remaining budget of approximately US$ 1.8 million. These initiatives are distributed across the three CPD outcomes: Outcome 1 (Economic Prosperity) and Outcome 3 (Environmental Sustainability) each account for about 37–38% of the project count, while Outcome 2 (Governance) makes up the remaining 25%. Notable projects include the SIU and KIP Chemicals initiatives, whereas others like D4SMEs, Rule of Law, and Youth Leadership.

The CPD positions UNDP as a trusted strategic partner to the Government of Bahrain, contributing to UNSDCF outcomes through integrated, multi-sectoral interventions that address complex development challenges at the intersection of economic prosperity, governance and human rights, and environmental sustainability. Under the Country Programme Document (CPD) 2025–2029, UNDP Bahrain’s engagement is structured around three interrelated CPD pillars:

(i) Economic prosperity and sustainable livelihoods;

(ii) Effective governance, human rights, and access to justice; and

(iii) Environmental sustainability and climate resilience.

These pillars reflect national priorities under Bahrain Vision 2030 and the Government Programme (2023–2026), and constitute UNDP’s substantive contribution to the implementation of the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) 2025–2029.

To ensure coherence, integration, and efficient delivery within a lean Country Office structure, the Bahrain CO operationalizes the three CPD pillars through two integrated programme clusters. The first cluster brings together economic transformation, sustainable livelihoods, and environmental sustainability, the second cluster focuses on governance, human rights, access to justice, and social inclusion.

This two-cluster delivery model enables the Country Office to manage complexity, promote synergies across CPD pillars, and apply a portfolio approach to programme design, implementation, and partnerships. Staff are therefore expected to work across thematic boundaries, contribute to integrated solutions, and support joint programming within the UN system, while ensuring results-based management, quality assurance, and alignment with national and UNSDCF priorities.

In this context the Programme Unit works to support achievement of UNDP strategic objectives and to help the Country Office act with both ambition and scale to address urgent problems facing the country, the region, as well as global conditions. Programme staff assist the Country Office in formulating and implementing programme strategies that go beyond solving immediate development challenges to create future smart and integrated systemic changes in resilience and capacity building within the country.

Background

The Green and Inclusive Development (GID) Programme is one of the main areas of focus in UNDP Lebanon; currently implements numerous projects in Lebanon that range in thematic areas from climate change, biodiversity conservation, institutional support, industrial depollution, decentralized renewable energy projects and solid waste management. The programme also works on the support of host-communities in response to the Syrian refugee crisis and is the Social and Environmental Safeguards focal point for the office; therefore, the Programme also ensures the integration of environmental best-practices into the overall implementation strategy of UNDP.

The Global Environment Facility (GEF) Small Grants Programme (SGP) is implemented by UNDP on behalf of the GEF Partnership. UNDP oversees the Small Grants Programme (SGP) through the Vertical Hub and the Nature Hub of Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS). Funded by the Global Environment Facility (GEF), the Small Grants Programme efficiently channels direct grants to non-governmental and community-based organizations to help them cope with climate change; conserve biodiversity; protect international waters; reduce the impact of Persistent Organic Pollutants; and prevent land degradation. Helping communities with their initiatives for sustainable livelihoods while generating global environmental benefits is the core inspiration of the Small Grants Programme.

Launched in 1992 as a corporate programme of the GEF, the GEF Small Grants Programme (GEF SGP) has supported local action for over thirty years to address global environmental concerns. SGP aims to deliver global environmental benefits in the GEF focal areas of biodiversity conservation, climate change mitigation, protection of international waters, prevention of land degradation, and elimination of persistent organic pollutants through community-based approaches. To date, SGP has funded over 29,000 community-based projects covering more than 120 countries. It has gained considerable experiences at the community level, including adapting to climate change while addressing issues of the GEF focal areas. Further information can be found at: https://sgp.undp.org/.

The current project intends to recruit a Project Technical Officer to coordinate and oversee the implementation of the SGP activities in Lebanon in addition to other environment-related initiatives managed by the Green and Inclusive Development programme in Lebanon Country Office.

Duties and Responsibilities:

a) Ensure effective management of the SGP Country Programme team

- Supervise the SGP Country Programme Associate/ Assistant and provide necessary guidance and coaching;

- Promote and maintain effective teamwork within the SGP Country Programme team, the National Steering Committee members, and with the UNDP CO team;

- Prepare and implement annual work plan, including strategic and/or innovative initiatives, with set delivery and co-financing targets; draft annual SGP Country Office administrative and project operational budget proposal

- Set annual performance parameters and learning objectives for the SGP Country Programme team, assess their performance and provide feedback.

b) Ensure Programme/Portfolio Development and Management

- Keep abreast of national environmental concerns and priorities as well as the socio-economic conditions and trends as they relate to the SGP and assess their impact on SGP’s work and programme.

- Ensure formulation and implementation of the Country Programme Strategy (CPS), and its periodic review and update.

- Manage the SGP grant allocations and country operating budget, maintain the financial integrity of the programme by ensuring adherence to SGP Standard Operating Procedures as well as UNDP rules and regulations, and ensure timely and effective use of SGP resources.

- Exercise quality control over the development of a portfolio of project ideas and concepts, and closely monitor the programme implementation progress and results.

- Organize periodic stakeholder workshops and project development sessions for civil society organizations (CSOs) and local communities, and potential applicants and other stakeholders to inform about SGP and its Strategic Initiatives.

- Work closely with Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and Community-based Organizations (CBOs) in preparation of project concepts and proposals to ensure that projects fit with the SGP Strategic Initiatives, Country Programme Strategy, and technical guidance notes;

- Authorize and manage project planning grants as required.

- Oversee ongoing SGP grant projects and conduct periodic project monitoring field visits and provide technical and operational support and guidance to SGP grantees as required.

- Plan and serve as secretary to the National Steering Committee meetings.

- Support and closely coordinate with the National Steering Committee and Technical Advisory Group where relevant, in the process of project proposal review, selection and approval, especially the initial appraisal of proposals and assessment of eligibility.

- Foster programme, project, and policy linkages between the SGP and the full or medium-sized GEF projects, planned or underway in the country, as well as those of other government, donors and development partners.

- Report periodically to the Central Programme Management Team (CPMT) on programme implementation status, including annual monitoring reporting, financial reporting, audit, and update the relevant SGP databases.

- Undertake monitoring and evaluation of SGP Country Programme and projects, and grant maker initiatives, in coordination with National Steering Committee (NSC) and CPMT.

- Perform and coordinate administrative tasks (i.e. procurement, travel) adhering to SGP SOPs procurement rules and regulation, as required for programme implementation.

c) Resource Mobilization and Partnerships

- Establish and maintain close working relationships with stakeholders as well as promote the value, comparative advantages, and ensure visibility of the SGP.

- Assess interest and priorities of key donors and other development partners and develop/update and implement the resource mobilization and partnership strategy to mobilize resources from and develop partnerships with the government, donors and other partners to best leverage SGP resources and develop programme level partnerships.

- Support SGP grantees in securing co-financing and project level partnerships and assist in identifying opportunities and resources for sustaining and scaling up projects.

d) Facilitate Knowledge Management and Communication

- Document programme/project stories, lessons learned, and best practices in SGP programme/project development, implementation, and oversight.

- Access SGP and other global and regional knowledge, distill best practices and facilitate their dissemination and incorporation within SGP Country Programme and projects, UNDP CO, and to counterparts and partners;

- Support capacity building and networking of grantees to facilitate knowledge exchange, and promote uptake through Knowledge platforms, Knowledge fairs etc.

e) Ensure Monitoring and Progress Controls

- Monitor and ensure that SGP programme results and impacts are aligned with national strategies and priorities, as well as SGP strategies and approaches, and contribute to transformational change, global environmental conservation, and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals.

- Oversee the development and implementation of an innovative, technically sound, and socially inclusive grant portfolio, ensuring quality, compliance, and delivery of intended results.

- Monitor the effective and efficient use of financial, technical, and operational resources to maximize programme and project impact and ensure value for money.

- Track performance and progress against approved work plans, targets, and results frameworks, and recommend corrective actions where necessary.

- Ensure timely monitoring, reporting, knowledge management, and documentation of programme results, lessons learned, and good practices.

- Foster trust and accountability among clients, donors, and stakeholders through transparent reporting and proactive engagement, while identifying opportunities to enhance programme visibility, partnerships, and co-financing.

f) Manage the implementation of GID Environment/Nature related projects

- Provide technical support and coordination through leading the planning, implementation, and monitoring of projects activities in alignment with national priorities, donor requirements and UNDP regulations.

- Prepare annual workplans, managing budgets and disbursements in compliance with UNDP rules, and developing terms of reference and implementation strategies.

- Review outputs from consultants and partners, producing regular progress and donor reports.

- Coordinate closely with government entities, research institutions, and local stakeholders to assess [MB3] [UT4] needs, set priorities, and design/ensure effective interventions, while mobilizing technical expertise, organizing awareness activities, and promoting synergies with other local programmes and partners.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Project Technical Officer will be working under the overall guidance of the Deputy Resident Representative, the SGP Regional Programme Specialist, and the direct supervision of the Programme Specialist of Lebanon’s Green and Inclusive Development Programme. The Project Technical Officer will be responsible for overseeing the implementation of the SGP at the country level, including direct supervision of the SGP Programme Associate if applicable and coordination of the National Steering Committee.

OCHA's mission is to mobilize and coordinate effective and principled humanitarian action in partnership with national and international actors to alleviate human suffering in disasters and emergencies, advocate the rights of people in need, promote preparedness and prevention and facilitate sustainable solutions.

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments
